title: Winless no more: Chargers hold off Ravens after forcing late fumble
summary: The Chargers' defense stifles Baltimore's running backs, and Justin Herbert steps up in Los Angeles' first win.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- The Los Angeles Chargers , who had opened the 2026 season at 0-8 and had not won a game since Week 16 of the 2025 campaign, finally breathed a sigh of relief after a 23-20 triumph over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night.
Not that they didn't have to slug it out to get there. The victory wasn't sealed until Tarheeb Still forced a fumble from Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers that fellow cornerback Elijah Molden recovered at the Chargers' 46-yard line with around two minutes left to play.
Los Angeles had been off to its worst start since opening the 2000 season 0-11 on the way to a 1-15 finish, but the Chargers scored on their first possession of Monday's contest and never trailed the rest of the way.
The Chargers were physical on both sides of the ball, as they limited Baltimore's run game to a season-low 16 yards while gaining 160 rushing yards of their own.
And they did what they had only done one other time this season -- score the first time they had the ball -- to set the tone. Quarterback Justin Herbert , who had a season-low 18 pass attempts, finished off the six-play, 63-yard drive with a 22-yard rushing touchdown.
Not only was it the first time since their Week 3 loss at the Buffalo Bills that the Chargers had scored on their opening drive, it was Herbert's first rushing touchdown since Week 9 last season. And as the evening unfolded, there were likely more smiles on the Bolts' sideline, including from coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert, than in the first eight games combined.
Most surprising performance: An offense that has struggled to find impact on the perimeter, especially in wide receiver Ladd McConkey 's absence (back), got a bump from Tre' Harris . Harris, who had just six yards receiving on seven targets in last week's loss to the visiting Houston Texans , posted 86 yards in Monday's first half alone. He registered five of the Chargers' six first-half receptions, and the 86 yards represented a career high before the second quarter was even over. (Harris didn't tally a catch in the second half.)
Stat to know: The Ravens' 16 rushing yards were Baltimore's season low and a season low allowed by the Chargers' D. Los Angeles handled the line of scrimmage with such physicality that Baltimore's Derrick Henry finished with 10 yards rushing on 10 carries. Before Monday, the Chargers had held just one team under 100 yards rushing this season ( Las Vegas Raiders with 57 in Week 2).
What to make of the QB performance: Herbert entered the game second in the league with 11 interceptions ( Daniel Jones has 12) and second in sacks (32), but he found some rhythm thanks to his mobility. His first completion -- a 22-yarder to Harris -- came on a roll to his right, and the signal-caller was a willing runner at critical moments. Herbert's 22-yard run to finish off the Chargers' first possession was his first rushing score since Week 9 in 2025. His 18 pass attempts were a season low, but the approach kept Herbert out of harm's way -- a week after he was sacked eight times by the Texans. -- Jeff Legwold
Next game: vs. New York Jets (4:05 p.m. ET Sunday)
The Ravens' season has officially bottomed out. The loss to the previously winless Chargers is one of the most embarrassing defeats in franchise history -- and it happened at home on the national stage.
Wideout Zay Flowers' fumble with 2:01 remaining was costly for the Ravens, who lost to a team 0-8 or worse for just the second time in their 31-year existence. The other was an overtime setback to the 0-13 Miami Dolphins 19 years ago that led to the firing of coach Brian Billick.
Holding onto the ball in critical situations has been a problem for Flowers, who has logged four lost fumbles in the fourth quarter (including playoffs) since 2023. That's the most by any wide receiver over that span, according to ESPN Research.
The Ravens were hoping to keep their season alive in case injured quarterback Lamar Jackson (right thumb) could return. But Baltimore's playoff chances took a major hit in falling to the NFL's last winless team.
Baltimore, which lost for the fifth straight time, has dropped two games back of the final playoff spot in the AFC with eight weeks remaining. The Ravens' projected playoff chances plummeted to 4%, according to ESPN Analytics.
In his Ravens debut, quarterback Jacoby Brissett was inconsistent, but he didn't receive much help from a struggling running game and a lackluster offensive line. Brissett was sacked twice but hit nine times.
The Ravens' home dominance has completely disappeared. Baltimore has lost seven of its past eight games at M&T Bank Stadium.
Trend to watch: The Ravens continue to dig themselves into an early hole, allowing a touchdown on the opening drive for the third straight game. To make matters worse, Justin Herbert went untouched on that 22-yard scoring scramble, which is tied for the longest run by a quarterback against Baltimore this season. Baltimore has allowed 57 points in the first quarter; only three teams (Raiders, Falcons and Browns) have given up more. Coach Jesse Minter, who calls the defensive plays, hasn't had this unit ready at the outset of games.
Stat to know: On a night when running back Derrick Henry did relatively nothing on the ground, he scored two touchdowns for his first multiple-score game in seven weeks. Henry recorded his ninth season with 10 or more rushing touchdowns, which ties LaDainian Tomlinson for the most in NFL history. Henry finished with 10 rushing yards, which were his fewest in three years. He was hit at the line or behind it on eight of his 10 carries.
Most surprising performance: Tight end Mark Andrews made an immediate connection with Brissett, catching eight passes for 82 yards. That's the most receiving yards for Andrews in 24 games, dating back to September 2025. Andrews has been dealing with a broken hand since Week 3. -- Jamison Hensley
Next game: at Carolina Panthers (1 p.m. ET Sunday)
author: Jeff Legwold and Jamison Hensley

title: Chargers finally get their first win: 'Thrilled, let's do it every week'
summary: The Chargers beat the Ravens 23-30 on Monday night to earn their first win since Week 16 of last season, bringing a franchise-wide sigh of relief.
full_text:
It took 331 days, and probably far more bouts with indigestion, but the Los Angeles Chargers finally closed out a game with a win.
The Chargers' 23-20 victory over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night at M&T Bank Stadium was their first since Week 16 of the 2025 season (34-17 vs. the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 21) and brought a welcome, franchise-wide sigh of relief.
"Thrilled, let's do it every week,'' Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters after the game. "Good to see the smiles back on the faces.''
In a season in which so much has gone wrong for the Chargers -- from an injury-ravaged offensive line that featured three rookie starters Monday night, to quarterback Justin Herbert 's struggles in the league's lowest-scoring offense -- Monday's game was a most welcome experience all around.
The Chargers equaled their highest point total of the season, Herbert did not throw an interception for the first time this season and Los Angeles never trailed after scoring on its first possession of the game.
And even that touchdown, a 22-yard run by Herbert, came with a notable tag attached given it was Herbert's first touchdown run since Week 9 of 2025.
It was also the Chargers' (1-8) first game of the season without a turnover.
"It's been a tough year,'' Herbert said. "It hasn't gone our way this year and for those guys to continue to fight, not point fingers, and stick together -- they've earned it and I'm really happy for them.''
The team had been off to its worst start since opening the 2000 season 0-11 en route to a 1-15 finish.
But after a cross-country trip, the Chargers showed physicality on both sides of the ball from the start. Their defense forced three-and-outs on the Ravens' first three possessions, and the offense scored on two of its first three possessions.
Quarterback Jacoby Brissett , making his first start since being traded to the Ravens, threw for 340 yards, but Los Angeles held Baltimore to a season-low 16 yards rushing. Derrick Henry finished with only 10 yards on 10 carries.
"Heck of a run wall, [a] big emphasis on that,'' Harbaugh said. "Just trying not to let [Henry] get started ... guys just battled the whole night.''
The Chargers' offense also pounded out a season-best 160 rushing yards as running back Omarion Hampton finished with 105 yards on 22 carries for his first 100-yard game of the season. Herbert added 51 rushing yards even as he had a season-low 18 pass attempts.
"It was awesome,'' Herbert said. "It was so much up front, they work so hard ... and [Hampton] is about as talented as it gets, the way he runs.''
Not that there weren't some tense moments before the Chargers were able to close it out. The Ravens, down 23-20, had started to move the ball just before the two-minute warning when cornerback Tarheeb Still forced a fumble on Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers that Elijah Molden recovered at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:03 left to play.
Los Angeles then failed to get a first down that would have locked up the win, so Baltimore had one last gasp. But cornerback Cam Hart knocked down Brissett's last-ditch pass at the Chargers' 4-yard line to finish the game.
"You cherish them, let's do this every week,'' Harbaugh said. "Good to see the smiles back and that was something [safety] Derwin (James ) said, lot of fight in this team, and we all see it, glad it was rewarded.''
author: Jeff Legwold

title: Hamilton says Ravens 'disgracing' standards after embarrassing loss to Chargers
summary: Pro Bowl safety Kyle Hamilton vented after the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the previously winless Chargers on Monday night, which was one of the most embarrassing defeats in team history.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- Pro Bowl safety Kyle Hamilton vented after the Baltimore Ravens ' 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night, which was one of the most embarrassing defeats in team history.
"Right now, we are disgracing those standards, as leaders, as players and as a team," Hamilton said. "Whatever flak we get is warranted."
Hamilton expressed more bitterness by adding, "All the talking that's been going on is all just talk. If you don't go out there and do what you're supposed to do, stop the run, nobody really cares, and stuff like this just stops mattering."
After losing their fifth straight game, the Ravens (4-6) watched their season bottom out and their reputation get tarnished by falling to the Chargers (1-8), who had been the NFL's last winless team.
Over the past 25 years, the Ravens had built a reputation as one of the league's most physical teams. On Monday night, Baltimore got pushed around by a team that hadn't won in 330 days.
Baltimore failed to establish the run on offense and couldn't stop the run on defense. When the Ravens had a chance to deliver a comeback victory late in the game, wide receiver Zay Flowers had the ball ripped from his grasp near midfield with two minutes remaining.
This marked the Ravens' second loss to a team 0-8 or worse in their 31-year existence. The other was an overtime loss to the 0-13 Dolphins 19 years ago, and that led to the firing of coach Brian Billick.
"At some point, you have to just decide about your manhood and what you want out of your job," Hamilton said. "This is our job. We can all get fired; that's the reality of it. If we don't do better, then we get fired."
The Ravens acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals 10 days ago, hoping to keep their season alive in case injured quarterback Lamar Jackson (right thumb surgery) could return late in the season. But those plans took a major hit with Monday's loss.
Baltimore fell two games back of the seventh and final playoff spot in the AFC. The Ravens' projected playoff chances dropped to 4%, according to ESPN Analytics.
"This week, we just have to have an outlook of, 'Look, it's do or die at this point," Hamilton said. "You show what you're made of, and we're going to rock with who we're going to rock with."
Unlike Hamilton, Flowers chose not to talk. He left the locker room as soon as reporters entered.
Flowers' four lost fumbles in the fourth quarter since 2023 are the most by a wide receiver during that span.
"You want the ball in his hands, but you also want to understand the situation [and] understand what they're going to be trying to do," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "[It's important to] know when the journey's over."
The Ravens' biggest struggle was running the ball, which has been a problem without Jackson. Running back Derrick Henry finished with 10 rushing yards because he was contacted at or behind the line of scrimmage on eight of his 10 carries.
Baltimore's 16 yards rushing were its third fewest in franchise history.
"Of course, Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it's a grown-man's league," Henry said. "We just haven't been doing our job good enough. It hasn't been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that."
The Ravens are in the midst of one of their most frustrating stretches ever. Baltimore entered Monday night having lost three consecutive games by 20 or more points for the first time in team history. Then, the Ravens lost to a winless team at home and on a national stage.
"You can hold people accountable; you can tell the truth," Minter said. "But in reality, you're playing on Monday night, and you have another game on Sunday, so it's going to be about getting up off the mat and coming back to work. And I think we have the guys to do that, but we have to do it. We keep talking about things, and [we need] more action."
author: Jamison Hensley

title: Sources: Patriots fear QB Maye has broken ankle, could miss rest of season
summary: The Patriots are concerned that Drake Maye sustained a fractured ankle, sources told ESPN, an injury that could sideline the star QB for the rest of the season.
full_text:
MUNICH -- The New England Patriots are concerned that quarterback Drake Maye may have sustained a fractured ankle during Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
Maye will miss an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season, sources told Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
Maye was knocked out in the first quarter of Sunday's 35-10 loss after he was sacked by Detroit defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , who suffered a serious knee injury while celebrating the play.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel declined to discuss specifics about the injury or Maye's return timeline with reporters Monday, saying he wanted to wait until Maye returns from Germany.
Vrabel said earlier Monday during an interview with Boston radio station WEEI that Maye remained in Germany and did not travel with the Patriots "just out of caution."
Vrabel told reporters that the he did not expect Maye to play in Week 12, when the Patriots (5-5) return from their bye to face the Los Angeles Chargers . Vrabel added, however, that he does not anticipate New England seeking a quarterback replacement outside the organization.
"I'm excited for this challenge, and I hope that everybody else is, because that's really what we're at," Vrabel said. "We're 5-5 in the middle of the season -- just past the middle of the season -- and we've got a bye, and looking forward to the challenge."
Maye, who wasn't in the locker room after the game when reporters were present, was replaced Sunday by backup Tommy DeVito .
The Patriots also have rookie quarterback Behren Morton , a seventh-round draft pick from Texas Tech, on the roster, and could look to add another quarterback to the team, potentially on the practice squad.
"Tommy and Behren Morton have been in our system, have been working," Vrabel said Monday. "Behren Morton's been improving. He's been working each week, and I know that if he has to play for us, that he'll be ready to go."
Maye's streak of 43 straight starts (including playoffs) is the third longest among NFL quarterbacks behind the Bills' Josh Allen (146) and Lions' Jared Goff (82).
Hutchinson sacked Maye on third down, ripping him down from behind with what appeared to be a possible hip-drop tackle. Hutchinson's right arm reached around Maye's right shoulder pad as he brought him down and landed on the quarterback's lower leg.
Sources told Rapoport that Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after initial tests revealed a torn ACL in his right knee. After leaping in the air to celebrate the sack, Hutchinson landed awkwardly and immediately clutched his knee.
On the Fox broadcast, rules analyst Mike Pereira said Hutchinson's tackle was "not a hip drop."
"Three things have to happen: you have to unweight yourself, swivel all around the back and land on the back of his leg below the knee," Pereira said. "This was more of a horse collar-type pulled down from behind. [But] certainly not a horse collar penalty."
Walt Anderson, the NFL's officiating rules analyst, confirmed Pereira's explanation through a league spokesman, noting it was not a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting.
It was also not a foul for a horse collar tackle, Pereira noted, because neither the collar nor the nameplate were grabbed. No penalty was called on the play by referee Clay Martin's crew.
Asked his view of the play, Vrabel said he wasn't going to assume there was any ill intent.
"However it happened, I don't think it was anything intentional. It's just part of the game," he said.
Maye was helped to his feet and limped to the sideline then later walked to the locker room for further evaluation as DeVito stepped in.
In other injury news, wide receiver A.J. Brown , who returned Sunday after missing two games with a knee injury, was ruled out in the fourth quarter after he sustained a hamstring injury.
"He wasn't able to finish. We'll see what the severity of that is once we get back and kind of go from there," Vrabel said.
author: Mike Reiss

title: Sources: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with torn ACL, possibly more knee damage
summary: Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with what tests showed to be a torn ACL in his right knee, sources told NFL Network.
full_text:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with what tests showed to be a torn ACL in his right knee, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
The two-time Pro Bowl defensive end likely suffered additional damage in the knee, with concern about his meniscus, sources told Rapoport.
Hutchinson received an initial MRI in Germany and was set to have additional tests in the United States now that he has returned, according to sources.
Hutchinson suffered the injury while celebrating a first-quarter sack in the Lions' 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Munich on Sunday.
Hutchinson leaped in the air after his sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye on New England's first drive of the game but went straight to the ground after landing. He immediately grabbed his right knee. He stayed down and eventually was able to walk to the blue medical tent for evaluation. He then walked gingerly to the locker room and didn't return to the game.
He was seen walking out of the stadium with the aid of crutches after the game.
Maye suffered an ankle injury on the sack and also did not return. Sources told ESPN that the Patriots fear Maye suffered a fractured ankle and could also miss the rest of the season.
Hutchinson is second on the Lions with six sacks this season. He has 49 sacks since being selected by the Lions with the No. 2 pick in the 2022 draft.

title: Sources: Jets QB Smith avoided major ankle injury, testing shows
summary: Imaging tests performed on Jets quarterback Geno Smith's injured left ankle did not reveal any major concerns, sources said Monday.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith , who underwent imaging tests Monday on his left ankle, avoided a major injury, sources told the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
Smith dealt with a variety of injuries during Sunday's game, but his ankle provided the biggest concern. He will continue to be evaluated throughout the week, but the hope is that he will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers .
"He's good," a source told ESPN. "He'll be fine."
Coach Aaron Glenn declined to comment on the injury earlier Monday but emphasized that Smith remains New York's starter and pushed back on the notion of playing rookie Cade Klubnik for evaluation purposes.
"Geno's our starter," Glenn said on a videoconference with reporters. "Come on now, let's not do that.
"I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter."
Smith exited twice in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills . He missed the first series of the third quarter due to a concussion evaluation, then returned for one series before hurting his ankle later in the quarter while falling backward on a knockdown by blitzing safety Cole Bishop .
The Jets (2-8), losers of five straight, face the Chargers (0-8) on Sunday at SoFi Stadium.
The 36-year-old Smith, whose contract expires at the end of the season, is having a solid year as the Jets' bridge quarterback. He's 19th in Total QBR (53.3), with 12 touchdown passes and three interceptions, but the Jets are only 26th in scoring (19.4 points per game).
Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson, made his NFL debut Sunday. He threw an interception and was sacked three times while completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.
The Jets' third quarterback is former Tennessee Titans second-round pick Will Levis , who is on the practice squad.
author: Rich Cimini

title: Rams lose center Shelton for 4-6 weeks in latest injury blow
summary: Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Cardinals.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams center Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring and is expected to sit out the next four to six weeks, a team spokesperson said Monday.
Shelton sustained the injury in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Arizona Cardinals . He had not missed an offensive snap this season for the Rams before his injury.
Shelton was replaced at center by Dylan McMahon , who played only nine offensive snaps before he injured his knee. The Rams said Monday that McMahon partially tore his patellar tendon and will be put on injured reserve.
Offensive lineman Beaux Limmer moved to center after McMahon's injury, and backup offensive lineman Bill Murray moved to left guard, playing 49 offensive snaps.
The injuries are just the latest for a Rams offense that is also currently without wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , tight end Terrance Ferguson , and guard Steve Avila .
The Rams, 6-4 after winning four games in a row, are on their bye this week. They host the Green Bay Packers in Week 12.
author: Sarah Barshop

title: Vikings WR Addison needs thumb surgery, is candidate for IR
summary: Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison needs to undergo surgery on his thumb and is a candidate for injured reserve, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Vikings receiver Jordan Addison could be out for a month because of a thumb injury that will require surgery, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.
O'Connell termed it a "freak injury" that occurred while Addison was "catching passes on air" during practice last Friday, aggravating a minor injury Addison had dealt with since training camp. The Vikings listed him as questionable on their injury report and then made him inactive after a short warmup Sunday morning before their 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
O'Connell said Addison's projected return is "right around hopefully that short-term IR kind of window." Players who are placed on injured reserve must miss at least four games.
"I don't anticipate it being a long-term kind of thing," O'Connell said.
If Addison goes on injured reserve, the earliest he could return is for the Vikings' Week 15 game against the Detroit Lions at U.S. Bank Stadium, scheduled to be played on "Sunday Night Football."
Addison missed the Vikings' Week 5 game against the New Orleans Saints because of a hamstring injury. In seven starts this season, he has caught 18 passes for 277 yards and one touchdown.
With Addison sidelined against the Packers, and veteran Jauan Jennings already declared out because of a calf injury, second-year receiver Tai Felton got his third NFL start alongside Justin Jefferson . Felton caught three passes for 33 yards. Another second-year receiver, Myles Price , caught four passes for 49 yards, including a 38-yard touchdown.
The Vikings waived veteran Odell Beckham Jr . last week but he re-signed to their practice squad and would be available for Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City if needed.
author: Kevin Seifert

title: Bears RB Monangai says he's 'on track' to return Sunday against Saints
summary: Bears running back Kyle Monangai said Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints after sitting out five games because of a thumb injury and turf toe.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- The Chicago Bears backfield is nearing the return of Kyle Monangai .
Monangai said Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the New Orleans Saints after sitting out five games because of a thumb injury and turf toe. He has not played since he rushed for a career-high 30 carries for 146 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears' 23-12 victory over the New York Jets on Oct. 4.
The second-year running back practiced Monday as the Bears returned to Halas Hall for a 70-minute session after their bye week. It marked the second practice for Monangai in more than month after he logged limited participation on Nov. 5, two days before the Bears hosted the Buccaneers on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 9.
"The time off definitely helped, but I mean it's going to be there," Monangai said. "Offseason I'll heal it. That will be for then. It's something I can manage now. The time off was needed though for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago."
Monangai said his turf toe injury, which is in his right foot, is something he can "manage" for the rest of the season with the support of plates and orthotics inside of his cleats.
Before his five-game absence, Monangai logged 60 carries for 324 yards and three touchdowns. His 5.4 yards per rush ranks fourth among all players.
The Bears leaned on a combination of running backs Roschon Johnson and Salvon Ahmed to compliment lead rusher D'Andre Swift in Monangai's absence. Chicago has the fourth-best rushing offense (144 yards per game) but has struggled to convert in goal-to-go situations (27th), which prompted coach Ben Johnson to reevaluate the run game during the bye.
"I think over the course of nine games, there's only been three of those nine where we're averaging over four yards a carry," Johnson said last week. "Which, simply in our terms, it's just not good enough right now. And those guys know that, particularly as the weather continues to turn into Bear weather, we're going to need to lean on that run game more and it's going to need to come through for us. I got to look at, is it the fact that we're not getting as many explosives in the run game right now? Is that why the average is low? Or is it, we're just not moving the line of scrimmage? What are those factors? And so being able to have nine games of sample size at this point is going to be really good for us to look into."
Monangai was originally classified as week-to-week by Johnson, which is why the Bears did not put him on injured reserve as they expected him back within four games. The running back did not initially understand the severity of his turf toe injury, which he called "very painful."
"Originally, I thought it was my thumb I was dealing with," Monangai said. "I thought I'd be back very quickly. I didn't foresee this length of time being out."
Getting Monangai back after more than a month is the kind of boost the Bears believe can reignite their run game during a difficult stretch of second-half games that features four NFC North opponents along with two AFC division leaders ( Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills ).
author: Courtney Cronin

title: 🥨 Amon-Ra St. Brown explains Munich fit, TD celly
summary: Inspired by his mother, St. Brown paired a memorable performance with a coordinated Bavarian look alongside his Lions teammates.
full_text:
Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown set off the German gameday tunnel walk sporting traditional Bavarian attire: a lederhosen and a Bavarian jacket and hat in a return to his mother's homeland. Editor's Picks 'I thought he was speaking gibberish': Untold stories of Amon-Ra St. Brown's German upbringing Eric Woodyard Amon-Ra St. Brown on celebrating Lions' win in Germany: 'Like a dream come true' 1 Related
St. Brown was joined by Lions receiver Isaac TeSlaa and long snapper Hogan Hatten , and the group carried beer mugs and offered a toast as they walked out prior to their 35-10 blowout win over New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
Asked after the game about the fit, St. Brown smiled while saying his mother suggested the look and told reporters, "I'm not going to put on some Amazon lederhosen." The @Lions have arrived in style! 🇩🇪

Amon-Ra St Brown, Hogan Hatten and Isaac Teslaa are repping traditional Bavarian outfits 👀 https://t.co/XQGjAjZAQt — NFL UK & Ireland (@NFLUKIRE) November 15, 2026
The @Lions have arrived in style! 🇩🇪

Amon-Ra St Brown, Hogan Hatten and Isaac Teslaa are repping traditional Bavarian outfits 👀 https://t.co/XQGjAjZAQt
St. Brown's mother was born in Leverkusen, and he spent a significant amount of his childhood living in Germany.
St. Brown scored two touchdowns Sunday and called his first score "one of the most memorable" of his career. The Lions added a memorable celebration following his second score to mark the occasion.
Rate the celebration from the @Lions... 😅 https://t.co/MfqzUFu6Qs
St. Brown said the "human centipede" celebration originated with Lions passing game coordinator Mike Kafka, who showed them an NFL Europe highlight as part of a pregame meeting. The NFL Europe players did the human centipede celebration after scoring a touchdown, and the Lions' skill players loved it.
"We were all laughing in the meeting room and said we've got to do it. I said first touchdown we got to do it," St. Brown said. "I scored the first TD, and I was too lit. I forgot to do it. So that was that. ... When I scored [my] second TD, I said now we need to do it. I was on the ground when they pushed me. I said TeSlaa, let's do the celebration. We all did it. It was lit."
Major love to St. Brown and the Lions for embracing the local culture in the NFL's second-to-last international game of the season.
author: Cameron Wolfe

title: NFL Week 11 Power Rankings: Updated 1-32 poll, plus the non-QB MVPs for every team at midseason
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 11? We made our 1-32 list and picked the non-quarterback MVPs for each roster.
full_text:
When the NFL Honors awards ceremony takes place the Thursday before Super Bowl LXI , it's almost guaranteed that the player who accepts the MVP award will be a quarterback. Former Vikings running back Adrian Peterson is the only non-QB to be named MVP since 2010, and only three non-QBs have won in the 21st century.
But what if quarterbacks were disqualified from winning the award? In addition to our weekly 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick the non-quarterback MVP for each team at midseason. Which defenders and skill players deserve love for what they've done this season?
To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings:
The Patriots' trip to Munich could not have gone any worse, as they left Germany with a two-game losing streak and without quarterback Drake Maye ( ankle injury ). That caused them to fall the most out of any team in our Power Rankings compared to last week (three spots), and Maye could be out for the season if his ankle is fractured. New England is 1-3 in its past four games, with all of its losses coming to NFC North opponents.
The Browns are in the top 15 of our rankings for the first time this season after another comeback win -- this time against the Texans . Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson has conducted a winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime in all six of the Browns' wins. Watson joins the Cowboys' Troy Aikman (1990) and Lions' Matthew Stafford (2016) as the only QBs in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to achieve that feat, per ESPN Research.
The Commanders made the biggest climb of any team this week (three spots) after a Thursday night win over the Giants. Washington is 2-1 since its bye week, and it's still not out of the NFC East race yet, two games behind first-place New York while owning the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Giants. However, the Commanders have only one divisional game left to boost their playoff odds -- Week 18 versus the Cowboys .
Let's get into the full list, starting with a slight change at No. 1 from last week .

title: Seven things Solak thinks: Burrow for MVP? Lions in trouble? Vikings-49ers is the game of the year?
summary: Get ready for Week 11 with what makes Vikings-49ers must-watch football, Joe Burrow's MVP case and how Aidan Hutchinson's injury could impact the Lions.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 11 ? At first, it might look like a sleepy slate. Jaguars at Giants and Raiders at Broncos are two of our marquee games. But there's one contest that, to this enormous football nerd, is the game of the season.
Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.
Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide'
This week, I'll expand on why Joe Burrow looks like an MVP, tell you about another Rams personnel innovation, project eventual QB changes for two NFC South teams and wonder if Aidan Hutchinson is the final defensive injury the Lions can't overcome. But first, here's one matchup you won't want to miss.
Jump to: Shanahan vs. Flores is matchup of the best Why Burrow is the MVP Rams should lean on their RBs Hutchinson's injury wounds Lions bad Do Falcons need a new 2027 QB? Do Saints need a new 2027 QB? Mendoza's debut is a scratch Some extra inklings
The Vikings have had a fraught three weeks. Everyone was excited to see them face the Lions in Week 8 -- the best offense they'd faced in a while. Detroit stuck it to 'em with a sick schematic wrinkle for which the Vikings were not prepared -- multiple tight ends lined up in the backfield as quasi-fullbacks to pave open rushing lanes.
pic.twitter.com/H0N9PKfBkX
Then the Vikings played the Bills in Week 9 -- Josh Allen and another grindy running game -- and the Packers in Week 10 with Jordan Love coming off a flamethrower performance against the Patriots. At various points over those three weeks, it has felt like the upcoming test for the Vikings has been the test for the Vikings. Will this be the offense to build a blueprint against Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unique defense? Or will Flores prove that his defense is insurmountable even by the league's top attacks?
The NFL rarely exists in such absolutes. All of those particular matchups were exciting and educational in their own ways. But if there's one game I've been waiting for with bated breath in the seasonlong pursuit of an answer to the Flores defense, it's this one: Vikings against 49ers in Week 11.
This is quite literally the best against the best. The 49ers lead the league in points per drive (3.0), success rate and EPA per play on offense. The Vikings lead the league in points per drive (1.24), success rate and EPA per play (if you eliminate the Bucs' rainstorm game against the Falcons, which is cheating, but I don't care) on defense. It does not get better for offensive football than what the 49ers are doing right now. It does not get better for defensive football than what the Vikings are doing right now. Snap the pool stick, toss it down at midfield and let's see who survives.
Not only are these the most effective units on their respective sides of the ball, there's actually some structural similarity between the two. The Flores defense has been exhaustively covered this season, but if you've missed them to this point of the season: The Vikings are blitzing on 72.3% of opposing dropbacks through 10 weeks. I shouldn't need to tell you where that ranks among league defenses, but just in case: It's first.
To blitz that much sounds deranged (and likely is), but Flores has greatly deepened the meaning of blitz packages in the modern NFL. He doesn't blitz to get the quarterback down, but blitzes to force the ball out fast to predictable hot reads. He blitzes to keep the back and tight end in protection and limit the pass-catching options the opponent can deploy. For many defensive coordinators, the blitz is an end to itself -- they want to get to third-and-long so they can blitz. For Flores, the blitz is a means to many different ends depending on the opponent and context.
Let's consider the route distributions. Opposing offenses get all five routes into the concept 31.2% of the time against the Vikings, which is the lowest number in any season as far back as I have data (2017). The aggressive blitz fronts -- with five or six (or seven or eight) bodies on them -- keep backs and tight ends in the formation to protect, which makes the Vikings all the more dangerous when they drop bodies into coverage and only bring four on the rush. Against the Vikings' four-man rush, opposing quarterbacks are averaging an eternity to throw the ball (3.34 seconds, highest in the NFL Next Gen Stats database) and still suffer a 44% pressure rate, which leads the league.
pic.twitter.com/UHBBPDyXiE
Flip the coin to the other side, and you'll discover that no offense gets five routes into the concept more often than the San Francisco 49ers . On 72.5% of Brock Purdy 's dropbacks this season, the 49ers have five eligible in the concept -- that's tied for the highest rate of any offense over the past two seasons with ... the 2025 49ers.
Why so many players out in the concept? It is indicative of a change that's been underway in San Francisco's offense since the Christian McCaffrey trade in 2022.
When you employ McCaffrey, you don't keep the back in to protect . Are you out of your mind? Have you seen this guy catch passes? The only season of the past five years in which the 49ers have been below 72.5% in five-out rate was 2024, when McCaffrey was hurt for much of the year. When the Cowboys called up a Cover 0 blitz in Week 10 in a got-to-have-it spot late against the 49ers, San Francisco had no issue getting McCaffrey into the route and quickly throwing him the ball against a defensive end ( Von Miller ) peeling off into coverage. A 74-yard touchdown later, the game was over.
pic.twitter.com/np7G3Y1UNI
This peeling defensive end is a big part of how the Vikings like to deal with pass-catching backs, mind you. No edge rusher drops into coverage more often than Andrew Van Ginkel . But for as special of a Swiss Army knife as the Gink is ... do you like him dropping with McCaffrey in space?
Much as Flores throws additional bodies at the offensive core to force players into protection, the 49ers throw as many eligible bodies as possible into the route to force defenders to win in coverage. Because the ball can go to George Kittle and McCaffrey at high volumes, it's hard to play man coverage against 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan -- your linebackers and safeties will be victimized -- so you have to drop into zone, which pulls players out of your blitz packages. Purdy has been blitzed on 29.1% of his dropbacks, 27th among 37 qualifying quarterbacks this season.
When I say "five receivers in the route," you might instinctively think about spreading the defense out -- and you'd be right. But the 49ers, critically, do not play from spread formations. No offense has been more condensed in the entire Next Gen Stats era than the 2026 49ers, who have an average formational width of 18.9 yards -- a full yard tighter than second place (the 2025 49ers at 19.9 yards).
This has been another big leap in the 49ers' offense since they acquired McCaffrey. From 2017 to 2021 -- B.C, or Before Christian -- the 49ers were in condensed sets on 42.3% of their offensive snaps. After the McCaffrey trade, that number leaps to 61.2% -- easily the highest among offenses.
The condensed sets serve several purposes. They allow the 49ers to get extra blockers into the run concept more easily -- they wouldn't have nearly as complex of a running game otherwise. They allow pre-snap motions to hit faster across the formation, which strains how well a defense communicates -- linebackers have to see a lot more when all 11 players are in the offensive picture. They all but guarantee opposing cornerbacks have outside leverage on the 49ers'…
author: Ben Solak

title: Concerns for four NFL teams on the playoff bubble: Barnwell on the Cowboys, Patriots, Raiders, Texans
summary: The Cowboys' defense got lit up, the Patriots lost Drake Maye, the Raiders are adjusting to Fernando Mendoza, and the Texans can't find support for C.J. Stroud.
full_text:
If the trade deadline marks the beginning of the NFL's stretch run, there are four teams that might already be pulling up lame. In the first game after the deadline, with rosters essentially locked for the remainder of 2026, four franchises that were already facing difficult paths forward to the postseason looked overmatched in Week 10 losses.
The Cowboys, Patriots, Raiders and Texans all lost in Week 10, and while they each had serious playoff aspirations at one point or another this season. none of the four is currently a favorite to make it into the 14-team field, per ESPN's Football Power Index .
Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'
They're collectively down ... but are they out? I'll start in Big D, where the Cowboys spent most of the day chasing shadows on and off the field.
Note: All playoff chance percentages are via ESPN's Football Power Index.
Jump to: Cowboys | Patriots | Raiders | Texans
Peak playoff probability in 2026: 82.1% (after Week 4) Current playoff probability: 42.1% Week 10: Lost 46-40 to 49ers
The Cowboys allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 yards, the most they've allowed in a home game in the 67-year history of the franchise . And if there's a play that will come to stand as the example of how badly things have gone wrong for the Cowboys on defense since the ill-fated decision to trade Micah Parsons to the Packers, it would be the 66-yard Christian McCaffrey touchdown that essentially sealed up the game with 3:23 to go.
Under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker, the Cowboys have not been a blitz-happy team. They blitz at the league's third-lowest rate, in part to protect a shaky secondary and in part to align with the Vic Fangio-style defense that the Cowboys chose to install as they hired Parker, two years after it was at its peak. They still manage to get pressure at a top-10 rate, but when the Cowboys don't get home, they have the second-worst pass defense in the NFL by Total QBR.
Quarterback Brock Purdy had sliced the Cowboys blitz apart when Parker did send extra rushers to this point, going 5-of-5 for 131 yards with a touchdown, but also took two sacks on seven dropbacks. Blitzing turned the game into a boom-or-serious-bust situation for the Cowboys. Most defenses would prefer to major in what they do best with the game on the line, but with the 49ers averaging more than 7 yards per play with a 50% success rate when the Cowboys didn't blitz Sunday, Parker must have felt like he needed to throw a changeup to have any hope of stopping them.
So, facing a second-and-10 situation after a George Kittle false start, Parker sent the house. The Cowboys sent six defenders, twisting their three down linemen and blitzing an extra rusher to the weak side of the line, hoping that the pass rush would get home and force Purdy off his spot. Even if it didn't work, the blitz might push McCaffrey to come across the formation to try to block the free rusher, taking a key receiver out of the progression for the 49ers.
That didn't happen. McCaffrey immediately released vertically out of the backfield. The defender responsible for him was the edge rusher on that side of the field, who dropped off the line as a product of the Cowboys overloading the weakside rush to leave them with five coverage defenders against five eligible receivers. And that's how the Cowboys ended up with 37-year-old Von Miller in man-to-man coverage against the best receiving back in football with the game on the line.
It wasn't much of a contest, although Miller did manage to hit 18.5 mph as he tried to chase down McCaffrey, the first time he has reached that speed on a single snap since 2021, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. This was probably the easiest catch and run of McCaffrey's career and his second long touchdown reception of the game, having turned a catch against a blown coverage on a scramble drill into a 74-yard score earlier in the contest (two linebackers had attempted to chase down Purdy and neither ran with McCaffrey). It was the third touchdown of 60 or more yards the Cowboys had allowed in the game, too, marking the first time a defense has allowed three of those in a single contest since October 2007.
It's too simplistic to blame Miller, who should never be expected to hold up in man coverage against McCaffrey. It's not as simple as blaming Parker, who dialed up the sort of exotic pressure that other teams have pulled out in key situations for stops. It's just the reality of what happens in Dallas. Since this team traded Parsons, the Cowboys have spent the past 27 games throwing stuff at the wall on defense and hoping something sticks.
That's how you end up with Miller, an edge rusher at the very end of his career and nearly a half-decade removed from his last season as a full-time starter, with the game on the line needing a stop. It's how you end up with Parker sending an all-out blitz despite the 49ers picking those blitzes apart for most of the game, in the hopes of fooling one of the league's best offensive coaches. It's how you end up with Parker, as the Cowboys followed a disastrous year with an experienced-but-uninspiring defensive coordinator in Matt Eberflus by hiring what they hoped would be the league's next exciting young defensive mind.
And trying to chase down the problems with their defense, the Cowboys and Jerry Jones have desperately made personnel decision after personnel decision. They traded first- and second-round picks to the Jets for Quinnen Williams , and while he has been very good during his time in Dallas, he hasn't been able to singlehandedly fix the defense. It seemed like a microcosm when Williams literally ripped the ball out of Kaelon Black 's hands to try to force a game-altering fumble on San Francisco's next and final possession, only for the 49ers running back to fall on the football before any of Williams' teammates could react.
The Cowboys have traded for Kenny Clark , Rashan Gary , Joey Porter Jr . and Dee Winters . They used first-round picks on Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence . They signed Cobie Durant and Jalen Thompson in free agency. None of those moves is egregious in a vacuum. In the big picture, though, there's no identity, no coherent plan and no short- or long-term vision. The Cowboys traded Parsons because they wanted to save money and spread the cash and draft capital around the roster, then traded most of that capital away to land Williams, who signed a massive extension. They're spending $182.2 million in cash on their defense this season, the fifth most of any team in the league, so they aren't saving anything by the decision to move on from Parsons. They look and operate like an organization that desperately wants something to work on defense but has no idea how to make it happen.
And so, while wildly chasing down solutions on defense as a personnel philosophy, the Cowboys do the same thing on the field. Deebo Samuel Sr .'s 70-yard touchdown on an end-around was one of the most dramatic collective overpursuits you'll ever see on a single snap, as Samuel was expected to gain 35 yards from the moment he touched the ball by the Next Gen Stats model, the most by any runner on any play since 2022.
It's one thing to get fooled on misdirection, but edge rusher James Houston and defensive tackle Elijah Garcia were the two down linemen on the backside of the play who might have forced Samuel back to their help or at least slowed down the hybrid receiver. Instead, after Samuel takes the pitch, Houston and Garcia each take what appeared to be nine false steps in the wrong direction before realizing something's up. By the time they confirm Samuel has the ball, they're completely out of the play.
Porter's the cornerback on the backside of the field and the last line of defense. While Samuel has a convoy, Porter wasn't able to fight through Purdy to get to the sideline and force Samuel back to the inside, where help might have been able to stop Samuel from scoring. Instead, Samuel eluded a diving…
author: Bill Barnwell

title: Tiering all 32 teams' chances to make the playoffs, from the locks to the long shots
summary: We placed all 32 teams into tiers based on their likelihood of making the playoffs.
full_text:
The back half of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, and the playoff race is heating up. Though the standings tell us a lot about teams' chances to reach the postseason , they don't tell us everything . Team strength, injuries, tiebreakers, future strength of schedule and more can shift those odds up or down and don't show up in the win or loss columns.
So, ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder placed all 32 teams into eight tiers of playoff hopes, ranging from clear Super Bowl contenders to those already looking ahead to 2027. There is some fluidity in between, because for as confident as we feel about the league right now, things could look quite different once Week 18 rolls around. The tiers are based on information from ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI), betting lines , metrics, health status and some instinct.
Walder ranked the teams within each tier too. All percentages and statistical rankings are through Sunday unless otherwise indicated, and playoff chances are from the FPI.
Jump to a team: ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF SEA | TB | TEN | WSH
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.7% Chances to win the NFC West: 95.5% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 39.9%
Injuries have hit some of the 49ers' best players -- edge rusher Nick Bosa missed five games and wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't played since Week 6 -- but San Francisco is the FPI's Super Bowl favorite for two main reasons. The Niners are basically a lock to reach the playoffs and a heavy favorite to win the NFC West given their lead and head-to-head wins over the Rams and the Seahawks . Brock Purdy entered Week 10 as the No. 1 quarterback in QBR, and he is arguably the league's MVP thus far. Kyle Shanahan might be the Coach of the Year thus far too.
Chances to make the playoffs: >99.9% Chances to win the AFC East: >99.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 30.0%
The Bills entered this season as the AFC favorite, and nothing that has happened in the first 10 weeks has dispelled that notion. Their hold on the conference looks even stronger now than it did then thanks to their conference-best record and the Ravens falling out of contention. Buffalo's defense (16th in EPA per play) is still a concern, but quarterback Josh Allen , running back James Cook III and the Bills' offensive line do more than enough damage on offense.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9% Chances to win the AFC South: 98.8% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 22.5%
The Jaguars were already playoff locks and clearly one of the top two teams in the AFC before the trade deadline, when they acquired safety Jessie Bates III along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux . The Davis deal from the Jaguars' perspective is one of the worst trades in years , but there's also little doubt Jacksonville is better today than it was a week ago. And the Jaguars were great a week ago! The Jaguars rank in the top five in EPA per dropback on offense and EPA allowed per dropback as well as EPA allowed per designed rush on defense.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.8% Chances to win the AFC West: 44.6% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 15.4%
The Chiefs faced three major questions entering the season:
How would quarterback Patrick Mahomes fare after recovering from a torn ACL suffered last December?
What kind of impact would free agent running back Kenneth Walker III have on the offense?
Could the defense survive the loss of starting cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson ?
The answer to every question has been positive for Kansas City. In particular, Walker has helped transform the Chiefs' rushing attack into a strength. And coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has managed to keep the defense strong too: It ranks sixth in EPA per play.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9% Chances to win the AFC North: 93.2% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 19.0%
It's something we've wondered about for years: What would happen if the Bengals could manage to combine a peak Joe Burrow season with simply mediocre defense? Well, we're finding out. Burrow is in the MVP race, and Cincinnati's defense is ranked 11th in EPA per play. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been outstanding and provide a sky-high ceiling for the passing offense. Plus, the Bengals have a very easy schedule the rest of the way.
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.6% Chances to win the AFC West: 55.4% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 9.5%
Somehow, it's working . Despite Bo Nix falling well short of expectations -- he entered Week 10 ranked 24th out of 31 qualifiers in QBR -- the Broncos are a virtual lock to reach the playoffs and have a great shot at winning the AFC West. The defense hasn't quite lived up to its reputation (13th in EPA per play), but Denver also hasn't had All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II for every game, either. If the offense can keep its recent momentum (the Broncos have put up 26 points in each of their past three games), Denver can be a threat in the postseason. The Broncos have a soft schedule the rest of the way, too.
Chances to make the playoffs: 97.0% Chances to win the NFC North: 45.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 14.4%
Minnesota's trade-deadline deal for quarterback Kirk Cousins breathed new life into its season. That move instantly increased the Vikings' playoff chances from 65% to 83% at the time of the deal, according to the FPI. But that deal was about what comes next. With Brian Flores' incredible defense leading the way, the Vikings can and should have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The moment Flores leaves, a real possibility in this upcoming offseason, the team's contention window vanishes, so the Vikings need to take advantage of this opportunity. Minnesota's 30-10 dismantling of the Packers on Sunday only reinforced what a good trade it was.
Chances to make the playoffs: 84.9% Chances to win the NFC North: 20.2% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 11.1%
Chicago entered its bye week as a near lock to reach the playoffs and very much a team that could go all the way. Quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a significant step forward, and the fact that the Bears are 7-2 despite Williams missing three games is a testament to the coaching staff and how strong this team is. Coordinator Dennis Allen was already getting the most out of a lacking defensive roster when the Bears acquired the best defensive tackle in the league in Jeffery Simmons as they prepare for what they hope is a Super Bowl run.
Chances to make the playoffs: 89.4% Chances to win the NFC North: 33.1% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 10.4%
If they played in a normal division, the Lions would be even safer than this, especially after the team's blowout win over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday -- albeit with New England missing quarterback Drake Maye for most of that contest . But Detroit's record has it on the verge of a playoff berth despite playing in a stacked NFC North and with the Seahawks and Rams looming as other wild-card threats. There's little doubt the Lions can score points. But the X factor down the stretch and in the postseason will be their defense, which ranks 23rd in EPA per play and now faces a significant knee injury to star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson .
Chances to make the playoffs: 83.6% Chances to win the AFC North: 4.9% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 1.6%
The Steelers are barreling toward another playoff berth thanks to their running game and defense. No team in the league is more efficient (by EPA per play) on the ground than the Steelers -- hello, Jaylen Warren ! -- and the team's run defense hasn't allowed opponents to rush successfully against them. Getting past the Bengals to win the division will be a tall order, but the fall of the Ravens helps widen the Steelers' path to the postseason.
Chances to make the playoffs: 62.6% Chances to win the NFC South: 62.3% Chances to make the Super Bowl: 5.5%
The FPI believes the Bucs are the best team in the…
author: Seth Walder

title: Drake Maye injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito carry the offense?
summary: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.
full_text:
The outlook for the New England Patriots ' 2026 season has been dramatically altered. After suffering an injury on the Patriots' first drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, quarterback Drake Maye did not fly back from Munich with the team out of caution, as the team is concerned he might have sustained a fractured ankle .
The 5-5 Patriots haven't been among the AFC's elite in 2026, but were hoping to make a charge to the playoffs -- and Maye potentially finding his past runner-up MVP form was one of their silver linings.
When Maye was taking care of the football and extending plays, the Patriots were explosive and flashed potential to hang with the best -- as a Week 4 win at the Buffalo Bills showed. But when Maye was not buttoned-up with his decision-making (he entered Sunday with 11 INTs) the Patriots struggled. When he was cleaner in that area, it was just enough to get by some of the league's lower-echelon teams, with close wins against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins , who have won a combined three games this season.
Coach Mike Vrabel often says it's hard to win when a team's best players don't play well, and simply put, Maye is the team's best offensive player.
Entering Week 10, he ranked top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3).
Now potentially without Maye for weeks or even the season, the question is can the team make it back to the playoffs?
ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss answers some of the top questions about the trickle-down effect of Maye's injury and analyst Matt Bowen answers a fantasy question on what to expect if you have Patriots players in your lineup.
When Vrabel was hired as head coach in January 2025, he said the team's goals were to win the division, host home playoff games and compete for championships. Their odds of doing that without Maye are closer to zero, starting with the current standings -- they are 5-5 while the AFC East rival Bills are 8-1.
Here is the rest of the Patriots' schedule: they are on the bye in Week 11 before a road trip to face the winless Los Angeles Chargers , then two huge home games in a span of five days -- vs. the Bills (Dec. 6) and the Minnesota Vikings (Dec. 10). Then they're at the Kansas City Chiefs and the New York Jets before finishing the year with home games against the Denver Broncos and the Miami Dolphins .
They have played poorly the past two weeks in blowout losses to the Packers and Lions, ravaged by injuries across the roster, but Maye's presence -- even as he battled through inconsistent play with turnovers -- gave them a sliver of hope.
Consider what happened Sunday: After New England's opening drive when Maye was injured on the final play, the Patriots totaled seven points and gained 82 yards over 10 drives, averaging 1.9 yards per play (not including kneel down). New England punted on eight of those drives, with seven three-and-outs.
Maye has been the driving force behind the passing game. Entering Sunday, Patriots pass catchers recorded 38.1% of their yards after the catch, the third-lowest total in the NFL behind the Texans (37.1%) and Giants (36.8%), per ESPN Research.
The defense has also mightily struggled as of late, giving the offense little room for error. Since Week 7, the Patriots are giving up the second-most yards per game (411.5), behind only the 1-8 Tennessee Titans .
With some of the NFL's elite teams on the horizon, life without Maye could look bleak.
The recovery timeline for similar injuries have varied, depending on the severity.
In January, Broncos QB Bo Nix suffered a broken ankle and underwent surgery two days later. The initial recovery timetable reported was 12 weeks . In April, he underwent a clean-up surgery to fix bone spurs. Nix, who had a history of ankle injuries, was ready for training camp in July.
In September 2022, 49ers QB Trey Lance underwent surgery on his right ankle after suffering "a fibula fracture and ligament disruption" in a game. The injury ended his season and required a follow-up surgery in December of that year to remove hardware that was causing irritation. He was cleared to participate in OTAs the following April.
In 2024, 49ers linebacker Fred Warner said he had been playing most of the season with a fractured bone in his ankle .
As we learn more about the specific type of ankle injury Maye has, the timeline will become clearer.
Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has been through this before, most recently in 2016 when Tom Brady was serving a four-game NFL suspension and Jimmy Garoppolo and Jacoby Brissett stepped in to help the team to a 3-1 record. McDaniels' offense has flexibility to play to the specific strengths of the quarterback, with an obvious example coming with some designed runs for Brissett in 2016 that never would have been called with Brady.
DeVito struggled Sunday when taking over for Maye, and Vrabel noted it was a tough position for him to be thrust into because backups don't receive many, if any, first-team repetitions during the week of practice.
"There were some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp, and really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye," Vrabel said. "I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand, whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket, get us in the right play, get the ball out quicker or look at protections or rotation, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve."
DeVito had success with the deep ball in the preseason, and made improvements processing information on defensive coverages, so some of the things he has going for him are similar to Maye. And, of course, DeVito briefly caught fire with the New York Giants when thrust into a similar situation.
In eight career starts (all with the Giants), DeVito is 3-5 with a 26.4 QBR, 65.3% completion rate, 1,170 passing yards for seven touchdowns, one interception and 34 sacks. He isn't as mobile as Maye, with only 36 rushes for 198 yards during those starts.
Vrabel reflected optimism in the backup QB they signed to a two-year contract with a maximum value of $7.4 million in March.
"I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said Monday. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
That is a longer-shot scenario in terms of signing someone to be the starter, mainly due to the intricacies of the offense and the time crunch -- and also because there aren't many, if any, capable starters available. A more likely option initially is to utilize the 17-player practice squad to add a third layer of quarterback depth behind DeVito and rookie Behren Morton , the seventh-round pick from Texas Tech.
Another avenue to explore would be other teams' practice squads to see if there is a worthy option to sign to the 53-man roster in a backup role. There are 15 quarterbacks on practice squads, a group including Will Levis (Jets), Nick Mullens (Jaguars), Kyle Trask (Cowboys) Hendon Hooker (Titans), Jake Browning (Chargers) and Luke Altmyer (Lions).
"I don't see that being the case right now, but we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see," Vrabel said Monday about the possibility of adding a quarterback.
New England mostly had good fortune health-wise in its surprise run to the Super Bowl last year, and 2026 has been the other side of the coin. Vrabel noted in a Monday radio interview that it evens out over time.
