It began in the spring when tight end Julian Hill , who they signed to be their No. 2 option and a blocking force, sustained a season-ending knee injury and veteran outside linebacker Harold Landry III had an undisclosed injury that landed him on the physically unable to perform list (where he remains). Then receiver A.J. Brown suffered a…
author: Mike Reiss

title: Two games, 14 hours, 242 plays: Inside four NFL referees' unprecedented same-day doubleheader
summary: An inside look at the 14-hour day of four referees who worked an afternoon game in Indianapolis and the Sunday night game in Cincinnati.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- IT'S HARD to tell when an NFL referee is actually in a hurry because they're always jogging from here to there.
Jogging onto the field with a bag of footballs, jogging to take their position behind the quarterback, jogging over to the replay monitor to screen a review. But at 4:37 p.m. ET Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium, when referee Don Willard power-walks with his suitcase and bag through the concrete bowels of the stadium, led by a police officer and flanked by three other game officials and an NFL security staffer, it's clear that he is in a hurry.
"Next stop: Beep! Beep!" umpire Terry Killens yells as the group walks out of the official's locker room in street clothes.
Kickoff for their second NFL game of the day is less than four hours away, and Cincinnati is still two hours down the dark and construction-interrupted I-74. The crew has a police escort to the highway and then they'll be on their own. Willard, Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew hold their snack boxes in one hand and roll their small suitcases with the other. Willard totes a pink Pedialyte -- necessary for replenishing the 3 hours and 13 minutes of intense focus he had just put in during the Colts' 24-22 victory over the Dolphins. Larrew munches on a cookie while he walks and then accidentally drops it on the floor.
Two stadium security workers wave goodbye and yell, "Drive safe!" But these four VIPs won't be driving themselves anywhere. A black sprinter van waits for the entourage, tucked just behind the Dolphins' team buses. Another stadium security worker escorts a CBS videographer into the area to capture their departure. He backpedals to get the perfect shot: four officials boarding a van that will take them from Indianapolis to Cincinnati for the Bengals' Sunday night game against the Steelers -- pulling double-duty to officiate two NFL games on the same day.
The security worker tells another stadium worker, "Wow, this is really a big deal, huh?" He explains that the CBS camera he has shepherded into place is going to send its footage to NBC's "Sunday Night Football" broadcast (which will later highlight the feat).
The NFL declined ESPN's request to speak to the four officials and Ramon George, the league's head of officiating training and development, who was responsible for sorting through the travel disaster created by the FAA's nationwide ground stop Friday.
George worked through the night Friday to create new crews for each game based on geographic convenience so the game officials didn't need to use unreliable air travel. The result was flip-card changes for the game officials that were longer than the inactive players lists.
Each of the four double-duty referees work on different crews. At the Sunday night game, the inactives sheet handed out to the media pregame featured an entirely different crew of the seven on-field officials than what had been previously slated, with the parenthetical "the instant replay official still is Chad Adams."
The situation is likely unprecedented in NFL history because it's risky. The league intentionally arranges for officials to travel on the day before games (except in the case of international games, for which they travel further in advance), so they are settled and adjusted and can get good rest before they work.
Former NFL vice president of officiating and current Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino told ESPN that when he was running the department, having a game official work two games on the same day "would be the last resort," which shows how extreme the circumstances were. Typically an emergency alternate scenario would impact one crew and two officials, not the entire 17-crew system.
"I am sure they went through all the different iterations and exhausted every option," Blandino said.
• How Harbaugh, Minter aim to revive season • What is wrong with the Chargers' offense? • McCarthy's growth is showing in the numbers • Patriots need to fix lack of defensive effort
Blandino said officiating two games in one day is the last resort because "it would be like playing two football games back-to-back. There's the physical aspect of running and the mental exhaustion after a game because you are doing a pre-snap routine for every snap, and then the eight-second play, and then a post-snap routine.
"The officials look like they are not exerting themselves the same way the players are, but they don't get breaks. They don't play one side of the ball. They are out there every snap and every kick. Then to say now I have to reset without any recovery time? That is a challenge."
"It's exhausting because you're looking for something on every single play," said Russell Yurk, ESPN's rules analyst and former VP of replay for the league office. "You're analyzing every single play. You're watching your players. You're watching your keys, you're making judgment calls, and it doesn't really let up the entire game."
Kickoff in Indianapolis. Willard, normally a side judge, has never refereed a regular-season NFL game before, only preseason games and Big Ten conference matchups before he began working for the NFL in 2018. So when he first speaks into the microphone at Lucas Oil Stadium to announce the coin toss, it sounds weird, because his voice is totally unfamiliar.
Following Willard's announcement of an illegal formation penalty that the Colts declined, CBS analyst Spero Dedes says, "I think we need to lower the volume on the officiating mic -- he is interfering with our call."
Walker, the field judge, calls two Miami field goals wide left, and an extra point is no good.
Willard and Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley have a spirited conversation with a lot of hand gesturing on Miami's sideline before the second half kicks off.
On the first play of the second half, Willard's instincts are tested. Colts cornerback Justin Walley hits Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord in the back of his throwing arm. McCord loses the ball with his arm drawn back, poised to throw. The Colts recover in the end zone for a touchdown. But is it a fumble or did he already start to move his arm forward? Willard throws his blue bean bag to mark the spot of the fumble and calls it a fumble recovery touchdown for Indianapolis.
"This is a tough play, because Walley comes behind Kyle McCord and it's the defensive arm that really hits the ball and makes it go forward. As an official you think that ball is going forward because of the pass," said Gene Steratore, a retired official and CBS rules analyst. "But Don has fumble all the way, and it's a great job by him."
Colts tight end Alec Ogletree gets to talking with Willard during a break. "Are you one of the ones going to Cincy after this?" he asks.
Yep, that's us, Willard tells him.
Ogletree knew there were going to be changes to the crew because on Friday, the Colts had gone over information about the officiating crew as a team, but it was all with an asterisk: it was only who they thought would be working the game.
"But we didn't really know who was going to be out there till we got out here," Ogletree said.
"I did ask [Willard], 'So how long you been the ref, like head ref?' He's like, 'First game.'"
Miami cornerback Chris Johnson picks off Daniel Jones and runs it it back 59 yards for a touchdown. Willard is standing at the Indianapolis 42, behind the quarterback as he throws, then runs that same distance back to the end zone to keep the play in front of him.
The first game ends after three hours and 13 minutes -- a long one because Miami kept it close. The double-duty refs shower and change into street clothes for their trip to Cincinnati. They've all packed a second uniform, this one for an outdoor game. It will be much colder at Paycor Stadium.
The weary travelers arrive at Paycor Stadium and bring their luggage straight into the security meeting at the 100-minute mark before game time. Willard carries a massage gun with him, hinting that his focus on the bus ride was as much about recovery as…
author: Kalyn Kahler

title: Let's overreact to Week 10: Cousins changes the NFC North? Hardware for Mahomes, Shanahan?
summary: Will Kirk Cousins be the difference in the NFC North? The Browns are going to the playoffs ... but not the Patriots? Patrick Mahomes for MVP and Kyle Shanahan for COY?
full_text:
We did not do post- trade deadline overreactions last week, preferring to see at least one weekend's worth of NFL games before rushing to judgment about the immediate impact of any of the completed deals.
Now that we've seen the bulk of the Week 10 Sunday games, though? Well, as Dak Prescott would say if we hired him to introduce the weekly overreactions column: Here we gooooo ...
Let's look at five potential takeaways from all the action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the end.
Jump to: Cousins as the difference for the Vikings? Mahomes to win MVP? Browns going to the playoffs? But Patriots missing the playoffs? Shanahan to win COY? Fantasy overreactions
The biggest move at the deadline was Minnesota shipping a third-round pick to Las Vegas for Cousins, the former Vikings QB who was instantly installed as the starter to no one's surprise. Kyler Murray is still hurt (and wasn't playing well anyway), and Carson Wentz 's disastrous performance last Monday night was the main reason the Vikings decided they needed to make this deal. Fair to say the early returns are positive.
Cousins was 21-for-31 for 207 yards, two touchdown passes and an interception in a 30-10 victory over the Packers on Sunday. Solid numbers, nothing eye-popping, but there is important context here about team confidence and vibes in general. This Vikings team looked energized by the return of Cousins, who ran the offense with a proficiency that has eluded all Vikings quarterbacks for the past two seasons. And he did it with just one week of practice.
Minnesota scored the first 20 points of this game. The Vikings' all-world defense overwhelmed Packers quarterback Jordan Love , becoming the first NFL team in 11 years to record eight sacks and three takeaways in the first three quarters of a game. They finished with four takeaways for the game. On offense, star wideout Justin Jefferson set season highs in targets with 13 and catches with nine, finishing with 74 yards and the kind of smile he hasn't flashed since 2024.
The Vikings completed the two-game season sweep of the division-rival Packers and moved into a three-way tie for first place in the historically awesome NFC North. Minnesota, Chicago and Detroit are all 7-2, and Green Bay is 6-4. The Vikings have a 3-1 record in division games, having beaten the Bears in Chicago and losing to the Lions in Detroit .
Yeah, you probably could have guessed where I was going with this answer just by reading the last two sentences of the last paragraph. There is no way to predict anything with confidence with four teams in one division playing this well. Sure, the Packers are 1-3 in division games and their offensive line is struggling, but they're also getting Micah Parsons back at some point. The Lions have won five in a row but might have lost star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a knee injury in Sunday's victory over the Patriots in Munich. The Bears are off this week, so there's not a ton new to say about them, but they've won four in a row and are obviously quite good.
What we can say with confidence is that the acquisition of Cousins forces us to take the Vikings' chances very seriously, even in a division where everyone seems to be excellent. They just need a representative offense to pair with their elite defense, and Cousins right now appears to give them that.
Will it last? No way to know. Cousins is 38 years old and certainly not all he used to be. But he's also clearly better than what the Vikings have been working with since they let Sam Darnold walk after the 2024 season. And the way they looked Sunday tells us his impact has already been felt beyond the white lines. It's a major move -- it's just way too soon to feel sure about anyone's chances to win this NFC North.
Josh Downs also had a fun debut after being acquired by Kansas City , as the Chiefs cruised past the Falcons 35-13 . Running back Kenneth Walker III has been the Chiefs' MVP so far this season, Kansas City's big free agent acquisition from the spring. But Walker missed this game because of a groin injury , which left the Chiefs to rely on rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who had 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, and of course Mahomes, who had a vintage game.
The quarterback was 22-for-35 for 348 yards and five touchdown passes, including an 18-yarder to Downs that put the Chiefs up 14-3 just before halftime. Mahomes has 19 touchdown passes this season.
I think Mahomes is still the best player in the NFL, and he reminded us of that a bit Sunday. But he has also won this award twice. Based on how the voting tends to go, it will probably be harder for him to win again this year. Voters like to give it to someone new. (Before you ask: I am not an NFL MVP voter and never have been.)
Mahomes has also taken a back seat on the hype train to Walker, and Mahomes's overall numbers, though very good, lag behind the performances of Brock Purdy , Joe Burrow , Josh Allen , Trevor Lawrence , etc. Comeback Player of the Year might already be in the bag, and if he keeps throwing five touchdown passes every week, then yeah, MVP would be, too. But I think Mahomes and the Chiefs are very happy to build this season's offense around the running backs and focus on postseason success ahead of individual awards.
Rough day in Munich for the Pats. Not only did they get smoked 35-10 by the Lions , but they lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury after the first series. Wide receiver A.J. Brown 's injury-plagued Patriots debut season continued, as he returned from his ankle injury but had to leave in the second half because of a hamstring injury. New England came into the game already banged up at running back and on the offensive line.
Tommy DeVito relieved Maye and was ineffective, leading us to wonder if the offense can function if Maye has to miss much time -- especially if Brown also sits. New England is 5-5, 3½ games behind first-place Buffalo in the AFC East and a game behind Cleveland, which holds the final wild-card spot, in the AFC standings.
Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION
Twelve of the past 26 teams to lose the Super Bowl have missed the playoffs the following season, and the Patriots are in danger of making that 13 of 27. After making it through last season as one of the healthiest teams in the league, the Patriots are feeling the sting of regression in that area. They have a bye next week, so maybe that gives Maye and/or Brown enough time to get back in the lineup. (It does sound like Maye will be out an extended period of time .) But the problems range beyond that, including a defense that has given up 80 points during the past two weeks and has suddenly developed a disturbing propensity for allowing explosive plays.
It's not over yet, don't get me wrong. I'm not locking the Browns into that No. 7 spot just yet, and the Raiders, Ravens and Texans -- all of whom are in similar spots in the standings -- have plenty of issues. But it's absolutely possible that the Patriots miss the postseason, and if Maye is out for a while, it might even be likely at this point.
After falling behind the Texans 17-0 in the second quarter and still being behind 24-20 in the final minutes of the game, the Browns stormed back for an improbable 27-24 victory and improved to 6-4. After missing last week's game , Deshaun Watson had 312 passing yards and 50 rushing yards, leading a winning fourth-quarter drive for the sixth time this season. The blitzing Browns defense of first-year coordinator Mike Rutenberg made life tough for C.J. Stroud , and Cleveland wore down Houston and kept the score in range for the comeback win.
The Browns are half a game behind the Steelers and 1½ games behind the Bengals in the AFC North. And again, Cleveland occupies the third and final wild-card spot in the projected AFC playoff field.
All due respect to the job that first-year head coach Todd Monken and Rutenberg are…
author: Dan Graziano

title: Big questions: Are Bengals a Super Bowl threat? Could 49ers' offense be even better?
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 10.
full_text:
The Sunday slate for Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Munich between the Patriots and Lions. Detroit improved to 7-2 with a win after the Patriots lost Drake Maye early to an ankle injury.
Back in the United States, the Vikings comfortably defeated the Packers in quarterback Kirk Cousins ' first game since being traded from the Raiders . Without running back Kenneth Walker III (groin injury), the Chiefs started rookie Emmett Johnson , who coasted to 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Falcons. And the Jets went their second straight game without scoring a touchdown, losing to the Bills.
In the late window, rookie quarterbacks Carson Beck (Cardinals) and Fernando Mendoza (Raiders) made their debuts as NFL starters. Beck threw two interceptions and zero touchdowns in a loss to the Rams; Mendoza finished with a rushing score and zero turnovers in a loss to the Seahawks. Offense was not an issue in 49ers-Cowboys, as both teams combined for 86 points in a San Francisco win. Sunday night saw the Bengals put on a clinic in a blowout win over the Steelers and rise to first place in the AFC North.
Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.
Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.
Jump to: PIT-CIN | SF-DAL | SEA-LV LAR-ARI | HOU-CLE | MIA-IND CAR-NO | JAX-TEN | BUF-NYJ KC-ATL | MIN-GB | NE-DET
Catch up on Thursday's game: WSH-NYG
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap
Are the Bengals a true Super Bowl contender? With how the offense is playing, it definitely looks like it. For the first time in franchise history, Cincinnati has scored 30 or more points in five straight games. After a dazzling performance in Madrid, the Bengals carried that momentum into a big AFC North showdown at home. With quarterback Joe Burrow (35-for-44 for 409 passing yards and four TDs) playing at an MVP level and receivers Ja'Marr Chase (11 catches for 231 receiving yards) and Tee Higgins (five catches for 66 yards) also playing as well as they have in their respective careers, this offense is good enough to carry Cincinnati on a deep playoff run.
What to make of the QB performance: At this rate, Burrow will be the unquestioned front-runner to win Most Valuable Player. There was nothing he couldn't do Sunday night -- including hitting Chase in stride on multiple deep balls. Burrow is the first player since 2013 with at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span. -- Ben Baby
Next game: at Commanders (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)
Did the Bengals expose the Steelers' foundational weaknesses? Yes, in every way. The issues that lurked during the Steelers' 6-2 start were shoved into the spotlight in their primetime annihilation by a division foe. The defense, though stacked with some of the league's best and most highly paid defenders, has a talent deficiency in the secondary, significant tackling issues and coverage busts. With games against injured and flawed teams in the second half of the season, the Steelers might still finish with a winning record and even make the playoffs again. But Sunday night's loss showed that the Steelers aren't a serious contender as currently constructed.
What to make of the QB performance: Aaron Rodgers had a career-high eight incompletions to open the game before he finally connected with tight end Darnell Washington for a 5-yard gain late in the second quarter. Unlike the last time the Steelers played in Cincinnati in primetime, Rodgers looked every bit his age Sunday night. In addition to being sacked three times, the 42-year-old finished the game completing just 15 of 29 passes for 143 passing yards, 54 of which came on two long completions to DK Metcalf with the game well out of reach in the fourth quarter.
Best quote from the locker room: "We're not going to drive down the drama road of those types of things. It's a waste of time. It's a waste of energy and we're going to pour our energy into ourselves looking in the mirror and stay focused on the things that we can control," Steelers HC Mike McCarthy when asked how to keep the Steelers' loss from impacting the rest of the season. -- Brooke Pryor
Next game: at Eagles (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)
Fantasy football takeaway: Chase Brown posted a season-best 28.3 points in Sunday night's win. Brown had 10 carries for 44 rushing yards, but it was the receiving numbers that boosted his totals. He finished with eight receptions for 39 receiving yards, adding his first two receiving scores of the season. In the Bengals' pass-heavy system, Brown has the traits to produce on backfield releases, but managers shouldn't expect him to be a primary target inside the red zone at the rate he was Sunday. Brown fits as an RB2 for the Week 11 matchup versus Washington. -- Bowen
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap
As players get healthier, how good can the 49ers' offense be? The 8-1 Niners got WR Deebo Samuel Sr . back from a hamstring injury Sunday and the offense took off, averaging 9.8 yards per play and posting 584 total yards -- the most in any game under coach Kyle Shanahan (since 2017) -- against a bad Cowboys defense. Samuel had 109 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. But San Francisco is about to move up a few weight classes with showdowns against the Vikings and Seahawks defenses the next two weeks. That should offer a strong indication of where the offense is headed, especially if WR Mike Evans returns from Achilles tendinitis for either or both of those games.
What to make of the QB performance: On a day when he was under pressure frequently and sacked five times, quarterback Brock Purdy was unfazed, leading San Francisco's outburst. He made plays on the move, including a 74-yard touchdown toss to RB Christian McCaffrey . More of that will be needed in the coming weeks. -- Nick Wagoner
Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET in Mexico City)
Is it time for the Cowboys to scoreboard watch? Anything is possible mathematically, but the only realistic way the 4-6 Cowboys will make the playoffs is by winning the NFC East. That means they will need help from the Giants (5-3-1). Five of New York's last eight games come against teams with a winning record (Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland, Detroit). Whatever progress the Cowboys thought they were making defensively was exposed by the 49ers. The Cowboys have four games remaining against teams with a winning record (Seattle, Rams, Jacksonville, Giants). The Cowboys almost certainly have to win five of their last eight games to have a chance. And they have not won consecutive games this season.
Trend to watch: In the past three games, the Cowboys have given up six plays of at least 50 yards (four touchdowns). On Sunday, they gave up three touchdowns of at least 66 yards, a first in AT&T Stadium history. On the season, the Cowboys have allowed a league-high eight plays of at least 50 yards. -- Todd Archer
Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)
Fantasy football takeaway: 49ers RB Kaelon Black scored a career-best 14.6 points after 11 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, plus two receptions for 13 yards. He has now seen 11 or more touches in three straight games, with at least 10 points and a touchdown in two. Given his recent usage -- and the 49ers' attempt to reduce the overall volume for Christian McCaffrey -- Black has value as a flex option in deeper leagues. -- Bowen
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap
Is the Seahawks' defense ready for Round 2 versus the 49ers? Seattle allowed the Raiders to net only 163 yards, and it sacked Fernando Mendoza six times. Coach Mike Macdonald's unit has set the bar so high that such dominance was almost expected, especially with Mendoza making his first start and Brock Bowers missing much of the game. It will get harder when the Seahawks return from their Week 11 bye for a game against 49ers QB…
author: NFL Nation

title: The next step in Bo Nix's development? Expanding his fourth-quarter success to the entire game
summary: Nix has a knack for coming through big late in games, but the Broncos want him to play better earlier to lessen the fourth-quarter drama.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos would like Bo Nix to go from being a fourth-quarter quarterback to a four-quarter QB.
This season, and for much of his three-year career, Nix and the team's offense have shown an innate, repeated ability to put it all together in the final quarter, regardless of whatever troubles they faced in the first three. Six of the Broncos' seven wins this season have been by one score. They've won 16 one-score regular-season games in a row, dating to 2025, and Nix has thrown five of his 11 touchdown passes this season in the final period.
So as the 7-2 Broncos emerge from their bye week to host the 4-6 Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday ( 4:25 p.m. ET, Empower Field at Mile High, CBS ), everyone -- from coach Sean Payton to Nix on down -- would like to see the offense utilize its fourth-quarter success much earlier, so the Broncos don't have to perpetually live in a one-score world.
"I don't have the answer," Payton said days before the Broncos beat the Panthers 26-21 in Week 9 after erasing another fourth-quarter deficit. "... I look at it internally myself like, 'Alright, let's get going.' [But] we want to start fast."
The Broncos enter the post-bye portion of their schedule riding a five-game winning streak -- the third time in four seasons under Payton they've had a 5-0 stretch. And Nix had arguably his three most impactful outings of this season in the three games preceding the bye.
The Broncos hope that recent uptick is a sign of things to come for the QB. Nix has thrown for at least 220 passing yards during each of the past three games (had done it only twice in Denver's first six contests). He has also completed 62% of his passes in three of the past four games after doing it only once in his first five. He has thrown five touchdown passes in the past three games, compared with six over the first six. And, yes, the Broncos have four one-score wins during the current win streak.
All of this has occurred since Payton abruptly reassumed playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb after a 2-2 start. Five wins later, the Broncos are tied with the Kansas City Chiefs atop the AFC West and are in the mix to secure home-field advantage in the AFC playoffs for a second consecutive season. And the numbers say that Nix has found a little more in his game over the past month, potentially leading to more consistent, four-quarter performances from him and the offense.
"Look, the guy we see every day is the same, ready, prepared, tough, never down, never looking to blame anybody, he shows up, works his ass off and we win," Broncos offensive tackle Mike McGlinchey said of Nix. "... I feel like that's been the same every week. I think maybe we've played a little better overall, all of us, and maybe people think they see a difference in him."
Nix's play has been a hot-button topic this season, especially during the first month. When Payton took over playcalling, Denver was mired at, or near, the bottom of most major statistical categories, as was Nix.
Some of the offense's struggles before the playcaller change have remained. The Broncos were 20th in passing yards before the change and are 25th now. They averaged 3.6 yards per carry before the change and 3.7 since. But they've scored more, going from 16.8 offensive points per game the first four weeks (tied for 28th) to 24.8 since Week 5 (11th). Their offensive EPA has also increased, going from minus-7.48 expected points added (21st) in the first four weeks to plus-14.49 since Week 5 (12th).

A key to that increased effectiveness is adding more runs to the mix. Payton has used words such as "efficiency" and "balance" to describe his efforts to calm the waters for Nix.
"When we improve the picture around him, it will improve what he can do," Payton said. "... It is truly all of us in there."
The Broncos were 29th in rushing yards per game (81.3), 27th in attempts per game (22.5) and tied for last in the league in runs of 10 yards or more (four) in the first four games. Though the rushing yards (99.6, 25th) and runs of 10-plus yards (nine, 25th) have slightly increased, the number of carries (26.6, 10th) has seen a more dramatic leap.
Defenses have also played Nix differently since Payton took over playcalling, most notably increasing the frequency of zone defense. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Nix has seen zone looks on a league-leading 74.8% of his dropbacks since Week 5, a drastic increase from 60.8% over the first four weeks (15th among NFL starting quarterbacks). Nix's touchdown-to-interception ratio has improved in concert, with him throwing six touchdown passes and one interception since Week 5 after tossing five touchdowns and three picks in the first four weeks.
His completion percentage has moved from 60% in Weeks 1-4 to 61.3% over the past five games, and his completion percentage above expectation has moved from 27th (minus-5.3%) in the first four games to 23rd (minus-2.1%) in the past five, per Next Gen Stats.
The improvements, though noteworthy, aren't significant enough for Payton and Nix to announce a cure. "We still have a lot of work to do ... a lot of things to fix," Payton said.
But there has always been a feeling that if Nix's late-game calm and precision could be more uniform across four quarters, the Broncos will be closer to having the offense everyone in the organization wants. The schedule could help continue the process. Five of the Broncos' final eight games, including Sunday's matchup, are against teams currently ranked 20th or worst in scoring defense. Only one of the Broncos' final eight opponents -- the Pittsburgh Steelers -- has a scoring defense ranked in the top half of the NFL.

Though Nix wants to spread his effective play throughout an entire game, he also hopes to keep the fourth-quarter edge that has defined his early career.
"I've always felt like I've wanted to feel like a clutch player," Nix said. "It's an important quality as a player when everybody's looking at you and the pressure's on. I don't think you do it individually ... I just think we have a lot of guys with a clutch gene.
"We have a lot of guys that when the game's on the line, will just find ways to go score ... I'd much rather be clutch than the other way around."
author: Jeff Legwold

title: Free agents: Replacing Drake Maye? Trust in Tyson?
summary: Eric Karabell lists the top available options to replace Drake Maye and more.
full_text:
The New England Patriots are one of six teams that will not be playing in Week 11, as bye weeks continue. However, even when the defending AFC champions resume playing in Week 12 versus the Los Angeles Chargers , QB Drake Maye (ankle) will not be on the field. Maye was injured in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions . So, while fantasy managers may have already had a plan to cover for Maye in Week 11, they are now likely to be scrambling for aid beyond that point.
Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza (19.5% rostered) was under constant pressure in his first NFL start on Sunday, a loss to the excellent Seattle Seahawks defense. He scored a rushing touchdown and finished with 13.92 points. Mendoza was sacked six times and did not have the services of star TE Brock Bowers for most of the contest.
Still, it sure looks like Mendoza (the first overall NFL draft pick) may be special, even this season . The Raiders face a Denver Broncos defense in Week 11 that has not been as awesome as expected, permitting 16.9 QB fantasy points per game (19th in NFL). Prepare to spend at least 3% of your FAB to acquire Mendoza.
Aaron Rodgers , Steelers (37.2%, 2% FAB): Rodgers salvaged his Week 10 outing on Sunday night against the Cincinnati Bengals with a pair of fourth-quarter TD passes, ending up with 15.62 fantasy points. More of those points should be coming when the Steelers face their intrastate rivals in Week 11, with the sputtering Philadelphia Eagles riding a seven-game losing streak.
Cam Ward , Titans (4.5%, 1% FAB): Ward entered this week outside the top 20 fantasy quarterbacks for 2026 scoring, but then he put up 19.14 points in Sunday's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , completing a season-best 71.8% of his passes. Ward boasts four TD passes over his past two games, and he will face the terrible -- and it really is awful -- Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 11.
J.J. McCarthy , Giants (27.6%, 1% FAB): McCarthy faces a tough Week 11 home matchup with the Jaguars, a defense that permits only 12.5 fantasy points against them per game. McCarthy is coming off a solid outing with 17.12 points in Week 10 -- and remember, six starting QBs will be on a bye.
Deep-league options/streamers
Baker Mayfield , Buccaneers (19.6%, 1% FAB): Mayfield (foot/ankle) is preliminarily listed as questionable for Sunday's road outing against the Detroit Lions , but if he is able to start, he will face a defense that permits the most QB fantasy points and a unit that will be missing two-time Pro Bowl DE Aidan Hutchinson (knee). If Mayfield cannot play, fantasy managers may wish to consider rookie backup Jalon Daniels , a runner who has made three starts, reaching double-digit fantasy points each time.
Several top wide receivers will not play in Week 11, including Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (fantasy's leading scorer), Green Bay's Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , and Atlanta's Drake London . For those needing some assistance at that position, may we offer up a rookie for your consideration?
The New Orleans Saints expected WR Jordyn Tyson to be one of the top rookie performers this season when they used the eighth overall pick on the Arizona State product. A preseason hamstring injury kept Tyson sidelined for the first half of the regular season, but Tyson debuted in Week 9 with four receptions for 30 yards. It was clear that better statistical days were pending -- if Tyson could remain healthy. That has been a problem for him.
Well, a healthy Tyson caught 11 passes for 80 yards in Sunday's last-second loss to the Carolina Panthers , earning 13 of Tyler Shough 's 35 targets. Shough is among the league leaders in passing attempts, completions and passing yards, in part because the team's running game is poor. Tyson was the team's only wide receiver to earn more than four targets. Chris Olave investors should not panic, but Tyson (rostered in only 42.2% of ESPN standard leagues) needs to be far more popular for Week 11 against the Chicago Bears and beyond. This may be your last chance to act.
Ryan Flournoy , WR, Cowboys (26.0%, 2% FAB): Flournoy continues to thrive for a team that scores myriad points and permits a whole lot more than that. He scored a season-best 19.1 points in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . That makes five double-digit scoring outings in Flournoy's past six games, even with Dallas featuring WRs CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . The Cowboys face the struggling Tennessee Titans and Eagles during the next two weeks.
Makai Lemon , Eagles (49.7%, 3% FAB): Lemon, the No. 20 pick in the most recent draft, has stepped up with teammates DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) both sidelined, reaching double-digit fantasy points in three consecutive games. The Eagles come out of their bye week to face the Pittsburgh Steelers . Even if Smith and/or Wicks play, we can assume Lemon, with 19 receptions in three games, figures to remain heavily involved in this struggling offense.
Malik Washington , Dolphins (33.5%, 2% FAB): Washington scored 13.3 points in Sunday's loss to the Indianapolis Colts , but he reached double-digit scoring for the second time in three weeks, doing so with second-year QB Kyle McCord starting. Washington is averaging just over 10.0 fantasy points per game this season and with myriad receivers on a bye this week, that may be enough to consider him for active lineups.
Xavier Hutchinson , Texans (8.7%, 1% FAB): Hutchinson scored a season-best 15.8 points in Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns , notching a TD reception for the third consecutive game. The nine targets were a great sign, too. Hutchinson isn't Houston's top wide receiver option, but QB C.J. Stroud throws enough to make others a reasonable flex option -- especially this week versus the Colts.
Deep-league options/streamers
Antonio Williams , Commanders (17.7%, 1% FAB): Williams scored 12.2 points in Week 10, the second time in three weeks he has reached double digits, although he got there only because of a TD reception. Williams saw just two targets. He should see more in Week 11 against the Bengals.
Laquon Treadwell , Colts (1.2%, 1% FAB): Treadwell, 31, is a journeyman catching passes for his sixth NFL team. However, with the Colts trading away both Keenan Allen and Josh Downs last week, he led the team's receivers with 11.4 points in Sunday's win. Treadwell caught only three passes. Still, that matched what Ashton Dulin and Anthony Gould achieved. This week, the Colts face a Houston Texans defense that permits the second-most WR fantasy points.
Seth McGowan , RB, Colts (10.9%, 3% FAB): McGowan is no longer just a curiosity. He outscored star Jonathan Taylor for the second consecutive game, turning 12 rushing attempts into 77 yards, a goal-line touchdown and 13.7 points. Taylor, notably not traded at the league deadline, earned 18 touches and tallied 103 yards, but he did not find the end zone. Even on an awful Colts team with a top-10 RB (though Taylor is fading), McGowan is becoming a reasonable flex option.
Kenny Gainwell , Buccaneers (49.4%, 2% FAB): Gainwell has been notably disappointing so far, but he scored double-digit fantasy points in his past two games entering the team's Week 10 bye week, where he slipped under our 50% roster threshold. It's not too late for Gainwell to help, especially after Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles told reporters the team plans to lessen volume for star RB Bucky Irving , on pace for more than 300 touches. Gainwell totaled only 122 scrimmage yards over the first six games, but he has a solid 304 yards during the past three contests.
Kaelon Black , 49ers (35.1%, 2% FAB): Black, the backup to star Christian McCaffrey , made the highlight shows with his bruising 25-yard TD run in Sunday's win over the Cowboys, finishing with 14.6 points. McCaffrey continues to thrive with modest volume -- he scored a ridiculous 46.3 points on just 17 Week 10 touches -- yet Black is averaging double-digit fantasy points during the past three…

title: Fantasy buzz: Downs shines in Chiefs debut and who else got the ball in Week 10?
summary: Week 10 closes with Chargers winning their first game as Baltimore's offense adjusts to new QB.
full_text:
Derrick Henry had an interesting game on Monday night. I mean, it's hard to say he had a bad game when he scored 19 fantasy points. However, it was one of those games where you're happy with the result, but worried about what it means moving forward. Henry was quite inefficient as he turned his 15 touches into just 20 total yards. His 10 rushing yards are the second fewest he's had in any game with double-digit touches in his career. It was his also fifth consecutive game running for less than 60 yards.
While Henry's struggles on the ground are worrisome, there's some good news. He was targeted much more frequently with Jacoby Brissett under center for the Baltimore Ravens . His five catches tied for the second-highest total of his career. More targets could help make up for the lack of ground production. Henry has a potential rebound opportunity next week against the Carolina Panthers who rank top-two in both rushing touchdowns and fantasy PPG allowed to RBs.
Other takeaways from Monday's game
The Ravens were not afraid to let Brissett air it out in his first start for the team. He threw 49 times, finishing with 340 passing yards and 11.8 fantasy points. Yes, the fact both Baltimore touchdowns came on the ground hurt his fantasy total, but the volume should not be ignored. With all the QB injuries, plus six teams taking their bye in Week 11, Brissett is in play as a streaming option against the Panthers.
Zay Flowers finished with six catches for 74 yards on seven targets. He has surpassed 11 fantasy points in every game -- except the two with QB Joe Fagnano . That safe floor, paired with his upside, means he should be started every week.
Mark Andrews had his best game of the season, turning eight targets into eight catches for 82 yards. He finished with 16.2 fantasy points, all of which were season highs. I believe a resurgence has arrived for the star tight end, due to the team's QB change. Brissett has always targeted tight ends at a high rate. Fantasy managers in need of TE help should try to get Andrews on their roster this week -- whether it be adding off the waiver wire or trading for him.
Omarion Hampton had the best night for the no-longer winless Los Angeles Chargers . He turned 22 carries into 105 yards and a touchdown. It was his second game of the season playing on over 60% of snaps and he reached 100 yards and scored a touchdown in both. Hopefully, the Chargers will continue to feature him. He has a favorable matchup coming up against the New York Jets , who allow the second-most rushing yards before contact per carry. Consider him to be a low-end RB2 during the upcomng Bye-mageddon.
Justin Herbert had his best game of the season, scoring 16.26 fantasy points. He threw for only 129 yards with no touchdowns. However, the bulk of his fantasy points came via his legs, as he ran for 51 yards and a score. I'm reluctant to jump back on his bandwagon, though, due to the lack of passing results.
Tre' Harris finished with 86 receiving yards, which is even more impressive considering how few yards Herbert actually threw for in this one. Harris benefitted from Ladd McConkey 's absence and is worth adding in deeper 12-team leagues. That said, I would be reluctant to trust any piece of this team's passing attack right now.
The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out.
Rhamondre Stevenson tried to play through his knee injury, but finished with just seven touches and 1.5 fantasy points. He narrowly outsnapped Corey Kiner , who had more rushing attempts (10-6) and ran more routes (14-12). Stevenson handled most of the backfield work early in the game but didn't play in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach. The upcoming bye week gives Stevenson more time to recover and, with TreVeyon Henderson on IR, he should remain the team's lead back. New England has upcoming favorable matchups against the Chargers and Bills, but much will depend on Drake Maye 's health .
A.J. Brown returned from a two-game absence against the Lions, finishing with two receptions for 27 yards and 4.7 fantasy points before exiting with a hamstring injury. Brown was already seeing a reduced role following knee and ankle injuries, playing on only 65% of offensive snaps in the first half, down from 92% in Week 7. The bye week gives Brown additional time to recover. Mack Hollins led New England's receivers in routes run, targets (6) and receiving yards (48). He is worth keeping on watch lists in deeper leagues if Brown were to miss more time.
Josh Downs caught four out of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut, finishing with a season-high 15.3 fantasy points after just three practices with Kansas City. Downs played on only 10 offensive snaps and ran eight routes, lining up exclusively in the slot. His presence also led to Rashee Rice lining up outside more frequently. Downs' playing time should increase as he becomes more familiar with the offense. He warrants flex consideration against the Cardinals in Week 11.
Drake London led the Falcons in targets and ranked third in routes run against the Chiefs. He finished with six receptions for 109 yards and 16.9 fantasy points before leaving late in the fourth quarter due to a possible concussion. It was London's first 100-yard receiving game since Week 5, and Atlanta's bye week gives him time to recover.
Kyle Pitts Sr . led the Falcons in routes, in part because Atlanta was playing from behind. Despite the additional playing time, Pitts has now seen just five targets in four consecutive games and hasn't scored double-digit fantasy points since Week 7 against the 49ers. He remains a TE2 moving forward.
Nico Collins caught nine of a season-high 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown against the Browns, finishing with 24.4 fantasy points. Xavier Hutchinson ranked second on the team in routes run and targets (9), scoring a season-high 15.8 fantasy points. Despite Marvin Harrison Jr .'s absence, Tank Dell 's route participation remained the same for the second consecutive game. According to Mike Clay's strength of schedule matrix , the Texans have the 10th-easiest remaining schedule and sixth-easiest fantasy playoff schedule for wide receivers. Hutchinson is worth adding, though managers should monitor his health following a concussion evaluation. Dell remains a boom-or-bust flex option.

Harold Fannin Jr . led the Browns in targets (9), receptions (7) and receiving yards (91) against the Texans. He's scored at least 12 fantasy points in each of his last four games, highlighted by a 23.4-point performance against the Steelers in Week 8. Dylan Sampson outsnapped Judkins for the third consecutive game and again led the backfield in routes run. Game script has contributed to this trend, with Cleveland falling behind 17-0 on Sunday. title: Why Raiders fans stayed seated for Fernando Mendoza's first touchdown
summary: Tom Joanides' social media campaign became a meaningful tribute when Mendoza scored in his first NFL start.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders fan Tom Joanides, 46, had his first viral moment on social media for a good cause.
He went on X asking Raiders fans, who were attending Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium, to stay seated after No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza scored his first touchdown.
Listen, everyone going to Allegiant Stadium this Sunday. Stay seated when Fernando scores his first touchdown. Will be an epic gesture from fans to player. Pass it along.
The idea was meant to honor Mendoza's mother, Elsa, who has been confined to a wheelchair due to her multiple sclerosis diagnosis.
Watching the game at home with his family, Joanides saw thousands of Raiders fans remain in their seats while celebrating Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run in the first quarter of his first career start. Elsa and Mendoza's father, Fernando Mendoza Sr., were seated in a suite, cheering on their son. Editor's Picks 'Punched in the face,' Raiders' Mendoza vows to learn from first NFL start Ryan McFadden
"The fan base has an understanding that these are people; I'm shocked and elated that it actually happened. I've never had anything go viral ever," Joanides told ESPN. "But I'm not surprised that Raider Nation has the heart that it does."
Despite the Raiders losing to the Seahawks 21-13 , Mendoza was "super grateful" for the fans' gesture, and it meant a lot to his family.
"On a dark day, that brings a smile to my face," Mendoza said postgame . View this post on Instagram A post shared by SportsCenter (@sportscenter)
A post shared by SportsCenter (@sportscenter)
In July, Joanides, a Los Angeles native, went on X and wrote a post, asking fans to stay seated whenever Mendoza scored his first touchdown at home.
However, his post didn't receive much traction .
"I don't have a huge account or anything, so I was like yelling into the void," Joanides said.
Five days before the Raiders' home matchup, Joanides went on X to reshare his message from the summer.
This time, the fan base heard him. Joanides' post received more than 800,000 views and close to 400 reposts.
Joanides, who began attending Raiders games with his dad when he was 3, said he would list "Raider Nation" as his ethnicity on government forms if he could.
Joanides was inspired after watching a Front Office Sports interview , in which Mendoza said he donated $500,000 to the University of Miami Health System and the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine to help fight against multiple sclerosis.
Mendoza's advocacy for the cause is inspired by Elsa, who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2008. His family launched the Mendoza Family Fund in April, which directly supports the National MS Society.
Through their foundation, Mendoza's family has raised more than $1 million .
"I just found it really touching," Joanides said. "This [was] an opportunity for this fan base to welcome [Mendoza] and his family in a very particular way and show what Raider Nation is all about."

title: Burrow tight-lipped after joining elite QB club, but admits he played like 'a great one'
summary: Bengals QB Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday night, becoming just the third player in NFL history after Tom Brady and Peyton Manning to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Even after a performance that was reminiscent of some of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history and enhanced his case as the current best in the league, Joe Burrow was not in the mood to bask in his latest achievement.
During the Cincinnati Bengals ' 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers , Burrow became the third player in NFL history to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span, according to ESPN Research. He joined Tom Brady and Peyton Manning.
Burrow let his guard down only a couple of times after the game, including when he was asked what kind of quarterback he was Sunday night at Paycor Stadium.
"A great one," Burrow said with one of the few smiles he offered after the game.
Despite Burrow being tight-lipped after Cincinnati's fifth consecutive win, the numbers said plenty: He was 35-of-44 passing for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Per Next Gen Stats, Burrow was perfect against the blitz (completed all 12 passes) and led Cincinnati to its fifth straight game scoring 30 or more points, the longest such streak in franchise history.
"I'm not watching every game, but I can promise you people who aren't talking about him aren't watching all of our games," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. "Because if you are, it's really hard to say this dude's not the best player on planet Earth."
The Bengals (7-2) bludgeoned the Steelers from the outset. Cincinnati scored on five of its first six drives, the lone exception coming on kicker Evan McPherson 's first missed field goal attempt of the season.
Against a Steelers defense that ranked fifth in fewest points allowed per drive entering Sunday (1.57), the Bengals had 337 yards by halftime and a 21-point advantage that partially illustrated Cincinnati's dominance Sunday night.
Burrow wasn't the only Bengal who had a big night. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase finished with 11 catches for a season-high 231 yards. He came within 26 yards of breaking his franchise record, which he set as a rookie in a 2021 win over Kansas City .
Chase has played with Burrow since they led LSU to a national championship in 2019. It's easy for Chase to see why Burrow is playing so well.
"He's confident in his craft right now," Chase said. "He's confident his receivers will be open, and that's what you want in a quarterback."
Burrow threw two touchdown passes to running back Chase Brown , one to tight end Drew Sample and one to first-year player Dohnte Meyers , the former CFL star who caught his first career NFL TD on Sunday night.
The Bengals' win avenged a 30-27 loss to the Steelers (6-3) in Week 3, when Burrow was sacked and lost a fumble on the final offensive drive.
Cincinnati is in sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but that didn't mean much to Burrow.
"Nobody's winning the division with seven wins," Burrow said. "Nobody is making the playoffs with seven wins. We certainly aren't satisfied."
Burrow knows that feeling well. Last season, he missed nine games because of a turf toe injury. Even after his return later in the year, Cincinnati still sputtered and finished with its worst record (6-11) since his rookie season.
Cincinnati is off to its best start in Taylor's eight years as coach, including the 2021 season, when the Bengals went to the Super Bowl, and the following season that ended in the AFC Championship Game.
After Sunday's win, Burrow can boast something he couldn't in either of those seasons. He leads the NFL in Total QBR (82.1) heading into Week 11. As Burrow walked off the field, he was serenaded with the same "M-V-P" chants he heard at various points during the game.
Burrow didn't put too much stock in that opinion after nine games. But when do those things start to be taken more seriously?
"We'll see," Burrow said with a smile.

title: Ranking the top 10 Super Bowl performances by a defender: From Aaron Donald to Richard Dent
summary: Not all Super Bowl MVPs were quarterbacks or offensive stars. We listed 10 standout individual defensive performances.
full_text:
Super Bowls are mostly remembered for offensive fireworks, miraculous fourth-quarter drives, gravity-defying catches and MVP quarterbacks who hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy in victory.
Yet, as the old adage in football reminds us, offense sells tickets while defense wins championships.
While team defenses such as the 1985 Chicago Bears , 2000 Baltimore Ravens and 2013 Seattle Seahawks dominated as collective units, a select group of defenders delivered singular, dominant, game-altering performances on the NFL's biggest stage.
Here are 10 of the best individual defensive performances in Super Bowl history, including four defenders who earned the game's Most Valuable Player award.
COUNTDOWN TO SUPER BOWL LXI: ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February. We are counting down to the big game with a Super Bowl Top 10 series , featuring rankings on everything from best catches and performances to biggest upsets, which will run every other Sunday leading up to Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027.
Score : Broncos 24, Panthers 10
Stats : 2.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 pass defended
Miller set the tone with a strip-sack of Cam Newton in the first quarter that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown to give the Broncos a 10-0 lead. With Denver up 16-10 late in the fourth quarter, Miller once again jarred the ball loose from Newton when he sacked the quarterback deep in Carolina territory to put the Broncos in position to score the game-sealing touchdown four plays later.
Miller's performance was so dominant he earned unanimous Super Bowl MVP honors, becoming the 10th defensive player and fourth linebacker in NFL history to win the award.
Score : Raiders 27, Eagles 10
Stats : 3 interceptions, 5 tackles
Martin created the standard for ball-hawking dominance on the biggest stage when he set the Super Bowl record for interceptions -- a record that is shared but still stands -- by picking off Ron Jaworski three times.
The linebacker staved off any chance of a Philadelphia comeback when he intercepted Jaworski in the first, third and fourth quarters of the Raiders' eventual 17-point win. He also added five tackles in Oakland's second Super Bowl victory.
Score : Bears 46, Patriots 10
Stats : 1.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 blocked pass, 3 tackles
The "Sack Man" in Chicago's legendary "46 defense" led the NFL with 17.5 sacks during the 1985 season and gave a master class in pass rushing during Super Bowl XX. Dent wreaked havoc in the backfield with 1.5 sacks, three tackles two forced fumbles while constantly ripping through blocks to keep Patriots quarterback Tony Eason under pressure.
Dent earned Super Bowl MVP honors and is the last true defensive end to win the award.
Score : Packers 35, Patriots 21
Stats : 3 sacks, 4 QB hits, 1 tackle for a loss
White established the Super Bowl record by sacking Drew Bledsoe three times.
After a quiet first half, White lived up to his "Minister of Defense" nickname when it mattered most. With Bledsoe and the Patriots trying to mount a comeback after pulling within a touchdown in the third quarter, White took over and recorded three second-half sacks, which included back-to-back sacks that flipped the game's momentum.
Score : Buccaneers 48, Raiders 21
Stats : Only player in Super Bowl history with 2 pick-sixes
While his teammate Dexter Jackson captured MVP honors for setting the tone in a rout of the Raiders, Smith delivered the decisive knockout blows against league MVP Rich Gannon when he returned two interceptions for touchdowns.
Smith picked off a third-quarter pass and took it 44 yards for a touchdown to extend Tampa Bay's lead to 34-3. He then punctuated the win with a 50-yard pick-six in the final seconds. Smith capped off a dominant five-interception defensive clinic by Monte Kiffin's "Tampa 2" unit and cemented his place in postseason lore.
Score : Rams 23, Bengals 20
Stats : 2 sacks, 2 tackles for losses, 4 tackles, 3 QB hits
Donald's second-half takeover came after fighting through constant double-teams and triple-teams. With Cincinnati trailing by three after just crossing into LA's territory with less than a minute to play, Donald blew up a run play on third-and-1 for no gain. He sealed the victory by pressuring quarterback Joe Burrow on fourth down and forcing an incomplete pass.
The Rams took over in victory formation, and many believed Donald's effect should have earned him game MVP honors over Rams' wide receiver Cooper Kupp .
Score : Colts 16, Cowboys 13
Stats : 10 tackles, 2 interceptions and a fumble recovery
Howley made history as the first non-QB and player from the losing team to win Super Bowl MVP.
The linebacker was a bright spot in a sloppy game that was nicknamed "The Blunder Bowl" due to 11 combined turnovers. He recorded two interceptions and recovered a fumble while single-handedly terrorizing Johnny Unitas and the Colts' passing game.
Score : Cowboys 30, Bills 13
Stats : 1 interception, forced fumble and fumble recovery, which he returned for a TD
Trailing 13-6 at halftime, the Cowboys desperately needed a spark, and Washington provided it 54 seconds into the third quarter when he recovered a fumble from Bills running back Thurman Thomas and returned it 46 yards for a game-tying touchdown.
The safety anchored Dallas' secondary with a team-high 11 tackles and terrorized Buffalo's offense by adding a crucial interception and another forced fumble later in the second half. He played a direct role in three turnovers that fueled Dallas's second-half takeover.
Score : Broncos 24, Panthers 10
Stats : 3 sacks, 2 tackles for a loss, 3 QB hits, an interception, pass defended, fumble recovery and forced fumble
Despite the Panthers' loss, Ealy delivered the most stat-sheet stuffing defensive performance in Super Bowl history. While logging only 23 defensive snaps (38%) as a rotational edge rusher, the second-year defender harassed Broncos quarterback Peyton Manning all night and matched the Super Bowl single-game sack record.
Ealy's efforts kept the game close. He intercepted Manning in the second quarter and forced a fumble in the fourth to put the Panthers within a touchdown. He became the only player in Super Bowl history to record multiple sacks and an interception in the game.
Score : Seahawks 43, Broncos 8
Stats : An interception, touchdown, fumble recovery and 10 tackles.
Smith was at the center of the Legion of Boom's dominant defensive performance. He racked up a team-high 10 tackles, recovered a forced fumble and blew the game open in the second quarter when he intercepted an errant Peyton Manning pass and returned it 69 yards for a touchdown. His opportunistic play made him just the third linebacker at the time to win Super Bowl MVP.
Miami Dolphins S Jake Scott, Super Bowl VII (Dolphins 14, Redskins 7): 2 interceptions, MVP
New England Patriots CB Stephon Gilmore, Super Bowl LIII (Patriots 13, Rams 3): 1 interception, 3 passes defended, 1 forced fumble
Dallas Cowboys CB Larry Brown, Super Bowl XXX (Cowboys vs. Steelers) 2 interceptions, 77-yard INT return, MVP
Pittsburgh Steelers DE L.C. Greenwood, Super Bowl X (Steelers 21, Cowboys 17): Unofficially 3 sacks (before it was an official stat), 1 forced fumble
Patriots S Rodney Harrison, Super Bowl XXXIX (Patriots 24, Eagles 21): 2 interceptions, 1 sack, 7 tackles, 2 passes defended

title: Report: Tests showed no major injury for Geno Smith

title: Rams C Coleman Shelton to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury
summary: The Rams are on their bye this week and that gives them some extra time to figure out how to address the center position before their return to action against the Packers in Week 12.
full_text: The Rams are on their bye this week and that gives them some extra time to figure out how to address the center position before their return to action against the Packers in Week 12. Starter Coleman Shelton hurt his hamstring during Sunday's win over the Cardinals and a team spokesperson announced on Monday night that he is expected to miss 4-6 weeks as a result of the injury. Shelton started all 10 games this season. The Rams' issues were compounded when Shelton's backup Dylan McMahon also left the game. The team announced that he will be placed on injured reserve with a torn patellar tendon.
