title: Jim Harbaugh on finally getting a win: "Let's do it every week"
summary: Before the season, many expected the Chargers not only to get back to the playoffs for the third straight year but to finally make some noise.
full_text: Before the season, many expected the Chargers not only to get back to the playoffs for the third straight year but to finally make some noise. Instead, it took them more than two months to make a peep. But they roared to life on Monday night, with a win over the Ravens in Baltimore. The 23-20 victory instantly restored the boundless optimism of coach Jim Harbaugh. "Thrilled, let’s do it every week ," Harbaugh told reporters after the game, via Jeff Legwold of ESPN. "Good to see the smiles back on the faces." Harbaugh should be smiling the most. His stubborn refusal to make major changes — starting with firing or reassigning offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and continuing with a failure to trade players who won't be there next year, like Khalil Mack — was putting Harbaugh in increasing danger of being fired. While the playoffs are a practical impossibility, Harbaugh's obvious goal is survival for 2027. That's ultimately why there was no fire sale; moving good players would have made Harbaugh's firing more likely. Surely, it's one of the reasons why he resisted stockpiling future picks. If he's not there to use them, who cares? Could Harbaugh and the Chargers stack some wins? They've got the 2-8 Jets, the 5-5 Patriots (without quarterback Drake Maye), the 3-6 Buccaneers, and the 4-6 Raiders over the next four weeks. It changes after that, with three of the last four games against the 8-1 49ers, the 7-2 Broncos, and the 7-2 Chiefs. Will they run the table and sneak into the playoffs? Most likely not. Can they win enough to get Harbaugh a fourth season with the Chargers? At this point, that's the only realistic goal left.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Hamilton: Ravens are "disgracing" their "standards"
summary: The Ravens wore all black on Monday night.
full_text: The Ravens wore all black on Monday night. It looked like they were going to a funeral. They were. The Ravens' season feels over after losing their fifth in a row, following a 4-1 start. And while it's easy to blame the free fall on the multiple injuries suffered by quarterback Lamar Jackson, new quarterback Jacoby Brissett managed to beat the Chargers with the Cardinals in Week 1. On Monday night, the Ravens were flat, lifeless, and uninspired in prime time against the previously 0-8 Chargers. The end result was a second straight home loss in a standalone, nationally televised game. "Right now, we are disgracing those standards , as leaders, as players and as a team," safety Kyle Hamilton said after the game, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. "Whatever flak we get is warranted. . . . All the talking that's been going on is all just talk. If you don't go out there and do what you're supposed to do, stop the run, nobody really cares, and stuff like this just stops mattering." Hamilton understands that performances like this can have consequences. "At some point, you have to just decide about your manhood and what you want out of your job," Hamilton said. "This is our job. We can all get fired; that's the reality of it. If we don't do better, then we get fired." Hamilton has enhanced job security from his contract. Hamilton's $17 million salary for 2027 is already fully guaranteed. And his $17 million salary for 2028 becomes fully guaranteed in early 2027. Still, others who lack that type of financial certainty could be facing a one-way ticket out of Baltimore. Compounding the latest loss is the fact that it came against Jim Harbaugh, the brother of longtime Ravens coach John Harbaugh and the mentor of current Ravens coach Jesse Minter. One of the explanations for the Chargers starting 0-8 was the departure of Minter, the Chargers' defensive coordinator during Jim Harbaugh's first two years in L.A. and his final two years at Michigan. The embarrassing loss to the NFL's last winless team creates an unfortunate bookend to John Harbaugh's 18-year tenure in Baltimore. The year before he arrived, the Ravens started 4-2 before going on a losing streak that included losing to the league's last winless team at home — the 0-13 Dolphins. That got Brian Billick fired. And while Minter is a long way from being one and done, the Ravens need to stop the bleeding. Quickly. The schedule isn't favorable. They have a short-week trip to Charlotte and a visit to Houston before a Week 13 bye. The stretch run includes a home game against the Buccaneers followed by a four-game tour of the AFC North: at Steelers, Browns, at Bengals on New Year's Eve, Steelers. In John Harbaugh's 18 seasons, the Ravens had fewer than eight wins only once (they were 5-11 in 2015). It's going to be very hard to get to eight wins in 2026. They may not get past five. Hell, they may not get to five. Things can change quickly in the NFL. But the more the losses pile up, the harder it gets to dig out of the ever-deepening hole. For now, they're fading into the rear-view mirror in a division with three teams that have six or more wins. If the Ravens lose on Sunday, good luck finding the focus and the discipline during Thanksgiving week to be fully prepared for a meeting with the Texans that could be a de facto elimination game. Even if the Ravens' all-black uniforms was a fitting demonstration of the fact that, for 2026, they're already dead.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills and Chiefs both favored by 16.5 on Sunday, biggest point spreads of the season
summary: The Bills and Chiefs are scheduled for a Thanksgiving night showdown, but before that they each have a game on Sunday.
full_text: ' The Bills and Chiefs are scheduled for a Thanksgiving night showdown, but before that they each have a game on Sunday. And both games are expected to be blowouts. The Bills are favored to beat the Dolphins by 16.5 points, and the Chiefs are favored to beat the Cardinals by 16.5 points. Those are the two biggest point spreads of this NFL season. The previous biggest spread of this season also featured the Dolphins, when they were 13-point underdogs against the 49ers in Week 2. (The 49ers covered that spread, winning 35-13.) The Dolphins and Cardinals are expected to be mere speed bumps on the way to one of the marquee games of this NFL season on Thanksgiving night. With the Chiefs likely to be 8-2 and the Bills likely to be 9-1 heading into that game, it has major implications for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Derrick Henry on 10 carries for 10 yards: I don't have an answer, just not good enough
summary: Overall, the Ravens totaled 15 carries for 16 yards, their lowest rushing output in more than 10 years.
full_text: With the Ravens starting a quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, who had been on the team for less than two weeks, they hoped to get good production from running back Derrick Henry on Monday night. That didn't happen. Henry gained just 10 yards on 10 carries, and another 10 yards on five catches. Afterward he said he couldn't explain what went wrong in a 23-20 loss to the Chargers. "I don't know. I don't have no answer. Guys who are out there are healthy, trying to do their jobs, we just ain't good enough," Henry said. Overall, the Ravens totaled 15 carries for 16 yards, their lowest rushing yardage output in more than 10 years. Henry did run for two touchdowns, but he also had five plays on which he got no gain or negative yardage. Asked if the absence of quarterback Lamar Jackson is the problem, Henry said the players who are there have to take responsibility. "We just haven't been executing. Of course Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it's a grown-man league," Henry said. "We just haven't been doing our jobs good enough, it hasn't been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that. Of course having 8 would help, but at the end of the day, we've got to go out there and do our jobs." The Ravens are 4-6 and the season appears to be slipping away, but Henry said he'll always believe they can turn the season around. "I'm never not gonna believe that we can turn it around and play the way we want to play," Henry said. "You've still got to go to work. The season is still going to be here, you've still got to play. None of us are going to be like, 'Let's lose the rest of them.' You've still got to do your best."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Arch Manning will participate in Senior Day, but won't comment on his future
summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning concludes his fourth slate of home games with the Longhorns on Saturday.
full_text: '' Texas quarterback Arch Manning concludes his fourth slate of home games with the Longhorns on Saturday. Whether he'll have another year there, or somewhere else, remains to be seen. The only clue, if it even is one, comes from his decision to participate in the Texas Senior Day. " I’m a senior, so I’m doing it ," Manning said, via the Associated Press. So what's next after he participates in the traditional farewell home game? "I'm not really thinking about the future right now," Manning said. The future entails three primary options: (1) enter the draft; (2) return to Texas; or (3) transfer. Manning started the year as the favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. That has changed. Last year, he had 26 touchdown passes and seven interceptions for the Longhorns, who finished 10-3 for a team that did not qualify for the College Football Playoff. This year, Manning has 19 touchdown passes and 10 interceptions through 10 games. Texas currently is No. 6 in the CFP rankings. After two straight losses (to Oklahoma and Florida), coach Steve Sarkisian didn’t rule out benching Manning. Texas has since won four in a row, capped by a come-from-behind victory over LSU in which Manning threw three interceptions but also engineered the game-winning drive. His uncles, Peyton and Eli, exhausted their full college eligibility before entering the NFL. Both were the first overall picks. For Arch, the final decision may come down to whether he believes he'll be taken No. 1 overall — and whether he can land with his preferred NFL team. He could get creative, declaring for the draft and going through the process and returning to college if he decides he won't be the first pick and/or can't get to the team he wants. While it may require the hiring of a lawyer and/or the filing of a lawsuit to perform an about-face, the NCAA's rules have been exposed as a house of well-worn cards in a wind tunnel. Regardless, Manning has a business decision to make. And there will be many factors to consider, from when he'd be drafted to where he'd be drafted to how much money he could make by returning to Texas to how much money he could make by transferring to another school — like Ole Miss, where Uncle Eli and his grandfather, Archie, played.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Chargers run past Ravens 23-20 for first win of 2026
summary: The Chargers outrushed the Ravens 160 to 16.
full_text: Jacoby Brissett had a chance to play the hero in his first start for the Ravens. He did his part, but Zay Flowers fumbled when Tarheeb Still stripped him and Eric Molden recovered for the Chargers at the Los Angeles 46 with 2:03 remaining. By the time Brissett got the ball back, the Ravens were in need of a miracle, and his Hail Mary on the final play fell incomplete. The Chargers won for the first time, holding off the Ravens 23-20. Los Angeles is 1-8, while Baltimore lost its fifth in a row to fall to 4-6. The Chargers led from start to finish, winning for the first time since Week 16 of 2025 when they beat the Cowboys. They twice had a double-digit lead in the second half. Brissett, acquired in a trade from the Cardinals last week, went 33-of-49 for 340 yards and an interception. It was his most passing yards since Week 11 of last season when he threw for 452 yards for the Cardinals against the 49ers. He had no help from the running game, which contributed 16 yards on 15 carries. Derrick Henry had 10 yards and two touchdowns on 10 carries. Mark Andrews caught eight passes for 82 yards and Flowers had six catches for 74 yards. The Ravens outgained the Chargers 347 to 287, but Los Angeles gained 160 yards on the ground. With 1:52 left, Justin Herbert completed an 11-yard pass to Charlie Kolar for a first down. The Chargers ended up punting, but the Ravens had only 11 seconds from their own 20. Brissett threw a 21-yard pass to Ja'Kobi Lane before R.J. Mickens knocked down a Hail Mary attempt intended for Lane to end the game. Herbert was 12-of-18 for 129 yards, with Tre' Harris catching five passes for 86 yards. Herbert ran for 51 yards and a touchdown on seven carries. Omarion Hampton had 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Derrick Henry's second TD has Ravens back within a FG
summary: Derrick Henry has 10 carries for 10 yards, but he has two touchdowns.
full_text: Derrick Henry has 10 carries for 10 yards, but he has two touchdowns. His second one has pulled the Ravens within 23-20 of the Chargers. The Chargers have twice had double-digit second-half leads at 20-10 and 23-13. It's the first time the Chargers have had a double-digit lead in the second half since beating the Cowboys 34-17 in Week 16 last season. That was Los Angeles' last win. The Ravens, though, have made it a game despite only 15 rushing yards. Jacoby Brissett, making his first start with the Ravens, is 25-of-39 for 280 yards and an interception. He led the Ravens on a 10-play, 71-yard drive that has them back within a field goal. The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) and list right guard Vega Ioane as questionable with a left shoulder injury. Ioane played through it into the second half before Chuma Edoga replaced him.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rex Ryan politicks for job with Cowboys
summary: Rex Ryan is plenty of things.
full_text: Rex Ryan is plenty of things. Bashful is not one of them. Days after being arrested for allegedly running over the feet of two people in Nashville with his pickup truck and fleeing the scene, Ryan is on the air — and he's using the bully pulpit to politick for a job with the Cowboys. “I could go there today and say, ‘Alright, we can have an average ass defense,'" Ryan said on ESPN New York, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing . "I’ll promise you they’d be average, I’d probably make them top-10 . But I’ll take that group right now, in one week, I’d go in and turn this thing out.” Ryan's pitch came after he ripped the current defensive coaching staff in Dallas. “It’s the worst coached defense I’ve ever seen,” Ryan said. “It really is. And I’ve seen some horrible defenses, this one’s awful, and it starts with coaching. . . . They make more mental mistakes than any defense I’ve seen, as well as the physical, they’re not a tough physical defense.” As noted separately by Michael McCarthy of Front Office Sports, Ryan also criticized the Dallas defense on ESPN's Get Up. “ It starts with the young guy they hired , Christian Parker," Ryan said. "What on his resume told you he was going to be a good defensive coordinator candidate for a team like the Dallas Cowboys with Super Bowl aspirations? By the way, what told you anything about him that would make you think he could be a leader in this? Because you better hire a leader for that spot.” (It would have been great if someone else on the show would have said, "Yeah, the Cowboys defense is extremely pedestrian.") “To me, absolute garbage," Ryan said. "You can’t fire them all yet, but you damn sure better. To me, it’s the whole defensive staff. It’s not just Christian Parker. It’s not. It’s every one of those coaches on defense.” Prior to the 2024 season, the Cowboys were considering hiring Ryan to be the defensive coordinator. Eventually, Dallas brought back former Cowboys defensive coordinator (and former Vikings coach) Mike Zimmer. In September 2024, Ryan said he would have had the job if owner and G.M. Jerry Jones had been willing to pay. “I could’ve fixed [the Cowboys’ defense] in a New York minute,” Ryan said at the time. “But, that being said, they couldn’t pony up the money , or I would’ve been there.” Jones obviously could have come up with the money. But he wouldn't. Because he doesn't. And it's hard to imagine Jones cleaning house on the defensive side of the ball and giving the keys to Ryan, who hasn't had a coaching job in more than a decade. Especially if Jones would owe any of the defensive coaches a buyout. Then again, if Ryan is willing to work for whatever Jerry will pay, that could be the key to getting Ryan a chance to put his feet where his mouth is.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL Honors moves from Thursday back to Saturday
summary: The NFL Honors ceremony is on the move, again.
full_text: ' The NFL Honors ceremony is on the move, again. The made-for-TV awards show, which shifts this year from broadcast to streaming, will also be sliding back to its original day. John Ourand of Puck reports that NFL Honors will be held not on the Thursday of Super Bowl week but on the Saturday of Super Bowl weekend. The show slid to Thursday in 2022. Netflix has acquired the rights to the show, which attracted 3.7 million viewers in February 2026. During the event, the various Associated Press awards are announced. Also, the new class of Hall of Famers is unveiled. As NFL programming goes, the numbers aren't great. As live TV goes, three million people at one time is nothing to sneeze at. Whether Netflix will realize that kind of audience remains to be seen — if the official figure is even disclosed. Regardless, the show will quickly be forgotten as the NFL pivots the next day to the biggest event of the year.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dolphins DT Zeek Biggers out for the season with knee injury
summary: Dolphins defensive tackle Zeek Biggers will require season-ending surgery to repair his lateral meniscus, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.
full_text: Dolphins defensive tackle Zeek Biggers will require season-ending surgery to repair his lateral meniscus, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports. Biggers' injury comes a week after Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler ruptured his biceps, and defensive tackle Jordan Phillips injured his arm in Sunday's loss to the Colts. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. are the only healthy defensive tackles left on the 53-player roster. Third-year defensive tackle Jordan Jefferson is on the practice squad. The Dolphins selected Biggers in the seventh round in 2025. In 2026, he played all nine games, with two starts, and totaled 18 tackles, a sack and a pass deflection.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: Chargers lead Ravens 17-10 at halftime
summary: Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton have touchdown runs for the winless Chargers.
full_text: The Chargers lead the Ravens 17-10 at halftime on Monday. That is more points than the winless Chargers have scored in five games and the same as they scored in a 23-17 loss to the Broncos. They scored 23 against Seattle and 22 last week against Houston. Los Angeles scored on 3-of-5 first-half possessions, getting a 22-yard touchdown run from Justin Herbert, a 38-yard Cameron Dicker field goal and a 1-yard Omarion Hampton touchdown run. Hampton's touchdown came on fourth-and-goal with 1:56 remaining in the half. Roquan Smith initially had Hampton stopped before the running back got a push from offensive lineman Cole Strange and a pull from fullback Scott Matlock. Officials should have penalized Matlock for the pull, as pulling is illegal. The Chargers outgained the Ravens 175 to 161, with Baltimore having no rushing yards on six carries. Herbert, who injured his left hand in last week's loss to the Texans but wasn't on the injury report this week, went 6-for-9 for 91 yards in the first half. He also ran for 45 yards on six carries. Hampton has 36 yards on 10 carries, and Tre' Harris has five catches for 86 yards. Jacoby Brissett, making his first start for the Ravens after the trade from Arizona, has completed 14 of 23 passes for 163 yards and an interception. Del'Shawn Phillips had the pick on a pass that was behind Ja'Kobi Lane and deflected to the Chargers linebacker. Derrick Henry has a 2-yard touchdown run, but he has minus-1 yard on five carries. Mark Andrews has four catches for 41 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Von Miller blames himself, not the play call, for Christian McCaffrey's late TD
summary: The Cowboys pulled within 38-32 of the 49ers with 3:42 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday.
full_text: The Cowboys pulled within 38-32 of the 49ers with 3:42 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Only 19 seconds later, Christian McCaffrey was celebrating in the end zone. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is under fire for calling cover zero on second-and-10. He sent a six-man blitz, leaving man-to-man coverage and Von Miller matched up with McCaffrey. McCaffrey called it " a perfect look for that play ." The running back ran a seam route, quickly got a step (or two or three) on the 37-year-old edge rusher, caught the ball at the 40 and was off to the races. Miller reached 18.5 mph while chasing McCaffrey, but it wasn't fast enough. Miller, though, defended Parker and the play call on Monday. “As a defensive coordinator in that situation, you want to be aggressive ,” Miller said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “We were trying to win the game. We were trying to create momentum. We were down by six points. If we could have just got off the field. . . . As a defensive coordinator, you want to be aggressive and want to win the game. That’s the type of mindset you want in these games.” Parker is three years younger than Miller, but has Miller's full support despite the struggles of the Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed 584 yards to the 49ers. “Nah, that’s crazy,” Miller said of the calls for Parker's job. “Christian is an incredible leader of men. All of these offensive and defensive coordinators are geniuses. It’s really getting your players to buy in. What happened with me yesterday is a microcosm of what has happened the whole season. Instead of me looking for a simpler way to do that job, I have to find a better way to do it. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I had been coached on how to play that route. I’ve had examples of that route, went over that play in practice this week. I just didn’t make that play. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I just didn’t execute."
author: Charean Williams

title: Derrick Henry draws Ravens to within 10-7 of Chargers
summary: The Ravens are on the board.
full_text: The Ravens are on the board. Derrick Henry ran for a 2-yard touchdown behind Vega Ioane to get the home team within 10-7 of the Chargers. It was Henry's ninth rushing touchdown of the season and 131st of his career. Jacoby Brissett, making his first start for the Ravens since they acquired him from Arizona, finally found some rhythm on the team's fourth possession. The Ravens went three-and-out on their first three possessions. Brissett, though, had throws of 10 yards to Mark Andrews on third-and-10, 17 yards to Zay Flowers, 16 yards to Andrews and 24 yards to Rashod Bateman. Brissett, the team's fourth starter of the season, is 8-of-13 for 81 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Texans estimate David Montgomery as a full participant, but Woody Marks doesn't practice
summary: The Texans did not practice on Monday, but they were required to release an injury report ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
full_text: The Texans did not practice on Monday, but they were required to release an injury report ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts. Running back David Montgomery was estimated as a full participant again, putting him on track to return this week. A groin injury has sidelined him the past four games. Montgomery returned to practice Thursday and was a full participant Friday, but he was inactive again Sunday. The Texans estimated linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin), wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring), tight end Brevin Jordan (foot/illness) and running back Woody Marks (concussion) as non-participants. Al-Shaair, Harrison, Hunter and Jordan did not play Sunday, and Marks was hurt in the loss to the Browns. Linebacker Jake Hummel (groin) was listed as limited Monday. Safety Reed Blankenship (hand), wide receiver Tank Dell (hand/shoulder), offensive tackle Blake Fisher (thumb), cornerback Kamari Lassiter (wrist), offensive guard Febechi Nwaiwu (knee), offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (shoulder), cornerback Jaylin Smith (hamstring) and offensive guard Wyatt Teller (back) were full participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Justin Herbert runs for 22-yard TD, giving Chargers a 7-0 lead
summary: Justin Herbert's left hand seems just fine.
full_text: Justin Herbert's left hand seems just fine. So, too, do his legs. The Chargers quarterback ran for a 22-yard touchdown, his first rushing touchdown since Week 9 of last season. The Chargers have struggled to score this season, but had no problem moving the ball on their first drive of the night. After the Ravens went three-and-out with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, the Chargers drove 63 yards in only six plays. Omarion Hampton had runs of 11, 4 and 4 yards and recovered his own fumble on the second one. Herbert was 1-of-2 for 22 yards, with Tre' Harris getting the only reception. Herbert injured his left hand in last week's loss to the Texans, but was not on the injury report this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: Andy Reid defends Xavier Worthy, who had no catches in 57 snaps
summary: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed 22 passes to eight different receivers and threw five touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
full_text: ' Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed 22 passes to eight different receivers and threw five touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. None of his completions went to Xavier Worthy. Worthy has 33 catches for 278 yards and a touchdown in nine games this season. The Chiefs have not used him in the run game. On Sunday, he led all Kansas City wide receivers with 57 snaps and drew three targets. He also made a special teams mistake, allowing the Falcons to recover the first successful onside kick of the season in the NFL. Coach Andy Reid was asked about Worthy's lack of production, which had to be at least part of the reason the Chiefs traded for Josh Downs last week. Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Kansas City debut. “He just needs to keep doing his thing and working, and he’ll be fine ,” Reid said Monday, via Charles Goldman of AtoZ Sports. “Some days will be his, and some days it goes to other guys. I mean, that’s just how this thing works. We’re spreading it around. Pat loves spreading it around and does a great job with it. Our coaches love doing that. It’s tough on defenses. Everybody’s kind of getting a little piece of the pie. You saw when he was only the guy against the Chargers and his production there was great. So, it’s not that he’s not capable of that.” Reid further explained that the Falcons' game plan was to take Worthy out of the game, which "allowed other guys to be available." Worthy, a first-round pick in 2024, had his best season as a rookie when he made 59 catches for 638 yards and six touchdowns, while also running for 104 yards and three touchdowns on 20 carries. In the 23 games he's played since, Worthy has 75 catches for 810 yards and two touchdowns, with 11 carries for 87 yards and no touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: No surprises among Chargers-Ravens inactives
summary: The Chargers will officially see the return of tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman.
full_text: The Chargers will officially see the return of tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman. The team activated them from injured reserve earlier Monday, and both are active for Monday Night Football. Njoku (fibula) has not played since Week 2, and he has six catches for 67 yards. Perryman (pectoral) will make his 2026 debut tonight. The Chargers' inactives are wide receiver Ladd McConkey (back), safety Kendall Williamson (calf), cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), outside linebacker Bud Dupree, wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) and defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle). The Ravens' inactives are safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), wide receiver Elijah Sarratt, cornerback Chandler Rivers, offensive guard Emery Jones, defensive tackle Aeneas Peebles and quarterback Kedon Slovis. Slovis is the emergency third quarterback.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Aidan Hutchinson has torn ACL but no additional damage
summary: Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson received a bit of good news after additional testing on his right knee.
full_text: Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson received a bit of good news after additional testing on his right knee. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that, while Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL, he has no other significant damage. Initial reports indicated the Lions feared Hutchinson "probably" had additional damage in his knee, specifically his meniscus. Hutchinson and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye were both injured on Hutchinson's third-down sack of Maye with 9:28 left in the first quarter. Maye injured his ankle on the play, and the injury could be season-ending. Hutchinson injured his knee on the celebration afterward. Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, said through a league spokesman that Hutchinson's tackle was not an illegal hip drop . This marks the second time in three seasons that Hutchinson's season will end early. He finishes 2026 with six sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Mike Vrabel disagrees with Milton Williams's claim that field conditions caused injuries
summary: On Sunday in Germany, both teams had key players go down with significant injuries.
full_text: On Sunday in Germany, both teams had key players go down with significant injuries. And both injuries could be season-ending. After the game, Patriots defensive tackle Milton Williams blamed the injuries suffered by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (ankle) on the playing surface in Munich. “Two top players in this league, probably got season-ending injuries playing on that [field]," Williams said, via Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald . "It was bad. But like I said, I ain't making no excuses. [The Lions] executed. They played on the same field we did, and they executed and made more plays than we did. Give them credit.” On Monday, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel disagreed with Williams's opinion. "I don't think Drake Maye's injury was caused by the grass," Vrabel told reporters, "and certainly we've seen other players that have celebrated or have left their feet and come down and had issues at that. So the field was the same for both teams, and that's kind of what the field was." Vrabel stopped short of commenting on whether the field was an issue independent of the injuries. But he's right; it's the same for both teams. Still, we know by now that every field is different. And there's surely a difference between American fields that host up to 10 games per year every year and the international one-off surfaces.
author: Mike Florio

title: The NFL's Week 12 flex decision is looming
summary: Thanksgiving week will entail a smorgasbord of football.
full_text: Thanksgiving week will entail a smorgasbord of football. But not every course will be particularly appetizing. The NFL's brand-new embrace of the previously quiet night before Thanksgiving, only a few years after Black Friday was invaded, creates nine separate windows for the weekend — and seven standalone games. The Wednesday night clash, pitting the 6-4 Packers against the 6-4 Rams, has huge implications for the slow-moving game of wild-card musical chairs in the NFC. The early Thanksgiving contest has the 7-2 Bears visiting the 7-2 Lions in a massive NFC North battle. The Eagles-Cowboys game at 4:25 p.m. ET is becoming increasingly irrelevant — and it'll still get more than 40 million viewers because any game in that window would generate a huge audience. The Thursday night game, between the 7-2 Chiefs and the 8-1 Bills, will be very relevant to the AFC West championship and the No. 1 seed in the conference. On Friday, it's the 7-2 Broncos at the 6-3 Steelers, which also has major playoff implications. Then comes the late-afternoon Sunday window. At 4:25 p.m. ET, the 8-1 49ers host the 6-4 Seahawks. Unfortunately, it doesn't end there. On Sunday night, the 5-5 Patriots (who likely won't have quarterback Drake Maye) visit the 0-8 Chargers. If the NFL is going to slide that game out of prime time, Tuesday is the deadline for doing it. For the Eagles-Commanders game in Week 8, the league opted not to move a more consequential game into the Sunday night spot. Will the NFL again stand pat, keeping the Pats and Chargers as, to borrow a classic line from John Madden, the last shot out of a Roman candle? The problem is that the playing of five games on Wednesday through Sunday leaves few options for Sunday night. In the 1:00 p.m. ET window, the games are Saints-Bengals, Raiders-Browns, Ravens-Texans, Giants-Colts, Jets-Dolphins, and Falcons-Vikings. Titans-Jaguars is due to begin at 4:05 p.m. ET, with Commanders-Cardinals being the other 4:25 p.m. ET game. There's no Sunday afternoon game (other than Seahawks-49ers) that carries huge meaning for both teams. The best option for a flex would be Falcons-Vikings, since it's the first home game of Kirk Cousins 2.0 — and it comes against the team that signed him to a deal with multiple years of full guarantees before shocking everyone (including Cousins) the following month by selecting Michael Penix Jr. with the eighth overall pick in the draft. The good news is that the Monday night game between the 4-5 Panthers and the 3-6 Buccaneers has direct relevance to the NFC South title, and the guaranteed postseason home game that comes with it. Still, the current Sunday night game stands out as being something that few will be interested in watching, especially after a five-day turkey-and-pigskin-induced coma. In the end, it's always the league's decision. Under the rules the NFL has put in place, that decision is due to be made tomorrow.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lions claim DE Tyrus Wheat off of waivers
summary: The Lions lost Aidan Hutchinson for the rest of the season on Sunday and they moved to add another defensive end to the roster on Monday.
full_text: The Lions lost Aidan Hutchinson for the rest of the season on Sunday and they moved to add another defensive end to the roster on Monday. They announced that they have claimed Tyrus Wheat off of waivers. Wheat was let go by the Cowboys over the weekend. It will be Wheat's second tour of duty with the Lions. He played in 15 games for the team last season and recorded 15 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble in those appearances. Wheat had three tackles in five games for the Cowboys this season and he also played 20 games for Dallas during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. The Lions waived defensive back Nick Whiteside in a corresponding move.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants sign WR Xavier Gipson, DB Tavierre Thomas to their active roster
summary: The Giants signed wide receiver Xavier Gipson and defensive back Tavierre Thomas to their active roster on Monday, the team announced.
full_text: ' The Giants signed wide receiver Xavier Gipson and defensive back Tavierre Thomas to their active roster on Monday, the team announced. Gipson was on the Eagles' practice squad, and Thomas was on the Vikings' practice squad. The Giants cut wide receiver Charlie Jones and defensive back Nikko Reed from their practice squad in corresponding moves. This is Gipson's third stint with the Giants. The Eagles signed Gipson to their practice squad on Sept. 11 after he spent training camp with the Giants. Gipson, 25, was with the Eagles and Giants in 2025. He has appeared in 41 regular-season games with three starts for the Jets (2023-25), Giants (2025) and Eagles (2025). Gipson has yet to appear in a game this season. Thomas played all 17 games each of the previous two years, but has appeared in only one game this season. He made his 2026 debut last Monday night against the Bills, playing 24 snaps on special teams. In 116 regular-season games with 22 starts for the Browns (2018-20), Texans (2021-23), Buccaneers (2024) and Vikings (2025-26). His career numbers include 193 tackles, seven forced fumbles, six tackles for loss, two forced fumbles and two interceptions.
author: Charean Williams

title: Raiders sign QB Brett Rypien to the practice squad
summary: The Raiders needed another quarterback after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.
full_text: ' The Raiders needed another quarterback after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings. They accomplished that Monday by signing Brett Rypien to the practice squad. Rypien joins Fernando Mendoza and Aidan O'Connell in the quarterbacks room. The Raiders released defensive end Bralen Trice from the practice squad to make room for Rypien. Rypien was most recently with the Buccaneers, signing with their practice squad in September, when Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb. Rypien, the nephew of Super Bowl XXVI MVP Mark Rypien, has appeared in games with the Broncos, Rams and Bengals. He has played 11 games, going 2-2 as a starter, but has not appeared in a game since 2023.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brian Schottenheimer on confidence in Christian Parker: We're still working through the process
summary: One constant of the 2026 Cowboys season has been a focus on defensive coordinator Christian Parker's job security in the wake of losses and things aren't any different in the aftermath of Sunday's loss to the 49ers.
full_text: ' One constant of the 2026 Cowboys season has been a focus on defensive coordinator Christian Parker's job security in the wake of losses and things aren't any different in the aftermath of Sunday's loss to the 49ers. The 49ers piled up 584 yards and scored three touchdowns that covered at least 66 yards in their 46-40 win, which led head coach Brian Schottenheimer to call their tackling unacceptable in his postgame press conference. Executive vice president Stephen Jones used the same word to describe the team's performance on Monday and Schottenheimer's press conference later in the day began with a question about whether he remains confident in Parker. "We’ll still working through the process," Schottenheimer said. "Talking to the guys is the first step. At the end of the day, there’s a lot of things we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me. You look at this game, the positives. Five sacks team that had been sacked eight times — you get five sacks. Probably missed another three or four, could have been almost double digits. But at the end of the day, the tackling and some of the coverage stuff led to the explosives. We're taking a deep dive, we're looking at everything." The answer notably didn't include an affirmation of confidence in Parker, which led to a followup asking if there's a chance that they could make a change involving Parker. “I’m not saying that. I’m saying we’re still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today," Schottenheimer said. The Cowboys may not choose to make a change, but it's hard to feel confident that there's going to be a major difference between their play over the first 10 weeks and their play over the rest of the season if everything about the defensive approach remains the same.
author: Josh Alper

title: The extensive officiating adjustments worked, but were they necessary?
summary: Friday's nationwide ground stop didn't affect any of the NFL teams that needed to travel from one place to the other for Week 10 games.
full_text: Friday's nationwide ground stop didn't affect any of the NFL teams that needed to travel from one place to the other for Week 10 games. It dramatically affected the officiating assignments. But not because the officials assigned to work the various games couldn't get to where they needed to be. The league decided to reshuffle the deck in order to avoid the mere possibility that the officials wouldn't get to their assigned games. It was a proactive approach by the notoriously reactive NFL. But it still may have been an overreaction. And it introduced the risk that something unusual could have occurred. For the twelve games played on Sunday, the assigned referee worked only two of the games . One of those games was played on Sunday morning (New York time) in Germany, where travel undoubtedly occurred before Friday's shutdown of the aviation system. Sunday night's game was due to be worked by Clete Blakeman as the referee, with umpire Scott Walker, down judge Andy Warner, line judge Kent Payne, field judge Karina Tovar, side judge James Coleman, back judge Jonah Monroe, replay official Chad Adams, and replay assistant Adam Choate. Instead, from the official Game Book, this was the crew: referee Don Willard, umpire Terry Killens, down judge Dana McKenzie, line judge Jay Bilbo, field judge Jabir Walker, side judge Justin Larrew, back judge Dino Paganelli. Chad Adams was still the replay official; however, all replay officials reportedly went to the league office and not their game sites. Willard was not scheduled to work in Week 10; he ultimately served as the referee for two games. Killens was due to work the Jaguars-Titans game as a member of referee Alex Moore's crew; like Willard, Killens worked Dolphins-Colts and Steelers-Bengals. McKenzie, like Killens, is a member of Moore's crew, which was due to be in Nashville. Bilbo is a member of referee Shawn Smith's crew, which was due to work Panthers-Saints. Walker, who also worked two games, is a member of Land Clark's crew, which was scheduled to work the Chargers-Ravens game on Monday night. Larrew, the fourth two-games-in-one-day official, is assigned to referee Shawn Hochuli's crew, which was scheduled to work the Chiefs-Falcons game. Paganelli is also a member of referee Shawn Smith's crew, which was due to work Panthers-Saints. Monday night's game, by the way, will be handled by referee Adrian Hill. Hill's crew was scheduled to work the Rams-Cardinals game on Sunday. While we don't have the time, the patience, or frankly the desire to prepare a full list of the crews that were supposed to handle the 11 domestic Sunday games and the crews that actually did, the fact that 10 of the 11 referees ended up elsewhere says it all. The changes were dramatic. Here's the real question. Were they necessary? In lieu of performing major surgery to the officiating lineup for 11 Sunday games (and, apparently, the Monday night game), the NFL could have committed to getting every official where they needed to be, for the games they were scheduled to work. Everyone else got to where they needed to be. The teams, the broadcasters, everyone. It presumably could have been done, if the NFL had decided to commit any and all resources to making it happen. Which brings us to an inescapable conclusion. In order to avoid the hassle — and the expense — of ensuring that the officiating crews made it to their assigned locations before kickoff on Sunday, the league had no qualms about making massive, eleventh-hour changes to the assignments. Which included the unprecedented move of requiring four officials to work a game, to take a two-hour ride to another city, and to work another game. For the details on working two games in one day, check out the story from Kalyn Kahler about the unprecedented doubleheader for four officials . "It's exhausting because you're looking for something on every single play," ESPN rules analyst and former NFL V.P. of replay Russell Yurk told Kahler regarding the difficulty of working two games in a day. "You're analyzing every single play. You're watching your players. You're watching your keys, you're making judgment calls, and it doesn't really let up the entire game." Fox rules analyst and former NFL senior V.P. of officiating Dean Blandino called assigning officials to two games a "last resort." "[I]t would be like playing two football games back-to-back," Blandino told Kahler. "There's the physical aspect of running and the mental exhaustion after a game because you are doing a pre-snap routine for every snap, and then the eight-second play, and then a post-snap routine. "The officials look like they are not exerting themselves the same way the players are, but they don't get breaks. They don't play one side of the ball. They are out there every snap and every kick. Then to say now I have to reset without any recovery time? That is a challenge." The league could have embraced the challenge (and the expense) of getting all officials where they needed to be. It surely would have been easier than completely disrupting the existing assignments, forcing officials to work games they hadn't prepared to handle, and requiring NFL executive Ramon George (whom the league declined to make available for an interview with Kahler) to move the various pieces around in a way that made it all work, even if the "last resort" of using four officials for two games had to be used. Given the wealth and power of the NFL (most if not all owners have a private jet, or jets ), the league could have gotten everyone where they needed to be. Either it wanted the risk of a single snafu to be as small as possible (even if that meant blowing up the existing assignments) or it hoped to make the expense as small as possible. It's hard not to think cost was a factor. And the NFL is very fortunate that Sunday's games went smoothly, after the major disruption to the officials' itineraries. Still, these games are too important for a rolling of dice or the pinching of pennies, relatively speaking. It would have been, in our view, far more prudent to open the checkbook and spend whatever was needed to get the officials to the places where the officials were originally assigned to be.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dolphins waive Jamree Kromah
summary: The Dolphins have let go of an edge rusher.
full_text: The Dolphins have let go of an edge rusher. Miami announced the club has waived Jamree Kromah. Kromah, 26, joined the Dolphins late last month after he was claimed off waivers. The Bears had let him go after they traded for defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons. Kromah appeared in two games for Miami, playing two defensive snaps and 10 special teams snaps. He could return to Miami’s roster on the practice squad if he clears waivers.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bucs sign QB Easton Stick from the practice squad to the active roster
summary: The Buccaneers signed quarterback Easton Stick from the practice squad to the active roster on Monday, the team announced.
full_text: The Buccaneers signed quarterback Easton Stick from the practice squad to the active roster on Monday, the team announced. They filled the practice squad spot by signing Cooper Rush. In addition, the Buccaneers signed wide receiver David Sills to the practice squad and released cornerback Brandon Johnson to make room on the 17-player unit. The quarterback maneuvers come as Baker Mayfield deals with a lower-leg injury. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his fourth start of the season if Mayfield can't play Sunday. Stick would serve as Daniels' backup. Stick was active for Daniels' three starts in Weeks 4-6 as Mayfield worked his way back from a dislocated right thumb. Stick is now out of practice squad elevations. The Bucs signed Stick to the practice squad on Aug. 31, but he has previous experience in offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's system. The two were together in Atlanta last season. Rush also has NFL starting experience, having opened 18 games with Dallas, Baltimore and Atlanta. That includes two starts for the Falcons this season. Sills was on the Buccaneers' active roster for three weeks before the team waived him Nov. 10. Johnson was on the Buccaneers' practice squad for five weeks. He previously saw regular-season action with the Eagles in 2025, appearing in three games with one start.
author: Charean Williams

title: Robert Saleh: We've put more on Cam Ward's plate and he's proving he can handle it
summary: The Titans lost their third straight game on Sunday, but head coach Robert Saleh continued to like what he saw from quarterback Cam Ward during Jacksonville's 40-23 win.
full_text: The Titans lost their third straight game on Sunday, but head coach Robert Saleh continued to like what he saw from quarterback Cam Ward during Jacksonville's 40-23 win. Ward was 28-of-39 for 231 yards, two touchdowns and an interception while running three times for 39 yards. That marked a season-high in completion percentage for Ward and he has completed at least 64.5 percent of his passes in all three of the losses. That run coincides with what Saleh called a decision to "shift our philosophy with how we wanted to approach offense and put more in his plate with regard to being a general at the line of scrimmage." Saleh said that Ward has done "a really nice job taking command" and has shown the Titans what they were hoping to see in the process. "To be fair to Cam, we've said from the beginning we were going to give him every opportunity to prove that he is a franchise quarterback of the Tennessee Titans," Saleh said at a Monday press conference. "So, philosophically, the change was: How are we going to evaluate whether or not is he capable of being our franchise quarterback if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it? And I think over the last three weeks he has done that. Or, at least is doing it ." The Titans scored 84 points in their first six games and they've put up 83 in the three games since the tweak in their offensive approach. That step in the right direction has not resulted in wins, but it is reason to hope that will change if Ward is able to sustain the improvement that the Titans have seen over the last few weeks.
author: Josh Alper

title: Prisco's NFL Week 11 Power Rankings: Patrick Mahomes returns to MVP form, which makes Chiefs scary
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 11 Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including the Chargers finally climbing out of the basement
full_text:
All we heard for much of this season was that the Kansas City Chiefs had taken on a new offensive persona. They were now a running team with Kenneth Walker .
Yes, they have leaned on the running game for the early part of the season, in large part because of a lack of quality receivers, the addition of Walker and quarterback Patrick Mahomes recovering from a torn ACL in 2025. But Sunday's blowout victory over the Atlanta Falcons reminded us that this team will go only as far as the right arm of Mahomes, who looked all the way back from the ACL injury Sunday and overcame an elbow injury suffered last week.
With Walker missing the Falcons game because of a groin injury, all Mahomes did was throw for 348 yards and five touchdowns to remind the doubters that he is much more than a game manager who just turns and hands the ball off.
Walker has been mentioned as an MVP candidate. Reminder: He isn't even the MVP on his own team. Mahomes is that.
The addition of receiver Josh Downs at the trade deadline helps give Mahomes more weapons. Downs had a touchdown Sunday, as did rookie speedster Cyrus Allen , who may be on the verge of breaking out.
The backfield was also in good hands with rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who scored two touchdowns and accounted for 171 total yards, rushing for 101. He was able to replace Walker easily, but that injury largely forced the Falcons to turn back to Mahomes of old.
The 7-2 Chiefs are still sixth in my Power Rankings this week, but as that passing game gets back to what we've come to see in other years from Mahomes, they will be a real Super Bowl threat.
When Walker comes back, they can run it with anybody. With Mahomes under center, they can throw it with anybody — especially with the receiver group improving.
The defense is ranked third in scoring, giving up just 17.3 points per game. They are eighth in total defense and tied for sixth in yards allowed per play.
Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has this young group playing good defense.
The Chiefs are back. Mostly, though, Mahomes is back, which is why they are a real threat in the AFC to go to the Super Bowl. You want to go to Arrowhead to play them in the playoffs with that guy? Didn't think so.
As for the bottom of the rankings, the Los Angeles Chargers have moved on up. Not much, but they are out of the cellar after beating the Baltimore Ravens Monday night. The Tennessee Titans are now the bottom dwellers of my rankings.
author: Pete Prisco

title: NFL Week 10 grades: Chargers earn 'A-' for picking up first win, Packers fail in showdown with Vikings
summary: We're handing out grades for every team that played in Week 10
full_text:
Welcome to the Week 10 grades!
It was a day of statement wins around the NFL and the biggest statement was made by the Minnesota Vikings .
In their first game since trading for Kirk Cousins , the Vikings pounded the Packers 30-10, and the impressive part is that they did that at Lambeau Field. Combined with their 39-22 win in Week 1, they became the first team since 1987 to beat the Packers by at least 17 points twice in a season.
Patrick Mahomes also made a statement on Sunday and that's the Chiefs offense can still function just fine without Kenneth Walker . In Kansas City's 35-13 win over Atlanta, Mahomes threw five TD passes in a game for the first time since 2022. He also threw for 348 yards, and a big reason was that he finally had the long ball working. Mahomes, who had gone 20 straight games without throwing a touchdown pass that traveled at least 20 yards in the air, produced two of those against the Falcons .
Deshaun Watson also made a statement. The Browns quarterback led ANOTHER fourth-quarter comeback and just became only the third QB in NFL history with a game-winning drive in each of his team's first six wins in a season (1990 Troy Aikman and 2016 Matthew Stafford ).
And then there was Joe Burrow. The Bengals QB made a statement on Sunday night against the Steelers with four touchdown passes in a dominating 38-18 win. Burrow now has at least four total touchdowns in five straight games, which is tied with Peyton Manning (2004) for the longest streak in NFL history.
On Monday night, the Chargers made a statement by winning their first game of the season. They shot out to a 10-0 lead and then held on for dear life.
And now, let's get to the Week 10 grades, starting with the Chargers' surprising win.
Commanders (5-3-1) 24-21 over Giants (3-5-1)

title: Ravens vs. Chargers prediction: Can L.A. get its first win on 'MNF' against the injury-plagued Ravens?
summary: Plus, how to watch, odds, a preview and a prediction for the Monday night matchup
full_text:
In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers . Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley .
Los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season.
Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes.
Justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston , Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options.
Los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton , Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries -- an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry.
Other than all that, though, things are going really well!
That said, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change.
It's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago.
We know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling.
We also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson , but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns . The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers , and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here.
Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside.
Still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry , so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle.
Henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season.
The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground quickly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to big plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews .
I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board.
Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20

title: Sophomore bounce-back or letdown? Will Campbell quietly improving, Ashton Jeanty among 2025 first-round busts
summary: Last year's top draft picks reached a pivot point in their careers, and not everyone is on the right trajectory
full_text:
Some positions take longer to evaluate than others, but a year and a half is enough of a sample size to determine whether or not most of the top 2025 NFL Draft picks are on track to live up to expectations. Some, like Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden , have already arrived as stars. Others, including running backs Ashton Jeanty and Omarion Hampton , regressed during the first 10 weeks of their sophomore season. And the jury is still out on some.
For those who opened their careers with quiet rookie seasons, it is imperative to turn things around in 2026 and solidify or expand upon their roles before it is too late. Consecutive underwhelming campaigns at the start of a career turn projected stars into busts.
Contract extensions are not far off in the distance for last year's top-producing early draft picks, while those who continue to disappoint may find themselves reaching free agency before they reach their option year unless they correct their course.
Below are 10 players who underwhelmed as rookies and where they stand just over halfway through their second NFL seasons.
The season-long passing numbers and team record still leave a lot to be desired, but Cam Ward might be turning a corner. In his last two games, he posted a personal-best 304 passing yards against the Cincinnati Bengals and the third-best completion rate (71.8%) of his career against the Jacksonville Jaguars . Impressively, those performances came without standout rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate in the lineup.
Ward's totals are always inflated by the Tennessee Titans ' negative game scripts and, thus, their reliance on the pass, but notably, he is beginning to use his high volume more efficiently than in the first year and a half of his career. Ward is completing more passes, getting the ball out quicker, and taking fewer sacks in the process.
This all comes as head coach Robert Saleh said that the team has decided to make "a shift philosophically" on how to let Ward handle the offense. "Philosophically, the change was, how are we going to evaluate if he's capable of being the franchise QB if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it," Saleh said during his Monday media availability . "Over the last three weeks, he has done that."
This could be a small blip, or it could be the first sign that Ward is the long-term answer at quarterback for the Titans. He would be far from the only signal-caller to require a long onramp into stardom. For instance, Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence is now among the most renowned passers in football, and his first 25 starts were as much of a slog as Ward's.
Tennessee has a decision to make in the 2027 draft: use another early pick on a quarterback or commit to Ward. If he keeps playing as he did in Weeks 9 and 10, it should earn a call in his favor.
A torn LCL in late October 2025 robbed the football world of Travis Hunter's rookie year just when it was starting to take off. Back at full strength in 2026, the two-way player recaptured the momentum he built in the final games of his debut season and built on it, flourishing into the star the Jaguars expected when they traded up to draft him.
Hunter's offensive snap count (47) shows he is a defense-first player, but he is not entirely absent from the receiving plan and has a touchdown to his name. In Week 6, Hunter became the first player since 2002 and just the fifth player since the merger to record a touchdown reception and an interception in the same game, according to Stathead. The Jaguars allowing him to hone in on his defensive role, however, has led to a complete breakout on that side of the ball.
The Jaguars' busy trade deadline means two stars will join Hunter in the lineup, but he may already be on level footing with Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III in terms of the playmaking he brings. His PFF defensive grade ranks 11th league-wide at cornerback, and the factors behind that evaluation are astounding: he has allowed a passer rating of just 52.8 across 35 targets and has hauled in the first three interceptions of his career. That figure leads all Jaguars defensive backs and is 10th in the league among all defensive backs with at least 20 targets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The athleticism he displayed on his latest takeaway was uncanny for a cornerback.
Travis Hunter dives for the interception! 🔥 JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RKvGzhsi9H
Will Campbell just completed his worst game of the season. The six pressures, 18.2% pressure rate, and two sacks he allowed in the New England Patriots ' loss to the Detroit Lions were all season highs. Even worse, one of those sacks was the one that injured Drake Maye' s ankle. It was a stain on what has otherwise quietly been a better year than the disastrous rookie campaign he turned in last fall.
Even before the costly performance in Munich, Campbell was not exactly considered a star on the left side of the Patriots offensive line. But he is still more reliable than he was in 2025. New England will take any improvement it can squeeze out of the former No. 4 pick. The quick pressures and blatant one-on-one sacks that marred Campbell's injury-impacted rookie year have mostly subsided. He also improved on his pressure rate and sacks allowed (down from 11.2% and 8.5 last year to 7.0% and 2.5 through 10 games, according to Next Gen Stats).
Sunday's game against Detroit also ballooned those numbers: through the first nine weeks, his 5.9% pressure rate allowed led the team and was fourth among all tackles with at least 100 pass blocks, per Next Gen Stats.
His mistakes remain devastating, but they are fewer and further between. There is growth here.
Jeanty was initially projected as a can't-miss running back prospect after his Heisman Trophy finalist senior campaign at Boise State, but he hasn't translated his dominant ball-carrying ability to the NFL. His 41% rushing success rate as a rookie was as underwhelming as the 975 yards and five touchdowns he ran for in the Las Vegas Raiders ' disaster of a season, and even though the team has taken a sizable step forward in 2026, Jeanty's production on the ground has regressed by a meaningful margin.
The skill set Jeanty brought from college made him an ideal fit for an every-down role, but coach Klint Kubiak instead placed him in a timeshare in the rushing department and has gotten more out of him as a receiver than a runner. Jeanty ceded playing time to rookie Mike Washington Jr . and even saw a soft benching in Week 8—which Kubiak said was unrelated to the poor-taste comments he made about the New York Jets defense, but it certainly seemed that way.
The split between Jeanty and Washington wouldn't be uncalled for if the former were a mid-round pick. But this is last year's No. 6 overall selection. The Raiders are not completely free of fault. The team averages a league-low 1.5 yards before contact per rushing attempt, the third-lowest mark of any team since Pro Football Reference began tracking the stat in 2018. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, the Raiders' 34 tackles for loss on called runs and 58 stuffed runs both lead the league through Week 10 (with the Ravens and Chargers still to play at the time of writing). However, it is evident Las Vegas is not getting their investment's worth from a player who was supposed to be a no-doubt bellcow back.
The San Francisco 49ers are consistently great at identifying defensive line talent, so when they made Mykel Williams the third player off the board at that position, the assumption was that he would quickly become the next stellar lineman to emerge from this franchise. He earned plenty of opportunities as a rookie to jumpstart that trajectory and started in all nine of his appearances but suffered a season-ending torn ACL and has not made his way back into the starting lineup since then.

title: Sean Payton disputes Jim Harbaugh's 'loophole' claim after Broncos-Chargers trade falls apart
summary: The Broncos coach rejected Harbaugh's criticism of the process that derailed Denver's trade for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley
full_text:
At the trade deadline last Tuesday, a rare inter-division deal was agreed to between the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos . The Broncos agreed to send the Chargers a fourth-round pick and a future fifth-round pick in exchange for linebacker Daiyan Henley , but the deal fell apart.
The trade was nixed after Denver reportedly found an issue with Henley's knee during his physical. ESPN reported that the Broncos then approached the Chargers and attempted to renegotiate the compensation. Denver still wanted to acquire the linebacker, but just not at the price George Paton and Sean Payton initially agreed to.
Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate .
"That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."
The Broncos were on a bye in Week 10, so we had to wait until Monday to hear their side of the story. Payton was indeed asked about the trade falling through, but didn't offer many details.
"I'm not going to get into the specifics. He's prospect we thought of — and still do — very highly of. It just didn't work out," Payton said, via The Athletic. "I'll leave it at that."
What did Payton think about Harbaugh's comments regarding a "loophole?"
"Listen, I thought I saw it all," he said, via Mile High Sports. "There's no loophole. It's just part of the trade process, every step of the way."
Whatever the Broncos found in Henley's knee hasn't affected him yet. He hasn't missed a game due to injury in each of the last two seasons. In eight games played this season, Henley has recorded 51 tackles, half a sack, two passes defensed and an interception. The Broncos and Chargers will see each other again in the regular-season finale when Week 18 rolls around.

title: Joe Burrow isn't just chasing MVP, he's chasing the greatest passing season ever
summary: With 20 touchdown passes during Cincinnati's five-game winning streak, Burrow has separated himself in the MVP race while closing in on historic territory
full_text:
Two years ago, Joe Burrow resigned himself to the fact that, despite having an MVP-caliber season, he likely wouldn't win the award based on the Bengals ' 9-8 record and absence from the playoffs.
"I'll win one one day," Burrow said at the time.
That time could very well be now.
Already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers , Burrow is now the clear front-runner. Against a team that defeated the Bengals back in Week 3, Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns while completing nearly 80% of his passes. It could have been much more, but Bengals coach Zac Taylor called off the dogs and took Burrow out of the game midway through the fourth quarter of Cincinnati's eventual 38-18 win.
Playing in the background of Burrow's performance were MVP chants from Bengals fans, which Taylor acknowledged hearing throughout the game. Taylor, as you'd expect, agrees with that sentiment.
"I mean it would be impossible to say that anyone is playing better," Taylor said. "I'm not watching every game ... but I bet the people that aren't talking about him aren't watching our games, because if you are, it's really hard to say that he is not the best player on planet Earth."
Burrow's performance not only strengthened his MVP case but also put him on a historic trajectory with eight games to play in the 2026 regular season.
Burrow is one of only five quarterbacks in NFL history with over 30 total touchdowns through nine games, according to CBS Sports Research. The other four won league MVP: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Patrick Mahomes in 2018.
Burrow joined Manning on Sunday night as the only two quarterbacks with five consecutive games with at least four touchdowns. Over that span, Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns (against just three interceptions) and ran for two more while completing 78% of his passes. The Bengals won each of those games while taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
Burrow is on pace to become the third quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season. He is on pace to throw 51 touchdown passes, which would put him behind Manning's 55 during the 2013 season. Burrow's 5,279 yards would rank fourth behind Manning (5,477 in 2013), Drew Brees (5,476 in 2011) and Brady (5,316 in 2021).
While he's not on pace to break those records, Burrow is on track to create his own category for quarterback excellence by becoming the first quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing 70% of his passes. If he does that, he will have a strong argument when it comes to having the greatest passing season in league history.
Burrow's success can be attributed to his growth as well as improvements across Cincinnati's entire roster. The Bengals' offensive line has improved, and the defense has greatly benefited from the offseason acquisitions of Dexter Lawrence , Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook . It goes without saying that the trio of running back Chase Brown and wideouts Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have helped, too.
Now in his fourth season, Brown has established himself as one of the league's more versatile running backs. He had two touchdown catches on Sunday night and was second on the team with eight receptions.
"We know what we have in Chase," Burrow said. "He's a big-time playmaker for us. When people devote too many resources to stopping the guys on the outside, Chase can beat you in a lot of different ways."
That's now two TDs for Chase Brown and FOUR TDs for Joe Burrow 😎 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/svZHSPGVmC
Chase and Higgins are the league's best receiving duo and have been for some time. They're on pace to become the first pair of teammates to each post 1,500-yard receiving seasons in the same year.
Higgins is on pace to record a career-high 1,556 receiving yards this season, while Chase (who actually trailed Higgins in receiving yards prior to Sunday night) is on pace to have 1,658 receiving yards this season after catching 11 passes for 231 yards against Pittsburgh.
Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3
Looking ahead, the Bengals have only three remaining games against teams with winning records (Cleveland in Weeks 13 and 18, the Chiefs in Week 14). The Browns have given Burrow fits in the past, but Myles Garrett (now a Ram) was a big reason for that. Burrow has historically played well against the Chiefs.
As Burrow alluded to in his postgame press conference, it's only mid-November with a lot of football left to play. That may be true, but it is also true that Burrow has put himself -- and his team -- in position to have a memorable, and perhaps historic, season.
