title: Drake Maye injury the latest for Patriots amid snakebitten 2026 Super Bowl hangover
summary: From Drake Maye to A.J. Brown, injuries have piled up for New England in 2026
full_text:
A lot was made about the New England Patriots facing a historically easy schedule during their surprise run to Super Bowl LX in 2025. What flew more under the radar, however, was how remarkably healthy they were throughout that campaign. Between Week 1 and Super Bowl LX, New England placed just eight players on injured reserve. That's an astounding run of good health amid an NFL season, but water has found its level in 2026 in dramatic fashion.
The Patriots have been hit hard by injuries through 10 weeks of their 2026 season, and Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany may have delivered the kill shot.
At the tail end of the opening drive, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury that is reportedly feared to be season-ending . Specifically, there's concern the third-year quarterback may have fractured his ankle after taking a sack by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson . Maye stayed in Germany for additional testing to see if surgery is required. He is already expected to miss a substantial period of time, possibly even the entire season.
That would be the death blow for a New England team already marred by injuries throughout 2026.
For instance, as noted by the Boston Herald , 16 of the Patriots' 22 Week 1 starters have either missed games or been knocked out of contests so far due to injury. That doesn't even include players like wideout Romeo Doubs , TreVeyon Henderson , and other rotational contributors.
For a broader view of just how much of a bit the injury bug has taken, here's a look at some notable Patriots who've missed time so far this season due to injury ( courtesy of Pro Football Reference ).
High ankle sprain, knee, hamstring
In total, 28 different players have been listed as out on gameday or placed on injured reserve heading into the Week 10 game in Germany, not including the loss of Maye that happened during that game. This is an entirely different circumstance than the health the team enjoyed last season, and it's adding up. New England now lost three of their last four games, moving to 5-5 entering the Week 11 bye.
Injuries reared their head almost instantly at the start of 2026. Most notably, A.J. Brown — the club's offseason prize acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Eagles — suffered a high ankle sprain in his Patriots debut. That landed him on injured reserve, keeping him out until Week 6. He missed two more games in Weeks 8 and 9, then left Sunday's contest early with a hamstring injury.
The hits have kept coming for Mike Vrabel's team, and they aren't limited to players who've missed games we highlighted above. There are plenty of Patriots who have been limited by injury, but still been able to suit up. Safety Kevin Byard (chest), left tackle Will Campbell (knee), linebacker Christian Elliss (chest), tight end Hunter Henry (foot), right tackle Morgan Moses (foot), running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), defensive back Charles Woods (shoulder, hamstring), and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) have all popped up on the injury report throughout the season.
These are foundational pieces to what New England hoped would be a 2026 season that carried the momentum of last year's Super Bowl run and let them contend again. Instead, injuries — coupled with poor execution on the field — have turned a season once looked at with such promise upside down, especially in the wake of Maye's potential season-ender.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: The lost years of Lamar Jackson -- and the greatness still within reach
summary:
Injuries keep taking pieces of his prime. How much greatness is still ahead?



Is this conversation helpful so far?
full_text:
Some years, Lamar Jackson's thumb hits another player and is fine. Some years, his ankle just gets hit rather than rolled up on. And those years, he has been -- and will be -- a player who can win an MVP and perhaps a Super Bowl .
It has not been one of those years.
Jackson's latest injury was almost too cruel to believe. After missing the previous three and a half games with a high ankle sprain, the two-time MVP was finally back. So, too, was the Ravens ' hope. Jackson had looked phenomenal -- MVP-level phenomenal -- in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system. Not only was he back, but he was back in a big spot: against fellow MVP Josh Allen in a crucial matchup vs. Buffalo on the first day of November, with Baltimore trying to end a two-game losing streak.
And then, on the Ravens' first play, Jackson hit his thumb on Greg Rousseau's arm. Jackson looked down at his injured right thumb, trotted toward the sideline and then took a knee.
"Oh boy," NFL on CBS analyst Ross Tucker said.
Medical personnel surrounded Jackson, draped a towel over his hand and brought him down the tunnel, off the field.
"Oh my goodness," Tucker said.
What more was there to say? Lamar Jackson, one of the defining players not just of the era but of NFL history, was hurt. Again. And it was serious. Again.
Jackson officially landed on IR with a thumb injury that will require surgery. It is "potentially" season-ending, and with the Ravens 4-5 and losers of four straight, it's looking like a lost season in Baltimore. This is the fourth time in the last six years the 29-year-old has missed at least four games. It has robbed the Ravens of their Super Bowl aspirations. It has robbed the NFL of a superstar. And it has robbed Jackson, a Heisman Trophy winner and twice an NFL MVP, of even higher levels of all-time greatness.
On the positive side, the thumb injury is the first ailment to land Jackson on IR. He has never had an ACL tear, an Achilles tear, etc. On the negative side, Jackson has racked up so many injuries of so many different kinds that it seems like something is constantly getting in the way, whether it's nagging at him or keeping him out of games. He even said the ankle pain entering the Bills game last week was merely "bearable," not gone.
Since the start of last season alone, Jackson has had hamstring, ankle, toe, knee, back, and thumb ailments. Not all of those kept him out, but they add up. He admitted he came back from last year's hamstring injury too early, impacting his play all season.
And yes, for what it's worth, it's bad luck. If Jackson's hand hits Rousseau at any other angle, he might not hurt his thumb enough to need surgery. If a diving Jermaine Johnson II doesn't awkwardly trap Jackson's ankle to the turf in Week 3, Jackson might not miss the next three games. Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have both had hundreds of similar plays and, with the exception of Mahomes' torn ACL last year, avoided injury for the most part. Sometimes, it's simply human anatomy, something Jackson cannot change.
For as prolific a runner as Jackson is, he does an excellent job avoiding hits on those plays. None of his injuries have been on runs. It has just been a constant parade of misfortune. Unfortunately for Jackson and the Ravens, the NFL rolls on, whether you're lucky or not.
Perhaps time and injuries have taken their toll and blocked our collective memory from how incredible Jackson has been. That would be truly unfortunate.
In 2019, Jackson's second year of the league, he threw 36 touchdown passes and ran for 1,206 yards. In NFL history, there are ...
There is ONE with both: Jackson in 2019.
In fact, only one other player ever has posted 1,200 rushing yards and merely double-digit passing touchdowns in a season: Spec Sanders of the New York Yankees (football version) in the All-America Football Conference in 1947. But he only threw 14 touchdowns. Jackson did things modern football has never known.
Jackson became the youngest quarterback to win MVP and joined Tom Brady as the only unanimous MVPs in NFL history. There are many ways to measure individual season greatness, but Pro Football Reference's "Approximate Value" is as good as any. Jackson had an approximate value of 25 in 2019, tied for the second-best season on record ; LaDanian Tomlinson's 2006 season, in which he scored an NFL-record 31 touchdowns, is the only one better.
Jackson was healthy in 2020 and had another strong season, including a second straight 1,000-yard rushing effort. He has as many 1,000-yard rushing seasons as all other quarterbacks in NFL history combined (Michael Vick and Justin Fields both have one).
Then the injuries started. In 2021, Jackson was on pace for another 1,000-yard rushing season, and the Ravens led the AFC North when Browns linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah dove at Jackson's ankles after Jackson released a pass. Jackson got carted off and didn't play in any of the final four games. The Ravens lost all four and missed the playoffs.
The next year, Jackson sprained his PCL when his left knee got driven into the ground on a sack by the Broncos ' Jonathan Cooper . He ended up missing six weeks -- the final five of the regular season and a wild card game, which Baltimore lost.
This was a strange one. John Harbaugh initially wondered if Jackson could be back the next week and added "If not, it'll be sometime after that shortly." Then, Ravens officials were confident Jackson would return for the playoffs, per ESPN , leaving Jackson to essentially rule himself out -- and give his own medical update -- via social media .
In 2023, though, Jackson was healthy and marvelous once again. Under new offensive coordinator Todd Monken, Jackson set career highs in completion percentage (67.2%), passing yards (3,678) and yards per attempt (8.0). He was still excellent on the ground with a team-high 821 yards. He won MVP and was one vote short of doing so unanimously.
He was somehow even better in 2024, with 4,172 passing yards and 8.8 yards per attempt. He threw 41 touchdowns and just four interceptions. He ran for 915 yards. He had already reached unprecedented levels. Now, he was reaching new ones, as the first player with:
His 10.25 touchdown-to-interception ratio was also the best ever in any 30-touchdown season.
Somehow Jackson didn't win MVP. He was a first-team All-Pro, but MVP went to Allen, an extreme rarity. Jackson would have been the youngest three-time MVP in NFL history. That's how good the start was.
From 2019 to 2024, Jackson ranked third in passer rating and touchdown-to-interception ratio and fourth in yards per attempt. He was also fourth in touchdown passes despite missing significant time in two seasons. He was also eighth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry.
He was the Shohei Ohtani of football. No one can be this good at two different aspects, right? Wrong. Jackson was truly exceptional, and he seemed to be getting better.
He had nine touchdowns and zero interceptions on an absurd 9.6 yards per attempt through three weeks of 2025. Then came the hamstring injury, which started an avalanche of injuries. The hits haven't stopped coming since.
If two things stand out as Jackson's career shortcomings, it's injuries and playoff performance. The two are somewhat intertwined. In 2021, Baltimore missed the playoffs. In 2022, Jackson missed the playoffs. Last year, his injuries derailed the Ravens, but they somehow got a Week 18 win-and-in game against the Steelers . Tyler Loop missed a game-winning field goal attempt. It's looking like he will not add to his postseason ledger this season, either.
Had Jackson been healthy in even two of those four lost seasons, is he a Super Bowl champ? Or does he at least have more postseason wins?
Jackson is one of nine quarterbacks to win multiple MVP awards since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger. Of those nine, Jackson has the second-fewest playoff wins (two) before his 30th birthday, only ahead of the famously late-blooming Steve…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Sam Darnold or Drew Lock? Breaking down the Seahawks' surprising QB debate
summary: Drew Lock is 4-0 as Seattle's primary quarterback and has dramatically outperformed Sam Darnold in several key metric
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks moved to 6-4 with their Sunday 21-13 victory over Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders . Drew Lock and Jaxon Smith-Njigba powered a strong second half, which included a 14-point third quarter to escape Sin City with the win, and now the Seahawks are going to need to have a conversation.
Should Mike Macdonald continue to roll with Lock under center and bench Sam Darnold ? Lock has now made three starts this season, and won all three. If you want to count the Week 1 comeback against the New England Patriots , where Lock took over on the second drive of the game, then he's accounted for four of Seattle's six wins. Lock is running the offense and taking care of the football, and it's working.
Below, we will make the case for starting Lock moving forward, and the case for rolling with Darnold, with evidence obtained by Doug Clawson of CBS Sports Research.
Lock is a perfect 4-0 as the Seahawks' primary quarterback. Again, we'll use the term "primary" to include the season opener against the Patriots even though Darnold "started" that game. In all, Lock has completed 73.1% of his passes for 837 yards, seven touchdowns and zero turnovers.
Lock ranks third in both EPA per dropback and yards per dropback this season (min. 75 attempts). The offense ranks eighth in EPA per play under Lock, and 28th with Darnold.
Lock is also playing the style of football Seattle wants to play. What does that mean? It means he's accounted for zero turnovers and is getting the ball to JSN. Eight of Lock's 14 pass completions on Sunday went to Smith-Njigba, who finished with a season-high 171 yards and one touchdown. The Seahawks ran the ball 35 times and attempted 17 passes, and relied on an elite defense to take over the game. That's what Macdonald wants to do.
The numbers prove it. Lock has been the more efficient quarterback this year, while Darnold leads the NFL with 29 turnovers over the last two seasons. He's turned the ball over seven times in the four losses this season, and they have been costly. Darnold threw zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the overtime loss to the Denver Broncos . He threw two interceptions in a three-point loss to the San Francisco 49ers , and two interceptions in the two-point loss to the Washington Commanders . Darnold actually hasn't finished a game this season without throwing an interception!
You can't argue with the record. Lock is 4-0 while Darnold is 2-4. If the season ended today, the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks wouldn't make the playoffs. You have to stick with what's working.
Sure, Lock is 4-0, but have you seen who he's played? He beat a Patriots team that is clearly not the same Patriots team that made the Super Bowl last year. Drake Maye was seeing ghosts and threw three interceptions in Seattle's 13-10 win. Then, Lock beat the lowly Arizona Cardinals twice, and a Raiders team that was touting a rookie quarterback who was making his first career start. No. 1 overall pick quarterbacks are now 1-16-1 in their first career starts since 2004. It would have been shocking if Vegas won that game. Meanwhile, Darnold has faced off against Brock Purdy and the 49ers, Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears , and Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs .
It's true that Darnold is turning the ball over too much right now, but he just became the fourth Super Bowl-winning quarterback in the last 35 postseasons to have zero turnovers in the playoffs. Darnold didn't have the most magical performance in the Super Bowl, but he was incredible in the NFC Championship Game vs. the Los Angeles Rams , throwing for 346 yards and three touchdowns with zero turnovers. He had to outduel NFL MVP Matthew Stafford .
We've seen Darnold play good football. We saw him play a part in a Super Bowl run just nine months ago. It hasn't been entirely smooth this year, but punting on Darnold for Lock right now would be an aggressive decision.
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin said on NBC Sunday night that Macdonald and Darnold are "tied together for life" after the two helped engineer a successful climb to the NFL's mountaintop. Macdonald has a special level of respect for Darnold -- who has "money in coach Macdonald's emotional bank account," as Tomlin put it. It's worth having this debate because Lock is playing good football, but ultimately, Darnold is the Seahawks' starter.

title: Joe Burrow strengthens MVP case with four more TDs; college football rankings projections
summary: Plus why Kayla Harrison should retire after UFC 334
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The nationwide ground stop the FAA issued Friday could not have come at a more disruptive time for football teams since it was a travel day for numerous squads. The NFL schedule went off without a hitch save for some referee reassignments and a rare instance in which four officials worked multiple games in one day . Travel hiccups were much more defined in the college game and impacted countless games , some of which were delayed multiple hours to accommodate teams' late arrivals.
Of the 14 highest-profile games that featured programs which experienced travel issues, those teams went 9-5 , so it's hard to say the flight disruptions were to blame for any poor play.
The biggest snag came in the matchup between Ole Miss and Oklahoma . A handful of challenges including a timed-out flight crew and a small airport left the Rebels grounded until Saturday and led the SEC to push the game to Sunday.
The conference's decision was highly unpopular among Oklahoma stakeholders. Sooners athletic director Roger Denny put the league on blast for forcing his program to comply with the schedule change. Legendary former Sooners coach Bob Stoops chimed in with his own criticism of commissioner Greg Sankey .
In the end, the Sooners pulled off a 24-17 win anyway. Their revitalized offense controlled the game flow in a victory over a ranked opponent and provided proof of concept that Jason Witten could be the answer as the team's potential full-time offensive coordinator. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott even said Witten could be an NFL coach .
LSU 's last chance to secure a resume-building win was dashed by Texas . The Tigers led by as many as 11 points in a marquee matchup and were two seconds away from closing it out when Arch Manning connected with Raleek Brown on a game-winning swing pass for the Longhorns . From the Tigers' standpoint, it was the most devastating loss for a CFP bubble team in Week 11 and another stain on Lane Kiffin 's young tenure. He was the biggest individual loser of the week .
Manning's heroics came in another clutch moment for college football's most polarizing quarterback , who relished in the fact that his team dealt the decisive blow to LSU's playoff hopes . On the opposing sideline, Kiffin watched his championship expectations come crumbling down in that moment. Our Chris Hummer was on site to tell the story.
In the Big Ten, Indiana has a quarterback controversy. Seventh-year senior Grant Wilson might just be the key to the Hoosiers' search for a second consecutive national championship, not Josh Hoover , the expensive transfer they brought in to lead them back to glory. Wilson guided Indiana to a 27-13 win over USC and left Lincoln Riley to tell the same old story to Trojans fans.
In the ACC, Miami turned in a "B" performance in its second game without Malachi Toney , and Wake Forest obliterated SMU in a statement game .
Week 11 also dialed up the heat on the hot seat . For now, the pressure is off Deion Sanders . He orchestrated Colorado 's first top-15 win since 2007 in a stunner against Houston . Dabo Swinney , on the other hand, reached a new low . Clemson has now lost nine of its last 11 home games against Power Four opponents.

title: Drake Maye injury update: Patriots reportedly fear QB fractured ankle, could miss rest of season
summary: Maye remained in Germany for additional testing after injuring his ankle against the Lions
full_text:
The New England Patriots may have to finish the 2026 season without their franchise centerpiece. Quarterback Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a significant lower-leg injury that is poised to sideline him for an extended period of time, according ESPN . The report notes that the injury has the potential to keep Maye out for the remainder of the year. Specifically, ESPN reports that the team fears Maye fractured his ankle.
Maye suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of New England's opening drive against the Detroit Lions during their Week 10 matchup in Munich, Germany. The third-year quarterback was sacked by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson on a third-and-goal play and was in noticeable discomfort after the hit. After being looked at on the sideline, Maye gingerly walked to the locker room where he was eventually ruled out with what the team called an ankle injury.
Immediately after the game, coach Mike Vrabel didn't have much of an update on Maye's status. However, Vrabel told WEEI's "The Greg Hill Show" on Monday morning that Maye stayed back in Germany.
"The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,' Vrabel said, via the Boston Herald . "He'll be traveling back here shortly. But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries, and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."
Given that Maye was unable to travel back with the team following the international contest, this lends credence to this latest report on the severity of the injury. ESPN's report highlights that Maye stayed in Germany to undergo additional tests to determine whether he needs surgery.
Maye -- along with the entire Patriots team -- has come back down to earth a bit in 2026 following his MVP runner-up season last year as New England made a surprise Super Bowl run. Through 10 games, Maye was 5-5 as the starter, completed 65.6% of his passes, averaged 233.0 passing yards per game, and threw for 18 touchdowns. He's also thrown 11 interceptions, which are already a career high.
Of course, it's never a good time for your franchise quarterback to endure a potential season-ending injury, but Maye going down comes at a critical juncture of New England's season. The club is reeling after losing three of its last four games, dropping it back to .500 on the season.
This latest loss to Detroit pushes them further behind the Buffalo Bills (8-1) in the AFC East race, and they are now on the outside looking in on the AFC playoff picture. Coming into Week 10, they were slotted as the No. 7 seed, but are now sitting as the No. 8 seed and looking up to the Cleveland Browns (6-4), Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3), and Denver Broncos (7-2) for the three wild card spots.
The Patriots will have the bye to collect themselves in Week 11, but the road ahead doesn't get any easier, particularly in December, when they'll face the Bills, Vikings , and Chiefs (road) over a three-week span. Not having Maye for those matchups would make New England significant underdogs, even with two of those games at Gillette Stadium.
With Maye on the shelf, the Patriots will first turn to top backup Tommy DeVito . He stepped in during their contest with Detroit in Germany on Sunday. In that game, DeVito put up less-than-stellar numbers, completing 12-of-24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He also rushed four times for 19 yards on the ground.
DeVito has been with New England for the past two seasons after being claimed off waivers in August of 2025 following his release from the New York Giants . Last offseason, he signed a two-year, $7.4 million extension with the team and became the primary back to Maye entering 2026.
The 28-year-old has starting experience, having logged eight starts over his career since entering the NFL in 2023 as an undrafted free agent out of Illinois. DeVito is 3-5 over those starts and has a 63.4% completion percentage to go along with an 84.6 passer rating for his career.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 11 early odds: Bills, Chiefs favored by 16.5 points; Bengals line jumps after blowout
summary: Buffalo and Kansas City are each favored by 16.5 points as four teams enter Week 11 laying double digits
full_text:
Week 11 is one of the smallest slates that we'll have during the 2026 season. With six teams on the bye, that leaves us with just 13 games on the docket next week. While small, the slate packs a punch with several heavy favorites. In all, there are four double-digit favorites in Week 11, two of which are above two touchdowns.
The Buffalo Bills are one of those favorites, opening as a 16.5-point favorite over the Miami Dolphins when they host their AFC East rival. Meanwhile, the Kansas City Chiefs are also laying 16.5 points after initially opening as a 14-point favorite at home against the Arizona Cardinals . These are true David vs. Goliath matchups, but it'll be fascinating to see how the public feels about laying such massive numbers, even with both Buffalo and Kansas City 3-1 ATS at home.
Those are just a couple of early lines that we'll sink our teeth into. Below, we're diving into all of the early lines for Week 11 and seeing who the oddsmakers project coming out on top.

Ravens +110, Panthers -130

Chicago is emerging from its bye as a 10-point favorite, which is up from the 9.5 points they were laying at the open. The Bears are 6-3 ATS so far in 2026, which includes a 3-2 ATS mark at Soldier Field. While the Saints fell to the Panthers at the Superdome, they've fared much better on the road for bettors. New Orleans is a perfect 3-0 ATS as the away team. They are the only team in the NFL without an ATS road loss so far.
Pittsburgh opened as a 4.5-point favorite on the road against the Eagles, who were on the bye in Week 10. Philadelphia is 0-5 ATS at home this season, and four of those ATS defeats have come as a home underdog. The Steelers are 1-1 ATS as a road favorite.
Carolina is up to a 2.5-point favorite after initially opening as a 1.5-point favorite at home as they face the Ravens. Baltimore still has its Week 10 matchup against the Chargers on Monday night, so this line could see some movement depending on how that game unfolds. That said, the Ravens playing on a short week is a tough turn of events. This season, Baltimore is 0-2 ATS when at a rest disadvantage. Carolina will hope that continues as they look to improve their 1-3 ATS record at home.
Kansas City has jumped out as a 16.5-point favorite after this line first opened at -14 when they host the Cardinals. The Chiefs are coming off a dominant win over the Falcons , in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdowns. They head back to Arrowhead Stadium where they are 3-1 ATS and have an average margin of victory of 15.8 (second-best in the NFL). Arizona is 4-2 ATS on the road.
The Lions are now a 5.5-point favorite at Ford Field after initially opening as a 6-point favorite over the Buccaneers. That could be due to a couple of factors, including star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffering a serious knee injury in the win over the Patriots in Germany. Speaking of Germany, Detroit will also be at a disadvantage in rest. As they come off the international game, the Bucs are coming out of their bye week. The Lions are 1-2-1 ATS at home this season, while Tampa Bay is 3-1 ATS on the road.
Dallas is a 7.5-point favorite as they host the Titans and look to bounce back following a loss to the 49ers on Sunday. title: Steelers' receiver problem proves they made a massive NFL trade deadline mistake
summary: Pittsburgh declined to add a receiver at the trade deadline, leaving Aaron Rodgers without the help he needed
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers lost Sunday night's game to the Cincinnati Bengals days before the game even started. OK, that might be a stretch. But the Steelers' decision not to acquire a receiver before the trade deadline has aged faster than milk on a hot summer day.
Hours after Josh Downs -- whom the Steelers were reportedly interested in acquiring before the deadline -- scored a touchdown in his Kansas City Chiefs debut, Pittsburgh fans were forced to sit through another game of watching DK Metcalf play dodgeball and Aaron Rodgers desperately looking for Jaylen Warren in the flat with no open options downfield.
Rodgers did not complete a pass until late in the first half. At that point, it was already 17-0 Bengals, a lead that swelled to 24-3 before intermission. It was 31-3 in the third before the Steelers finally found the end zone early in the fourth quarter. Ironically, the score was courtesy of Metcalf, but it was way too little, too late. Pittsburgh later tacked on another late score in garbage time in what was a 38-18 loss.
There was plenty of evidence before the deadline that the Steelers needed help at receiver. Metcalf entered Sunday with just one touchdown and only 33 catches on 64 targets. Germie Bernard has played well for a rookie, but he's not a No. 2 receiver, at least not now.
Despite their lack of weaponry, the Steelers were 6-2 heading into their bye week, which coincided with the trade deadline. Pittsburgh reportedly discussed trades involving Downs, Brian Thomas Jr. , and Calvin Ridley . Thomas and Ridley were not traded, but Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick were sent to Kansas City in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks. A very reasonable trade that the Steelers should have tried to make.
There are two likely reasons why the Steelers didn't trade for a receiver. Pittsburgh probably didn't want to give up too many future draft picks that could be used to acquire its next franchise quarterback, and it still has confidence in its receiving corps.
Let's address the second reason first. Pittsburgh had an eight-game sample size to assess their situation at receiver. It was clear before the deadline that reinforcements were needed, even with the prospect of Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman 's possible returns from injuries (Pittman, an expensive offseason acquisition, has seven catches this season and hasn't played since Week 4).
Regarding future draft picks, that's the price the Steelers continue to pay for not having found their long-term solution at quarterback. The Steelers have three other quarterbacks on their roster (including rookie Drew Allar ), so there's a good chance that Pittsburgh won't spend a high pick on a quarterback in 2027, anyway. Pittsburgh's current 2026 projection suggests they won't have a high draft pick again. That has been an ongoing issue for a team that still hasn't found Ben Roethlisberger's long-term successor.
Regardless of the reason, the Steelers' lack of movement at the deadline raises the following question: what was the point of bringing back Rodgers? If the Steelers were serious about maximizing their strong start (like the Chiefs and Jaguars did) in Rodgers' final season, they would have gotten a receiver at the deadline, among other things. Instead, the Steelers stood pat and were blown out on Sunday night by a Bengals team that moved past them for first place in the AFC North.
Pittsburgh's situation at receiver is a mess, but that's not its only issue. The defense was a disaster on Sunday night. They had no answer for Joe Burrow , who sliced and diced Pittsburgh's zone coverage.
Cincinnati, winners of five straight games, appears to be not only the front-runner to win the North, but possibly the entire AFC. Conversely, the Steelers are a decent team that has benefitted from an easy schedule.
Pittsburgh faces only two teams with winning records from here on out, so it's very possible that the Steelers can get to 10 wins for a fourth straight season. That's far from a guarantee, however. The Steelers suffered a serious loss Sunday night when guard Mason McCormick was carted off the field in the second quarter. While the severity of his injury wasn't immediately known, it appears that Pittsburgh will have to move forward without him.
Even if the Steelers reach 10 wins and earn a fourth straight playoff berth, their season appears headed for a disappointing finish. Rodgers deserved better than that in his final season.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Aidan Hutchinson injury: Lions star joins bizarre list of NFL players hurt while celebrating
summary: Aidan Hutchinson's sack celebration ended with a significant knee injury, recalling some of the strangest and most painful mishaps in NFL history
full_text:
The Detroit Lions ' win in Germany came at a high cost. Lions' talented pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a "significant" knee injury in the first quarter that was sustained during his post-sack celebration.
Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF
Despite Hutchinson's absence, Detroit rolled to a 35-10 win over the Patriots . The Lions received a big game from Hutchinson's backup, rookie Derrick Moore , who had two of Detroit's five sacks.
Hutchinson has joined the list of NFL players who have sustained injuries after celebrating. Here's a look at some of the others.
Greenlaw wasn't celebrating, but he joins the conversation because his injury occurred on a non-contact play during the Super Bowl . The 49ers ' linebacker was enthusiastically jumping in place before he tore his Achilles as he was in the process of jogging back on the field.
Dre Greenlaw appeared to injure himself jogging back onto the field pic.twitter.com/p3nwmTUsfO
The 49ers ultimately lost to the Chiefs in the second Super Bowl, which was decided in overtime. Greenlaw missed most of the following season while recovering from the injury.
Houston tore his ACL after celebrating his sack of Jimmy Garoppolo near the end of Chicago's blowout loss to New England in Week 8 of the 2014 season. Houston, who had signed a big contract before the start of that season, apologized to his teammates the following day.
THROWBACK: Lamar Houston tears his ACL celebrating a sack with Chicago trailing by 3 touchdowns pic.twitter.com/rXcsgAPKlc
Houston moved from defensive end to linebacker the following season and recorded a career-high 8.0 sacks. His last season was in 2017.
Five weeks prior to Houston's incident, Tulloch tore his ACL after celebrating a sack of Aaron Rodgers . In just the season's third week, Tulloch was lost for the season.
Former Detroit Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch tore his ACL in his left knee in 2014 while doing a similar celebration. https://t.co/TYxFD2PPRr pic.twitter.com/fOZUR95F5d
Tulloch returned from the injury and had 107 tackles, a forced fumble and two fumble recoveries in 2015. In 2016, he appeared in just 12 games for the Eagles in what was ultimately his final NFL season.
Gramatica tore his ACL after celebrating a 42-yard field goal during the first quarter of a Week 14 game against the Giants .
At the time, no one knew the seriousness of Gramatica's injury. Iconic Cardinals safety Pat Tillman handled the kickoffs for the remainder of the game, and Gramatica hit a short field goal and a point-after attempt in Arizona's eventual 17-13 loss.
Gramatica missed the remainder of the 2001 season. His replacement, Cedric Oglesby, made five field goals on six attempts. Those were Oglesby's only NFL regular season appearances.
Haven’t seen a worse Celebration injury since Gramatica! Prayers up for Aiden Hutchinson! pic.twitter.com/SwJDNA9wpU
A rookie at the time, Gramatica played four seasons in the NFL. He clarified the cause of his injury during a 2010 interview.
"You guys got it wrong," Gramatica said at the time . "You said I got hurt jumping. My jump was excellent. It was my landing I needed to work on. It was funny. It was part of my career. I talk about it all the time. You have to laugh about it."
Maybe the most infamous celebratory injury in NFL history. In Week 13 of the 1997 season, Frerotte -- a Pro Bowler the previous season -- suffered a sprained neck and a concussion after headbutting a padded cement wall after a short touchdown run against the Giants late in the first half.
With Aiden Hutchinson’s celebration injury, couldn’t help but think about Gus Ferrote concussing himself by headbutting the wall 😅 pic.twitter.com/i4HjiKB0EJ
Frerotte returned for Washington's next possession, but he was replaced in the second half by veteran backup (and former Giants Super Bowl-winning quarterback) Jeff Hostetler. Washington's offense didn't score another point and had to settle for a 7-7 tie.
Frerotte played a week later and sustained a season-ending hip injury. With Hostetler back under center, Washington won two of its last three games but missed the playoffs with an 8-7-1 record.
Frerotte played another decade in the NFL, but he never matched the level of success he had enjoyed prior to his injury against the Giants.
"You know, it didn't define me, and it still doesn't define me," he said back in 2017 . "And that's what's great. I think if I didn't laugh about it, I wouldn't have been able to go on and play another 10 years after that."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Bengals' blowout win over Steelers makes NFL history with 1,100th 'scorigami'
summary: Cincinnati's 38-18 victory became the 1,100th unique final score in NFL history
full_text:
It took 107 years, but the NFL has finally produced its 1,100th final score of all time, and it came on Sunday night in Cincinnati. In an AFC North showdown, the Bengals topped the Steelers 38-18, marking the first time that a game ended with that exact final score.
The scorigami only happened because the Steelers scored a garbage-time touchdown in the fourth quarter. With Pittsburgh trailing 38-11, Aaron Rodgers threw a 27-yard TD pass to Pat Freiermuth , and at that point, the Steelers could have gone for two, but instead, they decided to kick the extra point. If the kick had missed, there wouldn't have been a scorigami, because 38-17 has happened before, but Boswell's kick went through and that ultimately gave us the 1,100th final score in NFL history.
PIT 18 - CIN 38 🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨 That is the 1100th unique score in NFL history, and the 5th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/jIo0wxFPxX
For a game to end in a scorigami, you need a few bizarre things to happen and the Steelers definitely provided those.
With the Bengals leading 31-3 in the fourth quarter, the Steelers scored a touchdown and decided to go for two, even though it didn't make much sense at that point. They ended up getting the two-point conversion, bringing the score to 38-11. Surprisingly, that final score has actually happened before, so the scorigami didn't become official until Freiermuth got his touchdown later in the fourth quarter. On the second touchdown, the Steelers did NOT go for two, which was a bit bizarre considering they had gone for two on their first score.
The Bengals did their part of the scorigami by lighting up the scoreboard at Paycor Stadium. Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns to help the Bengals get to 38 points.
The Bengals actually had a missed field goal in the game from Evan McPherson and if that would have gone in, we also would have gotten a scorigami, because 41-18 has never happened before in NFL history. The missed kick ended McPherson's franchise-record streak for 25 consecutive field goals.
When it comes to scorigamis, the Bengals are the hottest team in the NFL right. This is the second straight home game where they've had a scorigami. Before Sunday night, their last home game came in a 43-36 win over the Titans that gave us the 1,098th different final score in NFL history .
As for the Steelers, this marks the first time they've been involved in a scorigami since a 48-37 playoff loss to the Browns back in January 2021.
This turned out to be a banner week for scorigamis. Not only did the Bengals and Steelers give us a new final score, but the 49ers ' 46-40 win over the Cowboys was also a scorigami .
This actually marks the second time this season that we've had two scorigamis in one day. It also happened back in Week 1 . And I already know what your next question is: This marks the first time since 2017 that we've had two scorigamis in one day happen TWICE in the same season.
Overall, there have been five scorigamis this year, tied for the most in the 2025 season. Basically, this is turning into the year of the scorigami.
author: John Breech

title: Cover 32: Two NFL awards already in the bag, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 10
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all of the biggest items from Week 10 in the NFL, including a historic day from Jahmyr Gibbs and statement return to Minnesota for Kirk Cousins
full_text:
In lockstep with Week 10 kicking off, the second half of the regular season is underway. Naturally, there's going to be plenty of twists and turns as we barrel down the stretch run. Teams will jockey for playoff positioning while players and coaches look to put themselves in contention for awards such as MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and more. When it comes to awards, two are already in the bag.
Even with seven weeks left to go in the regular season, I'm ready to call two awards right now:
What we saw from both of them in Week 10 only bolsters their case, if not outright putting the final nail in the coffin to eventually go home with the awards when we get to the NFL Honors during Super Bowl week.
When it comes to Monken, who opened at +1400 to win the award at DraftKings Sportsbook , he has remarkably put the Browns in the AFC playoff picture after jumping out to a 6-4 record. That record includes a 4-0 mark at home, the first time the franchise has done so since 1963.
He's also coached through some tightly contested games. In fact, Monken's Browns are the first team in NFL history to have their first six wins each come by four points or less. To his credit, Monken named Deshaun Watson the starter this summer, which is a move that has borne fruit. Watson has been solid this season, notching six game-winning drives. He's also thrown for at least 300 yards in each of his past three games, making him just the third Browns quarterback to do so.
Sunday's win over the Texans also inched Cleveland closer to securing a playoff spot. Even as they entered Week 10 with a 3-5 record, Houston was a dark horse to possibly oust the Browns from a playoff spot. However, after knocking them down to 3-6 and claiming the head-to-head tiebreaker, they've largely killed that possibility in its crib.
BROWNS WIN pic.twitter.com/mQGRiqo4mM
Moreover, when you look at the rest of the competition in the wild card race, there's not much to speak of.
The Ravens (4-5 before Monday night) are starting a backup after Lamar Jackson went down with a fractured right thumb. Meanwhile, the Patriots (5-5) could be starting a backup for the foreseeable future depending on the severity of Drake Maye's ankle injury. Then, you have the Raiders , who are 4-6 and are working in a rookie quarterback. The Browns host Las Vegas in Week 12 following their bye week, putting themselves in a strong position to pick up yet another key head-to-head tiebreaker.
The path is quite clear for them to secure a wild card spot. If/when that happens, Monken is the runaway favorite for Coach of the Year. Right now, he's +370 at DraftKings Sportsbook, tied with John Harbaugh for the second-best odds, as they both look up to Kyle Shanahan (+300). The smart money should be on Monken.
As for Mahomes, he was the favorite to win Comeback Player of the Year from the jump, but was still +185 to win i t at the start of the season. While they were short odds at the time, getting it at plus money feels like stealing right now.
After suffering a torn ACL and LCL last season, Mahomes has come back and helped Kansas City to a 7-2 record. Prior to Sunday, Mahomes largely managed games and leaned on the likes of Kenneth Walker III for the burst on offense. Week 10 was a different animal, however. Mahomes exploded for 348 passing yards and five passing touchdowns in a dominant win over the Falcons .
MAHOMES FIVE TOUCHDOWN PASSES 🔥 pic.twitter.com/G1ZClQomml
This was Mahomes' first game with at least five passing touchdowns since Week 1 of the 2022 season.
Sunday's win put Kansas City back atop the AFC West and in prime position to return to the playoffs in some capacity after a one-year absence in 2025. All that has Mahomes as a shoo-in to win Comeback Player of the Year.
So, even though we have plenty of time before these awards are handed out, you can start engraving COY and CPOY now.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
Gibbs was a man amongst boys in Detroit's Week 10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He finished with 252 yards from scrimmage, which were the second-most in a game in his career. It was also the second-most scrimmage yards in an international game all-time. Moreover, his 28-yard touchdown run (his second of the day) was his 62nd of his career, which is the most by any player in his four seasons in NFL history.
Penei leads the way for another Jahmyr Gibbs tuddy! pic.twitter.com/EuBi7Y2U4c
Jacksonville continues to roll and moved to 7-2 after a 40-23 win over Tennessee. Amid the winning effort, Parker Washington dazzled with some circus catches en route to 152 receiving yards for the day. That set a new career high for the Jags wideout. Dating back to last season, Washington has tallied 992 receiving yards over his last 12 games. That's the most in a 12-game span by a Jaguars player since 2015.
Parker Washington or Peter Parker? JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/l02kcfOngG
Chase may not have found the end zone, but he was the catalyst for the Bengals offense in a dominant win over the Steelers. The Cincinnati wideout hauled in 11 of his 14 targets for 231 yards. This marks the third time in Chase's career that he's recorded at least 10 catches and 225 receiving yards in a game, which is tied for the most in NFL history.
Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3
Kenneth Walker III, who? The Chiefs rookie back filled the shoes of the star back perfectly as he was inactive for Week 10 due to a groin injury. If you didn't look too hard, it was hard to tell the difference between Johnson and Walker in this game. The fifth-round pick out of Nebraska erupted for 171 scrimmage yards and was a key outlet for Mahomes in the passing game, particularly in the red zone. Johnson became just the second player since 1970 with at least 100 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards, and two touchdowns in his first career start.
Emmett Johnson is too quick 💨 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/sY1oGo45zY
Hubbard was the straw that stirred the drink of the Panthers offense as they outlasted the Saints in New Orleans. The veteran back accounted for both of Carolina's touchdowns and led the team in rushing as well as receiving. He's just the second player in franchise history to have at least 80 yards rushing and receiving and two rushing touchdowns in a single game, joining Christian McCaffrey (twice). Hubbard helped the Panthers notch their first road win against the Saints since 2023.
Chuba Hubbard for the lead with 1:49 to play! CARvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H1nYzGJl8G
McCaffrey became the first running back in NFL history with two 65-yard touchdown receptions in a game. The 49ers back was doing it all as San Francisco fended off the Cowboys in Dallas to move to 7-1 on the season. Amid a 21-point fourth quarter by the Cowboys, McCaffrey helped keep them at bay with two touchdowns of his own. The final was a 66-yard catch-and-run that proved to be the dagger.
Don't leave CMC in the open field 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/hGnsBSY5V5
Aidan Hutchinson has reportedly suffered a serious knee injury that could knock him out for the foreseeable future. To make matters worse, the injury didn't even come during a play. Instead, Hutchinson was celebrating a third-down sack of Drake Maye during Detroit's opening defensive possession of the afternoon in Germany. After taking down the Patriots quarterback, Hutchinson leaped in the air and then came down awkwardly on his knee.
The Lions have ruled out star DE Aidan Hutchinson for the game with a knee injury. pic.twitter.com/jR365USNf2
He limped off the field and into the locker room before being ruled out for the rest of the game. Now, it appears that the rest of his season could be in jeopardy.
One of the dagger moments of Minnesota's victory…

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Rams Winners & Losers: Arizona taken to the woodshed
summary: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win. They already defeated the Los Angeles Rams earlier this year with six Chad Ryland field goals. Can they defeat this divisional rival again? This one is completely different from the first contest. For one, instead of 10-year veteran Jacoby Brissett under center, rookie Carson Beck will be starting his […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals needed a win. They already defeated the Los Angeles Rams earlier this year with six Chad Ryland field goals. Can they defeat this divisional rival again? This one is completely different from the first contest. For one, instead of 10-year veteran Jacoby Brissett under center, rookie Carson Beck will be starting his very NFL game. Is he ready? Prior to Week 1, the answer from Beck was a resounding yes. His coaching staff agrees. For another thing. All-World EDGE rusher Myles Garrett made his Rams debut. Yikes. RELATED: BECK STARTS OFF STRONG The Rams came into this game 5-4-0 while Arizona is 3-6-0. Both clubs need a win badly. When the contest finished, Arizona was taken to the woodshed by Los Angeles to the tune of 34-6. What is odd is that in two games against the Rams this year, kicker Ryland has scored every point. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS First quarter offense – Things sure did begin well. Two drives: two scores. But like what mostly this offense has done all year, the points ended up as two field goals instead of touchdowns. The first drive was eight plays highlighted by a 10-yard completion to TE Trey McBride followed by a 21-yard gain by WR Simi Fehoko. But a third-and-two at LA’s 24 became a sack instead and a three-point lead. On the Cardinals next possession, it was also unicorns and lollipops that began on their own 35 with a huge 31-yard gain by WR Devin Duvernay’s and short runs by RB Tyler Allgeier to the Rams’ 26. Then a false start, coupled with an incomplete pass made it fourth-and-10, and out trotted Chad Ryland as Arizona led 6-3 going into the second quarter. Unfortunately for the Cardinals, there were three more quarters to play. First career INT for @Cody_Simon30 🙂‍↕️ #LARvsAZ on @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/cnQKQoX5JE — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 15, 2026 LB Corey Simon – Holding a three-point lead, the Rams gave it up on their next possession. What a great play by Simon on the pick as Los Angeles had driven to the 24-yard line. The play was intended for WR Konata Mumpfield, but Simon made an acrobatic catch and the defense averted a costly score. He nailed TE Colby Parkinson after just a one-yard gain in the second quarter. Six total tackles. Kickers – When your kicker and punter are in the running for offensive MVP, you know the offense is a complete disaster. K Ryland nailed both field goals, each from 49 yards. P Blake Gillikin had a great game, booting three kicks for a 50.0 average per punt, with one downed inside the 20 with a long of 56 yards. One of the league’s best punters. And with that, we must give a big shout out to long snapper Casey Kreiter who consistently passes the ball exactly where the punter likes it, and a swift spiral right to the holder. S Andrew Wingard – The talented safety came off an injury and was everywhere. On a third-and-10 in the first quarter, Wingard stopped RB Blake Corum for a nine-yard gain as he broke free to the third level. On the 22-yard completion to WR C.J. Daniels late in the first quarter, Wingard left his man and raced all the way over to the opposite side to assist in the tackle. Led all defenders with 11 total tackles. LB Mack Wilson – Wilson was also an active tackler with so many runners coming to the second level. Had 10 tackles with one tackle for loss and one pass defense. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Offensive line – Well, did anyone in the Cardinals fanbase expect anything different than what happened along the offensive line? Pretty much jailbreak all game. Poor QB Carson Beck. The rookie never had a chance all game. Agent 0 on the move! 💪 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/K04597Uvcf — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 The Rams had five sacks, while the rushing attack had a grand total of 34 yards. Geez. Can’t run and no time to throw. Back in the origins of American Football, if the offense didn’t get anywhere, oftentimes they would punt on second or third down and try to work on field position. Our next poll: Should the Cardinals punt on third downs? WESLEY BAILEY RIPPED IT AWAY FOR HIS FIRST NFL INTERCEPTION 😤 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/upvqsq5djk — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 QB Carson Beck – The best thing to happen to the rookie in his maiden NFL start, was that at no time was the cart summoned. Beck was flushed from the pocket for most of the contest, and he had no run game to depend on. Which meant after a while, the defense no longer thought about runners and was all out for the pass. Miserable day, and a miserable game. The second pick wasn’t his fault. Went 11 for 18 for 108 yards, a 6.0 average per pass completion, zero TDs, two picks, sacked five times (which could have been double digits), and a QB rating of 38.4. Welcome to the NFL. Defense three quarters – The Rams were stymied in the first quarter being held to a field goal. Then the first drive in the second quarter was the Simon pick. But the wheels fell off from there. The Cardinals could not stop the run, and were burned repeatedly with accurate passing from QB Matthew Stafford who completed passes for 31 yards, 22, 18, 27, 10, 22 (TD), 44, 10, and 19 (TD). BRADEN BRINGIN' THE BOOM 💥 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/ebyDOeJVKB — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 Offense final three quarters – When it was apparent that the Cardinals could not run the ball, and the offensive line wasn’t going to keep their pass rushers out for long, the Rams began stacking the box with seven and eight defenders. Final numbers for this offense: 142 total yards, 6 first downs, 0 for 6 third down efficiency, 0 for 1 on fourth down, 3.6 yards per play average, 34 rushing yards, allowed five sacks, zero Red Zone appearances, two turnovers, 3.9 yards per pass completion average, and time of possession: 17:37. Yes, it was that bad. Can you imagine how tired the Arizona defense was today? Cardinals’ drives beginning with Quarter 2: punt, punt, INT, half, INT, downs, punt. CB Kalen King – On the Rams first possession, King allowed WR T Atwell to gain 31-yards to the Cardinals’ nine which eventually set up a field goal. King was way off Atwell and then missed the tackle before scoring the TD. In the second quarter on a second-and-10, King lost WR Xavier smith who rambled 22-yards to Arizona’s 46. FIRST NFL TOUCHDOWN FOR XAVIER SMITH!! 🙌 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/ZIhTbMxp7i — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 With 9:37 left before halftime, King played off Smith who gained 18-yards. After the Cardinals were intercepted, the Rams were back in business at Arizona’s 32. On their third play, King was way off Smith and then missed the tackle before scoring the TD with just 13 seconds left in the half. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – Is it wrong that only one company makes the game Monopoly? DT L.J. Collier – Had the sack in the second quarter, but the Rams ran up the gut too many times to count. Three tackles with one sack, one tackle for loss, and one QB hit. Cookin' in the Kinchens 👨‍🍳 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/D0hbu0qVOR — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 WR Devin Duvernay – He had the 31-yard gain in the first quarter, but with 37 seconds to play in the first half, Beck rolled out and found an open Duvernay who tipped the ball up instead of securing the rock, and Rams’ S Kamren Kinchens not only got the interception, but Los Angeles scored another touchdown with just ticks left in the first half. But yet Beck got the negative stat.

title: Falcons – Chiefs recap: Wilting away in Mercedes-Benz Stadium
summary: If you were daydreaming about an improbable run, simply hoping for a miracle, or just looking for something enjoyable as the season very slowly winds down, the Falcons were determined to ensure your Sunday left you bereft. The quality of the opponent aside—the Chiefs are very good, obviously—this was the bottom for the Falcons, and […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 15: Josh Downs #12 of the Kansas City Chiefs carries the ball after a reception defended by DeMarcco Hellams #23 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you were daydreaming about an improbable run, simply hoping for a miracle, or just looking for something enjoyable as the season very slowly winds down, the Falcons were determined to ensure your Sunday left you bereft. The quality of the opponent aside—the Chiefs are very good, obviously—this was the bottom for the Falcons, and the point at which team and fanbase alike need to fully accept certain hard truths about the Atlanta Falcons of 2026. Those truths? The first and most obvious one is that this is a bad football team at the moment. Despite some promising signings and trades, the talent level is not good enough across the board to make them a playoff-caliber team even in a weak NFC South, something the Falcons appeared to accept when they traded away Jessie Bates and Ryan Neuzil. Also, while this team has more resources than just any other team in the NFL, they are going to need every dollar and draft pick just to overhaul what they have in a way that brings their talent level up to where it needs to be and exorcises all the weird ghosts that have been awkwardly floating around this team for most of the last decade. And finally , there are very few positions on this roster that are actually settled with 2027 looming, meaning this team could look very, very different than it does now by May of next year. There is a Sunday every year in this miserable stretch of losing seasons where the terrible weight of losing lands especially heavy on my shoulders, and this is the one for 2026. More than likely, I’ll come out of the bye ready to joke about the Falcons reeling off some unlikely wins and finishing this year with a losing record for the ninth straight season, and we’ll all lock arms and head into a pivotal offseason daring to dream of something better. But I’ll tell you with naked honesty that this Sunday got to me in a way the previous nine games did not, as I saw the this team continue a frankly brutal three game slide and make it fully clear just how limited their ceiling for this season really is. At 3-7 and driving that stake into this team’s hopes with relish, the Falcons ensured I can fully give up on 2026 and just try to find the bright spots in what’s to come, and I do intend to take full advantage. I hope you will, as will. For now, though, we’ll be digesting a game where Patrick Mahomes threw for five touchdowns and the Chiefs ran all over Atlanta despite not having Kenneth Walker, and the defense was still the more impressive unit. Atlanta’s offense has now scored 17 or fewer points in three straight games, which begs the question of whether Tommy Rees is the right coordinator, Penix is the right quarterback, and almost every player on that side of the ball is going to be part of the next great Falcons offense outside of Bijan Robinson, Chris Lindstrom, and Drake London. That seems like an overreaction to one game—and perhaps even three games—but this is an evaluation year for a regime with the resources to make substantial changes in 2027, and an offense studded with talented players looking this crummy will give them genuine pause. The Chiefs are a good, well-coached team, but the gulf between them and a frankly hapless Falcons team should give them further pause. The bye week will give these Falcons a chance to reset and try to make something of the rest of this year, but the fate of this team seems beyond obvious at this point. As we have so many times over the past decade, we Falcons fans are left to look ahead to better days after the last bloom has fallen off the rose. May this coming offseason finally bring those long-elusive days to us, so that we may put games like in the past where they belong. On to the full recap. The Good He hasn’t looked superhuman very often lately, but Bijan Robinson remains a player defenses fear and a back capable of breaking some jaw-dropping runs. His best carries in this game were like that, where through sheer will, balance, and power he managed to reel off 10-plus yards despite the at-times nonexistent threat of the Falcons passing game working against him. Someday the offense will sputter to life again and he’ll look like the Bijan of old. Jahan Dotson would ideally be your third receiver, but even with his ups and downs he’s been a very credible receiving threat for this team, and has had some really good weeks. He was a better pass away from a touchdown today and finished second on the team with three receptions for 63 yards, and is on his way to a career year in an offense that can and wants to get him the ball. Drake London deserves a medal of some kind. His career has been defined by a revolving door of play callers, quarterbacks, and surrounding personnel, and yet he continually blocks his ass off and shows out as the team’s best receiver. He somehow had over 100 yards in this one despite the passing game being dormant much of the day, and London deserves better than the results this team sees in the win and loss columns weekly. Harold Perkins had a couple of ugly reps on the first defensive drive, and that must have galvanized him because he was a man possessed after that point. Perkins was fantastic against the run, a demon as a pass rusher, and more stingy in coverage after that point, standing out over and over again no matter what he was asked to do. There’s little question Perkins is a player the Falcons plan to count on in 2027 and beyond, and he showed why on Sunday. Brandon Dorlus and Gervon Dexter remain one of the best duos on the interior in the NFL, and Dexter in particular was a man possessed with five pressures, three run stops, and multiple plays where he rampaged through the overmatched Chiefs offensive line like Godzilla through the financial district. If the Falcons can bring more consistent pressure off the edge to help out D&D, quarterbacks will be miserable. The defense did the heavy lifting on Sunday against a good Chiefs team minus key pieces, and reminded us they’re the unit that is much closer to being a finished product, even if the overall results were still rough. It’s not that difficult to talk yourself into Billy Bowman Jr., Xavier Watts, Kendal Daniels, Perkins, Dorlus, Dexter, and company just getting better a year from now with better complementary pieces around them. Jake Moody came uncomfortably close to missing an extra point, but otherwise he was excellent. Moody hit both short field goal tries and had the NFL’s first successful onside kick attempt, with a major assist from Chris Blair, in his Falcons debut. Hopefully he can prove to be the team’s long-term solution at kicker, and the early returns were promising, even if the kicks weren’t particularly challenging. Blair, as mentioned above, had a phenomenal play. He wasn’t quite there on a potential touchdown pass from Penix, but the onsides kick recovery was flawless, as Blair very confidently grabbed it away from a sleepwalking Xavier Worthy and kept his feet inbounds to give Atlanta a last gasp chance they couldn’t take full advantage of. The Ugly Yes, the offense has holes and weaknesses that need to be addressed in the offseason, but it’s not so bereft of talent that it should look like it did on the first four drives. The Falcons started this game with one productive Bijan Robinson carry, one eight yard catch for Kyle Pitts, and a whole lot of incompletions, penalties, and ineptitude that led to four straight three-and-outs. That represented all four drives in the first quarter, and was evidence enough that this team selling at the deadline was an accurate read of their potential. It was, as the broadcast noted, the first time since 2000 that the Falcons started the game with four…

title: Ravens discussion: is Baltimore’s season over? If so, what’s next?
summary: The Ravens’ season isn’t technically over – far from it. There are seven (potentially painful) games to go. But after Monday night’s loss to the Chargers, it certainly feels like 2026 is all but wrapped. Darkness fell in Baltimore, and the prospects of this team winning at least two of their next three games to keep […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Head coach Jesse Minter of the Baltimore Ravens reacts against the Los Angeles Chargers during the fourth quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens’ season isn’t technically over – far from it. There are seven (potentially painful) games to go. But after Monday night’s loss to the Chargers, it certainly feels like 2026 is all but wrapped. Darkness fell in Baltimore, and the prospects of this team winning at least two of their next three games to keep their playoff hopes alive are dim at best. A heroic return from Lamar Jackson may not even matter, even if he comes back on the earliest end of his recovery timeline. Nikhil’s take: Whether or not the Ravens can miraculously qualify for the postseason is almost a moot point. Right now, it is virtually impossible to see this team storming through the AFC to meet their initial expectations for the season. There is still plenty of work to be done – namely, development for young players and coaches – but Baltimore has not earned the benefit of the doubt to believe they can make any kind of noise. Some fans will rightfully start looking ahead to the 2027 draft with dreams of a franchise left tackle or a blue-chip pass rusher. Others will break down every tiebreaker scenario and weigh the Ravens’ playoff chances with every AFC team’s wins and losses. And some (read: me) will pull out their calculators and start crunching the cap in preparation for what could (and should) be a major offseason roster churn. Let’s ignore the elephant in the room and assume the Ravens can finalize an extension with Lamar Jackson. That still leaves a tight cap situation without much flexibility unless significant cuts are made. Of course, that will only up more holes in a roster that is starting to resemble Swiss cheese. Baltimore’s front office should start doing this math now. They will have to walk a narrow path to shed dead weight and upgrade the roster enough to take this team where they belong: championship contention.
