title: 5 Bears Takes: Grading The First Half and Dissecting The NFC North
summary: Following a fast and furious nine games, the Chicago Bears enjoyed their bye over the weekend. In the process, they watched two divisional foes beat each other up and got a live look at their Week 11 opponent as the Panthers beat them at home. The playoff picture continues to take shape, and the Bears […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Rome Odunze #15 celebrates with Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears after scoring a touchdown during the first quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following a fast and furious nine games, the Chicago Bears enjoyed their bye over the weekend. In the process, they watched two divisional foes beat each other up and got a live look at their Week 11 opponent as the Panthers beat them at home. The playoff picture continues to take shape, and the Bears will start practice early next week as they gear up for a second-half run. We’ll cover all of that, and more in a special installment of 5 Bears Takes. 1. Grading out the offense over the first nine games of the season. Before the season, head coach Ben Johnson spoke about wanting to set the NFL’s scoring record. While some took those words and ran with them, the Bears were well on pace after a Week 1 that produced 59 points on the road. Since that point, the offense has yet to break the 40-point mark again, but they’ve eclipsed the 30-point mark four separate times. All of which were with starting quarterback Caleb Williams under center. Through nine games, the offense ranks within the Top 5 in yards per game (383), Top 10 in points per game (26.8), 11th in EPA/play, and 10th in success rate. In total, their numbers are right around where they sat for the majority of last season, with one major caveat: They missed their starting quarterback for a third of the season (so far). They’ve also faced four of the Top 10 defenses in the league through that stretch. Overall, there’s still plenty of meat left on the bone when looking at this unit’s production and what it could (or should) be. With better health at the quarterback position and no clunkers in the second half of the season, the Bears have a real opportunity to finish as a Top 5 offense. Part of that will depend on health at key positions like running back and receiver, but the offensive line will play a key part, too. We’ve seen multiple flashes of dominance, but there’s still plenty to clean up, especially when it comes to penalties and self-inflicted mistakes. With a better-than-expected defense, they’ve been able to control most games, but for them to take the next step and be scarier down the stretch, the offense must be more consistent. Grades: Quarterback: A Running Backs: C+ Wide Receivers: B Tight Ends: C- Offensive Line: B+ 2. Grading out the defense over the first nine games of the season. Coming into the season, the defense felt like the Achilles’ heel of what could be a Super Bowl contender. During the offseason, the front office did very little to improve the defensive line, and through the first month and a half of the season, it seemed clear the interior defensive line wouldn’t be good enough. Despite what their depth chart has looked like on paper, they’ve performed better than expected, even before the acquisition of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Through nine games, the defense ranks 1st in third-down percentage (22.8%), Top 5 in fourth-down percentage (30.8%), Top 10 in EPA/play, yards per game, and sacks, and gives up just 20.4 points per game. It’s also worth mentioning that they were 9th in pressure percentage coming into Week 10. With Simmons in the mix on the interior, the biggest hole this group has is at cornerback. The hope is that with a healthy Malik Muhammad, either Jaylon Johnson or Tyrique Stevenson can step into the spot opposite the rookie and provide consistency and stability. With any luck, they’ll get Coby Bryant back at some point in December. It’s worth pointing out how well Cam Lewis has played since taking over the starting spot opposite first-round rookie Dillon Thieneman. With the divisional defenses starting to shake out, this group must continue its upward trajectory. Getting back Dayo Odeyingbo should help the defensive line, but Austin Booker, Montez Sweat, and even Grady Jarrett have been noticeably better since the arrival of Simmons. Many expected the Bears to make another move or two before the deadline, but with nothing materializing, they’re stuck with what they have. Similar to the offense, health will be key down the stretch, but overall, the team should feel pretty good about where they stand. The only real concern heading into the second half is how well their cornerbacks can perform against top offenses. Grades: Defensive Line: A- Linebacker: B Cornerback: D- Safety: B- 3. Dissecting the NFC North after another hectic week that saw the Bears drop from first to third place. With the Bears’ bye week, they were the only team in the division that was not in play on Sunday. The Detroit Lions took their crack at the piñata that has become the New England Patriots in the early-morning slot, and outside of the opening drive, it wasn’t much of a game. The Patriots lost quarterback Drake Maye early, and, to put it nicely, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was ineffective. For as impressive as the Lions were, they lost another star defender when Aidan Hutchinson went down with what appeared to be a serious knee injury following a sack of Maye on the first drive. The play (and subsequent celebration) took two of the most impactful players out of the game before it could really even get going. Although the Lions have been playing much better defense as of late, losing their top two leaders, Jack Campbell and Hutchinson, will wear on them as the season goes on. During the next time slot, the Packers hosted the Kirk Cousins-led Vikings. What looked like a good matchup on paper turned into a season sweep for Minnesota, following a 30-10 drubbing. The Vikings’ defense continues to be one of the best overall units in the league, and with Cousins under center, the offense looked more cohesive, even if it wasn’t a perfectly played game. Cousins has plenty of familiarity with the offense, so it’s fair to assume that he’ll continue to hit the ground running. For the Packers, it’s hard to know whether Sunday’s 20-point loss was simply a bad day at the office, or a sign of things to come. Green Bay has shown clear holes all season, and although they’ve looked considerably better over the last month, there are still ways to attack them. All in all, the division once again had another winning week. With the Lions and Vikings both winning, there’s a three-way tie at the top with all three teams sitting at 7-2. The Packers will go on an abbreviated bye week before going to Los Angeles to face a red-hot Rams team on Thanksgiving Eve. Ultimately, their bye week will amount to the same number of days off as it would if they played on Thursday night and then played a Monday night game the following week. It’s clear that all four teams are playoff-caliber, but it remains to be seen if all four can make the playoffs come January. With Sunday’s results, the Packers have now fallen a game and a half behind everyone else, while sporting a 1-3 record within the division. Even more troubling is that their 4-4 conference record won’t help them much in tie-breakers once more games are played. Heading into Week 11, all four teams fill out the seven teams that would comprise the NFC playoff picture, but with plenty of head-to-heads remaining (both in the division and the conference), this is still a long way from a resolution. Heading into Week 11, here’s how the divisional standings look: Detroit Lions (7-2) Minnesota Vikings (7-2) Chicago Bears (7-2) Green Bay Packers (6-4) Here’s how the tie-breakers come out: Lions win the head-to-head tie-breaker against the Vikings and have a better divisional record than the Bears. Vikings win the head-to-head tie-breaker against the Bears. After Week 11, each team will have seven games remaining. Both the Bears and Lions have favorable matchups, while the Vikings will play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday Night Football. Barring a surprise,…

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ uplifting win over the Steelers
summary: It’s good to sometimes take a step back and appreciate how far the Cincinnati Bengals have come since drafting Joe Burrow. The lead-up to primetime games used to be filled with anxiety. Bengals fans knew the likelihood of getting embarrassed was high, But now, primetime is where the Bengals shine. And last night’s game might […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Ja'marr Chase #1 of the Cincinnati Bengals catches a pass against Asante Samuel Jr. #22 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the second quarter at Paycor Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s good to sometimes take a step back and appreciate how far the Cincinnati Bengals have come since drafting Joe Burrow. The lead-up to primetime games used to be filled with anxiety. Bengals fans knew the likelihood of getting embarrassed was high, But now, primetime is where the Bengals shine. And last night’s game might be the best example. Cincinnati went head-to-head with their heated rivals, who were tied with them for the division lead. And they absolutely destroyed them. Here are three things we learned from the clinic Burrow and the Bengals put on against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The pass blocking isn’t just serviceable; it’s great Amarius Mims dominated T.J. Watt, making him look like a child. Amarius Mims vs. T.J. Watt tonight 👀 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WYtWQuZ29j — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 And Orlando Brown Jr., considered to be the weak link at the start of the season, just delivered the best pass protection game of any left tackle this year , not allowing a pressure on 44 dropbacks. Burrow had clean pockets almost the entire game, similar to the game against the Atlanta Falcons. And, as a result, he methodically picked those defenses apart. There’s no more playing scared on offense In the past, the Bengals would fall behind early, trying to force a run game that wasn’t there. Against the Steelers, they used the short game to get the pass in a flow, and sprinkled in deep shots down the field. Burrow and the offense came out firing, confident in their ability to have their way with any defense, even one as intimidating as Pittsburgh’s. Ja’Marr Chase is in the zone He’s probably been the best receiver in the league for a couple of seasons, but he’s somehow reached another level. After a slow start, Chase has 527 yards receiving in his last three games. He had probably the most casual 200 yard receiving game you’ll ever see against the Steelers. And his 231 total was the highest for any receiver this season. The combination of Burrow having time, the offense finding its identity, and Tee Higgins emerging as the most physically dominant receiver in the league have led to Chase being able to break out his entire bag on a regular basis.

title: Ja’Marr Chase has spectacular showing in Bengals’ big win vs. Steelers
summary: Ja’Marr Chase said he loves primetime games. On Sunday night, he showed everyone why. Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals‘ 38-18 win over Pittsburgh at Paycor. It was the fourth 200-yard game of his career and the third-best yardage total he’s ever had, and it came against a Steelers team […]
full_text: Ja’Marr Chase said he loves primetime games. On Sunday night, he showed everyone why. Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals ‘ 38-18 win over Pittsburgh at Paycor. It was the fourth 200-yard game of his career and the third-best yardage total he’s ever had, and it came against a Steelers team that walked in tied for first in the AFC North and walked out a game behind. Chase didn’t find the end zone, and it didn’t matter. He was the engine of the drives that buried Pittsburgh early. His two deep shots, a 53-yarder and a 43-yarder, each set up Bengals touchdowns. The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions and took a 24-3 lead into the locker room, while the Steelers managed just 40 total yards and four first downs before halftime. The only thing that stopped Chase was the scoreboard. With the game in hand, the Bengals eased off in the fourth quarter and brought in Joe Flacco for mop-up duty. Sunday was Chase’s fourth regular-season game with at least 200 receiving yards. The headline record of the night belonged to his quarterback. Burrow threw four touchdown passes, giving him five straight games with at least four total touchdowns, which ties Peyton Manning’s 2004 run for the longest such streak in NFL history. The Bengals also completed 21 passes before Aaron Rodgers completed his first, tying the most by one team before its opponent’s first completion since 1978. None of that happens without No. 1 stretching the defense. When Chase is getting behind safeties like he did Sunday night, everything underneath opens up for Chase Brown, Drew Sample, and Dohnte Meyers, which is exactly how all four touchdown passes were scored. The Bengals are 7-2 and alone in first place in the AFC North. And their best player just reminded everyone that the bigger the stage, the better he gets. Bengals Reacts In our most recent Bengals Reacts survey, 84% of fans voted that the Bengals will win the AFC North. After Sunday’s thrashing of the Steelers, I’d say that confidence level just took another nice bump. This survey was brought to you by FanDuel Sportsbook .

title: Bengals News: Statement win vs. Steelers
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals absolutely whooped the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. It ended up 38-18 thanks to some late scores for Pittsburgh. After the Bengals made it 31-3 early in the third quarter, the game was essentially done. It has to be one of the best performances the Bengals have had when both teams […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals absolutely whooped the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. It ended up 38-18 thanks to some late scores for Pittsburgh. After the Bengals made it 31-3 early in the third quarter, the game was essentially done. It has to be one of the best performances the Bengals have had when both teams still have something to play for in the season. Being 7-2 now, the Bengals are tied with three other teams also at 7-2 (Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Jacksonville Jaguars), trailing only behind the Buffalo Bills. These past few weeks, people have pointed out Cincinnati’s closer games with struggling teams and that all of their wins had come against teams below .500. That ended tonight as they dominated offensively and defensively against Pittsburgh. The rest of the Bengals schedule is fairly easy as well. The only teams with a winning record, currently, are the Chiefs and Browns twice. So they do not have many more chances to show what their ceiling is, but the Steelers sure got a taste tonight. Bengals news Bengals Beat Steelers 38-18 | POSTGAME RECAP, NOTES & QUOTES Burrow sets the tone by talking about how they aren’t satisfied at 7-2. This team should have more on their minds after this win, but you could end up finding yourself growing complacent looking past the opponents on your schedule. Joe Burrow throws 4 TDs as Bengals rout Steelers to top AFC North Over the past five games, Burrow has thrown for over 1,600 passing yards, 22 total touchdowns, and only three interceptions. People will have to come to terms with the fact that, even though he has Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, he is absolutely the leader for the MVP award. Back from Madrid, Bengals face Steelers team that is back from a bye The Bengals also had this performance with arguably one of the biggest disadvantages a team can have in the NFL. Teams are now 1-5 coming back to the States after playing internationally against a team coming off a bye week. Even with the deck stacked against Cincinnati, they dominated from the first snap. NFL News Patriots QB Drake Maye suffers ankle injury early in loss to Lions This has a pretty big impact on the AFC playoff race. Not only does it seem to take a team out of the race, which may make it easier for the Cleveland Browns to sneak in, but it also makes the AFC East even more of a cakewalk as the Bills face them in a couple of weeks, and they also play the Chiefs and Broncos down the road. Kirk Cousins emotional after win over Packers in Vikings return: ‘There’s more to this story’ This has to be one of the best stories of the week. Cousins wins in his return while also exorcising some demons after it being on the field he suffered a terrible injury. It will be interesting to see how high the Minnesota Vikings can go. NFL Network: Lions’ Aidan Hutchinson feared to have suffered significant knee injury on sack celebration There are plenty of people with hindsight talking about how players shouldn’t jump when celebrating. Well, these guys jump just a ridiculous amount. It is ridiculous to look back on this and see it as anything more than unfortunate for one of the best pass rushers in the NFL. Now, whether you are upset with him about the hip tackle on Maye right before that injured him is your prerogative.

full_text: Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season concludes on Monday Night Football, but Cleveland Browns fans get two weeks to relax and enjoy their team’s 6-4 start to the season and holding a current spot in the AFC Playoff picture. The bye week comes at a perfect time, according to HC Todd Monken, as the coaching staff will get a better chance to self-scout for the closing schedule. Perhaps that will help Cleveland start faster after the same concern has popped up week after week , including in their Week 10 victory over the Houston Texans . Either way, the time off will be good for the players’ bodies, while the coaches rework the plan. As of now, the Browns do not play again until November 29th at 1 PM against the Las Vegas Raiders. “As of now” is important, as the NFL can flex that game to Sunday Night Football instead of the early slot . That decision will have to be made by Tuesday. After facing the Raiders, with rookie QB Fernando Mendoza , Cleveland then welcomes the Cincinnati Bengals, the current AFC North leaders, and the Atlanta Falcons, led by their former head coach Kevin Stefanski, to finish off their four-game homestand. That leaves a finishing stretch with three out of four on the road: at the New York Giants, at the Baltimore Ravens, at home with the Indianapolis Colts, and finishing on the road against the Bengals again. Seven games, four at home and three on the road, starting with six wins on the record books coming out of the bye week. Some juicy storylines are included in that schedule as well. If the Browns can win two of the next three, Cleveland fans will start the 12 Days of Christmas with a clear sight of the NFL playoffs, and that is all we can ask for. title: Browns proving that TD passes may be overrated
summary: The Cleveland Browns continued to befuddle the NFL on Sunday with their latest comeback victory. After falling behind 17-0 to the Houston Texans, the Browns did what they seem to do almost every week: the defense put a chokehold on the Texans, the offense slowly found its footing, and when Quinshon Judkins crossed the goal […]
full_text: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns continued to befuddle the NFL on Sunday with their latest comeback victory. After falling behind 17-0 to the Houston Texans, the Browns did what they seem to do almost every week: the defense put a chokehold on the Texans, the offense slowly found its footing, and when Quinshon Judkins crossed the goal line with 53 seconds remaining, the Browns had their sixth victory of the season. No one can really explain how the Browns are doing it, not even the coaches or the players themselves, but they’re doing it because Cleveland has followed the same basic script in each of their six victories. Chief among the reasons that the Browns find themselves in a hole each week, but also one of the key reasons they have been able to overcome those deficits, has been the play of quarterback Deshaun Watson, who has generally been poor to bad for the first three quarters of each game, only to come alive in the fourth quarter. Deshaun Watson in final 2 minutes of 4th quarters this season 19 completions (t-most in NFL) 273 Pass Yards (most in NFL) 2 Pass TD (t-most in NFL) 0 INT (t-best in NFL) 141.8 Pass Rating (best in NFL) pic.twitter.com/DnYLKGMprV — PFF (@PFF) November 15, 2026 Watson has been especially effective in the final two minutes of games, as Pro Football Focus highlighted after Sunday’s win, as Watson is: Tied for the most completions (19) First in passing yards (273) Tied for the most touchdown passes (2) First in interceptions (0) First in passer rating (141.8) Tied for the most touchdown passes (2) That last bullet point is an interesting one, given a narrative that has emerged surrounding Watson, as his detractors are eager to point out that he has not thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5 against the New York Jets. But you know who did throw touchdown passes on Sunday? Cam Ward had two for the Tennessee Titans and lost Tyler Shough had one for the New Orleans Saints and lost Dak Prescott had five for the Dallas Cowboys and lost Aaron Rodgers had two for the Pittsburgh Steelers, and oh boy did they lose. Touchdown passes are fun and can make for great highlights, and there is no doubt Watson would love to have back that errant pass to Jerry Jeudy on Sunday that would have been a walk-in touchdown. But they are just one part of the bigger goal: outscore your opponent by any means necessary. Think back to the three touchdowns the Browns scored on Sunday: Watson had a six-yard run after hitting Jeudy on a 65-yard pass KC Concepcion had a six-yard run to finish a drive that included an 18-yard pass to Malachi Corley Judkins scored the game-winner on a five-yard run to finish a drive that featured a 30-yard completion to Harold Fannin Jr. Would it have made any difference if any of those scores had come on a pass instead of a run? Unless the NFL changes its rules overnight, a touchdown still counts as six points no matter how it is scored. Think back to all those times over the years when the Browns have been in a first-and-goal situation only to bumble their way into a turnover or settle for a field goal instead of a touchdown. The type of drive that goes something like a run on first down for minus-2 yards, a sack on second down, then an incompletion on third down that deflates a once-promising drive. At some point, Watson will throw another touchdown and another nonsensical narrative will die from a lack of oxygen. As long as the Browns finish more of their drives with touchdowns than field goals, does it really matter if they do it via the run or the pass? Bring the Dawg Pound with you on the SB Nation app! title: Browns Week 10 review: Grit, overcoming, big plays, and playoffs? Playoffs!
summary: If you were to ask anyone to describe the 2026 Cleveland Browns, a lot of words will come to mind. Confusing. Frustrating. Resilient. Gritty. Heart. After falling into a 17-point deficit in the 2nd quarter against the Houston Texans, the Browns followed it up with 20 unanswered points in Week 10. It ended up being […]
full_text: If you were to ask anyone to describe the 2026 Cleveland Browns, a lot of words will come to mind. Confusing. Frustrating. Resilient. Gritty. Heart. After falling into a 17-point deficit in the 2nd quarter against the Houston Texans, the Browns followed it up with 20 unanswered points in Week 10. It ended up being enough as Cleveland improved to 6-4 heading into their bye week with some momentum and bigger picture questions. Now, on to our 4-Downs review from the Browns’ Week 10 win over the Texans : 1st Down: Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face When the Houston Texans jumped out to a 10-point lead, it was looking pretty dark. Defensively, the Browns couldn’t get a stop as Texans QB CJ Stroud was doing whatever he wanted in the passing game. Offensively, Cleveland couldn’t sustain drives or get any form of rhythm going. It appeared that Houston was going to turn this game into a rout. It wasn’t until this play specifically that things started to change: a HUGE catch to set up the score 👏 #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/KUwh2NXJBx — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 Quarterback Deshaun Watson later scored on that drive, and then the Browns forced a turnover a couple of plays later: Tyson with the hands to take it back! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/rkBxeAhLME — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 15, 2026 After that, the entire complexity of the game changed. In the 2nd half, Cleveland outcoached and outplayed the Texans. After getting punched in the mouth early in the game, the Browns responded with a punch of their own. 2nd Down: QB Change talk is over and done with After Cleveland’s loss against the New Orleans Saints in Week 9, in which quarterback Shedeur Sanders started over quarterback Deshaun Watson, who missed the game while recovering from a concussion, there was a lot of quarterback conversation. Sanders played well, but the topic of discussion was whether Watson’s leash was short after how Sanders played. After Watson’s performance on Sunday, any talk of a QB change should be over. Watson’s 1st half was rough, but he responded with a solid 2nd half. It’s a night-and-day difference between how Watson looks now in 2026 and how he looked in 2024. He looks more confident, mentally tough, and has an unwavering belief in himself. Confidence is key when playing the quarterback position, and if you don’t have it, it will be a short stint for you in the NFL. It’s clear that the Browns offense runs more efficiently and effectively with Watson under center, and Monken trusts Watson more than Sanders. Watson hasn’t been perfect, but he has provided competent quarterback play. 3rd down: Cornerbacks have a huge day, defense shines Overall, the Browns defense had a solid day overall, but Cleveland’s secondary (mainly their cornerbacks) were the star of the show. Cornerback Denzel Ward is one of the most underrated corners in our league. The Texans’ wide receivers were finding success early and often with the route combinations, but Cleveland eventually found a way to slow them down. The Browns are going to live and die by playing man coverage on the back end, but the corners are sticky in coverage, so it doesn’t matter as much as it should. Cornerback Tyson Campbell also had a solid day and, overall, the secondary stood out once adjustments were made. Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg’s adjustments once again stood out. It feels as if Cleveland’s defense was trying to figure out what Houston’s offense was going to do, and it led to a ton of hesitation and overthinking early. At their best, this defense is best at attacking and causing chaos. It worked as Stroud looked uncomfortable in the 2nd half. Credit to the defense for a solid performance, especially the cornerbacks. 4th Down: Postseason seems like a possibility If the season ended today, the Cleveland Browns would have the last playoff spot in the AFC. Yes, you read that right. For a team that many people thought would be picking towards the top in next year’s draft, the Browns have completely changed that. Remember when owner Jimmy Haslam said this before the season started: #Browns owner Jimmy Haslam on what success looks like this season: “I think the odds are for us to win 5.5 games. I’ll take the over.” pic.twitter.com/7z98HSKaaS — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) July 31, 2026 Haslam knew something we didn’t. With 7 games remaining and the second-youngest team the NFL, the Browns have already exceeded their win total from last season. Cleveland is the AFC’s seventh seed and in control of its destiny when it returns from the bye. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) November 15, 2026 The Browns have exceeded expectations, and it should be commended. Yes, Cleveland is 6-4 with a negative point differential, but who cares? Honestly? Winning in the NFL is hard, and the Browns are finding ways to win every week. The scary part about this team is they haven’t played their best football yet. Granted, no one is saying this team is a Super Bowl contender, but if they continue to get better, this team can find a way to get into the postseason and maybe make a little noise. Extra Points Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans getting fired after this season is a strong possibility. The Texans have been a massive disappointment, and today might have been the nail in their coffin in terms of their playoff hopes. The Browns offensive line had one of their best outings of the season. Cleveland only had 2 penalties for 47 yards. Impressive. Don’t want to hear about the officiating on the late-game call when the Browns have been on the wrong end of it more times than not, including the DPI on Emmanuel McNeil-Warren wasn’t a DPI 6-4 heading into the bye week sounds pretty good to me. title: Cowboys news: Dallas can’t even take a moral victory from 49ers game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are staring directly in the face of another lost season where a talented roster will underachieve. The biggest culprit at this point is the defense giving up far too many explosive plays that lead to points, allowing 46 to the 49ers on Sunday to waste a 40 point output from their own […]
full_text: Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are staring directly in the face of another lost season where a talented roster will underachieve. The biggest culprit at this point is the defense giving up far too many explosive plays that lead to points, allowing 46 to the 49ers on Sunday to waste a 40 point output from their own offense. The front office and veteran leadership still believes the big goals of this season can be achieved, and technically the Giants also losing in week ten leaves that door open. The Cowboys will have to repeat something they did under Brian Schottenheimer last season to keep it this way, winning two games in five days on Thanksgiving week. Eatman: This one makes other losses even worse – Nick Eatman, DallasCowboys.com Coming so close to beating a one-loss team this late in the season should normally be some kind of positive feeling, but not for the Cowboys this season. But the Cowboys can’t do that because they lost to the Ravens in a game they were knocking on the door to win inside the 5-yard line, but still lost. And they lost to the Buccaneers with a backup quarterback here at home in a game in which they let Bucky Irving turn into Barry Sanders. And they lost to the Cardinals despite having a 14-point lead here at home, but let a backup quarterback slice them up in the final minutes and win the game in overtime. That’s why you can’t sit here and take away any positives from a game in which you actually scored 40 points on a good defense. The Cowboys Stars are Making Schottenheimer Look Better than He Is – Cody Warren, Inside The Star The Cowboys have been putting up empty stats and charting moral victories for years, and still aren’t done doing so in 2026. I don’t see enough motion and too little play-action for a team with this many guys worth faking the ball to. On the other hand, Shanahan gave Dallas a pretty good demonstration with Kaelon Black. Once Black scored from 25 yards out, every Cowboy who had to stop the run had a reason to pay attention to him. Shanahan used that on the next possession to send Deebo Samuel back the other way on a 70-yard reverse . Even Brock Purdy was out there blocking. I could see what the coach did for Deebo before Deebo had to beat anybody. 6 plays that cost the Cowboys vs. 49ers – LP Cruz, Blogging The Boys Christian Parker’s defense gave up so many long touchdowns to the 49ers that Kaelon Black’s touchdown to open the second half floodgates is being forgotten about. Down by a one point, letting the 49ers score a touchdown would be detrimental. Unfortunately, Dallas could not prevent that from happening and rookie running back Kaelon Black ran all over the defense to make a point. The play puts another red-hot spotlight on Caleb Downs. The rookie safety was run over by Black on a touchdown that helped San Francisco seize control of the second half. Downs also had trouble finishing plays in space, including a missed opportunity to contain Purdy before the quarterback found McCaffrey for a long touchdown. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Overshown benched? Porter’s high snap count notable in Cowboys’ W10 loss – Todd Brock, The Cowboys Wire The Cowboys seemingly disciplined linebacker Demarvion Overshown after his unsportsmanlike conduct penalty while inactive last week. Like, why did DeMarvion Overshown get only five defensive snaps? He was inactive the week prior versus the Colts with a hamstring issue (though that didn’t stop him from sprinting onto the field in street clothes and earning a penalty), but he practiced in full to close out the week. He had logged 65% or more of the defense’s snaps in every other appearance this season, so his sudden drop to 8% in such a critical game- where the opponent absolutely tore up the middle of the field- needs to be explained. Was it just punishment for the week prior? Or is there more to the story? Von Miller takes a wild stance on both Cowboys loss and controversial playcall that ended things versus the 49ers – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports Overshown may not have made a difference for the Cowboys defense, but the 49ers certainly took maximum advantage of the mismatches on the second and third levels. According to Miller, he’s the man for the job when it comes to covering McCaffrey. “I think I’m the one that’s best suited for that situation when it comes to coverage,” Miller said. “If it’s an alternate reality, alternate universe, I’m in that position every single time.I could have played that, that play better. That’s not on (Parker). It’s a cop-out to say, hey, you know, I’m a pass rusher, or I could do that. I cover well. I have a great understanding of coverage and how to cover guys like that. You know, I wish I had that play back.”

title: AT&T Stadium has become a house of horrors for Cowboys
summary: It was hardly the most decorated time in Dallas Cowboys franchise history. Nobody is saying that a banner was deserved. But tell me you would not immediately trade the current version of the Dallas Cowboys for what we saw from 2021-2023. That group played stable football over a 1,000-day period, and while they fell short […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was hardly the most decorated time in Dallas Cowboys franchise history. Nobody is saying that a banner was deserved. But tell me you would not immediately trade the current version of the Dallas Cowboys for what we saw from 2021-2023. That group played stable football over a 1,000-day period, and while they fell short of the ultimate goal after each season, “stable football” is so far away from what the current group is offering on a weekly basis. What’s more is that group took care of business in their house, something the current group doesn’t do either. AT&T Stadium has become a house of horrors This was true before a snap had been taken. Well before kickoff it was obvious that the Cowboys had absolutely no home field advantage to speak of on Sunday as 49ers fans had full well taken over AT&T Stadium. The San Francisco 49ers fans who traveled to AT&T Stadium today are making it a question of whether or not this is a #DallasCowboys home game. Loud cheers for the 49ers during pregame introductions and loud boos for the Cowboys during pregame introductions. pic.twitter.com/iYtJ9ltH7y — Garrett Podell (@garrettpodell) November 15, 2026 Make of this what you will. Some will offer that it is a result of ticket prices being so high. Others will claim that the 49ers have a massive fanbase, like the Cowboys, and that it travels well. The reality is that this is all likely the result of a combination of things, and one of them is that Dallas has hardly been stellar when playing football in the building as of late. Consider that during the three-year span we started this conversation with the Cowboys played 25 games at home. They went 21-4 in them and notably, infamously, were undefeated there through the 2023 regular season before the Green Bay Packers broke the franchise in a way they are still not recovered from. This discussion is sort of an actual measurement of that point, one that many people claim. Dallas has played, from 2024 to present, 22 games in the same building. They are a moribund 7-14-1 in them. It is important to note that AT&T Stadium was hardly ever a football fortress. It was never Seattle, Kansas City, or even other notable NFL home environments like Green Bay, Buffalo, or Philadelphia. Again this is likely the result of several factors, but the point here is that at the very least the home team made sure that people got what they paid for way more often than not. Like with everything involving the Cowboys since 2024, that has withered away. All that is left to show for the work that the franchise did from 2021-2023 (again not saying it was serious work, but just in a relative-to-context way) are the uniforms and logos. Nothing about who this team is right now is recognizable even compared to a part of franchise history where nothing serious was achieved. This team pales in comparison to those from ‘21-’23 and that group is among the least accomplished in franchise history at large! The current group is simply so moribund that even that is way out in the distance. You aren’t imagining things when you feel like the Cowboys have become a more difficult proposition. This is true in more ways than we can even count. Lately it has borne itself out in the building they call home, though. And now they have two more games in the building through Thanksgiving Day. Joy.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys have no edge to beat 49ers, out-coached and outplayed again
summary: Another year, another uncompetitive Dallas Cowboys defense that doesn’t leave much left to play for in a losing season by mid-November. The box score will say the Cowboys lost by just six points to the San Francisco 49ers, but the full 60 minutes of football proved the now 8-1 49ers and now 4-6 Cowboys are […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images Another year, another uncompetitive Dallas Cowboys defense that doesn’t leave much left to play for in a losing season by mid-November. The box score will say the Cowboys lost by just six points to the San Francisco 49ers, but the full 60 minutes of football proved the now 8-1 49ers and now 4-6 Cowboys are simply in different competitive tiers for a wide facet of reasons. Also for the second year in a row, the Cowboys scored exactly 40 points in a home game and did not win – giving up the most yardage they’ve ever allowed in a home game along the way to lose 46-40. In this spot against their other archnemesis the Green Bay Packers last year, the Cowboys managed a tie. That game still serves as the only non-loss on head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s record against NFC teams that aren’t the New York Giants, Washington Commanders, or Philadelphia Eagles in the NFC East, as this most recent week ten loss makes it 0-9-1 in such games. The Cowboys run defense gave up 214 rushing yards, allowing at 7.4 yards a carry. Also for the third week in a row, the Cowboys faced exactly 16 third-down attempts on offense, a number that is too high. Dallas was lucky enough to win the penalty differential 11-5, with the 49ers having 65 more penalty yards against them, but it ultimately did not matter. It will be a busy week for the Cowboys as they turn the page from this game, preparing for two winnable games next week on Sunday and Thanksgiving Thursday. Let’s get to some notes on how they fell short against the 49ers, which makes both games next week feel damper, as the team will be fighting to be .500 at best. Dictating Matchups It will be a wash, rinse, and repeat week for Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys coaching staff as they had their fingerprints all over yet another loss, and the criticism will surely follow. This Cowboys loss to the 49ers was hardly an outlier though, as we know it was their fifth straight spanning back to the 2021-22 playoffs. One thing the Cowboys have not been nearly good enough at doing at any point over this entire stretch of time is recognizing individual matchups they can take advantage of and scheming to do so on a consistent basis. This one sentence could be the mission statement for the Kyle Shanahan 49ers, and while the Cowboys have shuffled the coaching and personnel against Shanahan constantly, it’s Kyle that continues to come out with the wins. This was evident even in the way both teams got their first points of the game in the first quarter, as part of a bigger picture first half where the Cowboys put up a good fight just to get worn down and exposed in the second. The Cowboys needed a roughing the passer call from their own former defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa to move the chains on the opening drive, and were held to a field goal without completing a pass. The 49ers answered quickly with their first of six touchdown drives on the game. With the Cowboys having both DaRon Bland and Joey Porter Jr. on the field against a hobbled group of 49ers wide receivers, the matchups on the outside actually had a chance to tilt in Dallas’ favor. Shanahan’s response to this was a masterclass, as he found the Cowboys own hobbled position group in the backend which was safety, and went after them. George Kittle drew a holding penalty against Caleb Downs to negate a sack, and then Kittle went to work for the first of several times against backup safety Markquese Bell. This was a matchup dominated by Kittle, as he took a screen pass for 20 yards one play before the touchdown to Deebo Samuel on another screen. Malik Hooker was the other safety out of position for the first of what was also many times this game on the touchdown, and the 49ers made it a point to test the tackling of the entire Cowboys defense, especially in the secondary. This was a test Christian Parker’s defense failed. Parker’s defense did get Porter Jr. matched up against Kittle for a key third-down stop on the ensuing 49ers possession to earn a three and out, but the scary trend of the Cowboys offense not rising to the occasion of scoring, or even holding onto the ball when their defense does get a stop, reared it’s ugly head again. The Cowboys promptly went three and out themselves with an incomplete pass to Lamb on third down. The best singular example of the Cowboys making offense look as easy as it came for the 49ers in this game was on George Pickens’ second touchdown, the slant pass that always seems to work yet isn’t called often enough. Pickens’ touchdown could have put his team up two scores if Quinnen Williams finished a sack on 3rd-and-12 on the previous 49ers drive, something he made up for by getting a red zone sack to keep the 49ers out of the end zone in the red area – something that’s been nearly impossible for defenses this season. Instead, the door was left open for the 49ers to respond again, and the defense couldn’t get Brock Purdy on the ground again. Extending the play, he hit Christian McCaffrey for his first backbreaking touchdown of 74 yards, and just like that the 49ers were up 17-16. Another third-down incompletion to Lamb put the defense back on the field one last time before halftime, getting the desperation stop to preserve the one-point deficit. Only trailing by one at halftime could still be seen as a win considering how tough the 49ers are as a matchup for the Cowboys, but the way it came about with both the offense and defense being stressed more than needed planted the seed for the second half runaway. The second half felt like a runaway because Shanahan dug even deeper into his bag of tricks to dictate the terms of this game to the Cowboys defense, getting a Deebo Samuel 70-yard reverse touchdown to go up 31-19. The ultimate dagger came with McCaffrey matched up against Von Miller for a 66-yard touchdown to go back up two scores late at 46-32. Everything the Cowboys did offensively to storm back late felt empty, hollow, and like a rerun of a bad movie we’ve seen too many times before anyway, but seeing McCaffrey sprint right down the middle of the field untouched to put it away might be the image of the season for why the Cowboys still are where they are. QB Mobility One other thing that proved itself out on the scoreboard along the way of Shanahan calling a better game for his offense compared to Schottenheimer for the Cowboys offense was the mobility of Brock Purdy compared to Dak Prescott. Purdy was comfortable and in control almost all game, though the Cowboys did get to him for five sacks. His scramble ability was a real difference maker though, and came naturally for big play after big play as he completed 78.6% of his passes for 13.9 yards per attempt – a career high. Compare this to yet another game where things felt laborious for the Cowboys offense for long stretches, and like the weight of the world was on Dak Prescott’s shoulders again too, and the home team not being able to rely on Dak’s mobility makes it an even sadder state of affairs. Purdy’s scrambles were unscripted plays that should be the equivalent of “50/50 balls” in basketball, but it was more like “90/10” for the visitors in week ten. Prescott’s throws from outside the pocket were forced and off-target. Some were scripted plays that served as more examples of Schottenheimer being in over his head, and ultimately failing this franchise QB. Wasted season after wasted season is becoming the story of Prescott’s career, his mobility has not been a true strength of his game for some time, and now it just feels like yet another thing that’s come and gone without the Cowboys getting anything out of it. In all of those ways this loss felt familiar, but it did make history for Prescott as it was the first of his career with five touchdowns. It was also just the second loss in his career losing with four or more touchdowns, the other one also coming at home. Prescott was 0-5 targeting CeeDee Lamb in the first half, as his…

title: Cowboys vs 49ers: George Pickens proves he’s must-see TV
summary: It was more of the same for the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. As has become a constant throughout almost the entirety of this regular season, Dallas’ offense had their moments while the defense got embarrassed time and time again. The Cowboys scored 40 against a very impressive 49ers’ defense that had not surrendered that amount […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images It was more of the same for the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. As has become a constant throughout almost the entirety of this regular season, Dallas’ offense had their moments while the defense got embarrassed time and time again. The Cowboys scored 40 against a very impressive 49ers’ defense that had not surrendered that amount of points in over a calendar year. Since the start of the 2023 season, Dallas became the fifth team to score 40 or more points in a regular-season game but lose the matchup. While things were close to disastrous on the defensive side of the ball, the Cowboys offense was effective at times, but failed to capitalize totally during the middle part of the game. Several players had standout performances, but wide receiver George Pickens stood above the rest, earning him this week’s game ball award. After missing last week’s game, Pickens returned with a vengeance on Sunday. Dallas finally got their star wideout involved early and often, and the results were stellar. Pickens finished the day with a career-high 11 receptions to go with a season-high 145 receiving yards. Pickens also had the first three-touchdown game of his NFL career, scoring more than half of Dallas’ offensive touchdowns. George Pickens says hello to your wives and your girlfriends 👋 (Via @dallascowboys ) pic.twitter.com/0k98qarV0t — 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) November 15, 2026 GEORGE PICKENS SCORES ANOTHER SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hITd6CtBqp — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 George Pickens with the head & shoulder fake to win the slant pic.twitter.com/f6iZv06EbH — Receiver School (@ReceiverSchool) November 16, 2026 In the first half of the season, we rarely saw Dallas come into a matchup with an offensive game plan of feeding Pickens early to get him off to a good start. Finally, the Cowboys did just that on Sunday, and it paid dividends in a big way. Moving forward, it’s pretty clear the Cowboys are going to have to score 30 or more points in every game if they want to record any more victories the rest of the season. Following Sunday’s game plan of getting Pickens involved early and often will be their best shot at keeping up the offensive success they had on Sunday afternoon.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys loss to the 49ers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a disappointing 46-40 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers in what turned out to be a super high-scoring affair. Despite teasing us with an early lead and staging an interesting fourth-quarter comeback, defensive breakdowns and explosive plays ultimately derailed the team’s hopes. Here are 10 thoughts on the game. 1. […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys suffered a disappointing 46-40 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers in what turned out to be a super high-scoring affair. Despite teasing us with an early lead and staging an interesting fourth-quarter comeback, defensive breakdowns and explosive plays ultimately derailed the team’s hopes. Here are 10 thoughts on the game. 1. False hope early Many expected the 49ers offense to roll right out of the gate, yet the Cowboys defense surprisingly kept things close early. After allowing an opening-drive touchdown, the defense forced a three-and-out and then held the 49ers to a field goal, jumping ahead 16-10 with 4:08 left in the first half. For a fleeting moment, it actually looked like they had a real chance. 2. The onslaught As great as things were early, the game got out of hand quickly. Starting late in the second quarter and carrying into the fourth, the 49ers went on a 28-3 run with four drives of 75 yards or more. The Cowboys’ defense was hanging on for dear life on every possession, and whatever magic they had working for them early completely fell apart. 3. Death by big plays This game featured over 1,000 total yards, with the 49ers racking up 584 of them, the most Dallas has allowed since Week 10 in 2013. Against a highly efficient offense, the Cowboys repeatedly fell victim to massive chunk plays. Christian McCaffrey broke loose for touchdown catches of 74 and 66 yards, while Deebo Samuel added a 70-yard touchdown. Any time the Cowboys felt like they might pick up a little steam, one of these guys would have a big play that just let the air out of AT&T Stadium. 4. Duel threats The 49ers offense is an enigma because you never know where the damage will come from next. On Sunday, their top playmakers swapped traditional roles, as wide receiver Deebo Samuel finished as their leading rusher while running back Christian McCaffrey led the team in receiving. Of course, those numbers got a massive boost from the big plays the defense surrendered. 5. Purdy escapes trouble San Francisco’s quarterback Brock Purdy was precise, throwing for 389 yards, three touchdowns, and zero turnovers while completing 79% of his passes. Beyond making one smart decision after another, Purdy repeatedly escaped the pocket to hit his targets on the run. He consistently turned near-stops for the Cowboys into monumental gains for the 49ers. What a cotton-headed ninny-muggins. 6. The pressure’s on While Purdy scrambling out of trouble hurt the Cowboys, the defensive front still deserves credit for harassing him all afternoon. Most of the heat came right up the middle, resulting in five sacks, the most Purdy has taken all season. Five different defensive tackles got a piece of the action. Five. That’s crazy. All the DTs are making plays. It’s a group effort. 7. Dak airs it out A balanced attack was never going to cut it against the 49ers, so the Cowboys wisely took to the air. Dak Prescott attempted 51 passes, completing 30 for 343 yards and five touchdowns. His lone interception came on fourth down when he launched it downfield instead of running for the sticks, marking the only time the offense was stopped in the second half. Of course, one false step is all it took for the game to fall out of reach. 8. Welcome back, GP The Cowboys got a huge lift from the return of George Pickens, who hauled in 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns. He and 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir battled all afternoon, exchanging shots throughout the contest. Pickens proved nearly impossible to guard, and the only thing that really slowed him down was his own taunting penalty. 9. Fourth-quarter surge Trailing 38-19 in the fourth quarter, the game looked finished until the offense sparked a rally with three straight touchdown drives, each taking three minutes or less. After cutting the deficit to 38-32 with under four minutes left and all three timeouts remaining, the Cowboys just needed one more stop. Sadly, they didn’t get it. Instead, it took the 49ers less than 20 seconds to crush any remaining hope that existed. 10. Clean game Brian Schottenheimer catches plenty of deserved flak, yet he did nothing to hurt his team on Sunday. Penalties were down, and his aggressive fourth-down calls paid off with four conversions, even if a fake-snap charade briefly toyed with our emotions. Going for two when they were trailing eight points late in the fourth was also the right call, giving his team a chance to win the game had they somehow found the end zone one last time.

It stands to reason that they will each be out for a little bit. Somehow, on November 16th, there are still three more games to go until the Cowboys have their bye week. It could make sense to place the duo on injured reserve, but obviously the roster gymnastics are to be determined. Whatever the case it looks like Dallas will be down two starters for the foreseeable future.

title: Cowboys vs. 49ers Stock Report: Caleb Downs has rough day
summary: The scoreboard can often lie. On Sunday, the final between the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers read 46-40 in favor of the visiting Niners, but anyone who watched the game knows that it was in no way that close. It is a stretch to call Dallas’ flurry late in the game “garbage time,” but […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The scoreboard can often lie. On Sunday, the final between the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers read 46-40 in favor of the visiting Niners, but anyone who watched the game knows that it was in no way that close. It is a stretch to call Dallas’ flurry late in the game “garbage time,” but it all came when San Francisco was clearly ready to get on a plane and head home. The point is that nothing felt seriously in doubt. You only lose games so soundly, regardless of what the scoreboard said as noted, because of a collective failure from people involved. It should come as no surprise that our stock report is filled with more downs than ups as a result of it all. Let’s begin. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer We say it every week. What more is there to say? The scoreboard is a liar as noted, so it is in no way like Brian Schottenheimer had his team ready to play. What’s more is that he saw them take another third quarter off so that the game got out of hand, and then everybody started caring as time was running out in the fourth quarter. Maybe if the Cowboys were better we’d give Schotty a pass for this being the big, bad San Francisco 49ers. But you know what? They are the big, bad 49ers. Someone has to stand up and make Dallas respectable to a team they were once proper and legitimate rivals with. Someone has to be the head coach that has a second winning streak before Thanksgiving of his second season. Those people were not Brian Schottenheimer this week. Stock Down: Christian Parker It is Kyle Shanahan. We know that. But goodness. The Dallas Cowboys defense appeared to be taking a few steps these last few weeks, but we were cautious because of the quality of opposing quarterbacks they played. It turns out that context mattered. I’ve long been against moving on from Parker because the defense needs consistency at some point. But what is there to hang your hat on? How can you justify what is happening? In what world? Stock Down: Caleb Downs This was far and away Caleb Downs’ worst game as a professional. It unfortunately came a week after his best. I guess that’s what happens when you are tasked with hanging on for dear life against George Kittle. Downs fell short of that challenge, but at least unlike the rest of his defensive teammates, he can still say he is learning all of this on the fly. Still though, we really hyped Downs up over the offseason. We believed he was ready for this. On Sunday he wasn’t. Stock Down: Cobie Durant Caleb was one of two Cowboys defenders to get completely run over by San Francisco’s Kaelon Black as Cobie Durant was the other. The Cowboys are never ready for the physical fight that is the 49ers. Never. It is a shame. Stock Down: All linebackers It was impossible to boil this down to just one. San Francisco is very talented, but notably they are exceptionally well-coached. Kyle Shanahan had every Cowboys linebacker criss-crossing themselves all day with all of his uses of motion and play action. On the second Deebo Samuel touchdown, literally 10 Cowboys players bought the fake and left Joey Porter Jr. on one side to take on what Tom Brady called a red wave. You can’t get got every time. Stock Down: KaVontae Turpin He had a drop of a pass that landed squarely in his hands. How does that even happen? Remember when Turpin was regarded to be a special teams ace, though? Remember when he was providing the team with an elite advantage? Where is that? What is he offering that anyone else can’t from a return game standpoint? I will take any answer. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey His only miss in this game was an extra point, but the point (no pun intended) is that he missed yet another kick. We are sort of running out of excuses for Aubrey at this point. It can’t always be this, that, or whatever is convenient. He is the top-paid kicker in the NFL and he is in no way among the most reliable kickers in the league right now. His miss was an extra point as noted in this game. An extra point! At home! Indoors! The Cowboys hardly lost because of that missed point, but these keep piling up. Stock Up: Quinnen Williams The Cowboys absolutely have a war daddy. Quinnen Williams might be the best player on the Cowboys period right now. He did his best to singlehandedly save the team at the end as he forced a fumble that almost made the attempted rally actually possible. It is legitimately impressive how Quinnen is not allowing the state of things to impact his effort. I suppose spending a ton of time with the New York Jets will harden you in that way. Stock Up: George Pickens Let’s state that the taunting penalty was silly. We all agree. But wow what a game from George Pickens. He essentially was the entire offense for much of the game, at least before it got away from Dallas and they were playing catch up. It is hard to wonder what could or would have happened if this performance came right before the trade deadline. It didn’t, though. And now he and Dallas are stuck with each other until contract negotiations that will surely be calm and easy. Stock Up: LT Overton In addition to Quinnen Williams the Cowboys also saw some force up front from one of their rookies in LT Overton, including an impressive batted pass. If the Cowboys are ever going to find true and proper form in the future it is going to be because they develop a bevy of options along the defensive line. Hopefully Overton is a part of that future alongside Quinnen Williams and whoever else the Cowboys fan find between now and that hypothetical day.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 6 plays that cost the Cowboys vs. 49ers
summary: 46 points. The Dallas Cowboys defense, that we know isn’t very good, allowed 46 points on 9.4 yards per play. How many times can you be disappointed before you’re no longer surprised? At least just once more as we saw the defense surrender multiple big plays to San Francisco. The offense made their mistakes as […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images 46 points. The Dallas Cowboys defense, that we know isn’t very good, allowed 46 points on 9.4 yards per play. How many times can you be disappointed before you’re no longer surprised? At least just once more as we saw the defense surrender multiple big plays to San Francisco. The offense made their mistakes as well, but it’s hard not to focus on giving up nearly a 50-burger at home. You can pick so many plays to choose from as to why the Cowboys lost but perhaps it’s easier to choose the ones that most irritated you in watching the Cowboys lose to the San Francisco 49ers yet again. Here are the plays that should get under your skin the most and why they matter in the grander scheme. 1. Christian McCaffrey’s 74-yard touchdown on third-and-long The Cowboys looked like they had wrestled the early momentum back from San Francisco after a George Pickens score. It’s not too many times the Cowboys have led by multiple scores this season and the defense has needed any possible large lead it could get. Facing 3rd-and-8 with the 49ers on their own 26-yard line, the Dallas defense proved why. The Cowboys did a great job of putting initial pressure on Brock Purdy but he managed to scramble out of the pocket and found Christian McCaffrey as got behind the defense for a short pass from Purdy. From there he went untouched for a 74-yard score. For a moment you felt that the Cowboys could put the pressure on the 49ers for a change but boy would that be an ominous sign of things to come. 2. Deebo Samuel’s 70-yard touchdown run The theme of today was one explosive play after another. If there’s one thing you expect from a Kyle Shanahan offense is misdirection and out-leveraging the defense for an advantage. Deebo Samuel historically has been a thorn in the side of the Cowboys, and once again he stuck the Cowboys right where it hurts. Samuel took a reverse pitch from Kaelon Black and raced 70 yards down the sideline for a touchdown. When you watch the replay, notice how long it takes for the defense to process what is happening. Samuel has a convoy of blockers out in front while the majority of the Cowboys defense is on the other side of the field. What are some of the basic principles of defense at at any level let alone the NFL? Defensive pursuit and perimeter containment. That’s where the Cowboys tend to struggle mightily an Samuel made them pay. One missed assignment or poor angle against a player like Samuel can turn an ordinary running play into an instant touchdown. 3. Kaelon Black’s 25-yard touchdown run The Cowboys avoided letting the 49ers score points at the end of the first half before they received the second half kickoff. Down by a one point, letting the 49ers score a touchdown would be detrimental. Unfortunately, Dallas could not prevent that from happening and rookie running back Kaelon Black ran all over the defense to make a point. The play puts another red-hot spotlight on Caleb Downs. The rookie safety was run over by Black on a touchdown that helped San Francisco seize control of the second half. Downs also had trouble finishing plays in space, including a missed opportunity to contain Purdy before the quarterback found McCaffrey for a long touchdown. For a player with his expectations, the Cowboys need more consistency, particularly against offenses that force defenders to make decisions in space. We need to see better from Downs down the stretch. 4. Brandon Aubrey’s missed extra point and Dallas’ failed two-point attempt This is where the wheels started to fall off. Sure Brandon Aubrey made two kicks beyond 50 yards. However, Aubrey hasn’t been as automatic anymore and now you sometimes have to hold you breath if he can make the routine kicks. With Cowboys looking to take seven-point lead, Aubrey missed the extra point. This left the Cowboys chasing points for the remainder of the game. With the game going the way that it did, any points at all were needed. Dallas had an unsuccessful two-point try in an effort to make up the difference after Aubrey’s miss. Aubrey has also had kickoff penalties this year and onside kick attempt at the end of the game wasn’t nearly good enough. There’s something off with Aubrey, and whatever it is, it is hurting the Cowboys. 5. Dallas’ comeback is undone by another McCaffrey touchdown For all intents and purposes, this was the last straw. The Cowboys fought tirelessly to get back in the game but fell short on defense. After Prescott connected with Ryan Flournoy for an 11-yard touchdown on fourth down, Dallas had reduced San Francisco’s lead to 38-32 with 3:42 remaining. The Cowboys needed one defensive stop to give Prescott a chance to win. Instead, just 10 seconds of game clock later, Purdy found McCaffrey for a 66-yard touchdown on second-and-10. San Francisco added a two-point conversion, extending its lead to 46-32. This was arguably the most decisive moment of the game. Dallas had finally pulled within one possession, only for the defense to surrender another enormous touchdown immediately. 6. Quinnen Williams almost forces the turn over the Cowboys need After the Cowboys drew the score to 40-46, it was longshot that the Cowboys could get the ball back with enough time to take the late lead. Quinnen Williams who has been one of the few bright spots for the Cowboys defense almost came up huge. Looking to drain the remaining time off the clock, the 49ers handed the ball of to Kaelon Black. Williams darted through the 49ers offensive line to meet Black in the hole. Williams was able to dislodge the ball from Black’s arms. The Cowboys had a chance to recover the ball before Black quickly regained possession for the 49ers. If the defense can’t be average, the least it can be is opportunistic and Williams almost gave that much when the team needed it badly. The Cowboys scored 40 points and still found a way to lose. That’s the frustrating reality of this team. Dak Prescott threw five touchdowns, George Pickens delivered three scores, and Quinnen Williams nearly gave Dallas one final opportunity to steal a victory. Yet none of it mattered because the defense couldn’t stop San Francisco from producing one explosive play after another. At some point, these breakdowns stop being isolated mistakes and become the identity of your football team. For Dallas, that point may have already arrived.
author: LP Cruz

title: Cowboys news: Dallas defense gets trampled in loss to the 49ers
summary: Dallas walked into Sunday afternoon’s game as an underdog with a lot to prove. With the Giants losing on Thursday night to the Commanders, and following a victory last week to the Colts, if the Cowboys defense showed some semblance of life, Dallas could turn the season around. Unfortunately, that is not what happened at […]
full_text: Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Dallas walked into Sunday afternoon’s game as an underdog with a lot to prove. With the Giants losing on Thursday night to the Commanders, and following a victory last week to the Colts, if the Cowboys defense showed some semblance of life, Dallas could turn the season around. Unfortunately, that is not what happened at all. Dallas allowed multiple explosive plays and the defense gave up 580 yards of offense and 46 points. The Cowboys’ defense was historically bad in 46 – 40 loss to 49ers- Shane Taylor, Inside The Star The Dallas Cowboys faced their biggest test of the season. And in a game where the Cowboys could have made a statement, they fell flat on their face. The Cowboys allowed 3 touchdowns of longer than 65 yards — all of which occurred without the player scoring the touchdown being touched. They gave up 46 points, 580 yards of offense — 370 passing and 210 rushing. If this was any other team, the defensive coordinator would be FIRE by tomorrow. Don’t Forget These 5: Effects of Aubrey’s missed extra point- Nick Eatman, DallasCowboys.com It is tough to pin the loss on a single play, given that the Cowboys defense had multiple opportunities to give the team a chance and continually fell short. However, these five plays definitely had a big impact. Onside kick decision? – The Cowboys were able to score and cut the lead to six with just 46 seconds left. While the onside kick made sense to try to get the ball back, the fact that the Cowboys had three timeouts could’ve made the case that they should have just kicked the ball deep. Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys’ Predictable Week 10 Loss to 49ers- Mike Moraitis, Sports Illustrated This is not a game that Dallas was expected to win. But given the defensive improvement over the last few weeks, one would have hoped to see a little more from that side of the ball. The Niners averaged an obscene 9.4 yards per play. The 584 total yards the Cowboys gave up amounts to the most Dallas has allowed in a home game in team history. We might very well be watching the worst defense in Cowboys history. 5 blunt reactions from Cowboys’ deflating loss to 49ers in Week 10- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat This game feels like another lowlight in a disappointing season. Although the final score may make it seem like Dallas was in it, they were thoroughly beaten by the 49ers. Brian Schottenheimer is his own worst enemy When looking back on why/how Dallas lost, Schottenheimer’s decision to punt on 4th-and-2 at the end of the first half looms very large. While the offense was at its own 43-yard line, it was also 2-for-2 on fourth downs at that point in the game. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . 49ers poke fun at Cowboys multiple times to headline NFL Week 10 trolls- Anthony Gharib, ESPN The 49ers and Cowboys obviously do not share much love for each other. And in a game where the 49ers did whatever they so chose to do on offense, the jokes will follow. The 49ers poked fun at the Cowboys multiple times with Texas- and Dallas-specific posts, including cowboy boots outside of AT&T Stadium with a 49ers cowboy hat on top of them. In one post, lyrics from country star Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” were in the caption, while another caption read: “Brought the star power.” 4 losers and 2 winners from the Cowboys loss to the 49ers- David Halprin, Blogging The Boys Playoff hopes The Cowboys were given a chance to really tighten the chase in the NFC East. The New York Giants loss to the Washington Commanders gave Dallas a little opening to apply pressure on the Giants, and get their own momentum going.
