title: Chargers-Ravens Game Recap: Omarion Hampton, takeaways spur Bolts to 1st win
summary: Maybe there is something to this correlation between turnovers committed and losing, huh? In Justin Herbert’s first game this season where he managed to avoid throwing an interception, the Chargers managed to hang on and beat the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football for their first win of the 2026 season. It was an […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Omarion Hampton #8 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the second quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maybe there is something to this correlation between turnovers committed and losing, huh? In Justin Herbert’s first game this season where he managed to avoid throwing an interception, the Chargers managed to hang on and beat the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football for their first win of the 2026 season. It was an overall quiet day from Herbert (12-of-18 passing, 129 yards), but that’s all the Chargers needed when they also got big performances from running back Omarion Hampton (105 yards, TD) and their defense (two turnovers forced), the latter of which held All-Pro back Derrick Henry to 10 rushing yards on 10 carries. Henry did score a pair of touchdowns which went a long way in keeping this game closer than it felt for much of the night. Since the Ravens could not establish much of a run game, it was up to recently-acquired quarterbac Jacoby Brissett to lead the offense. He passed for a very respectable 340 yards, but threw zero touchdowns and the aforementioned pick. The Chargers defense could not muster much of a pass rush Monday night, settling for just a pair of sacks from defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. Just like he did when he was leading the Cardinals, Brissett showed a propensity for getting the ball out fast before the likes of Khalil Mack or Tuli Tuipulotu could ever get close. To counter that, the Chargers second and third-level defenders did a phenomenal job rallying to tackle underneath and overall keeping the energy high which led to Del’Shawn Phillips’ interception off a Cam Hart deflection. Defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary has the Chargers work at punching and a jarring balls loose in practice and that showed up in this one when Tarheeb Still knocked the ball loose from wideout Zay Flowers, leading to Elijah Molden’s recovery that all but sealed the win for the Bolts. Jim Harbaugh, Herbert, and the Chargers are now 1-8 with the win dropping them down to the second-overall pick in next year’s draft. The win also gives them just a 15 percent chance to own the number one pick by the end of the year. Next up, the Cade Klubnik-led Jets who are 2-8 after losing to the Bills in Week 10. After that, it’s the Drake Maye-less Patriots on Sunday Night Football (before they flex the game out, presumably). Don’t look now, but the Chargers could end up going on a bit of a run to end the year which, depending who you are and where you stand on tanking, could be a very good or bad things in your eyes. There’s plenty of time left before the next draft, but for now, the Chargers are winners and the fan base deserves every ounce of joy it may bring them. Go celebrate already. Continue on to check out the recap of tonight’s game below! First Quarter The Chargers won the coin toss and chose to defer. Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens offense was up first. Brissett handed off to Derrick Henry on first down but a combined effort by Daiyan Henley and Khalil Mack stopped the massive back for a loss. After a pressure forced an incompletion on second down, Elijah Molden tackled tight end Mark Andrews short of the sticks on third to complete the three-and-out. The Chargers turned that early momentum into a phenomenal opening drive that began with a strong run by Omarion Hampton for 11 yards. Disaster was avoided on the very next play, however, as a Hampton wild-cat play almost ended in another lost fumble by the second-year back, but the ball was recovered by LA after cornerback Marlon Humphrey stripped it near the sideline. On second-and-six, Herbert rolled right and hit Tre’ Harris for a 22-yard gain to the Baltimore 26. Two plays later, Herbert dropped back, saw nobody was open, then hit the gas up the middle and outraced the defense for a 22-yard touchdown run to give the Chargers an early 7-0 lead. Both teams combined for three three-and-outs over the next few drives, two of which were by the Ravens. During the Chargers’ third drive of the game. Harris made an incredible catch for a 31-yard gain after Herbert escaped a sack and found the second-year wideout just before he got to the sideline. The Bolts offense was flagged twice over their next four plays, including an ineligible man downfield on right tackle Travis burke that derailed another promising drive. Cameron Dicker came on after an illegal formation penalty was declined on third down (Herbert scramble short of the sticks) to make it 10-0 with a 38-yard field goal. Second Quarter Brissett finally settled in for the Ravens to begin the second drive, making a number of tough throws to the likes of receivers Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, and tight end Mark Andrews. The completion to Bateman put the Ravens at the Chargers two-yard line and Derrick Henry bounded his way in to cap the drive and cut LA’s lead to 10-7 with 12:33 left in the first half. The Chargers offense got off to a rocky start with Keaton Mitchell fumbling the ensuing kickoff backwards, putting them back at their own 12. Mitchell was then tackled for a loss of five to put the Bolts well behind the sticks. A screen on third was short of the sticks and the Bolts punted. Just two plays into the next Raves drive, Brissett fired over the middle to wideout Ja’Kobi Lane but the ball was batted up into the air and linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips was able to come down with it for an interception. The Chargers turned that takeaway by the defense into a lengthy 13-play, 48 yard drive that took 7 minutes and 35 seconds off the clock before capping it with a short touchdown run by Hampton on fourth-and-one. Herbert hooked up with Harris for 16 yards on an earlier third-and-four which put the latter up to five receptions for 86 yards all in the first half. With 1:56 remaining in the half, the Bolts held a 17-7 lead. Brissett led the Ravens down the field with a very crisp pass attack which utilized a ton of underneath passes to the tight ends with the Chargers secondary playing deep. They eventually halted the Ravens short of the end zone and Riley Patterson converted a chip shot to close the gap to 17-10 as both teams headed to the locker rooms. Third Quarter The Chargers received the opening kickoff and the offense was off and running (literally) with a 19-yard run by Hampton to begin the drive. Two plays later, he added a nine-yard tote on second-and-10. Unfortunately, Hampton was then stuffed on third-and-one by linebacker Roquan Smith and the Chargers were forced to punt. Fortunately the defense returned to their first quarter form, forcing the Ravens offense into a quick three-and-out that was punctuated by Tomlinson’s second sack of the night. Derius Davis then returned the ensuing punt 24 yards to set the offense up with great field position. A screen pass to running back Kimani Vidal went for 15 yards on the first play of the drive which put the Bolts down to the Ravens 22-yard line. From there, the Chargers authored a run for zero yards, a six-yard pass, and an incompletion on third which led to another Dicker field goal from 34 yards out. Ravens responded with a field goal of their own on their next drive, going 54 yards in 12 plays to make it a seven-point game. Fourth Quarter Herbert and the offense tacked on a 35-yard field goal just after the start of the fourth quarter to once again stretch their lead back to 10 points. Brissett answered the moment with a 10-play, 71 yard drive that ended in Henry’s second rushing touchdown of the night. With the minutes ticking by, the Chargers couldn’t seem to muster any momentum on offense with the game coming down to the wire. They posted back-to-back three-and-outs and the Ravens found themselves with the ball and the clock reading 2:24. Luck broke towards the Chargers on the third play of the ensuing…

title: Chargers-Ravens Game Preview: Harbaugh, Minter reunite under the primetime lights
summary: The Chargers and Ravens face off this week on Monday Night Football after eight weeks of failed expectations. Jim Harbaugh was supposed to have the Chargers gearing up for a Super Bowl run this season. It’s year three of his tenure and back-to-back 11-win seasons were seemingly going to be the stepping stones to finally […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (83) fends off Arizona Cardinals linebacker Jack Gibbens (50) during the NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 13, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers and Ravens face off this week on Monday Night Football after eight weeks of failed expectations. Jim Harbaugh was supposed to have the Chargers gearing up for a Super Bowl run this season. It’s year three of his tenure and back-to-back 11-win seasons were seemingly going to be the stepping stones to finally getting Justin Herbert passed the wild card round. Now, they’re 0-8 and the season is already far past being “lost.” The 2027 season, and maybe even 2028, is now currently viewed as their next opportunity to be competitive. That’s one heck of a wrench thrown into the plans for the team that entered 2026 with the sixth-best Super Bowl odds. As for Minter and the Ravens, the young defensive genius was supposed to come in and fix the other side of the ball so Lamar Jackson did not have to be Superman each week and outscore the opposing offense all by himself. Well, Jackson has only been healthy for about two-thirds of the season and now they’re down to a brand new quarterback who they just traded on top of being the 25th-ranked scoring defense. That’s a bit of a far-cry from his two top-10 units with the Bolts. Even with all the negatives surrounding these teams, Monday night should still be entertaining (in the good OR bad way). The connections and storylines hold well here, even if the final viewership numbers don’t. With all that said, let’s go ahead and dive in to the three things I’ll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Monday night. 1.) Is this the best chance for the Chargers to get their first win? The Chargers have come close on several occasions this year in getting their first win of the season, but ultimately couldn’t capitalize on anything that may have went their way through the first three quarters. This week MAY be different as they are on the road to face a 4-5 Ravens team that is now starting their fourth different quarterback of the year in Jacoby Brissett. Injuries have sidelined both Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano started in Week Nine, but it went about as bad as you’d expect. Brissett is a career backup who got some starting time with the Cardinals last year and to begin this year, but his momentum from 2025 did not carry over into this season. That led to him ultimately being dealt. Baltimore’s defense under Minter has not been great, either. They’re middle of the pack in total defense (15th), but rank 23rd in defending the pass (229.8) and 25th in points allowed (26.2). All of this combines to become the Chargers’ best chance at winning a game before they face the Jets in Week 11. After that, the best remaining matchups on the schedule are the Bucs (3-6), Raiders (4-5), and Dolphins (1-7). Do the Chargers even get to four wins this year if they lose to the Ravens? Even three? Yikes! 2.) Will Minter get the best of Mike McDaniel again? The Chargers narrowly beat the Dolphins in 2025 by a score for 29-27. Minter’s defense was gashed by running back De’Von Achane for a pair of touchdowns, but they did intercept Tua Tagovailoa three times and held him to just 205 yards through the air. With that experience under his belt, will he execute a similar strategy to put Justin Herbert in the same kind of hell? Herbert has been throwing plenty of interceptions already this year so you’ve got to think Minter is expecting at least one takeaway, but could he have key to unlocking an even bigger turnover party for his current defense? The Ravens pass rush is fine enough this year with 17 sacks in nine games. They’re led by Tavious Robinson and Mike Green, both of whom have 3.5 QB takedowns. Trey Hendrickson, the team’s big offseason addition, only has two in seven games played. As much as this may tell us Herbert could have a better day in the pocket, the Chargers offensive line is coming off a Texans loss that saw them allow a career-high eight sacks on their quarterback. Chances are it’s not going to be an easy time given the intimidating atmosphere in a loud venue fill of black and purple. 3.) Will offensive reinforcements make a difference? I basically used this storyline in last week’s game preview, but of course the players I highlighted were once again ruled out after I had published. Well, we’re going back to that well as the likes of Kayode Awosika and David Njoku were listed as questionable this week as opposed to being ruled out in the final injury report. It’s been a long time since either played and both are going to be welcomed additions around Justin Herbert. Awosika will replace rookie Logan Taylor at left guard and immediately raise the floor of the whole unit. Taylor has played admirably, but Awosika was playing legitimately good football before his injury. Njoku, on the other hand, was one of Herbert’s top targets through the first two games of the year against the Cardinals and Raiders. Prior to his injury, he was top two on the team in both receptions and yards (bad drop-into-interception, aside). If both are active and back to 100 percent Monday night, then I’ll have hopes for one of the best offensive outputs of the year. If they don’t, well it’s likely to be another go-round on this awful carousel ride called the 2026 season.

title: RAMalytics: How will Rams deploy their new offensive wrinkle?
summary: Sean McVay looked at the Los Angeles Rams’ depth chart following their recent rash of injuries and said “I’m just going to put our best remaining players on the field.” At times Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, that meant deploying both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams at the same time. Two-back sets, commonly referred to […]
full_text: Sean McVay looked at the Los Angeles Rams’ depth chart following their recent rash of injuries and said “I’m just going to put our best remaining players on the field.” At times Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, that meant deploying both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams at the same time . Two-back sets, commonly referred to as “pony personnel”, unlocked LA’s passing game despite a limited corps of pass catchers. McVay’s wrinkle was to play with three tight ends in lieu of having a receiver on the field. This wasn’t 21 or 22 personnel. It was something else. The interesting part? 207 (89%) of the Rams’ 234 passing yards came with both Corum and Williams on the field while 12 yards and 15 yards came from 11 and 13 personnel groupings, respectively. Matthew Stafford was 13 of 17 on such plays. In the Rams’ bread and butter 13 personnel? He completed just three of six passes for 15 yards and took a sack. It’s mildly strange that the Rams leaned into the passing game with two backs on the field. They had little rushing production to show for it otherwise. Out of LA’s 202 rushing yards, 19 came from the “other” personnel grouping, per SumerSports. They ran 40 times for 183 yards out of 13 personnel, and then netted zero yards between 12 and 21. This is a dichotomy that must be assessed and bridged together. If McVay’s newest offensive wrinkle is going to have staying power, the next step is to also threaten on the ground. There should be plenty of opportunities for changeups and misdirection based on the tape LA left for opponents against Arizona. It remains to be seen whether the two-back sets are a means to getting by without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. LA could brush the idea aside once their receiver room returns to health. Or, as we saw last season, the Rams may be finding lightning in a bottle that will eventually be emulated by the rest of the NFL. At least for now, Sean McVay has our attention. His inventiveness is trademarked. How long is the runway for the newest trick up his sleeve?

title: Sean McVay hypes up Rams’ OC, possibly for head coaching job?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have not had a smooth season, and the offense has under-performed relative to expectations, but Sean McVay was quick to credit offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase with helping Matthew Stafford stay on track in Week 10’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. The Rams scored 34 points, had 436 yards of total offense, […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have not had a smooth season, and the offense has under-performed relative to expectations, but Sean McVay was quick to credit offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase with helping Matthew Stafford stay on track in Week 10’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. The Rams scored 34 points, had 436 yards of total offense, and their +22.9 EPA was the second-best total of the season for L.A.. McVay told reporters after the game that Scheelhaase deserved all the credit for Xavier Smith’s 22-yard touchdown just before the half, allowing the Rams to take a 17-6 lead. It’s a perfect example of how McVay has been able to expand his coaching tree faster and wider than virtually any other head coach now or before him. The Rams are always quick to let other teams know: “We got talent on our staff” and Scheelhase could be the next to find himself running one of L.A.‘s rivals. It won’t hurt that by hiring Scheelhaase, the Rams would receive third-round compensatory picks in 2027 and 2028. Sean McVay revealed that offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase was responsible for suggesting the screen pass that resulted in Xavier Smith’s 22-yard touchdown against the Cardinals. McVay also shared how rewarding it is to see players like Smith capitalize on their… pic.twitter.com/2DegWqaQzd — RambLAng Man (@RambLAngMan) November 16, 2026 The Rams hired Scheelhaase in 2024 as a passing game specialist after he spent three years at Illinois and six years at Iowa State. Among the players on those Cyclones teams was quarterback Brock Purdy. Scheelhaase was promoted to passing game coordinator in 2025, then offensive coordinator when Mike LaFleur was hired as head coach of these very same Cardinals. Perhaps seeing LaFleur inspired McVay to brag about the possibility that he might like his new offensive coordinator even better. But how much longer will Scheelhaase be working for McVay…and not against him? Bucs fans, this is Nate Scheelhaase who is the Rams OC. 34 years old, super bright, has playcalling experience, and played the QB position in college. Good understanding of play design, communication skills and has risen quickly under Sean McVay. He is big on player development,… pic.twitter.com/I2CjpO9OVx — RealBucsTalk (@RealBucsTalk) October 5, 2026 Not a single head coach has been fired during the 2026 season. It’s the latest the NFL has gone into a season without firing a head coach since 2017. That year, a coach wasn’t fired until Ben McAdoo in Week 13. Among the first teams that you would think might fire their head coach soon: Dan Quinn, Commanders Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys Aaron Glenn, Jets Todd Bowles, Bucs It is unlikely that Tampa Bay fires Bowles in the middle of the season because the Bucs might actually be the best team in the NFC South. It’s just a really bad division. But seeing how badly Baker Mayfield needs a good play caller, Tampa Bay might love to replace Bowles with Scheelhaase in 2027. Other teams that could get closer to making a change at head coach include the Eagles, Saints, and Panthers. It doesn’t sound like the Chargers would fire Jim Harbaugh even if they go winless, instead putting the axe to Mike McDaniel. Would the Titans fire Robert Saleh after one year? Will the Colts blame Shane Steichen? Whatever happens, Scheelhaase is sure to be among the first phone calls by teams that need a head coach and want to focus on offensive-minded play callers, similar to the success that Liam Coen is having with the Jaguars. Scheelhaase was popular last time, interviewing with the Ravens, Browns, Steelers, and Bills. Pittsburgh reportedly thought he had a “Mike Tomlin vibe”. It’s certain that Scheelhaase isn’t long for the Rams. Can he stick around long enough to help right this ship in time to make the next Super Bowl?

title: Rams’ injuries provide silver lining of depth chart changes
summary: Using a punishing ground attack, the Los Angeles Rams methodically overwhelmed the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 in Sunday’s Week 10 matchup. L.A. overcame another slow start, trailing the Cards well into the second quarter before the offense came alive to the tune of 436 yards. With injuries stacking up, the Rams offense was forced to improvise, […]
full_text: Using a punishing ground attack, the Los Angeles Rams methodically overwhelmed the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 in Sunday’s Week 10 matchup. L.A. overcame another slow start, trailing the Cards well into the second quarter before the offense came alive to the tune of 436 yards. With injuries stacking up, the Rams offense was forced to improvise, both in new formations and personnel groupings. Sets and names that Rams fans were not familiar with. Head coach Sean McVay gave Arizona a steady diet of three tight end formations, but also mixed in two running back sets split on each side of QB Matthew Stafford’s shot gun and he used a handful of jumbo blocking packages with six offensive linemen. It was bully ball and the Rams pounded out 200 yards on the ground. The Rams wide receiver unit, ‘The Island of Misfit Toys” edition, stood up quite well. Konata Mumpfield (48 reps), rookie CJ Daniels (46), Tutu Atwell (16), and the recent return from exile, Xavier Smith (9) all made plays. Running back Ronnie Rivers (17) chipped in 81 rushing yards. On the offensive line, Beaux Limmer (76) got the start at guard and after the Rams lost not one, but two centers, he moved into the pivot. Bill Murray (49) jumped in at guard, his first regular season action since Week 5 of 2024. Is relying on a group of lesser-knowns down the stretch sustainable? Here’s a review of the snap counts from Sunday. Players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (76, 100%) Started out cold, but got into the groove as the second quarter progressed. A good job overall, but another bad interception needs to be noted. Staff feeds off emotion and excitement, the new offensive changes seemed to energize him. I didn’t see him shooting the finger pistols, but he clearly was playing with emotion. Running back Kyren Williams (39, 51%) Blake Corum (39, 51%) Ronnie Rivers (17, 22%) L.A. trotted out two running back formations on 17 plays and ironically, threw the football on every one of them. The Rams still ran for 200+ yards. Over this four-game win streak, the Rams have out-gained their opponents by nearly 450 yards on the ground. Corum gets the highest snap count, play time percentage, and number of touches in his career. To close out the final 12 minutes of the game, Rivers humped the rock on 15 consecutive plays. Wide receiver Konata Mumpfield (48, 63%) CJ Daniels (46, 61%) Tutu Atwell (16, 21%) Xavier Smith ( 9, 12%) Brennan Presley (2, 3%) Coming into the game with 261 total receiving yards amongst them, the Rams young corps booked 174 for Sunday’s game alone. Even better was reeling in 70 percent of targets. Time and again, they found open areas, whether by scheme, created on their own, or the Cardinals ineptitude. All had catches for nice gains. Atwell’s dropped pass near the goal line, may let Smith sneak by him on the depth chart. This was a sick route by CJ Daniels. Shame they couldn't connect for 6. pic.twitter.com/1oBiGS0hrV — Sosa Kremenjas (@QBsMVP) November 16, 2026 Tight end Colby Parkinson (53, 70%) Davis Allen (52, 68%) Tyler Higbee (51, 67%) Max Klare (4, 5%) L.A. used three tight ends on 63.5 percent of reps, 47 plays, running the football on 40 of them. They weren’t just pack horses carrying the run game load, they combined to haul in six of seven passes and notch two touch downs. Offensive line Beaux Limmer, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (76, 100%) Alaric Jackson (74, 97%) Bill Murray (49, 64%) Coleman Shelton (17, 22%) Dylan McMahon (10, 13%) David Quessenberry (6, 8%) When you can pound out 46 rushing attempts, you’ve had a good showing by the big uglies. L.A. used Quessenberry as a sixth lineman on a handful of snaps, something fans have wanted to see. Poor McMahon, he gets a shot at his first extended action since Week 18 of the 2024 season and gets hurt. Shelton has had a solid season, it will be a big loss if he’s out for extended time. It looked like he tweaked a hamstring getting out on a second quarter screen play. Limmer showed his versatility, it was his style of game, a slobberknocker run fest. Murray played fair to well, considering it was his first action since Week 5 of 2024 and cold call to boot. Special teams Backup cornerback Damarion Williams rates a shout out, he’s been a practice squad elevation in the two games since being signed. He’s had a kick coverage tackle in both. Really gets after it and plays with hustle and emotion. Hard to say what the Rams will do with him once his three PS elevations are up, but if he stacks another good game after the bye, it will be a tough decision. Defensive line Aaron Donald (23, 66%) Tyler Davis (22, 63%) Braden Fiske (20, 57%) Ty Hamilton (15, 43%) Larrell Murchison (9, 26%) Dominating performance from the first line of defense. On only 36 defensive snaps, they allowed a paltry 34 yards rushing between the tackles and logged 10 tackles with 3.5 sacks. In support work, Hamilton has been getting good push in the past few games and Murchison got his hand up to knock down a short pass. With opposing teams forced into the short, quick passing attack, I’d like to see more hands up in the passing lanes. Edge Byron Young (22, 63%) Josaiah Stewart (18, 51%) Myles Garrett (17, 49%) Wesley Bailey (15, 43%) While Garrett was quiet, Young stacked another solid outing. Stewart’s time on the field has been trending steadily down and his production has run hot and cold. Bailey is still in the learning process, but if/when he can match game savvy with his athletic traits and effort, the Rams will have a keeper. rush/drop … right edge Wesley Bailey undercut … saw it all the way pic.twitter.com/CGZteInqzJ — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) November 15, 2026 Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (20, 57%) Omar Speights (13, 37%) Shaun Dolac (13, 37%) Interesting happenings here. Landman’s snaps and play percentage have gone down for three straight games. It could be that he’s been nicked up a lot this season, but worth watching. Most of reps for Dolac and Speights came late, after the Rams had put 31 points on the board. Dolac hasn’t received a huge increase, but has double-digit reps in three of the last four games and produced well. Speights’ play time is trending down ever so slightly over the past three weeks, but production has been very consistent. Safety Quentin Lake (35, 100%) Kamren Curl (30, 86%) Kamren Kinchens (25, 71%) Jaylen McCollough (6, 17%) Cornerback Trent McDuffie (30, 86%) Josh Wallace (30, 86%) Emmanuel Forbes (21, 60%) Cam Lampkin (1, 3%) If you’re only giving up 108 yards passing, the secondary had a solid day. Two plays accounted for nearly half of that total. One for 21 yards into the soft area of a two-deep zone and Lake got burnt in man coverage for a 31-yard explosive. Lake hasn’t been lining up much in the slot, about 15 percent of the time, and even less on wide receivers. The Cards caught him on one of those times. One thing that stood out was McCollough’s snap counts and play percentage, down substantially from the past four games. Going forward It feels as if the Rams have endured a long, arduous journey getting to 6-4, but have a grasp, however tenuous, of a wildcard seed. Now they’ve earned 10 days to scab up and get heads straight for the stretch drive. You cannot overplay, over state, or over hype the importance of the Thanksgiving Eve tilt with the Green Bay Packers. It is a necessary first step for a successful conclusion to the season. There is reason for optimism. On offense, Sean McVay broke away from his standard approach. Yes, still controlled and methodical, but just enough of a tweak to freshen things up. Establishing a run game early, using an extra offensive lineman to gain a numbers advantage, lining up two running backs, and attacking the whole field, both vertical and horizontal. It’s vintage McVay, just updated packaging. Defensively, L.A. has been, excepting the Buffalo Bills game, stingy versus both run and pass. Getting Aaron Donald and Myles…

The Rams defeated the Eagles 24-20. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams dominated the Arizona Cardinals with a convincing 34-6 victory , but the win did not come without a few injuries – which has been typical for LA this year. Los Angeles suffered two significant injuries along the offensive line, a position that had been healthy for the first 8 1/2 weeks of the season. In a strange sequence of events, Los Angeles lost both centers during Sunday’s divisional matchup. Rams postgame notes — Rams 34, Cardinals 6 Center Coleman Shelton got hurt, then backup Dylan McMahon got hurt after replacing him. Bill Murray also came in. Sean McVay on the center spot: "Can't say enough about Beaux Limmer. He starts the game at guard, slides into center."… — NFL Wire (@nflpresserwire_) November 16, 2026 Coleman Shelton, C Coleman Shelton was the first to go down, suffering a hamstring injury during the Rams’ second offensive series of the game. Shelton was initially considered doubtful to return before eventually being ruled out for the remainder of the afternoon. Dylan McMahon, C Unfortunately, his replacement didn’t last much longer. Backup center Dylan McMahon suffered a knee injury shortly after entering the game and was also ruled out. Suddenly, the Rams were without their top two options at center. Sean McVay and the coaching staff responded by moving Beaux Limmer from left guard to center and inserting Bill Murray at left guard. The adjustments allowed the offense to continue operating without significant disruption. The good news for Los Angeles is that the team now enters its Week 11 bye, providing additional time for both Shelton and McMahon to recover. With a challenging stretch of games approaching, getting healthy along the offensive line will be particularly important considering Steve Avila (hamstring) was injured in Week 9 and is expected to miss multiple weeks. The Rams will need all hands on deck when they return to action against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, November 25.

summary: The NFC playoff picture is beginning to take shape, but the Los Angeles Rams are still on the outside looking in. full_text: The NFC playoff picture is beginning to take shape, but the Los Angeles Rams are still on the outside looking in. Despite remaining firmly in the postseason hunt, the Rams currently sit ninth in the NFC standings, just outside the playoff picture with several teams competing for the conference’s remaining spots. Their latest win over the Arizona Cardinals certainly helps their postseason hopes, but there is still work to be done if Los Angeles wants to secure a playoff berth. With the NFC West race heating up and the conference standings continuing to shift, every remaining game carries significant weight. The Rams have positioned themselves to make a push, but they can no longer afford to let opportunities slip away. The NFC North & NFC West Playoff Race with 8 Weeks Remaining pic.twitter.com/xietx29RrW — ProGridSports (@ProGridSports) November 16, 2026 Current NFC Standings… #1 Seed: San Francisco 49ers (8-1) San Francisco is going to finish with the NFC’s #1 seed. It’s just a matter of what week they lock it up. #2 Seed: Detroit Lions (7-2) The Detroit Lions may have moved up in the NFC standings over the last few weeks but now its come at the cost of Aidan Hutchison being out for the rest of the season due to a likely ACL tear via a sack celebration. Yikes… I’m not sure the Lions are built to win track meets even despite having the easiest schedule in the NFL In all likelihood, Detroit finishes as the 6 or 7 seed. #3 Seed: New York Giants (5-3-1) By default. The NFC East is terrible. #4 Seed: Carolina Panthers (4-5) Also a division that no one wants to outright win – the NFC South. This week Carolina is in the poll position. Next week it will be? #5 Seed: Minnesota Vikings (7-2) The addition of Kirk Cousins will make the NFC North race interesting. The Vikings simply have to be mediocre on offense and they will guarantee themselves a playoff birth. #6 Seed: Chicago Bears (7-2) The Bears should finish as the #2 or #5 seed. They have a more complete team than Detroit. #7 Seed: Green Bay Packers (6-4) Green Bay has the tiebreaker over Seattle due to conference win percentage. Green Bay may be playing for its postseason life in Week 12 because a 5th NFC conference loss may be too tough to overcome. #8 Seed: Seattle Seahawks (6-4) Seattle has the tiebreaker over Los Angeles because of divisional record. Seattle has a bye in Week 11 but will have two weeks to prepare for the 49ers. A Seattle win could make the NFC West a three way race again. But is this Sam Darnold’s team or Drew Lock’s? #9 Seed: Los Angeles Rams (6-4) The Rams are on the outside looking in right now. They have rattled off four straight wins (albeit against the Raiders, Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals). A Week 11 bye comes at the right time as the team needs to get healthy for its last 7 games which features: Green Bay, Seattle (x2), San Francisco, Dallas, Tampa Bay, and Kansas City. All those games are against competition still in the playoff hunt, if not currently positioned to make the playoffs. Another interesting note on the Rams is that they are 4-1 on the road this year. And that bodes well for the team as they will likely have to navigate 3 road playoff games if they want to play for Super Bowl LXI.

title: Ronnie Rivers’ game-ending performance makes history
summary: Ronnie Rivers did more than help the Los Angeles Rams secure a 34-6 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The third-string running back put together a historic performance, taking 15 consecutive rushing attempts to close out the game and accomplishing something that had not been seen in the NFL in 25 years. With 12:15 […]
full_text: Ronnie Rivers did more than help the Los Angeles Rams secure a 34-6 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The third-string running back put together a historic performance, taking 15 consecutive rushing attempts to close out the game and accomplishing something that had not been seen in the NFL in 25 years. With 12:15 remaining in the fourth quarter, the Rams took possession at their own 4-yard line. Rather than putting the ball in the air, Sean McVay turned to Rivers and let his running back take over. The result was a remarkable 17-play drive that effectively ended Arizona’s afternoon. Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers Ronnie Rivers pic.twitter.com/EsU0LjBddo — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 15, 2026 Rivers carried the football 15 straight times, totaling 81 yards on the possession. He helped Los Angeles drain the clock down to the two-minute warning before Matthew Stafford took two kneel-downs to finish the game. The drive consumed more than 10 minutes of game time, leaving the Cardinals without another opportunity to possess the football. But the accomplishment was even bigger than simply running out the clock. According to ESPN Research, Rivers became the first NFL player in the last 25 seasons to record at least 15 touches on a single drive. The previous high during that span was 13. Run Ronnie Run 🏃🏾‍♂️ Ronnie Rivers closed the Rams game in historical fashion! @ThriftyIceCream #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/bv85SmsGU1 — ESPN Los Angeles (@ESPNLosAngeles) November 16, 2026 For a running back who primarily contributes on special teams and is the third string running back, it was an incredible opportunity to make his mark. Rivers turned 15 consecutive handoffs into NFL history, putting an exclamation point on the Rams’ fourth consecutive victory.

title: Rams’ Sean McVay changing personnel again?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have never been afraid to get creative with their offensive personnel groupings, and injuries are once again forcing Sean McVay to think outside the box. What started with 11 personnel has evolved into 13 personnel and, most recently, 20 personnel as the Rams continue searching for ways to keep their offense […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have never been afraid to get creative with their offensive personnel groupings, and injuries are once again forcing Sean McVay to think outside the box. What started with 11 personnel has evolved into 13 personnel and, most recently, 20 personnel as the Rams continue searching for ways to keep their offense productive despite losing key playmakers. McVay’s ability to adapt when his back is against the wall is one of his greatest strengths as a head coach. Rather than stubbornly sticking to an offensive identity that no longer fits the available personnel, McVay has consistently found ways to maximize the players at his disposal. The Rams’ latest adjustment is simply another example of that creativity. 11 personnel In 2017, McVay began building an offense around 11 personnel, featuring one running back, one tight end, and three wide receivers. Cooper Kupp was an important piece of that identity. During training camp, McVay recognized Kupp’s ability to operate in tight spaces and perform some of the responsibilities traditionally associated with a tight end while maintaining the route-running finesse of a wide receiver. Kupp’s versatility helped make the formation so difficult to defend. The Rams could spread defenses out while still having receivers capable of winning underneath and creating opportunities after the catch. The Rams dominated the NFL in 11 personnel usage from 2017-2024. Since the data was tracked from 2021-2024 by Sharp Football Analysis , LA led the NFL with 89% of their play calls. 13 personnel Fast forward to 2025, and McVay found another way to reinvent his offense. After losing Puka Nacua to injury, including his absence against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, the Rams leaned into 13 personnel, featuring one running back and three tight ends. The Rams used Camden Yards in Baltimore to test their new personnel change and since then, the Rams have been at the forefront of leading the NFL in 13 usage. Rather than trying to replace Nacua’s production with another traditional receiver, McVay used his tight ends to create mismatches, establish the running game, and give Matthew Stafford different throwing windows. What initially looked like an injury-driven adjustment became a legitimate offensive identity. 20 is the new 13 Sean McVay deserves a lot of credit for the way the Rams offense performed today without Puka, Davante, Ferg and others. He pivoted to a personnel grouping he had never used before as the Rams' head coach. https://t.co/2VWk6UJQ8r — Cameron DaSilva (@camdasilva) November 16, 2026 20 personnel Now, in Week 10 against the Arizona Cardinals, McVay introduced another wrinkle. With Terrance Ferguson, Nacua, and Davante Adams unavailable, the Rams turned to 20 personnel, featuring two running backs and three wide receivers. Rams have gone with 20 Pony personnel with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum both on the field as their main personnel grouping today. Split back formation on all of them with a 100% pass rate so far. pic.twitter.com/6cA7N1hQVF — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 15, 2026 The grouping gave the Rams another way to create offensive opportunities without relying on their depleted tight end and receiver rooms. Los Angeles used the grouping for 17 plays, generating 197 yards and a touchdown. Three different personnel identities, all built around the same philosophy. McVay doesn’t need a perfect roster to manufacture an effective offense. He just needs to find another way to attack.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 01: Coleman Shelton #65 of the Los Angeles Rams leaves the field after defeating the Los Angeles Chargers 24-9 in a game at SoFi Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Inglewood, California. Duarte (@michaeljduarte) November 15, 2026 Latest Rams injuries puts Matthew Stafford in terrible position ahead of pivotal game vs. Packers (nypost) “Starting center Coleman Shelton exited early in the first half with a hamstring injury. His replacement, Dylan McMahon, suffered a knee injury shortly before halftime, forcing the Rams into another round of musical chairs. Beaux Limmer, already starting at left guard for the injured Steve Avila (hamstring), shifted to center while Bill Murray took over at left guard.“ The Sports Report: Shorthanded Rams rout the Cardinals (latimes.com) “And not just when the typically forthcoming Rams coach deflects credit or sidesteps answering a question. No, McVay showed an uncanny change of direction — and formations — when he switched to a tight-end heavy set that helped the Rams’ offense flourish into the NFL’s most productive unit. On Sunday, with star receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the resourceful McVay masterfully did it again.“ 4 winners and 2 losers from Rams’ resounding win over the Cardinals (ramblinfan) “Churning out the clock in garbage time, running back Ronnie Rivers set a career-high in rushing yards with a magnificent 15-carry, 81-yard performance – all on the Rams’ final drive. Bonkers. In the end, there were far too many highlights to acknowledge them all. What follows is an attempt to pick out a few deserving Rams, along with a pair of losers. Despite the final score it was not, in fact, all sunshine and rainbows. Winners and losers from Rams’ Week 10 win in Arizona Winner – Blake Corum Firsts of note: Corum’s first 100-rushing-yard game since Week 13 last year (also vs. the Cardinals); Rams’ first individual 100-yard rusher this season.“ Arizona Cardinals Daily Links: Cardinals given ‘F’ in lopsided loss to Rams (sports.yahoo) “There truly wasn’t much in the way of positives to cling to in this one, which is why CBS Sports’ John Breech gave the Cardinals a big fat “F” for their most recent performance. Here’s what he hadto say: “ Carson Beck’s first career start was a total disaster. When you’re a rookie QB, it helps when you have a ground game that can take some pressure off you and/or an offensive line that can protect you, but Beck had neither of those. Beck got sacked five times and he threw two interceptions, including one that Devin Duvernay practically handed to the Rams. The Cardinals had a big first quarter with 71 yards, but they never really moved the ball after that, totaling just 52 yards for the rest of the game. If this is what the Cardinals are going to look like for the second half of the year, don’t expect many fireworks from this team for the rest of the season. “ Rams win their 4th straight game, overcoming a slow start to crush the Cardinals 34-6 (espn) “But the Rams continued to show their depth and resourcefulness Sunday in a 34-6 road victory over the Arizona Cardinals , picking up their fourth straight win heading into a much-needed bye week. “Luckily, we’ve got a lot of good football players at different positions,” Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said. “Really proud of those guys, just their composure, their effort, and their ability to not get a lot of reps in practice and still go in there and execute in the game. It’s awesome.” Stafford threw for 249 yards and three touchdowns behind third-string center Limmer for most of the game, Blake Corum gained 100 yards on the ground and the Rams overcame a slow start by scoring 31 straight points to close the game.“ Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur delivers brutal truth bomb on Arizona’s season (sports.yahoo) “The Arizona Cardinals hit another low point in a lopsided loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday , and head coach Mike LaFleur did not pretend that help was on the way. Arizona fell 34-6 at State Farm Stadium, dropping to 3-7 on the season. After the game, LaFleur revealed the blunt message he delivered to his players. “I said, I owe it to you guys to tell you the truth. There’s no magic savior coming right now. Like, this is what we got. And we can make plays, like you guys believe in yourself. Like, you can make these plays, you can help everyone. You know, we can collectively play better than that. And I really believe that. And I know some people might not, but I do,” LaFleur said, via PHNX Cardinals.“ Division rivals Rams demolish Cardinals 34-6 (azfamily) “The Los Angeles Rams overcame a slow start to earn their fourth straight win by beating the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 on Sunday.” From the Podium: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford and Blake Corum detail Rams’ dominant win over Cardinals (therams.com) “GLENDALE, Ariz. — The Rams get their revenge on the Cardinals with a 34-6 win in Arizona, extending their win streak to four games and heading into the bye week with a 6-4 record. The defense was highlighted by five sacks and two interceptions, as the offense shared the wealth in the passing game for 249 yards and was led by a rushing attack that accounted for 202 yards. Head coach Sean McVay, quarterback Matthew Stafford and running back Blake Corum talked about the offense’s creativity and complementary football from the podium.“ “THAT’S HOW YOU GO INTO THE BYE!” Sean McVay’s victory speech after Week 10 win vs. Cardinals (therams.com) Watch Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s victory speech after Sunday’s Week 10 win against the Arizona Cardinals. Matthew Stafford, Rams offense spread the wealth in win over Cardinals (therams.com) “Without Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, questions all week were centered around who could be the individual player that would step up for the Rams. Instead, Stafford elected to share the wealth in the passing game to get everyone involved. “Luckily we got a lot of good football players at different positions,” Stafford said. “Obviously, some young guys got some more opportunities today in the receiver room. I thought our tight ends played fantastic. Both our backs played great.” Against Arizona, Stafford connected with nine different receivers, tight ends and running backs. And no one pass catcher had more than three receptions, while three different players had a receiving touchdown. “(We were) just trying to spread the ball around,” Stafford said. “Obviously, wasn’t perfect, but proud of those guys. Each guy kind of got their opportunity and made the most of it, which I was happy for.” Stafford was 18-for-26 for 249 yards, three touchdowns and an interception, averaging 13.8 yards per reception. Multiple catches went for big gains of 20-or-more yards to boost that yards-per-reception number — including a 31-yard catch from Tutu Atwell, a 22-yard catch for CJ Daniels Jr., 27-yard and 44-yard receptions from Konata Mumpfield and a 22-yard touchdown reception from Xavier Smith.“…

title: Kirk Cousins looks sharp in 1st game after being traded by Las Vegas Raiders
summary: Week 10 saw the Las Vegas Raiders lose their sixth game in seven tries, falling 21-13 to the Seattle Seahawks. But let’s check in on a few old friends and see how the weekend treated Kirk Cousins, Amik Robertson and Jakobi Meyers. Kirk Cousins Score: 30-10 Vikings win Stats: 21/31 (67.7%), 207 yards, 2 TDs, […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 10 saw the Las Vegas Raiders lose their sixth game in seven tries, falling 21-13 to the Seattle Seahawks . But let’s check in on a few old friends and see how the weekend treated Kirk Cousins, Amik Robertson and Jakobi Meyers. Kirk Cousins Score: 30-10 Vikings win Stats: 21/31 (67.7%), 207 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 3 rushes, 11 rushing yards Cousins didn’t get to practice with his new teammates until last Wednesday, but that was hard to tell on Sunday. He was very sharp and hit the ground running, allowing Minnesota to jump out to a 17-0 halftime lead in Green Bay. Justin Jefferson was certainly happy to see his old quarterback back, as Cousins targeted Jefferson 13 times, connecting for nine catches and 74 yards, the most catches and third-most yards the receiver has had in a single game this season. That helped the Vikings keep pace in the NFC North, as they’re tied with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears for first place at 7-2. Kirk Cousins man I’ll tell you what pic.twitter.com/5vX8egvFAM — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) November 15, 2026 Amik Robertson Score: 24-21 Commanders win Stats: 5 tackles, 2 TFLs, 1 PD This was a crazy game to start the weekend, as the Washington Commanders pulled off a comeback on Thursday Night Football to take down the division-leading New York Giants. Robertson was a big part of the effort, making a couple of notable plays against the run and coming up with a PBU. According to Pro Football Focus , he was targeted seven times and gave up four catches for 43 yards against the Giants. The 2020 fourth-round pick has quietly been having a good year with a career-high 75.7 PFF grade and an elite 90.1 mark against the run. Jakobi Meyers Score: 40-23 Jaguars win Stats: 3 catches, 34 yards Meyers didn’t have a big game on Sunday, but it’s been a while since we’ve checked in on him. The veteran receiver is far from the No. 1 target in Jacksonville, Parker Washington is, but he plays the role of a reliable safety net well. Fairly consistently, Meyers sits around 30 to 60 receiving yards per game and has totaled 26 catches for 374 yards and two touchdowns through nine games.

full_text: (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have been expected to add to their quarterback room and Monday they did. Las Vegas announced they have signed veteran quarterback Brett Rypien to the practice squad. He joins new starter Fernando Mendoza and backup Aidan O’Connell. The need for another quarterback came last Tuesday when the Raiders traded then starter Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round draft pick. Rypien, 30, entered the NFL in 2019 and this is the 12th NFL program (he was with Minnesota twice) he has been part of. Rypien played in four games for the Denver Broncos when Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak was their passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach in 2022. Rypien last threw a pass in a regular-season game in 2023. To make room for Rypien on the practice squad, defensive end Bralen Trice was released. He spent less than three weeks in the Raiders’ program.

full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders were riding high after Fernando Mendoza’s first touchdown. However, they received bad news after their first drive of the game. Brock Bowers injured his ankle while blocking on a run play in the first quarter. They took him inside the tarp, and he returned briefly. After the touchdown, they took him to the locker room. Reports indicate he is questionable to return. Times like this are why you paid Michael Mayer. He and Ian Thomas will have to step up and take over at tight end. Mendoza will have to lean on those two to make plays and other weapons on offense. Hopefully it is not a serious injury for Bowers, as he is vital to the offense. He is the best tight end in football, and he will be missed if he can’t go for now. Update: Bowers has returned to the game after coming back from the locker room. Now, Bowers went back to the locker room in the second quarter. The Raiders ruled him out of the game at halftime. Raiders’ coach Klint Kubiak didn’t have an update on Bowers after the game. Monday, NFL Media reported Bowers did not suffer a major injury and he is “day-to-day.” thus he may be able to play Sunday at Denver, Monday afternoon, Kubiak said Bowers is “day-to-day.” Kubiak said the injury wasn’t as bad as the team initially thought, but he did add it’s still a significant injury that will be monitored.

title: Klint Kubiak coached scared in Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 10 loss to Seattle Seahawks
summary: Fernando Mendoza’s starting debut for the Las Vegas Raiders started out hot, with the Raiders taking a 10-7 lead into the locker room at halftime. However, a second-half collapse led to a 21-13 Seattle Seahawks victory, handing the Raiders their sixth loss in seven games. That leads to another somber mood for this week’s winners […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza’s starting debut for the Las Vegas Raiders started out hot, with the Raiders taking a 10-7 lead into the locker room at halftime. However, a second-half collapse led to a 21-13 Seattle Seahawks victory , handing the Raiders their sixth loss in seven games. That leads to another somber mood for this week’s winners and losers. LOSER: Klint Kubiak To Kubiak’s credit, he had a good opening script that included a lot of easy throws for Mendoza. That led to scores (a touchdown and a field goal) on Vegas’ first two possessions. However, the offense put points on the board just once on the eight proceeding possessions, including a run of five straight three-and-outs to begin the second half. Of course, Brock Bowers getting injured early and leaving the game at halftime didn’t help, but neither did Kubiak’s play calling. He even left meat on the bone during the field goal drive in the second quarter, running the ball on third and five when Mendoza had completed six of seven passes for 41 yards and had an eight-yard scramble to get the offense into the red zone during the possession. The run, unsurprisingly, was stuffed for a one-yard gain. That ended up setting a precedent for the rest of the game, as the offensive play caller got way too conservative after any negative play happened, allowing the lost yards to turn into drive killers. Sure, not having Bowers for the second half played a factor, but that’s where a creative offensive mind should help bridge the gap by scheming other players open. Ultimately, Kubiak coached scared by trying to protect Mendoza and ended up doing the quarterback a disservice. He admitted as much after the game, stating: “I’ve got to help him better in second half. What happened in second half to go 0-for-7 on third down is unacceptable,” while also saying he should have called more bootlegs. LOSER: Eric Stokes Stokes wasn’t the secondary’s biggest problem against Seattle and hasn’t been the unit’s biggest issue all season. However, he hasn’t been the stabilizing presence he was expected to be either. The veteran is less than 200 yards away from giving up a career-high in receiving yards (417) this season and has already matched his career-high in touchdowns allowed with four, according to Pro Football Focus . The biggest play that landed Stokes on the losers list this week was a 34-yard touchdown to Cooper Kupp — Kupp’s only target of the game — on a scramble drill where the corner seemingly gave up on the play. That can’t happen from someone who is supposed to be a leader in the defensive backfield, and he ended up giving up the second-most receiving yards (54) on the team for the entire game, per PFF . LOSER: JSN Coverage Plan While Stokes got singled out above, he didn’t do a terrible job against Jaxon Smith-Njigba, drawing two targets and allowing just one catch for 11 yards. The problem was that the reigning Offensive Player of the Year was targeted 10 times and caught eight passes for 171 yards and a touchdown, and it’s impossible to single out one player as the primary culprit. JSN drew at least one target against seven different defenders and caught at least one pass against all of them en route to posting his season-high yardage total, according to PFF . The most notable catch came on a third-and-three scramble drill that left linebacker Quay Walker isolated against the receiver and led to a 71-yard touchdown, which is the play most people will harp on. But the fact of the matter is that Smith-Njigba still had seven catches for 100 yards and five first downs outside of that reception. From defensive coordinator Rob Leonard to the players on the field, it was a total failure by the entire coverage unit. WINNER: Tyler Linderbaum Linderbaum faced plenty of scrutiny earlier in the season for not living up to his contract. However, the free-agent signing has been playing a lot better recently, and Sunday was arguably his best game with the Silver and Black. He posted season-highs in overall PFF grade ( 84.2 ) and as a run blocker (88.8). Since Week 7, Linderbaum ranks first among centers with an 81.7 grade . LOSER: Jack Bech Tre Tucker could be listed here too, because the Raiders needed a pass catcher to step up once Bowers went down, but no one did. Meanwhile, Bech drew more targets than anyone on the roster with seven and only managed to come away with two catches for 10 yards. PFF had him on the hook for one drop, and at least one more target could have gone down as a drop, too. Also, contested catches and run blocking are supposed to be the second-year pro’s calling card. He was 0-for-2 on contested targets and posted a team-low 33.5 run-blocking grade . LOSER: Spencer Burford Speaking of run-blocking grades, Burford was one spot ahead of Bech with a 43.2 mark. He was also on the hook for three pressures — including a sack — in pass protection, according to PFF . What’s frustrating is that the majority of the offensive line graded out well in the ground game, with Kolton Miller posting a 90.9, Linderbaum at 88.8 and Trey Zuhn III coming in at 71.7. But the unit was let down by one lineman and poor perimeter blocking. LOSER: Michael Mayer Part of the poor perimeter blocking is that Mayer had 15 run-blocking snaps and posted the third-lowest grade (44.6) in that department. He also had a missed chip block in pass protection that led to Mendoza getting hit on a third-down throw, which was open for a first down if the pass wasn’t impacted by the pressure. Also, Mayer is a prime candidate to step up without Bowers on the field. Instead, the second tight end had just two catches for 16 yards.
author: Matt Holder

title: Mendoza, Raiders get punched in face the by visiting Seahawks 21-13
summary: For two quarters and the first possession of the third quarter, the Las Vegas Raiders held a precarious 10-7 advantage against the visiting Seattle Seahawks this past Sunday. But that opening second-half possession was a sign of the avalanche that was coming. It as a three-and-out series where the Silver & Black netted negative two […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images For two quarters and the first possession of the third quarter, the Las Vegas Raiders held a precarious 10-7 advantage against the visiting Seattle Seahawks this past Sunday. But that opening second-half possession was a sign of the avalanche that was coming. It as a three-and-out series where the Silver & Black netted negative two yards. That showcased the second-half adjustments Mike Macdonald’s Seahawks made to walk out of Allegiant Stadium 21-13 victors. “I’ve got to give the Raiders a lot of credit,” Macdonald said. “In the first half, I thought they had a good plan. They made it challenging for us in the first half. Our guys did a great job adjusting and sticking together and finding a way to win in the end.” Realizing the Raiders were starting a rookie quarterback in Fernando Mendoza and without all-world tight end Brock Bowers — who injured his ankle early in the first quarter and returned to the game, only to exit in the second quarter — Macdonald dialed up the pressure resulting in four-second half sacks. All of those arrived in the fourth quarter with the Raiders in catchup-mode and neither head coach and offensive play caller Klint Kubiak or Mendoza had an answer. “I thought overall when we lost Brock, you definitely saw a big change in production. So I look at myself; I have to do a much better job of moving the ball, getting and spreading the ball around,” Kubiak said after the game. “Yeah, Seahawks have a fantastic defense. We’ve seen it all season, so a lot of credit to them and Coach Macdonald. Fantastic,” Mendoza said after the game. “And it’s good to get punched in the face because now it’s a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game, as a future hopeful leader of this offense.” the @Seahawks defense came to play 😤 pic.twitter.com/uEiwuyKXyd — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 Like Mendoza said above, dissecting the game tape and learning from this battering he received from Seattle’s defense is integral for Las Vegas going forward. How the quarterback takes the hard lessons learned facing a top NFL defense going forward in the Raiders remaining seven games — four of which are AFC West clashes — will dictate the future of the Silver & Black. Mendoza did get walloped quite a bit by the Seahawks aggressive defense but he took the hits and kept getting back up. Surely his 6-foot-5 and 225-pound frame helps absorb that punishment but seeing their franchise quarterback getting rocked isn’t ideal. To his credit, Mendoza shouldered the blame for the sacks for holding on to the ball too long and not getting rid of it absolving his offensive linemen of the blame. The accountability for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft is endearing, but absolution has no business in the Raiders locker room, despite what the 23-year-old signal caller said at the podium. The ineffectiveness on offense was offensive and it was only a matter of time before the Seahawks offense found some rhythm to take advantage of the Raiders much-maligned defense. With the impotence from Kubiak’s offense to open the second half, Seattle engineered an eight-play, 87-yard touchdown drive to jump ahead 14-10. And, after another three-and-out where Las Vegas could only gain a single yard before punting, the Seahawks hit the jackpot play: Elite (and arguably the best) wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s freelance sprint that left Raiders linebacker Quay Walker and cornerback Eric Stokes in the dust for a 71-yard catch-and-run touchdown. Drew Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba is looking like a dangerous connection 👀 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/6hXecLdtM6 — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 15, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as JSN had the Raiders defense in a blender: —Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby powered the team’s defensive effort with eight total tackles, four stops for loss, and a sack. But unlike Mendoza, who was sacked six times and hit 12 times, Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock was sacked and hit three times, respectively. —Seattle nickel cornerback Devon Witherspoon paced the Seahawks defense with two sacks while DeMarcus Lawrence, Byron Murphy II, Dante Fowler, and Derick Hall each had a sack. Witherspoon and Lawrence paced Seattle with three quarterback hits, each. —Lock finished 14 of 17 for 240 yards and two passing touchdowns. He also added 20 yards on six carries. Running back Zack Charbonnet paced Seattle’s ground game with 20 carries for 94 yards. Rookie Jadarian Price had nine totes for 36 yards and a touchdown. —Las Vegas pitiful run game was powered by Mike Washington Jr. who finished with eight carries for 23 yards (2.9 yards per carry average). Fellow tailback Ashton Jeanty had nine carries for 18 yards (2.0 yards per carry) and tight end Michael Mayer had one carry for two yards. —The Raiders avoided setting a new modern era record of allowing 30 or more points for the seven-straight game. Instead the team is tied for that awful record in six-straight contests. But allowing 150 rushing yards and 232 air yards to the Seahawks ailing offense wasn’t ideal. —Mendoza, meanwhile, finished 17 of 29 for 143 yards passing with no touchdowns or interceptions. He added 22 yards on six carries including his first-career touchdown — a 10-yard run that was a play similar to the one he scored on during Indiana’s national title win last season. Fernando Mendoza rushes it in for his first career TD 🗣️ SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gcKUNMIZUH — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Quote of Note “Yeah, in the second half, because of how the game was going, our defense did a fantastic job, but because of how we were playing offensively, at the forefront myself, we got behind there, and so it’s a little bit more of a passing situation. And then Coach (Mike) Macdonald dialed it up and did great. There was a couple times that we tried to check someone else’s protection, and he was playing chess, and he fooled me, and he got me a couple times. And I think it’s important to learn and grow from this, to throw my hot routes more often, to throw accurate balls when getting hit, and to practice that rather than everything just being sunshine and rainbows, then move forward and give our team a better chance each and every week.” —Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza on the second-half performance “He got up after every hit. … He’s a tough dude. He’’s ready to fight, right? And it should piss us off when he’’s on the ground and you have to pick him up. … We’ve got to sit in there and protect him.” —Las Vegas Raiders tight end Ian Thomas on rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza Up Next The 4-6 Raiders hit the road for a Week 11 matchup at the 7-2 Denver Broncos next Sunday. The hard-charging Broncos come off their bye week victors of five-straight games and are tied atop the AFC West with the Kansas City Chiefs. Not only that, but Denver is unbeaten at home this season at 4-0. So the division tilt will be another daunting task for Kubiak, Mendoza, and Co. The Mile High matchup between the two AFC West foes is the first of the divisional two-game tilt and both will face off again in under a month from now.

So, the only team we’re checking in on is the Kansas City Chiefs, who took advantage of the Broncos being off. Chiefs vs. Falcons Score: 35-13 Chiefs win Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 22/35 (62.9%), 348 yards, 5 TDs, 0 INTs, 2 rushes, 15 yards RB Emmett Johnson: 22 carries, 101 yards, 6 catches, 70 yards, 2 receiving TDs WR Josh Downs: 4 catches, 53 yards, 1 TD EDGE George Karlaftis: 2 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 1 PD CB Mansoor Delane: 3 tackles, 2 PDs No Kenneth Walker III, no problem for Kansas City’s offense. Johnson stepped in, and it was like the Chiefs weren’t even missing an Offensive Player of the Year candidate. The rookie totaled over 170 yards from scrimmage. Also, Downs, who was added at the trade deadline and playing in his first game for his new team, looked sharp with a handful of catches and a score, showcasing some immediate chemistry with Mahomes, who might have played his best game of the season. After a two-game skid, the Chiefs have bounced back with back-to-back wins to pull even with the Broncos at 7-2. Since those two split the season series, Kansas City has the current tiebreaker with a 3-1 division record to Denver’s 2-1. title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins Week 10 defeat
summary: The Miami Dolphins traveled to Indianapolis to take on the Colts on Sunday — and despite a spirited effort from an injury depleted squad that nearly eeked out their second victory on the season, the South Florida squad fell to their opponents by a score of 24-22. Unfortunately, Dolphins’ former kicker Zane Gonzalez missed two […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Michael Taaffe #16 of the Miami Dolphins is introduced prior to a game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins traveled to Indianapolis to take on the Colts on Sunday — and despite a spirited effort from an injury depleted squad that nearly eeked out their second victory on the season, the South Florida squad fell to their opponents by a score of 24-22. Unfortunately, Dolphins’ former kicker Zane Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point attempt in the loss — a performance that cost him his job on Monday. While the result wasn’t a positive one for the standings, it does keep Miami in the running for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Dolphins are currently third — sitting behind the winless Los Angeles Chargers and the single-win Tennessee Titans in the draft order. Losing to the Colts hurts the New York Jets’ draft stock, as they own the Colts’ first round selection due to the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. So, there’s your silver-lining. FINS UP Our Fins Up player of the week is rookie safety Michael Taaffe. Taaffe intercepted a Daniel Jones pass in the second quarter of Sunday’s loss, giving him a team-leading three interceptions on the season. The fifth round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has vastly outplayed his draft position thus far, giving Miami a player with game-changing ball skills in the secondary at a discount. Don’t look now, but Taaffe could soon find himself in the Defensive Rookie of the Year award conversation as he is currently tied for the league lead when it comes to most interceptions by a rookie defender this season. Will he win? Probably not, but having multiple players in the running (Jacob Rodriguez) is a very good thing for the future of Miami’s defense. FINS DOWN Our Fins Down personality is once again Special Teams coordinator Chris Tabor. As mentioned above, Miami’s former kicker Zane Gonzalez missed two field goal tries and an extra point try against the Colts. Those missed kicks cost the Dolphins a win and Gonzalez his job. However, his coach, Tabor, still remains employed despite burning through two kickers (Riley Patterson) this season, while also being the leader of a unit that has consistently ranked in the bottom-five of all special teams units in the NFL this season. In a year when wins and losses don’t necessarily mean as much as they would if the Dolphins were considered a viable contender for a playoff spot, Tabor keeping his job isn’t the end of the world, but general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan does have an opportunity to show his coaching staff, players, owner and fans of the franchise that he means business when it comes to preparation equaling production on game days. Let’s see if he takes it.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 10 loss to the Indianapolis Colts
summary: The Miami Dolphins were extremely shorthanded heading into their Week 10 road-trip against the Indianapolis Colts. Starting quarterback Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a lingering groin issue. Stud center Aaron Brewer missed Sunday’s tilt due a concussion he suffered in last week’s loss to the Detroit Lions. Defensive […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts runs with the ball against the Miami Dolphins during an NFL football game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins were extremely shorthanded heading into their Week 10 road-trip against the Indianapolis Colts. Starting quarterback Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a lingering groin issue. Stud center Aaron Brewer missed Sunday’s tilt due a concussion he suffered in last week’s loss to the Detroit Lions. Defensive leader Zach Sieler tore his biceps in that same loss — forcing him to not only miss Miami’s game against Indianapolis, but the rest of the 2026 season as well. Well, as we all know, adversity is opportunity . The Dolphins — while starting rookie quarterback Kyle McCord — nearly overcame all of that adversity to upset their foes on Sunday. Instead, despite a spirited effort from Jeff Hafley’s squad, Miami lost by two-points against Indianapolis, dropping their record to 1-8 on the year after falling by a score of 24-22. GOOD Miami’s rookie defensive backs shine In a season where finding bright spots has sometimes felt like searching for a needle in a haystack, seeing two young players make game-changing defensive plays for Miami on Sunday was encouraging. Rookie safety Michael Taaffe and rookie cornerback Chris Johnson each came away with an interception of Colts’ quarterback Daniel Jones. Taaffe got things started with an interception with 10:30 left in the second quarter — giving Miami’s defense a much-needed takeaway while the Colts were driving for points. It was Taaffe’s third interception on the season. Not bad for a 5th round pick! But it was Johnson who provided the highlight of the afternoon. Miami’s 1st round rookie cornerback intercepted Jones with 8:52 left in the 3rd-quarter and returned the ball 59 yards for a dazzling touchdown — giving Miami a big lift and injecting some life into a game that was quickly getting away from the South Florida squad. Obviously, one game doesn’t make a career, but Taaffe and Johnson have been playing solid football for the Dolphins all season long. There hasn’t been a whole lot to celebrate in Miami this year, but seeing two rookies stepping up when their team needs them is part of the fuel that keeps the fires of hope burning as Dolphins fans look towards a brighter future. Now, if only the rest of the defense could figure out how to stop somebody… BAD Dolphins gashed on the ground by Colts On Sunday, Indianapolis ran the football 34 times for 172 yards, averaging a whopping 5.1 yards per carry. The Colts didn’t need to get particularly creative. They didn’t need to rely on some elaborate offensive scheme or trick plays. They lined up, handed the football to their running backs Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan, and repeatedly found themselves moving the chains. The Indianapolis rushing attack consistently found room to operate, putting Miami’s defense on their heels and making life difficult for the Dolphins throughout the afternoon, despite the fact that Miami’s defense only gave up 104 yards passing. When an opposing offense can consistently pick up five yards every time it hands the ball off, you’re eventually going to run out of opportunities to get off the field. The Dolphins have plenty of things to figure out defensively, but stopping the run needs to be near the top of that list — especially when a date with Josh Allen, James Cook and the Buffalo Bills is circled on the calendar for next Sunday. UGLY Zane Gonzalez misses two field goals and an extra-point try in a two-point loss When the Dolphins gave kicker Riley Patterson his walking papers on October 20th so they could sign Zane Gonzalez to take over kicking duties for the team, fans were encouraged by the move. Fast forward four games and that warm and fuzzy feeling has vanished in a hurry. On Sunday, Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point try. That’s 7 points Gonzalez was unable to put on the board for a Dolphins team desperate for them. Reminder: Miami lost Sunday’s game by two points. Gonzalez’s first missed opportunity came on a 47-yard attempt in the first quarter. Later, after Miami had clawed their way back into the game, he missed the extra point try following Chris Johnson’s spectacular interception return for a touchdown. However, Miami’s kicker saved his most heart-breaking moment for the fourth quarter when he missed a long try that would have given the Dolphins the lead in a tight, back-and-forth contest. As I gaze into my crystal ball, I predict the Dolphins to look elsewhere for a place kicker in very short order. ___ The Dolphins, with their backs against the wall, played a close game against the Colts on Sunday. Alas, they fell short — dropping the team’s record to 1-8 on the year. Were you impressed with quarterback Kyle McCord’s first start? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up .
