title: Miami Dolphins news: Recapping Dolphins Week 10 loss to Colts
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost to the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, falling 24-22 and dropping to 1-8 in 2026. The game featured Miami starting a quarterback in his NFL debut, a shuffle among the defensive tackles due to injuries, an All-Pro center dealing with a conucssion, and a starting wide receiver missing the game due to […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Kyle McCord #14 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, falling 24-22 and dropping to 1-8 in 2026. The game featured Miami starting a quarterback in his NFL debut, a shuffle among the defensive tackles due to injuries, an All-Pro center dealing with a conucssion, and a starting wide receiver missing the game due to injury. Yet, none of those were the reason behind Miami’s two-point loss. Football is a team sport, and there are always moments on offense and defense that could have been executed better. The Dolphins’ offense gave up a defensive touchdown on a sack fumble – not ideal. The defense could have been tougher against the run, stopping Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan from leading the team to over 170 yards on the ground. But, even with those issues, Miami was within two points of pulling off the upset win. Miami did enough to win on offense and defense. They fell apart on special teams, specifically with placekicking. Kicker Zane Gonzalez missed a 47-yard field goal in the first quarter. After connecting on a 53-yard kick, he missed an extra point in the third quarter. He also missed a 51-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Miami lost seven points on three kicks from Gonzalez. Even the extra point would have changed things; a converted extra point in the third quarter could have let Miami kick a tying extra point in the fourth quarter instead of attempting a failed two-point conversion. Maybe it is too harsh to blame the loss on a single player, but Gonzalez missed kicks Miami had to have, and this is not the first misses he has had recently. Gonzalez has struggled since joining the Dolphins, first on the practice squad, then being promoted to the active roster for Sunday. In four games, he is 6-for-10 on field goal attempts and 6-for-7 on extra points. Gonzalez has also struggled on kickoffs, leading Miami to move to punter Bradley Pinion to handle those responsibilities. Miami should have come out of Indianapolis with a win. It was there for the taking. They just could not connect on the kicks that would have changed the result. The kicking woes were among the top talking points around the web following the game. title: Jordan Addison to Have Thumb Surgery, Miss Several Weeks
summary: As the Minnesota Vikings gear up for the stretch run of their 2026 season, they’re going to be without their #2 wide receiver for the next few weeks, at the very least. At his Monday press conference, Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell announced that wide receiver Jordan Addison will have thumb surgery and will miss […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 9: Jordan Addison #3 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a pass during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Minnesota Vikings gear up for the stretch run of their 2026 season, they’re going to be without their #2 wide receiver for the next few weeks, at the very least. At his Monday press conference, Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell announced that wide receiver Jordan Addison will have thumb surgery and will miss the next several weeks and could, potentially, wind up on injured reserve, a move that would cause him to miss a minimum of four games. Addison suffered what O’Connell called a “freak” injury during practice in the week leading up to Sunday’s game against Green Bay. He apparently tried to give it a go in pre-game warmups, but was ultimately deactivated for Sunday’s game and watched from the sidelines. In his absence, along with the absence of Jauan Jennings with a calf injury, Kirk Cousins was able to find alternative targets in Myles Price and Tai Felton. Price had four catches for 49 yards and a 38-yard touchdown, while Felton had three catches for 33 yards. Addison is now the second Vikings’ skill position player who will miss significant time because of a thumb injury this season. Running back Jordan Mason suffered a thumb injury that also required surgery in the Vikings’ Week 1 victory over Green Bay, returning to the lineup after the team’s Week 6 bye. Here’s hoping that the recovery for Jordan Addison goes as quickly and as smoothly as possible so that the Vikings can get him back into the lineup at the earliest available opportunity.

title: Vikes Views: Sunday King: Week 10 – Vikings at Packers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings strolled into Green Bay and destroyed the Packers, 30-10. It was another dominant performance by the Viking defense, so much so it’s hard not to pick nearly every player in the front 7. The Vikings offense looked much better under Kirk Cousins despite missing T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison. A win is […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Jalen Redmond #61 of the Minnesota Vikings sacks Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers during the third quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings strolled into Green Bay and destroyed the Packers, 30-10. It was another dominant performance by the Viking defense, so much so it’s hard not to pick nearly every player in the front 7. The Vikings offense looked much better under Kirk Cousins despite missing T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison. A win is always fun, a dismantling of Green Bay in Wisconsin is electrifying. Let’s take a look at Sunday’s best Vikings. Levi Drake Rodriguez The defensive front was overwhelming on Sunday. Levi led the team with 2 sacks and 4 hits on Jordan Love. Dallas Turner Turner showed off his versatile skill set on Sunday. He was in the backfield all day wreaking havoc. He recorded a sack on a bull rush straight through to Jordan Love and recovered the errant snap Love launched in the third quarter. Turner nearly added an interception as well, diving in coverage to break up a pass. Turner has become exactly the player the Vikings hoped they were getting when they drafted him in 2024. Eric Wilson Wilson was the signal caller (green dot) Sunday, filling the shoes of Blake Cashman. He also led the team with 7 tackles, including a sack of his own. Andrew Van Ginkel Van Ginkel made an immediate impact on the Packers’ 2nd offensive play of the game. He just stole the ball from TE Mark Redman. After the Vikings started with a three and out, he stepped up and gave them the ball back on the Green Bay 10. The Vikings were unable to punch it in, but it started them off on the right foot. Kirk Cousins Cousins wasn’t perfect on Sunday, but it was the best quarterbacked game by the Vikings this season. He made the throws neither of the previous quarterbacks could. The touchdown pass to Myles Price was a reprieve from the QB incompetence we’ve endured as fans. There’s no guarantee it will continue, but it was fun to enjoy yesterday. Honorable Mentions: Nolan Teasley – I originally had Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on my list, but the system only allows me six voting options. Trading for a starting QB mid-year is a bold move and it paid immediate dividends on Sunday. Jakobe Thomas – Thomas played his first game on Sunday. He took advantage of his window on special teams with a beautiful hit on the Packers kick returner to force a fumble. Harrison Smith, Elijah Williams, Kyle Van Noy, Jalen Redmond – they all had impact plays and were part of an elite defensive performance. There were too many to list. The Vikings have now beaten Green Bay twice this season by a combined score of 69-32.

title: Patriots playoff picture after loss to Lions in Week 10
summary: The New England Patriots are stumbling into their bye week, and — courtesy of their 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions — have also stumbled out of the AFC playoff picture. The reigning conference champions are now the eighth seed in the conference standings, and to make matters worse are expected to be without their […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are stumbling into their bye week, and — courtesy of their 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions — have also stumbled out of the AFC playoff picture. The reigning conference champions are now the eighth seed in the conference standings, and to make matters worse are expected to be without their starting quarterback for the foreseeable future. Let’s take a closer look at where they stand in the division and conference with Week 10 in the books. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (8-1) New England Patriots (5-5) New York Jets (2-8) Miami Dolphins (1-8) The Patriots retain their second position in the AFC East, but their chances of keeping the division crown are getting progressively smaller. For one, Sunday’s loss put them at 5-5, and 3.5 games behind an 8-1 Bills squad that has been firing on all cylinders this season. Additionally, Drake Maye’s injury situation creates an uncertain outlook for both himself and the Patriots as a whole. Considering all that, it would take a breakdown of monumental proportions for Buffalo to not win the division this year. New England does still enjoy a sizable cushion over the next two teams in the division, the Jets and Dolphins. However, if the team comes out looking like it did against the Lions after Maye was injured, the Patriots staying ahead of them in the standings is not a guarantee either. AFC playoff standings Buffalo Bills (8-1) Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) Denver Broncos (7-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) Cleveland Browns (6-4) On the bubble: 8. New England Patriots (5-5) , 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5), 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-6), 11. Houston Texans (3- 6) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 12. Indianapolis Colts (3-7), 13. New York Jets (2- 8 ), 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) , 15. Miami Dolphins (1-8), 16. Tennessee Titans (1-8) The Patriots dropped out of the playoff picture on Sunday and they are facing long odds to return. According to The Athletic’s playoff simulator , the team of head coach Mike Vrabel has only a 30% chance of making the postseason — the eighth-highest such number in the AFC, and the first time all season it has dipped below 50%. The odds speak against the Patriots, and so does their injury situation particularly at quarterback. It might become time to set the sights on 2027 sooner rather than later. NFC playoff standings San Francisco 49ers (8-1) Detroit Lions (7-2) New York Giants (5-3-1) Carolina Panthers (4-5) Minnesota Vikings (7-2) Chicago Bears (7-2) Green Bay Packers (6-4) On the bubble: 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4), 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4), 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-6), 11. Washington Commanders (3-5-1), 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6), 13. New Orleans Saints (3-6), 14. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 15. Arizona Cardinals (3-7), 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) Thanks to their win over New England, the Lions are now the new leaders in the NFC North because of their superior head-to-head tiebreaker against the Vikings and Bears. Speaking of the Vikings, they climbed up a spot after their 30-10 win over the same Green Bay team that blew out the Patriots the previous week. The Packers stay in the seventh seed, but the Seahawks and Rams are booth breathing down their necks.

title: Patriots reportedly weighing QB additions despite confidence in Tommy DeVito
summary: The New England Patriots are expected to be without starting quarterback Drake Maye for an extended period. Maye reportedly suffered a fractured ankle in Germany, an injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the season. With only Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton on the roster then at quarterback, the Patriots are reportedly […]
full_text: Nov 15, 2026; Munich, DEU; New England Patriots quarterback Tommy DeVito (16) throws during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Allianz Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots are expected to be without starting quarterback Drake Maye for an extended period. Maye reportedly suffered a fractured ankle in Germany, an injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the season. With only Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton on the roster then at quarterback, the Patriots are reportedly expected to explore the market for additional help during their bye week, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. Those options include free agents such as former Patriot Jimmy Garoppolo, who has experience playing under offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, or signing a quarterback from another team’s practice squad. Moments before Schultz’s report, head coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he did not currently anticipate the team adding another quarterback. “I don’t see that being the case right now. But we’ll have conversations and we’ll discuss it and we’ll look and see,” Vrabel said Monday morning. “Tommy and Behren have been in our system and working. Behren’s been improving. Been working each week and I know if he has to play for us that he’ll be ready to go. I’m excited for this challenge and I hope that everybody else is because that’s really what we’re at.” DeVito struggled after replacing Maye on Sunday, completing just 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception. The 28-year-old had issues seeing the field and with ball placement. Vrabel, however, expressed confidence moving forward with DeVito, who the team signed to a two-year extension this offseason to elevate him as Maye’s primary backup. “The assessment [on DeVito’s performance Sunday] was pretty much like the team, it wasn’t good enough,” Vrabel said. “I think there was some things that he missed. But also not having a ton of live action since training camp, I think he’ll be ready to go coming out of the bye. “He’ll be ready to look at some things and understand. Whether thats being able to transfer up in the pocket, get us in the right play, or get the ball out quicker, look at protections, rotation, whatever that may all be. I think that’ll all improve. So, I have a lot of confidence in Tommy and I know his toughness will be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need.”

title: Mike Vrabel gives updates on Drake Maye after injury
summary: Update 11/16/2026: Mike Vrabel gives updates on Drake Maye after injury Mike Vrabel met with the media at Gillette Stadium on Monday at noon, and the topic of Drake Maye’s ankle injury was also discussed. He did not provide any specific updates beyond the information already out there, but he did say that Maye’s availability […]
full_text: Update 11/16/2026: Mike Vrabel gives updates on Drake Maye after injury Mike Vrabel met with the media at Gillette Stadium on Monday at noon, and the topic of Drake Maye’s ankle injury was also discussed. He did not provide any specific updates beyond the information already out there, but he did say that Maye’s availability coming out of the Week 11 bye is in doubt. “I’m not going to make any comments about his status until he gets back here. He’s en route back here,” Vrabel said about Maye, who per a prior statement of his had a longer stay in Germany to make him fit for travel. “He stayed with a few of our people, and they’re en route back here. Once he get back here, our people are able to visit with him again and talk to him again I think we’ll have more to offer. But I wouldn’t imagine him being available when we come out of the bye.” Original story 11/16/2026: Mike Vrabel gives update on Drake Maye after injury The New England Patriots flew back from Germany to the United States shortly after their loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. One player wasn’t with them: quarterback Drake Maye, who was unable to finish the game after suffering an ankle injury in the first quarter. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, Maye initially stayed behind to best prepare him for the trip across the Atlantic. “The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,” Vrabel said during an appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday morning. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” Maye hurt his ankle on a third-down sack on the game’s first series. He limped off the field and shortly thereafter made his way into the blue medical tent on the sidelines. The 24-year-old headed straight to the locker room when he emerged, and was ruled out for the rest of the game shortly thereafter. The Patriots reportedly fear that Maye suffered a fractured ankle . He will be out “indefinitely” and is set to undergo further testing once back in the U.S. “We’ll have to see what comes back and what he looks like when he’s back here,” said Vrabel, “and make sure we’re doing what’s best for him and his health.”

title: Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status
summary: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due […]
full_text: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury. Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation. What happened? The Patriots started Sunday’s game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart. Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye’s right ankle. He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team’s medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game. Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out. What do we know about the injury? Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye’s status during their post-game media availability. “Obviously, he wasn’t able to finish the game, so we’ll have to get some more tests run and we’ll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has,” Vrabel said at the podium. “I know that it was a low leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it but I know he couldn’t go back in. … He couldn’t function. Couldn’t play. Couldn’t run. Couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level.” Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room. “I talked to him,” Campbell told MassLive’s Mark Daniels. “He’s in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he’s going to be fine. He’s a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he’s going to attack it full head of steam and come back better.” The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team’s arrival on Monday. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Initial reports suggest that Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that might keep him out for the remainder of the season. For the Patriots, this is very much the worst-case scenario. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] The Patriots are concerned that Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Lions. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Drake Maye did not travel back to the United States with the rest of the Patriots, per head coach Mike Vrabel. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If indeed diagnosed as a fractured ankle, Drake Maye would “almost certainly” be out for the rest of the season, according to a report by Ian Rapoport. What does it mean for the Patriots? “Any time your starting quarterback goes out and is not able to return, there are questions,” safety Kevin Byard told the media after the game. The questions mentioned by Byard are manifold in the direct aftermath of both the injury and the contest as a whole. Information about severity or a potential recovery timeline is limited, which in turn also limits the avenues the Patriots might have to explore in the immediate or long-term future. What we do know is that for however long Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito will be the top quarterback on the depth chart with third-stringer Behren Morton backing him up. DeVito completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each after entering the Lions game midway through the first period. DeVito described his and the offense’s performance after he took over for Maye as “not good enough.” The next chance to improve upon it will come after the Patriots’ upcoming bye, with a Sunday Night game versus the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. New England will not start its on-field preparation for that game until a few days beforehand; the team will return to its usual in-game schedule following the bye. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If the injury is indeed as significant as believed, here is a rundown of how it would impact the Patriots moving forward.

title: Did Drake Maye get injured on an illegal play?
summary: Penalties played a decisive role in the New England Patriots’ opening drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, but it was a flag that wasn’t flown that generated the most discussion after the game: should Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson been penalized for taking down Drake Maye and, along the way, injuring his ankle? Before […]
full_text: Penalties played a decisive role in the New England Patriots’ opening drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, but it was a flag that wasn’t flown that generated the most discussion after the game: should Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson been penalized for taking down Drake Maye and, along the way, injuring his ankle ? Before trying to figure out whether or not referee Clay Martin and his crew should have flown penalty flags, a look at the play in question. This was Drake Maye's final play before leaving the game questionable with an ankle injury. pic.twitter.com/Yi1rQYpMeW — Doug Kyed (@DougKyed) November 15, 2026 Hutchinson quickly worked his way into the backfield on an apparent communication breakdown involving left tackle Will Campbell, and wrapped up Maye from behind as he was climbing the pocket. In doing so, he lifted his entire body off the ground and subsequently came down on Maye’s now-injured ankle. Was Hutchinson’s form illegal, though, and should have been penalized as a hip-drop tackle? Not according to NFL rules Section 2, Article 18: Article 18. Hip-Drop Tackle It is a foul if a player uses the following technique to bring a runner to the ground: – grabs the runner with one or both hands or wraps the runner with both arms; and – unweights himself by swiveling and dropping his hips and/or lower body, landing on and/or trapping the runner’s leg(s) at or below the knee. FOX rules analyst Mike Pereira gave a similar explanation on the air. “Three things have to happen,” he explained. “You have to unweight yourself, swivel all around the back and land on the back of his leg below the knee. This was more of a horse collar-type pulled down from behind. [But] certainly not a horse collar penalty.” The NFL agreed, as reported by ESPN’s Mike Reiss: Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, confirmed Pereira’s explanation through a league spokesman, noting it was not a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting. It was also not a foul for a horse collar tackle, as Pereira noted, because neither the collar nor the nameplate were grabbed. No penalty was called on the play by referee Clay Martin’s crew. Mike Vrabel, who has been at odds with the officials multiple times so far this season, also saw nothing nefarious on the play. “I don’t think it was [a hip-drop tackle],” he said on Monday. This comment follows up similar remarks made by Vrabel after the game on Sunday. “I’m not going to assume there was something there,” he said. “However it happened, I don’t think it was anything intentional. I’m sure that it wasn’t. That’s part of the game.” Neither Maye nor Hutchinson have since commented on the play, because both got injured. Whereas Maye suffered the aforementioned ankle injury, Hutchinson is believed to have suffered a torn ACL while celebrating the sack.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Drake Maye injury: Patriots QB might miss rest of the season
summary: Update 11/16/2026: Drake Maye out indefinitely with potential ankle fracture The New England Patriots fear that Drake Maye suffered an ankle fracture during Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions. According to a report by ESPN’s Adam Schefter, he underwent further testing in Germany to determine whether or not surgery would be necessary. Regardless of that […]
full_text: Update 11/16/2026: Drake Maye out indefinitely with potential ankle fracture The New England Patriots fear that Drake Maye suffered an ankle fracture during Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions. According to a report by ESPN’s Adam Schefter, he underwent further testing in Germany to determine whether or not surgery would be necessary. Regardless of that decision, Maye will be out ‘indefinitely’ and potentially for the remainder of the season. Original story 11/16/2026: Drake Maye might miss rest of the season with ‘significant lower leg injury’ The New England Patriots appear to have suffered a major blow on Sunday. Quarterback Drake Maye, who exited the game against the Detroit Lions in the first quarter, is expected to be “out an extended period of time” and might even miss the remainder of the season altogether. According to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” in the Patriots’ 35-10 loss to the Lions . Maye, 24, exited the game after the opening drive. He had completed three of his first four pass attempts for 48 total yards and also gained 11 yards on a scramble, but was taken down for a third-down sack to end the series. After the play, which also saw Lions edge Aidan Hutchinson suffer a potentially season-ending injury while celebrating, the Patriots’ third-year QB limped of the field. He later entered the blue medical tent on the sidelines and after emerging made his way to the locker room. Maye was initially announced as questionable to return with an ankle injury, but was ruled out for the remainder of the game shortly thereafter. In his absence, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito entered the contest. DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception. New England scored once with him under center. The Patriots flew back to the United States on Sunday, after their game against the Lions in Munich. Maye is expected to undergo further testing to determine the exact severity of the injury and establish a recovery timeline. The Patriots are on their bye this week before a Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Lions
summary: For a second week in a row, the New England Patriots got blown out by an NFC North team on Sunday. Once again, they looked listless and disengaged for the majority of the game. Let’s get into our lessons learned from the Patriots’ 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany. If Drake Maye is […]
full_text: For a second week in a row, the New England Patriots got blown out by an NFC North team on Sunday. Once again, they looked listless and disengaged for the majority of the game. Let’s get into our lessons learned from the Patriots’ 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany. If Drake Maye is out for any extended period, the Patriots are going to borderline unwatchable The Patriots haven’t had many playmakers on offense this year, but Drake Maye has still put together a (mostly) solid year. Without him, however, it looks like one of the worst offenses in football. Sunday’s game was concrete proof of that. Tommy DeVito couldn’t get the ball to open receivers, separation was on and off, and they couldn’t run the ball. If Maye misses time after the bye, and it’s looking increasingly likely that that is going to be the case , it’s going to be tough to watch. Tommy DeVito isn’t good Speaking of Tommy DeVito, after Drake Maye went out with an injury, the Patriots were forced to turn to him. The media likes DeVito and the Patriots clearly like him too, since they gave him a contract extension this offseason. Unfortunately, he just isn’t that good of a quarterback. On Sunday, he missed open receivers left and right and on more than one occasion threw guys directly into contact. I understand that he’s the backup inserted on short notice, and that the Patriots aren’t asking him to be a great player because they really don’t want him playing at all, but it would be nice if he was at least able to competently run the offense. Against Detroit, he wasn’t. The A.J. Brown trade keeps looking worse by the day A.J. Brown’s inability to do anything positive this year has been almost laughable. He got hurt in the first game, missed a good chunk of time on injured reserve, came back, was a non-factor, and then got hurt again. He returned on Sunday, was unable to get open and had a drop as well. He finally made a nice catch-and-run to move the stick on a third down, and then promptly went to the locker room with a hamstring injury . It’s been a rough year for Brown, and the Patriots front office: they effectively bid against themselves to trade for him and still gave up a first-round pick in 2028 to do so. Unless he somehow manages a complete 180, the trade is going to go down as a massive failure, and potentially hamstring the Patriots for years to come. The defense continues to play without any fire Their defense was the reason the Patriots made the Super Bowl last year, and the hope was that it would take another step forward in 2026. Unfortunately, that has not happen and the unit has instead taken a step back. It did register a couple of turnovers on Sunday, but the unit was unable to stop its opponent more or less all day long. They came out without any fire, missed tackles all over field, and put the Patriots in a hole right away. We all were impressed with the job that Zak Kuhr had done last year, but the league has seemed to figure him out, and whatever he’s doing isn’t working. Yes, they have dealt with some injuries, but, for the most part, the defense has been fairly healthy. They have been out-coached, out-played, and, to be frank, it oftentimes looks like the other team simply wants it more than they do. With this defense, the Patriots aren’t going anywhere, especially if Drake Maye ends up missing time. Christian Gonzalez gets burned again, but recovers with a pick Christian Gonzalez is one of the best corners in the NFL, and surely one of the best players on the Patriots. The last two weeks, however, saw him have back-to-back rough games for the first time in his career. On the game’s first third down against the Lions, his struggles continued, when Amon-Ra St. Brown caught a pass in the flat, shook Gonzalez into oblivion, and then took the ball 56 yards for a touchdown. It was a bad start for Gonzalez, who later also fell victim to a pick play on another St. Brown score. it wasn’t all bad, however. He also registered an interception on a play where he ran the route for St. Brown and undercut him for the pick. It was a play that showed the player he has been, and will try to be again. The Patriots finally win the turnover battle While we are on the topic of interceptions, the Patriots have finally won the turnover battle for the first time this season. They picked off Jared Goff twice, and only turned it over once. In a game where they got embarrassed again, and with everything looking absolutely terrible in New England now, I’ll take any positive notes I can get. Now, if they only were able to go a game without turning the ball over… Jahmyr Gibbs might be the best player in the NFL The NFL is filled with players who are really fast, really strong, and really elusive. None of those players, however, measure up to Gibbs. His ability to stop and start is ridiculous, and his speed is nothing short of blazing. He leads the NFL in touches, and there is no sign of him slowing down. People had thought that TreVeyon Henderson would be the Patriots’ version of Gibbs, but there is no one in this league like him, and, just like most teams that have played the Lions this year, New England had no chance of stopping him on Sunday. In fact, he ended up out-gaining them by himself: Gibbs had 153 rushing yards and 99 receiving yards for a total of 252 yards. The Patriots offense finished the day with a grand total of 151. Reggie Gilliam has a tough first game back The Patriots activated Gilliam off of injured reserve before the game, and they were hoping he would be a factor in the running game and on special teams. Instead, the Patriots couldn’t run the ball to save their lives, Gilliam twice ran into his return man when he was trying to block, and he also committed two penalties on special teams. Personally, I didn’t love activating him off the IR, and, for Sunday at least, the Patriots didn’t get any better with him on the field. With Drake Maye set to miss time, however, they might have to start relying on him and the running game. We might have to start questioning Mike Vrabel Mike Vrabel did a fantastic job last year, there is no denying it. The culture he was trying to build was obvious, and the result was a mentally and physically tough team that reveled in the opportunity to go on the road and prove itself. This year, however, the team has been a disaster. There have definitely been a lot of injuries, but the mental toughness has almost completely disappeared. The amount of pre-snap penalties is alarming, and the unforced errors in judgement and physical play have been bad. To go along with that, the way that he and some of the players have been speaking to the media is confusing as well. If you’re going to be a culture guy, then the culture has to matter, and it doesn’t look good right now. I’m not saying that they should fire Vrabel or anything, but it bears watching. If the team doesn’t start playing better, and they don’t fix the fundamentals (turnovers, penalties, tackling), then there might be a reason to move on sooner rather than later. Obviously, not every team is going to be great every year, but he has hand-picked a lot of these guys for the culture here because he coached them before. If this team has any sort of culture issue, it’s squarely on Vrabel’s shoulders. (I also think that it’s notable that they seemingly rushed A.J. Brown back twice instead of giving him a long rest, and he’s been hurt both times. Maybe that’s the medical staff, but it’s ultimately the coaching staff who makes the decision to play the guys, even if they are physically cleared.) Thank god for the bye Perhaps no team in the NFL has needed a bye week as much as the Patriots do. They played two bad games in a row, have a ton of injuries, including at quarterback, and desperately need to get their minds right and get healthy. The Patriots are going to have to come up with something significantly better than what they’ve brought lately, because they are getting crushed and look…
author: Pat Lane

title: What the reported Drake Maye injury means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots did not just lose their Week 10 game to the Detroit Lions, they also saw their starting quarterback depart early in the 35-10 contest. And not just that: Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that is reportedly expected to keep him out an extended period […]
full_text: The New England Patriots did not just lose their Week 10 game to the Detroit Lions, they also saw their starting quarterback depart early in the 35-10 contest . And not just that: Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that is reportedly expected to keep him out an extended period of time and might even end his season. While further tests will be conducted to determine a return timeline, Maye’s immediate future is, at the very least, in question. What does this mean for the Patriots? Let’s find out. On to 2027? The Patriots are 5-5 and despite dropping out of the playoff picture on Sunday remain in the race for a postseason spot in the AFC. However, if Maye is indeed forced to miss extended time or even the rest of the season, the outlook changes drastically: given all of the issues, this does not look like a playoff-caliber team without its Pro Bowl-caliber quarterback. At least publicly, the Patriots and head coach Mike Vrabel won’t care. We will hear the classic “next man up” and “everybody is preparing like a starter” lines, while there will be no outward readjustment of the goals. Make no mistake, however. This is the worst-case scenario for the Patriots and their 2026 season. It might not mean they will go 0-7 down the stretch, especially if Maye does come back, but the sights might have to be set on 2027 sooner rather than later. It’s the Tommy DeVito show Sunday’s game against the Lions might not have been an accurate reflection of their capabilities, but that doesn’t mean the Patriots’ offensive outlook is not bleak. Fact is, after all, that Tommy DeVito is a serious downgrade from Drake Maye. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . That said, the Patriots are still expected to rely on their backup for however long Maye will ultimately be out. Rookie Behren Morton, who served as the emergency third option throughout the season thus far, will be elevated to the No. 2 spot with a third passer potentially being added to the roster or practice squad if need be. DeVito, 28, entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie with the New York Giants in 2023. He started eight total games over two year but was waived in 2025. He subsequently joined the Patriots in a backup role, serving as the third passer behind Maye and Joshua Dobbs. When Dobbs was let go earlier in the year, DeVito officially took over the backup spot. As such, he saw minimal action over the first nine weeks of the season. Against the Lions, however, he played most of the game and finished with 12 completions on 24 attempts for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception. The Patriots scored once with him at the helm and punted eight times, including seven three-and-outs. Cultural stress test However long the Patriots’ medical staff determines Maye will be out might also have an impact on other injury situations. Frankly, if the starter is sidelined and the losses keep piling up, there would be no need for any players to be rushed back from injury. There shouldn’t be any way, to be honest, but the threshold of “pushing through” an injury might be reconfigured should Maye indeed be out an extended period of time. That “pushing through” process, however, appears to be an integral part of New England’s culture this season. Multiple players are currently banged up or still dealing with the effects of injuries they suffered earlier; the bye week will come handy in that regard. If the overall goals begin to shift, however, so might the culture — for better or worse. It will be on Mike Vrabel, who was hired in 2025 in large part due to his abilities as a leader and team-builder, to make sure the locker room sees through this latest challenge in a season full of them. The schedule might change As of Monday morning, three of the Patriots’ final seven games of the season are scheduled as prime time games. One of those is a realistic candidate to be flexed out of its spot, and would have been so even before Maye got hurt: the Sunday night game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. That being said, with Thanksgiving that weekend and games taking place on Thursday and Friday as well, the alternatives are actually minimal. Unless the league wants to flip it to the 1 p.m. ET spot currently occupied by Raiders-Browns, only the 4:25 p.m. ET contest between the Seahawks and 49ers makes sense. Whether or not FOX will give that one up, however, will be seen. As for the other prime time games on the schedule, they likely will stay in their slots due to their nature as Thursday (Week 14 vs. Vikings) and Monday (Week 15 vs. Chiefs) games. Still, the two undetermined slots in Weeks 17 (vs. Broncos) and 18 (vs. Dolphins) could now very well end up as 1 p.m. games. Grain of salt It could very well be tied to the “pushing through” culture at One Patriot Place, but on multiple occasions this season players have come back sooner than their initially-reported injuries made it sound. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is the latest example: he was expected to miss multiple weeks due to the knee injury he suffered in Week 9 against Green Bay, but was back at practice four days later and ended up playing 26 snaps against the Lions. With that in mind, Monday’s reports might have to be taken with a grain of salt. With the bye week coming up, the Patriots do have some extra time at their hands for recovery. At the end of the day, of course, they would be wise to play the long game with Maye. Yes, the playoffs are still a distinct possibility even at 5-5, but they need to be careful with their franchise quarterback.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: 2 winners and losers from Patriots loss to the Lions
summary: The New England Patriots were uncompetitive again in a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-5 on the season, and currently find themselves out of the playoff picture. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 10 contest. Winners Nobody: […]
full_text: The New England Patriots were uncompetitive again in a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-5 on the season, and currently find themselves out of the playoff picture . Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 10 contest. Winners Nobody: There could be an argument for Drake Maye, who generated four positive plays on the Patriots’ opening possession before leaving with an ankle injury . Anyone who still had doubts (for some reason) about Maye’s impact on the offense got their answer once he left the game. Still, nobody earns a spot here after an embarrassing 35-10 loss. Losers Everybody: The No. 1 pillar of Mike Vrabel’s team identity is effort and finish. Yet it was another week without seeing enough of either across the roster. Kevin Byard called it a “slap in the face” game. Tommy DeVito said the team got bullied. It was an alarming performance for Vrabel himself and the program he is trying to build. As for more specific performances: Honorable mentions Injuries continued to be one of the storylines of the season as the Patriots lost the one player they couldn’t: Drake Maye. The QB left after the first drive with an ankle injury and the offense was uncompetitive from that point forward. The Patriots also lost A.J. Brown (hamstring), Robert Spillane (illness), Charles Woods (unknown) and Dre’Mont Jones (cramps). DeVito struggled mightily in relief competing 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards and one touchdown and interception. It’s a tough spot for any backup being thrusted into the fire, but DeVito generated -0.32 EPA per play (10th percentile) against the worst pass defense in football. He struggled to see the field missing several open receivers downfield and led his pass catchers into multiple big hits due to poor ball placement. A.J. Brown caught just two-of-six targets for 27 yards before leaving with a hamstring injury. He had another drop. In his return, fullback Reggie Gilliam was called for two special teams penalties and lost a fumble that Brown recovered. Will Campbell struggled in pass protection allowing six pressures on 33 pass blocking snaps, per Next Gen Stats. Campbell allowed 2.0 sacks, including one to Aidan Hutchinson that led to Maye leaving the game. The Patriots defense does not have the injury excuse like the offense. Outside of Carlton Davis (knee), this is their unit and it has been ugly. They generated two turnovers, but missed 12 tackles while the explosive plays against piled up again. Detroit nearly totaled 500 (!) yards of offense. Christian Gonzalez matched up with Amon-Ra St. Brown 15 times on Sunday. While he hauled in his first interception of the season he allowed two receptions for 84 yards and two touchdowns across three targets. Vrabel noted Gonzalez got no help elsewhere on the first touchdown after he missed the initial tackle attempt. Safety Kevin Byard had perhaps his best sequence of the season with a pass breakup then interception in the end zone to end the first half. Byard was among the group, though, that did not help Gonzalez which appeared to be an issue on multiple occasions. Shoutout Mitch Wishnowsky for continuing to punt well. 8 punts and zero touchbacks as he has been one of the few bright spots this season.
author: Brian Hines

title: Game Recap: Saints host Panthers in Week 10 for divisional lead
summary: The New Orleans Saints had the chance to take sole position atop the NFC South when they faced off against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Here’s a recap of all the action from the Caesars Superdome. First Quarter The Saints received first, and Tyler Shough got off to a positive start, completing his first pass […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Chase Young #99 of the New Orleans Saints rushes past Tommy Tremble #82 of the Carolina Panthers during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints had the chance to take sole position atop the NFC South when they faced off against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Here’s a recap of all the action from the Caesars Superdome. First Quarter The Saints received first, and Tyler Shough got off to a positive start, completing his first pass to the returning Travis Etienne Jr for 11 yards. After a few more short gains, the Saints went for a 4th-and-1, but Shough’s throw intended for Chris Olave was deflected and picked off by Devin Lloyd. With a short field after the return, runs from Chuba Hubbard and a 6-yard pass from Bryce Young to Tommy Tremble set up 3rd down from the 3-yard line. But Young was incomplete on 3rd down, before being sacked by Carl Granderson on 4th down to keep the game scoreless. New Orleans proceeded to three-and-out and punt from deep inside their own territory before Carolina were soon forced to punt themselves, on a drive hampered by penalties. Shough completed a few more short throws to Etienne on the ensuing series, but the Saints had to punt again. Second Quarter The Panthers moved the ball past midfield as Hubbard broke off a 17-yard run, before three straight incompletions would follow. Ryan Fitzgerald’s 48-yard attempt was wide left, and the game remained scoreless. Shough found a chunk gain of 20 yards to Juwan Johnson, but fumbled a play later to return possession to Carolina. Young then found Tremble twice for a total of 41 yards as Carolina entered the red zone. He connected with Darren Waller for 13 more, before Hubbard ran in the 2-yard score to give the Panthers the lead. Shough kicked into gear with a 20-yard pass to Jordyn Tyson, followed by a 17-yard scramble. But the Saints rattled off multiple runs for no yardage before Audric Estime was stuffed on 4th-and-1 to turn the ball over. Despite a 20-yard pass to Tetairoa McMillan to move the drive to midfield, the Panthers had to punt with just over a minute on the clock. Shough was then sacked twice as New Orleans failed to move into scoring position before halftime. Third Quarter Carolina had to punt to begin the second half, with Colby Wooden sacking Young on a 3rd down. The Saints then embarked on a 64-yard drive, highlighted by an 18-yard catch by Tyson and an 11-yard pass to Olave to convert a 3rd down. Alvin Kamara would run in a 3-yard touchdown to tie the game at 7-7. Young returned to the field and continued to move the ball, connecting with a variety of receivers as the Panthers moved into field goal range before coming up short on a 3rd-and-9. Fitzgerald converted this time from 55 yards to give the visitors a 10-7 advantage. The teams would then exchange three-and-outs, with New Orleans getting the ball to begin the fourth. Fourth Quarter Shough completed a number of short throws to Tyson, but was incomplete on 3rd down to force the black and gold to punt again. The Panthers didn’t fare any better, punting back to the hosts after finding just 16 yards on their series. Shough then spread the ball across the field as Carolina were guilty of a number of penalties, quickly moving the drive into the red zone. A pass interference penalty cost the Panthers 17 yards, setting up Kamara for his second touchdown of the day with a 4-yard touchdown catch. But trailing 14-10, Carolina responded in a big way. Young found Hubbard on 29- and 34-yard passes as he drove into the red zone in rapid fashion. Hubbard then ran in a 1-yard touchdown to give the Panthers the lead. Shough found Olave, Tyson, and Kamara as the Saints sought a response, but came up short on a 3rd down. Charlie Smyth’s 55-yard kick tied the game with just under a minute left. Looking to get into field goal range and win the game, a pass interference penalty against Kool-Aid McKinstry gave Carolina the opportunity to do exactly that. Fitzgerald’s 54-yard effort was good as time expired, giving the Panthers the 20-17 victory. The Saints are now back on the road as they pay a visit to the Chicago Bears this weekend.
author: Sam Mackenzie

McCarthy’s growth is showing in the numbers | ESPN.com McCarthy’s QBR has skyrocketed from 36.1 to 56.3 this season. His completion percentage has gone from second to last among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts at 57.6% to 63.5% with the Giants. title: NY Giants cut struggling kick returner, sign another shaky one
summary: The New York Giants cut wide receiver and kickoff/punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday amidst a flurry of roster moves. They also cut defensive back Nikko Reed. Added to the roster were defensive back Tavierre Thomas and wide receiver return man Xavier Gipson. Jones signed with the Giants when he was cut by the Cincinnati […]
full_text: Charlie Jones | Getty Images The New York Giants cut wide receiver and kickoff/punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday amidst a flurry of roster moves. They also cut defensive back Nikko Reed . Added to the roster were defensive back Tavierre Thomas and wide receiver return man Xavier Gipson . Jones signed with the Giants when he was cut by the Cincinnati Bengals when they trimmed their roster to 53 players. A four-year veteran, Jones averaged 10.0 yards on 16 punt returns and 23.8 yards on 14 kickoff returns. Jones had a key fumble in a loss to the New Orleans Saints. He also muffed a punt against the Philadelphia Eagles, and has been dealing with a thumb injury. Gipson is being signed off the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad. This will actually be Gipson’s third time as a Giant. He was claimed off waivers from the New York Jets in 2025, then lost to the Eagles. He was re-signed to the practice squad late last season, and was with the team throughout training camp before being released in final roster cuts. Gipson, 25, has extensive experience as a returner. He has averaged 9.1 yards on 74 punt returns and 25.9 yards on 51 kickoff returns. Gipson’s issue has always been ball security. He has 12 fumbles in 163 career touches, one every 13.6 touches, and has lost jobs with the Jets and Eagles largely because of those issues. If the Giants are looking for added ball security, turning to Gipson is risky. Reed, who was signed off the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice squad earlier this season, appeared in three games for the Giants. He played entirely on special teams. He was cut to make room for Thomas, whose signing was reported earlier in the day. The Giants also worked out running back Antonio Gibson, who spent four seasons with the Washington Commanders and two with the New England Patriots. Gibson had a 1,000-yard season in 2021 with Washington.
author: Ed Valentine

title: 5 players the NY Giants need to step up to make the playoffs
summary: The New York Giants are heading into the toughest stretch of their schedule for the 2026 season. They have teams with winning records in four of their next six weeks, starting with their Week 11 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. After that the Giants will face the rebuilding Indianapolis Colts, then the San Francisco 49ers […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images The New York Giants are heading into the toughest stretch of their schedule for the 2026 season. They have teams with winning records in four of their next six weeks, starting with their Week 11 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. After that the Giants will face the rebuilding Indianapolis Colts, then the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks. Those games are followed by the Cleveland Browns, Detroit Lions, and Dallas Cowboys before the season finale against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Giants are still in control of the NFC East, but their grip on the division is tenuous after a frustrating Week 10 loss to the Washington Commanders. They still have control over their destiny and a playoff berth is within their grasp. The Giants will need to continue to rely on their most important players if they want to realize their playoff dreams. QB J.J. McCarthy The quarterback position is the single most important position in sports, so it follows that J.J. McCarthy is the most important player on the Giants’ roster. McCarthy has played very well since coming onto the field in the fourth quarter against the New Orleans Saints. McCarthy only joined the Giants on Sept. 28, when they traded their fifth-round pick for him. McCarthy has been a significant upgrade over Jameis Winston, adding a couple much-needed elements to the Giants’ offense. We’ve talked about how his athleticism has helped to open up the running game, giving defenses a speed option to worry about. What has gotten less conversation is the vertical element that McCarthy’s passing has added into the offense. McCarthy currently leads the NFL in Air Yards, averaging 10.4 yards downfield. Perhaps even more impressively, McCarthy is also 10th in the NFL in completion percentage over expected at +3.3 points above expected. In other words, he’s attempting a high rate of relatively difficult throws and completing them at a higher-than-expected rate. That’s been particularly helpful for the offense since the Giants have pretty consistently asked McCarthy to convert long third downs through the air. The Giants have faced 20 3rd downs of at least 7 yards over the last two weeks, and they usually lead to McCarthy trying to convert those long downs. He has, largely, been better than the Giants could have hoped since they traded for him, and has given hope and life to a season that appeared on the brink after Jaxson Dart was lost for the year. McCarthy will need to continue to play well as the Giants’ starting quarterback. The Giants are going into the toughest stretch of their schedule with games against the Jaguars, 49ers, Seahawks, and Cowboys remaining on the schedule. The Giants have the potential to win any of those games, but they’ll need McCarthy to keep building on what he’s done in order to do so. Those teams represent some of the best offenses in the NFL, and the Giants will need their own offense to finish in the end zone for more often than they have this year (8.1% of drives, 21st in the NFL) if they want to keep pace. The offensive line Okay, this is cheating a bit, but I do believe that it’s much better to think of an offensive line as a unit and not group of five individuals. The Giants’ offensive line struggled mightily in Week 9 against the Philadelphia Eagles and has been something of an issue throughout the year. The pass protection has been uneven, generally holding up well against four-man rushes (8th best pressure allowed rate in the NFL), but having a tendency to surrender pressure when blitzed. Each of the Giants’ linemen have had technical failures when faced with the blitz, with issues in footwork, leverage, hand usage, and correctly picking up stunts or twists. And, when combined with the Giants’ tendency to land in 3rd and long situations, sacks in big moments. The Giants’ line has also been a frustratingly poor run blocking unit. They’ve been among the worst in the NFL at opening holes and are averaging just 0.9 yards before contact per run. The good news is that the line has upside to improve over the remainder of the season. Both right guard Sisi Mauigoa and center Bryan Hudson are first-year starters, and also new to each other. Familiarity and chemistry are vitally important to offensive line play, and the more reps the young players get together, the better. Each has had some embarrassing failures this year, but also impressive blocks as well. Blocking will be key to whatever the Giants do, or do not, accomplish over the remainder of the year. They’ll need their pass protection to hold up against three of the best defenses in the NFL over the next four weeks so McCarthy can continue to grow. Likewise, if John Harbaugh wants to be a run-first team (despite the Giants being better at passing right now), the offensive line will need to do a much better job at opening holes up front. LB Arvell Reese It’s honestly remarkable just how quickly the Giants’ rookie linebacker has become a focal point of the Giants’ defense. And I confess that I could have gone a couple different ways for this section. I could have highlighted Abdul Carter, Deonte Banks, Jevon Holland, or even Kayvon Thibodeaux as defenders who will be instrumental in the Giants’ pursuit of a playoff berth. And the fact of the matter is that so much of what Dennard Wilson does on defense is within the context and structure of the whole play and not just 11 guys running around. But, like I said, Reese has quickly become a focal point for the defense and he is frequently the tip of the spear. Reese is now the favorite to win DROY and could even be a factor in the DPOY conversation. He has a rare blend of length, speed, explosiveness, and power, as well as the ability to process quickly and be a three-dimensional defender. One of Dennard Wilson’s greatest strengths so far has been scheming opportunities for Reese to make impact plays. Each of the aforementioned defenders plays a role in unleashing Reese — Abdul Carter’s elite speed off the edge commands double-teams or forces quarterbacks off their spots. Kayvon Thibodeaux’s versatility allows him to occupy blockers, drop into coverage to waste blocks and muddy reads, or pressure QBs into moving. Holland’s communication and range enables the coverage rotations to slow down passers, while Banks’ sticky press-man coverage ability takes away receiving options and forces quarterbacks to hold the ball. All of which combine to give Reese the opportunity to make impact plays, and the Giants’ defense is at it’s best when he’s taking advantage of those opportunities. He took a step forward over the course of the Giants’ Week 8 bye, and the mini-bye after Thursday Night Football offers another opportunity to take a breath and incorporate the lessons he’s learned so far. The Giants’ don’t necessarily need Reese to take over every game from here on out. However, they do need him to continue to consistently take advantage of opportunities as the rest of the defense creates them for him. The Giants are among the very best teams in forcing 3-and-outs and punts, and Reese’s play has been a big reason why. They need players like Carter and Thibodeaux to have more individual impacts when they’re only rushing four too, but Reese needs to continue to wreak havoc when they set him up to do so. WR Malik Nabers The Giants want to be a run-first team, but Nabers is the Giants’ star offensive player. He, and tight end Isaiah Likely, account for 56% of the Giants’ passing targets and 40% of the Giants’ offensive yardage. Likely is having a career year and proving well-worth the contract the Giants gave him. Nabers, on the other hand, has been more uneven. Conversations about his body language aside, he hasn’t had the consistent impact that the Giants need from him, and his production is largely in line with his rookie year despite a better quarterback situation. Nabers has also shown the kind of streakiness that was a frustrating…

title: NY Giants sign veteran DB off Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad
summary: The New York Giants on Monday poached veteran defensive back Tavierre Thomas off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad, in news first reported by Adam Schefter. The 30-year-old Thomas entered the NFL in 2018 as an undrafted free agent out of Ferris State. He has played for the Cleveland Browns, Houston Texans, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and […]
full_text: Tavierre Thomas | Getty Images The New York Giants on Monday poached veteran defensive back Tavierre Thomas off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad, in news first reported by Adam Schefter . The 30-year-old Thomas entered the NFL in 2018 as an undrafted free agent out of Ferris State. He has played for the Cleveland Browns, Houston Texans, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and spent the last two seasons with the Vikings. Last season, Thomas played in all 17 games for Minnesota. This year, he was on the team’s practice squad and has appeared in just one game. Thomas has been a core special teams player throughout his nine-year career. From 2020-2023, he was a regular part of the defensive rotation for the Browns and then the Texans. Since 2024, however, he has been almost exclusively a special teams player. In 2024, he played just 45 defensive snaps. Last season, that number was just 18. A corresponding move to make room for Thomas on the 53-man roster has not yet been announced.

title: Replace Dominic Zvada? Do the NY Giants have any good options to do that?
summary: There is a vocal part of the New York Giants fan base that believes the team should have already booted rookie plackekicker Dominic Zvada to the curb. That is understandable. When something goes wrong, fans always want someone to blame, and invariably they want someone to lose a job so they feel like they got […]
full_text: Dominic Zvada | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is a vocal part of the New York Giants fan base that believes the team should have already booted rookie plackekicker D ominic Zvada to the curb. That is understandable. When something goes wrong, fans always want someone to blame, and invariably they want someone to lose a job so they feel like they got their pound of flesh. The Giants have not been willing to do that as Zvada, after a 9-for-9 start, has made just 8 of 14 field-goal attempts over the past four games. Zvada has a much-discussed issue from the right hash mark. “You can’t, as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, start firing people left and right,” said head coach John Harbaugh. It is always easy to say “that guy’s gotta go.” It is a lot tougher to look around and find a solution, to find someone you are certain is a better option. Let’s look around and see what kind of options the Giants would have if they were to consider replacing Zvada. Ben Sauls The common refrain from Giants’ fans who want Zvada gone is, basically, “Better call Sauls.” Left-footed Ben Sauls was an elixir for the Giants’ kicking woes at the end of the 2025 season. Sauls made all 15 of his kicks over a three-game span, eight field goals and seven extra points. Yes, Sauls was perfect over that three-game stretch. Remember, though, his longest kick was a 45-yard extra point. Zvada has already been asked to try nine field goals of 50 yards or more, making six. Sauls has the leg for those kicks, but it’s never been tested in an NFL game. It is also important to remember that Sauls, like Zvada is currently, went through his own technique issue in the spring and summer while competing with Zvada. He was terrible in the spring, consistently pushing kicks to the left. He was better in the summer, but wasn’t nearly as consistent kicking the ball as Zvada was. It was easily to decide which of the two kickers should win the job. Sauls is not currently on a 53-man roster or practice squad. To my knowledge, he may have only had one or two tryouts. You can romanticize Sauls as the perfect solution to the placekicking issue if you want, but Sauls lost his job to Zvada because — based on the evidence at hand this summer — that is exactly what should have happened. Zane Gonzalez Gonzalez, 31, has had an up-and-down eight-year career. He made 19 of 22 field-goal attempts (86.4%) for the Atlanta Falcons in 2025. He got waived on Monday by the Miami Dolphins after he missed two field goals and an extra point in a 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. Gonzalez had replaced Riley Patterson earlier this season. It’s hard to make a case that Gonzalez would be a better option that Zvada. Old guys The 42-year-old Matt Prater made 18 of 20 kicks (90%) for the Buffalo Bills last season. The last time he made less than 80% of his kicks in a season was 2020. He made a 57-yard kick for the Arizona Cardinals in 2024, so there should still be something left in his leg. Are the Giants reaally in a situation where replacing Zvada with a guy almost 20 years older than he is would be the right move? Graham Gano is also out there. And, he misses football . Practice squad guys Harrison Mevis is on the Baltimore Ravens’ practice squad. He went 5 of 9 for the Los Angeles Rams earlier this year. Justin Tucker is with the Kansas City Chiefs. Once the best kicker in the game for Harbaugh’s Baltimore Ravens, Tucker made just 22 of 30 field goals (73.3%) in 2024. He served a supension in 2025 related to sexual misconduct allegations. Tucker turns 37 in a few days. Final thoughts Quite honestly, I don’t see any “no-brainer” decisions guaranteed to be better than working with Zvada and trying to get through his issue from the right hash mark.
author: Ed Valentine

title: 4 things the NY Giants have to do better to win the NFC East
summary: The New York Giants’ loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday tightened the NFC East race and made their weekend off less enjoyable than it could have been. Thanks to the San Francisco 49ers outscoring the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, though, the Giants’ division lead entering Week 11 is not as tenuous as it could […]
full_text: Abdul Carter | Getty Images The New York Giants’ loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday tightened the NFC East race and made their weekend off less enjoyable than it could have been. Thanks to the San Francisco 49ers outscoring the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, though, the Giants’ division lead entering Week 11 is not as tenuous as it could have been. The 5-3-1 Giants have a 2½-game lead over the 4-6 Cowboys and a two-game lead over the 3-5-1 Commanders. The Athletic’s playoff simulator gives the Giants a 56% chance of winning the NFC East and making the playoffs. The Cowboys are at 28%, and the Commanders 16%. Much has been made of the fact that the Giants’ schedule, beginning this weekend with the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars, is about to get tougher. Over the Giants’ first nine games, their opponents were a combined 25-49-1, a .340 winning percentage. Their upcoming opponents are a combined 43-33, a .566 winning percentage. Head coach John Harbaugh said recently that the Giants “don’t live in that scared world” of worrying about schedule difficulty. The Giants are a resilient team. Harbaugh has made them that way. They have, to this point, overcome the losses of quarterback Jaxson Dart and star edge defender Brian Burns. In each of their five wins, they have made plays late in the game to secure the victory. Fight and resilience alone, though, won’t win the NFC East title for the Giants. The Giants are an imperfect team that has things to fix in order to win the division. Below are some of the things the Giants are going to have to do better over the final eight games. Four-minute offense The Giants, holding a 21-17 lead, intercepted Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels twice in the last 5:31 of Thursday’s game. That should be enough for the Giants to have won that game. But it wasn’t. The Giants went three-and-out after both interceptions, failing to run significant time off the clock or force the Commanders to use up their timeouts on either occasion. The first possession included three runs, with the last being a Jameis Winston third-and-1 sneak on which running back Cam Skattebo never really got out of his stance to participate in the play. Harbaugh explained that this was a straight sneak, not a tush push. The second possession, which started at the Washington 46-yard line with 2:15 to play, also featured three runs. The last was a designed quarterback run for J.J. McCarthy on which the Giants didn’t even have a running back on the field. Sonny Styles said absolutely not on 3rd down. WASvsNYG on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1d9S7zwsT3 — NFL (@NFL) November 13, 2026 You can see from the jump he got that Washington linebacker Sonny Styles knew this play before the ball was snapped. Center Bryan Hudson had no chance to block him. “We had thought we had good runs. We thought we could get it with the runs. Also keep the clock running and make them burn the timeouts. We thought we could do both,” Harbaugh said. “But looking back on it, I think a good pass there might’ve been good too. I think if you throw the ball and you throw three incompletions or whatever, the question is flipped, you know, “why didn’t you run the ball, make them burn the timeouts?” Being successful really is the bottom line. It’s not like we’re trying to play it safe or anything like that. We’re not afraid to throw the ball there. The run that we had, the last run that got the two-yard loss, that’s got a chance to crack them. It’s a quarterback-driven run with an extra blocker. They had everybody up on the line. Honestly, on that one play, we can block that play better. And so that’s the way the game went in that situation.” The problem is, four-minute offense failure has been a theme for the Giants. In Week 3 against the Tennessee Titans, the Giants got the ball with 5:31 to play, protecting a 12-7 lead. They got a quick first down on a 12-yard Jameis Winston to Malik Nabers pass, but then punted with 3:12 to go after two runs and an incomplete pass. Jevon Holland bailed the Giants out, intercepting Cam Ward in the end zone with :24 to play. In Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, the Giants got the ball at midfield with a 3-point lead and 4:47 to play. They could muster only 16 yards in five plays, with a Dominic Zvada 52-yard field goal giving them a 20-24 lead with 2:16 to play. It took a Deonte Banks 98-yard interception return on the final play to seal that victory. In Week 5 against Washington, Skattebo’s fumble at the two-minute mark in overtime cost the Giants a chance to win. In Week 8 against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Giants got the ball with 1:56 to play after a Jake Elliott field goal pulled the Eagles within one score. After three handoffs to Devin Singletary netted just 2 yards, the Giants punted and once again relied on their defense to bail them out. “That’s something that I’ve always prided myself [on], playing on an offense that’s able to ice the game,” fullback Patrick Ricard said after Thursday’s loss. “I feel like this year we haven’t been able to do that as an offense. Only probably Week 1 that we actually ran the ball or got first downs, and were able to kneel the game out. “We’ve always had to rely on our defense, and our defense is very clutch, and they’ve been winning a lot of games for us. It’s something that we as an offense have to really harp on to finish games out like that because we can’t keep relying on our defense to keep going out there and just keep getting stops after stops. We need to be able to convert first downs in those moments.” I don’t have the answer. A head coach in his 19th season and a veteran offensive staff, though, need to do everything they can to figure it out. The Giants can’t ask their defense to close every game in the final seconds. We saw that on Thursday night. Placekicking consistency We went in-depth on Zvada’s issues from the right hashmark on Saturday. It simply isn’t possible to design an offense to get every field goal attempt from the left hashmark. This is something that Zvada and veteran special teams coordinator Chris Horton are going to have to figure out. Harbaugh’s refusal to move on from Zvada, an undrafted rookie who won the job with a fantastic summer, after his struggles since Week 9 has driven the fan base to distraction. I understand Harbaugh’s desire to ride things out with Zvada and hope he becomes the kicker the Giants believe he can be sooner rather than later. Look around the league. For every team that has a Brandon Aubrey, Cam Little, or a solid veteran like Chris Boswell, there are teams riding what former special teams coordinator Thomas McGaughey called the “kicker train”, and finding it an unpleasant experience. Just like there aren’t 32 top-10 caliber quarterbacks in the NFL, there aren’t 32 kickers teams feel good about every time they need three points. Or even one point. Zvada, 23, has the leg strength and talent to be one of those long-range placekicking weapons every team is seeking. Hall of Fame kicker Adam Vinatieri kicked for 24 years, but made 80% of his field goal attempts just once in his first four seasons. Former Giants kicker Lawrence Tynes certainly believes in Zvada: Right footed kickers can struggle on the right hash when they try to "steer" the ball to the left vs having a bullet proof alignment process and just kicking the ball normally. You want to just "kick" the ball and swing away when kicking, let your alignment take care of the… https://t.co/GC2wOm1Zem — Lawrence Tynes (@lt4kicks) November 15, 2026 Over the years, the Giants have seen many good young placekickers like Chris Boswell, Brandon McManus, and Joey Slye get away from them and go on to have excellent careers. They don’t want Zvada to be the next one. Still, with a playoff berth at stake, how patient can they be? Don’t be so conservative Everything good about the Giants’ season comes from Harbaugh. The credibility he brought when the Giants hired him and the way he has led this team…

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans!
