McCarthy | Pro Football Network “And if I wanted to speak for you in regard to J.J. McCarthy, you hated […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the headlines you need to start your week. ‘The Coach Hated Him’ — Ex-NFL Scout Raises Eyebrows With Claim About Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell’s Feelings Towards J.J. McCarthy | Pro Football Network “And if I wanted to speak for you in regard to J.J. McCarthy, you hated his guts as a player. You couldn’t (expletive) stand him,” Middlekauff insisted. “Because you were clearly the driving force for making him the third quarterback and helping the GM: ‘We gotta get this guy out of here. Fifth-round pick, I’ll drive him to the airport.’ Which is fine. You’re not the first or the last coach to feel that way toward a QB.” “It’s happened before and it will happen again. Then a couple of weeks later, when you’re starting Carson Wentz, who couldn’t hit water from the middle of the ocean and then J.J.’s making plays like that for (Matt) Nagy and Greg Roman you’re like, ‘Uh, no one is acting like this guy is Joe Montana, but this is way better than what we had.’” What I’m hearing about Chargers-Broncos trade bitterness, why Jonathan Taylor stayed | The Athletic But the Colts weren’t high on dealing Daniel Jones, who played well before his torn Achilles last year. Anecdotally, it appears players are better two years out from Achilles tears, and Jones tore his 11 months ago. Though he hasn’t played well lately, the hope is he will improve. And Jones needs a quality running back in Jonathan Taylor, whom the Colts might have overvalued these past few weeks. League sources aren’t sure a deal of a second and fifth will be on the table for Taylor in March, so it could be easy to say Indy should have dealt him this past week. But by trading players on expiring deals and keeping a quality running back like Taylor and a quarterback who could improve (but could also be released before the team pays him $38 million more), Dodds has created optionality for the next GM. That GM could be Dodds himself, who has been on short lists across the league the last few years, or it could be an outsider. Giants’ Sneak Over Tush Push Call Remains a Head-Scratcher | Giants on SI The numbers supported a tush push on 3rd-and-1, so why didn’t the Giants run it? We have some a theory. Continued Giants growth requires John Harbaugh fourth down adjustments | Daily News The Washington Commanders didn’t win Thursday’s game. The Giants lost it . John Harbaugh and his staff have given this franchise a coaching advantage this season, but their decision-making fell short in their biggest game to date. Teams lose in the NFL. The Giants still look like they’re going in the right direction. But Harbaugh needs to learn from his mistakes if the first-place Giants (5-3-1) intend to win the NFC East. The coach’s conservative calls on fourth downs on offense in the fourth quarter stood out in particular: Former Pro Bowler Donte Whitner says Jameis Winston should be cut for ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’ stunt | New York Post “I’d cut Jameis Winston this morning,” Whitner said on ESPN’s “Get Up” on Friday. “It was so unrealistic. You have 10 other guys out there and guys on defense that are busting their butt every week, and it’s very hard and difficult to win a game in the National Football League. So, when you get up there – first and foremost, whoever says hut 1, hut 2, hut 3? That’s 1950s football! “And then when you go into ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’? Are you serious? He’s clearly just trying to go viral on social media while they’re trying to win a football game. He’d get his pink slip this morning.” There are plenty of reasons to believe these Giants have what it takes | New York Post The weekend off for the Giants could have been a glorious respite if they had been able to hang on and beat the Commanders on Thursday night. title: New York Jets News: NYJ to be Aggressive in HC Trade Market?
summary: We have seven more games left in the Aaron Glenn era for the New York Jets. I will not remember this time period fondly whatsoever, but don’t worry, because there is a light at the end of the tunnel. ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast that he could potentially see the team […]
full_text: Jan 13, 2025; Glendale, AZ, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell and Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay shake hands after the NFC wild card game at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con We have seven more games left in the Aaron Glenn era for the New York Jets. I will not remember this time period fondly whatsoever, but don’t worry, because there is a light at the end of the tunnel. ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast that he could potentially see the team making an aggressive move to trade for their next head coach. Cimini said, “The name I would watch for is KOC, Kevin O’Connell. I was just talking to a couple of people in the league today, and they said they could see [Darren] Mougey giving up a high draft pick for Kevin O’Connell. They went to college together; they have maintained a relationship. If something falls apart there in Minnesota, if they collapse down the stretch, or if they decide that they want to elevate [Brian] Flores instead of losing him to another team, maybe they make that move.” Cimini revealed that, “I was told Mougey even in meetings like offseason and preseason has spoken, internal meetings with the Jets has spoken highly of O’Connell has mentioned him in meetings and so I wouldn’t totally dismiss that. I mean, he would come in, they would get along great, they have a history, he is an offensive-minded coach with coaching experience. Now, he has made a couple of questionable quarterback decisions in Minnesota. I don’t know how much of that is him or the GM or the previous GM, but I think it’s a name to watch for; let me put that out there.” Oh baby! Spicy! Sexy! Interesting! Now I’m sure there will be a huge debate in the comment section about whether this is too crazy or even worth it. Before you run to the comments, I would just like to provide some statistical data about KOC. The Jets, in their team history, have only ever won 12 games in a regular season once (1998). O’Connell is in his fifth season as a head coach in the NFL. He has already surpassed that number twice with a 14-win season (2024) and a 13-win season (2022). Who knows if he will add a third such year to his resume; the Vikings are currently 7-2. KOC is awesome, and if the Jets can find a way, they should absolutely explore it. J-E-T-S! title: After Further Review: Jets-Bills
summary: After each game, we’ll be sharing a comprehensive review that breaks down some of the controversial decisions from the officiating crew in the game. You may disagree in some cases, and that’s fine… Penalty Count Bills 7-35 (leading to zero Jets first downs)Jets 7-53 (leading to two Bills first downs) Note: This does not include […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - DECEMBER 29: Referee Clete Blakeman #34 looks on during the third quarter of a game between the Buffalo Bills and the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on December 29, 2024 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images After each game, we’ll be sharing a comprehensive review that breaks down some of the controversial decisions from the officiating crew in the game. You may disagree in some cases, and that’s fine… Penalty Count Bills 7-35 (leading to zero Jets first downs) Jets 7-53 (leading to two Bills first downs) Note: This does not include penalties that are declined or off-set. Plays where the call was obvious, uncontroversial or not visible on broadcast footage Jets Penalties Defensive holding on Kingsley Enagbare on 3rd-and-goal at the one-yard line. There is no argument here as Enagbare, who was initially engaged as he would have been assuming his man was a blocker, had a fistful of jersey as the receiver tried to get away from him. Offensive holding on Joe Tippmann to negate a 19-yard Garrett Wilson catch. There was a loss of leverage here and his man beat him into the backfield while he was still reaching across and holding on, so this was probably reasonable. Olu Fashanu false start. Flinch before the snap. Too many men on the field on 1st-and-goal at the nine-yard line. Not sure what happened here, but Breece Hall seemed to be the only player who came off the field after it. You can say it had an impact because Hall caught a 10-yard pass two plays later which would have been a touchdown. Malik McClain holding penalty to negate a nice Isaiah Davis kickoff return. Lost leverage and pulled his man back, then dragged him to the ground. Armand Membou false start. Not sure about this one, as no movement from Membou or any other Jet was obvious from broadcast footage. Bills Penalties Michael Hoecht offside on a punt. Jumped early. This took it from 4th-and-6 to 4th-and-short but the Jets were too close to their end zone to risk going for it. Ed Oliver neutral zone infraction, also on 4th-and-6. Reacted to the hard count. This time the Jets converted on the next play. Dawson Knox false start. Went very slightly early as the ball was being snapped. Dion Dawkins false start on a field goal. Well spotted by the officials as Dawkins shifted his weight before the ball was snapped. Offside on Bradley Chubb. Went early. This didn’t matter because Wilson caught a 25-yard pass anyway. Alec Anderson false start. Big flinch before the snap. Illegal shift on 3rd-and-7. Basically had two men in motion at the same time as the ball was snapped. Certainly neither was set for a full second. Hoecht offside again. Went early, but again it didn’t matter as Breece Hall ran for a first down. Spencer Hawes false start. Flinched, reacting to the right tackle moving but because he wanted to turn around and clarify something with Josh Allen. Plays that require further discussion Jets Penalties Malachi Moore defensive pass interference. There was some hand-fighting going on here but it looked for all the world like Moore made every effort NOT to grab or impede the receiver’s ability to make the catch. It was reminiscent of one of those NBA plays where the person with the ball deliberately tucks his defender’s arm under his own to create the illusion of defense-initiated contact. Offensive pass interference on Mason Taylor to negate a 45-yard catch-and-run for Isaiah Williams. Collided with the defensive player trailing Williams on a crosser. In real time, it looked like Taylor changed direction and made a bee-line for the defensive player when the design of this play calls for him to make his initial route look naturally like it just happened to get in his way a bit. However, to a degree, it’s possible Taylor’s man was leaning on him a bit, perhaps cognisant of what was happening, which forced him into a collision. As for the defender Taylor blocked off, you need to contrast this with what Azareye’h Thomas did last week. In a similar situation, he actively avoided the contact and went around the defender, leading to a 31-yard gain, instead of letting the contact happen and drawing the flag. That’s likely because he knows there’s a chance they won’t get the call, whereas the Bills player was obviously confident he would. Bills Penalties Illegal use of the hands on Davison Igbinosun. This was on the same play where Williams long catch-and-run did not count, and offset the Taylor flag. There was fairly incidental contact on Adonai Mitchell’s facemask but the Jets had a couple of big ones similar to this, including one on Thomas that negated an interception against the Bears. The difference here is that the receiver did not initiate the contact by leaning or ducking into the attempted jam as was the case on those two Jets penalties. Notable no-calls etc Here were some of the other notable missed calls, replay situations and controversial moments: Brandon Stephens’ early third down stop on James Cook was correctly marked short and also correctly not ruled as a fumble as his elbow hit before the ball was jarred loose. The fumble rolled out of bounds for what would have been a couple of yards loss to prevent it from being a makeable 4th-and-1. It goes without saying that every Bills’ tush push was a textbook example of “assisting the runner” but the NFL has turned a blind eye to that for years. The Jets ran their own, which didn’t have anything as egregious as Dalton Kincaid literally shoving Allen like a grocery cart across the line to gain. DJ Moore wanted pass interference on Stephens downfield early on but the no call was probably right. Stephens was leaning a hand on Moore quite a bit though, which isn’t a great habit even if you’re not actively preventing him from going in the direction he wants to. On the play where Omar Cooper got hurt, the block was legal as he timed it right after the pass was released. However, there could have been two penalties on the Bills here – a facemask on the player who tackled Kenyon Sadiq and an illegal hands to the face call on the play who shoved Cooper back. There was no defensive pass interference on the deep ball that Geno Smith underthrew to Mitchell. If only it was a worse underthrow – then Mitchell would have been drawn into Christian Benford, whose head was not turned, to create obviously flaggable contact. The electronic measurement system, which is pointless anyway because it still uses the official’s on-field spotting of the ball, had Cook marked less than an inch short on one play. The officials overlooked a blatant bear-hug by O’Cyrus Torrence on Harrison Phillips on a short yardage conversion. He literally had him wrapped up to prevent him from getting lateral, but you get away with these kinds of things on the interior. On Khalil Shakir’s jet sweep, Keon Coleman had his hand on the outside of Moore’s shoulder, pulling him back slightly from getting outside. He did let go of this pretty quickly, though. Brown flinched slightly before one of Buffalo’s successful sneaks and the officials did not notice. Benford had early contact with two hands on Wilson on a high throw to the pylon before half time. Under the old rules maybe that was uncatchable but that’s not a thing these days. The controversial hit on Smith had Aaron Glenn saying there’s no way they don’t make the same call if it was Josh Allen and he has a point. The difficulty here is that Smith initially starts to run and then sets and throws. To be clear on the rules, you’re not a defenseless player if you are attempting to run outside the pocket, but a helmet-to-helmet hit can still be called on a non-defenseless player. Additionally, he did ultimately throw the ball so roughing the passer can still be called even though he is outside the pocket. This could have been a flag if there was a low hit, but in this instance the Bills player was initially going in for the tackle and actively tried to roll away from…

title: After the loss to the Bills, it feels like Aaron Glenn’s fate is sealed
summary: “I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs.” That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the […]
full_text: Nov 15, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn looks on during the first half against the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs.” That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the television series, The Office . Michael Scott didn’t end up losing his job as branch manager of Dunder-Mifflin in the end. Nevertheless, the review remains relatable. Sometimes people can improve their job performance, but other times you reach a realization that they just aren’t capable of doing it. We are past that stage with Aaron Glenn. We can point to any number of dubious marks of his resume as Jets head coach. He is now 5-22, sporting a worse winning percentage as an NFL head coach than Hue Jackson. Glenn now has more than twice as many double digit point losses than he has wins. The latest defeat was the ugly 31-12 blowout at the hands of the Buffalo Bills in Week 10. There isn’t much drama left surrounding Glenn. Barring an unexpected late season surge, he will not retain his job as Jets head coach for a third year. Even if there is a late season winning streak, it still might not be enough. NFL teams don’t reassign their coach to a different department. Coaching contracts aren’t written that way, and practical considerations make the sort of demotion recommended for Scott unviable. Glenn will be let go. He will make enough money to leave football if he so chooses. If he decides to continue his coaching career, he will be an in demand candidates for teams seeking a new defensive coordinator. In the meantime, we will have to endure seven more games. That will be no easy task. I am sure the Jets will invent new ways to lose along the way. In some ways, the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills was familiar. Like a week earlier against the Chiefs, the Jets stayed competitive through one half of football. Their offense settled for field goals instead of scoring touchdowns. Then things fell apart in the second half. This loss still was in many ways different from what we have seen before. Leave it to the Aaron Glenn Jets to lose by three scores in a game where they had an equal number of first downs to their opponent and only 13 fewer total yards. The Jets showed many of the coaching flaws that have plagued the team throughout the season. On offense this team shows no understanding of how to use its talent to the greatest effect. At this point, it feels like salary is the main consideration driving the decision to lean on Breece Hall as the lead back over Braelon Allen. It certainly isn’t performance. The Jets can lean on saying, “A starter can’t lose his job to injury,” all they want. Whether or not Hall missed time from injury, Allen has outplayed him. The Jets struggle just as much to play to their strengths in the passing game. It’s easy to dismiss Kenyon Sadiq’s lack of a role as a developing rookie showing inconsistency. But when backup wide receiver Isaiah Williams gets 7 targets, and a mismatch like Sadiq only gets 2, it speaks to mistaken priorities in the game plan. The Jets can’t put the ball in the end zone. There are no simple explanations for that. I’m sure it didn’t help that they had a fourth round rookie quarterback with zero first team reps through the week playing half the game, but the inability to score touchdowns has been a season-long problem. Anyone watching the team would likely conclude that play calling has been a factor. On the defensive side of the ball, the Jets are simply playing bad football. Aaron Glenn referred to play calling as his superpower, but Glenn’s inability to orchestrate this defense has him looking like a mere mortal. I think there’s a danger for the Jets in blaming all of their problems on coaching. The roster isn’t good enough just yet. Part of this is that the team had a long way to rebuild after their attempts to win a Super Bowl around Aaron Rodgers failed. Part of it is the team has made too many personnel misfires. The Jets need to ask themselves hard questions about the way they do business on many levels as they chart out their future. For now, though, the coaching is the obvious and glaring problem at the center of everyone’s attention. Seven games remain, and unlike binging a television show, we can’t just skip ahead to the next season when we don’t like what we are seeing.

title: 12 takeaways from NFL Week 10
summary: This Philadelphia Eagles season hasn’t been a ton of fun. With the Birds on their bye, it was nice to get a break from them and watch other teams play instead. Here are some Eagles-related takeaways from the NFL Week 10 games. 1 – The NFC East remains open. If you’re holding out hope for […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots runs onto the field prior to the NFL game against the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images This Philadelphia Eagles season hasn’t been a ton of fun. With the Birds on their bye, it was nice to get a break from them and watch other teams play instead. Here are some Eagles-related takeaways from the NFL Week 10 games. 1 – The NFC East remains open. If you’re holding out hope for the Eagles to come back and win their division, Week 10 was a good one for this rooting interest. The first-place New York Giants and second-place Dallas Cowboys both lost. Accordingly, Philly’s playoff chances (via FTN Fantasy ) increased from 0.4% … to 0.7%! A huge development. OK, not really. The Eagles are still massive long shots to win the NFC East: But the division would’ve effectively been sealed with a Giants win on Thursday night. They would’ve clinched a head-to-head tiebreaker over Washington in addition to gaining ground on the Cowboys. Instead, the Giants choked away a 93.2% win probability with 2:15 remaining in the fourth quarter. Props to Washington for capitalizing and keeping their season alive, if only for a little longer. I’m curious, which team do you think is going to win the division? The Commanders are suddenly not a bad bet; they have the easiest remaining schedule in the NFC East and seventh-easiest overall in the NFL. The Giants, meanwhile, have the toughest remaining schedule in the NFC East and fourth-toughest overall. The Cowboys’ defense is absolutely dreadful but their offense might do enough to help them win some games. The Eagles can be ignored in this context until they provide reason to be relevant again. I’m still going with Dallas. But I don’t feel great about it. As for the team that Eagles fans should prefer to win the division, assuming it’s not going to be Philly? I previously felt like the Giants were the answer to this question because I can see them beating their chests about barely winning a bad division and overestimating how close they are to being serious contenders. But I actually think Washington might be the preferable choice. Maybe the Commanders keep Dan Quinn and put too much stock into coming back to win the NFC East, only to then struggle again in 2027. What do you think? 2 – Christian Parker is cooked. I do not feel bad for the Cowboys, obviously, but I do feel bad for the former Eagles passing game coordinator/defensive backs coach. He deserved a defensive coordinator job after his success in Philly. It’s too bad for him that he looks completely in over his head in his new role. I’m not sure how he hasn’t already been fired (as of me typing this sentence) after the San Francisco 49ers dropped 46 points and 584 (!!!) yards on a Dallas defense that ranks dead last in basically any relevant rankings. In defense of Parker, this level of defensive ineptitude isn’t simply on one person. And this unit also stunk terribly last year with Matt Eberflus at defensive coordinator. Still, keeping him at this point seems hard to justify. If he’s dismissed, the Eagles shouldn’t rule out a return to Philly (as a position coach). 3 – The A.J. Brown trade sure isn’t looking good for the Patriots. Although there has been reputable reporting about his degenerative knee, I don’t subscribe to the idea that Brown was totally cooked when the Eagles traded him to the New England Patriots. He looked pretty dominant when the Eagles went up against the Pats in joint training camp practices back in the summer. And that was with All-Pro Quinyon Mitchell largely covering him. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain injury in Week 1 that landed him on injured reserve. It seems like he returned too early since he was pretty ineffective upon playing again and had to miss more time before giving it another go in Week 10. Now he’s dealing with a new hamstring injury that could keep him out of action. Many seem to enjoy Brown’s struggles. I can understand why that’s the case after his less than charming finish to his Eagles career. Also because screw the Pats. I don’t begrudge anyone for feeling that way, though I do think it’s pretty corny how some of the same people now delighting in Brown’s failures previously insisted any idea that the Eagles were going to trade him was purely a media fabrication. I’m not among those delighted by Brown’s downfall. I enjoyed watching him be a dominant receiver and Super Bowl champion with the Eagles. I’m fairly nostalgic, so, I like to think of the good times more than his bad ending in Philly. Regardless of how you feel about him, there’s no denying that the Eagles are looking like big-time winners in this trade. Despite Howie Roseman seemingly not having much leverage in a Brown trade, he extracted the Patriots’ 2027 fifth-round pick and 2028 first-round pick. It’s only too bad Roseman didn’t manage to get New England’s first-rounder in the 2027 NFL Draft with the Pats now likely to fade down the stretch. Drake Maye suffered a potential season-ending injury in Week 10 and Tommy DeVito stunk up the joint in relief duty. At least that 2027 fifth-rounder could be improving. I don’t know that the Pats will definitely rebound in 2028. But I do think it’s typically tough to be the team coming off a Super Bowl-losing season (as we saw with the 2023 Eagles). So, they could be better. I also think Brown could be much more effective if he’s able to get healthy and stay that way, though the latter part of that equation is a question mark. 4 – There’s another team in Texas for the Eagles to hate on. Well, sort of. The Eagles should be rooting for the Houston Texans in an effort to knock the Jacksonville Jaguars (who owe their 2027 first-round pick to Philly after the Jordan Davis trade) out of the top spot in the AFC South. But that much is probably not going to be happening now. It’s no surprise that the Jags managed to win as 10.5-point road favorites against the Tennessee Titans. But the Texans lost as 4.5-point road favorites against the Cleveland Browns. And this despite having a 17 to 0 lead in the second quarter. Had the Texans won, maybe they could’ve won their division. Instead, the Jags are overwhelming AFC South favorites via FanDuel: Jaguars: 7-2 (-2500) Texans: 3-6 (+1800) Colts: 3-7 (+10000) Titans: 1-8 (+10000) The Jags are also now -30000 to make the playoffs. If Jacksonville makes the postseason, their first-round pick owed to the Eagles will officially be outside of the top 18 selections. And it could be as low as No. 32 if they win the Super Bowl. Thanks for nothing, Texans! But here’s to hoping they somehow win out and the Jags lose out, or something close to that. If we’re to assume the Jags are not losing the AFC South, you’ve gotta root for the likes of the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, and Cincinnati Bengals to win enough to drop the Jags to the No. 4 seed in the AFC playoff picture. At that point, they’ll be hosting the top wild card team in their conference in the first round. 5 – The Eagles’ Week 11 opponent isn’t looking so hot. Returning from their bye, the Eagles opened as 4.5-point home underdogs to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11. Might the Eagles actually beat this team?! Probably not. But the Steelers hardly seem unbeatable at the moment. They just allowed 38 points and 484 yards in a loss to the Bengals. Old ass Aaron Rodgers is predictably struggling. Through 10 weeks, Aaron Rodgers ranks 26th in EPA per pass play and 27th in success rate. His numbers in both metrics are worse than they were last season. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) November 16, 2026 It’s not like they’re a terrible team. Prior to the Bengals loss, they won four in a row. They could very well rebound in Philly. Maybe the Eagles make it interesting, though? That’s probably the most you can ask for at this point. 6 – I hope some team knocks…

summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced seven roster moves on Monday. In addition to these transactions, there were some more Eagles-related items listed on the NFL’s November 16 personnel notice. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. HOLLYWOOD BROWN and FRED JOHNSON These veterans are now free to sign with any […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 19: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Xavier Gipson (87) warms up before the NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Philadelphia Eagles on October 19th, 2025, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced seven roster moves on Monday. In addition to these transactions, there were some more Eagles-related items listed on the NFL’s November 16 personnel notice. Here’s an overview: WR Hollywood Brown and OT Fred Johnson cleared waivers. WR Xavier Gipson was signed away from the Eagles’ practice squad to the New York Giants’ active roster. DT Leki Fotu had a tryout with the Eagles. WR Quentin Skinner had a free agent visit with the Eagles. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. HOLLYWOOD BROWN and FRED JOHNSON These veterans are now free to sign with any team. The Eagles could add them back to their practice squad … but I’m guessing they’ll be looking for new NFL homes. Will be mildly interesting to see if they’re able to latch on anywhere. XAVIER GIPSON You may recall Gipson spent time as the Eagles’ punt returner in 2025 before a disastrous fumble in a loss to the Dallas Cowboys ultimately contributed to him getting cut. The Birds originally acquired him off waivers from the New York Giants. Then he returned to the Giants after being waived by Philly last year. Then he signed to the Eagles’ practice squad in September after New York cut him. Now the Giants are bringing him back to the Meadowlands. He must be well-versed with the New Jersey Turnpike by now. LEKI FOTU The 28-year-old Fotu is a 6’5”, 330 pound defensive tackle who’s made 26 starts in 66 career games played from 2020-2025. With the Eagles trading Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Birds have a need for more nose tackle depth. Fotu can help to fill that role, be it on the practice squad or the roster. QUENTIN SKINNER Skinner previously joined the Eagles’ practice squad on October 28 before getting cut on November 3. The Eagles could be interested in him providing some wide receiver depth.

title: Eagles reportedly bring Jeff Stoutland assistant back to Philly
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are not bringing Jeff Stoutland back on their coaching staff. Yet, at least. But they are bringing back one of his old assistants! The Eagles are re-hiring two-time Super Bowl champion T.J. Paganetti, their former run game specialist/assistant offensive line coach, in a consultant role for the rest of the 2026 season, […]
full_text: Feb 9, 2025; New Orleans, LA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles run game specialist T.J. Paganetti arrives before Super Bowl LIX at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Philadelphia Eagles are not bringing Jeff Stoutland back on their coaching staff. Yet, at least. But they are bringing back one of his old assistants! The Eagles are re-hiring two-time Super Bowl champion T.J. Paganetti, their former run game specialist/assistant offensive line coach, in a consultant role for the rest of the 2026 season, according to a report from NFL insider Adam Schefter . (The news was first teased by T.J.’s brother and fellow former Eagles assistant, Ryan, on social media .) T.J. Paganetti left the Eagles after the 2024 season to follow Kellen Moore to the New Orleans Saints as their run game coordinator. Here’s what we wrote back at the time: After beginning his coaching career at Oregon, Paganetti joined the Eagles as part of Chip Kelly’s original staff in 2013. A snapshot of his coaching experience since then: 2013-2014 — Eagles analyst (offense and quarterbacks) 2015-2016 — Oregon Graduate assistant/linebackers coach 2017-2018 — Eagles offensive quality control/assistant offensive line coach 2019-2020 — Eagles assistant running backs coach 2021-2022 — Eagles offensive quality control coach 2023 — Eagles run game specialist/assistant tight ends coach 2024 — Eagles run game specialist/assistant offensive line coach Paganetti, a two-time Super Bowl champion, clearly has experience working with legendary Eagles offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland. With the Saints unable to hire Stout, they went for one of his proteges instead. Now it’s the Eagles going for a Stoutland protege instead of Stoutland himself. Paganetti was fired by the Saints on November 4 due to their run game struggles. It’s not like dismissing him has fixed their problems: The Saints had an 11.8% success rate on their running back runs in Week 10, the third-worst mark of the 2026 season so far. It is the second time this season their backs have gained 0 or negative yards on more than 35% of their carries. pic.twitter.com/C6xLgBqbGs — Matt Harmon (@MattHarmon_BYB) November 16, 2026 How much of an impact will Paganetti have in his return to Philly? That much remains unclear. Chris Kuper is seemingly still in charge of the Eagles’ offensive line room, though it seems like Paganetti is now being granted a voice there. I wonder if they might eventually fire Kuper and promote Eagles assistant offensive line coach Greg Austin (another former Stoutland assistant) … and then backfill Austin’s role with Paganetti. Bringing Paganetti back doesn’t magically make the Eagles’ offensive line significantly better, nor does it make an injured Saquon Barkley healthier. But, hey, no real reason not to give it a shot. Beyond the scope of this season, which is likely already lost, it’s fair to wonder if the Eagles bringing Paganetti back is an olive branch to Stoutland in an effort to make him their offensive line coach again in 2027. That is, assuming he even still has interest in the role after being cast aside by the team this year. Nevertheless, welcome back, T.J. Paganetti. I don’t comment on things like this often, but T.J. Is an outstanding coach. He brought a ton of value for us in Philadelphia, and was a big part of our success up front. One of my favorite coaches from my time with the Eagles. He’s extremely knowledgeable, driven, and always… https://t.co/7PGX8OpGVn — Jason Kelce (@JasonKelce) November 3, 2026

title: Eagles roster news: Zach Ertz’s promotion among 7 moves
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced seven transactions on Monday afternoon in the aftermath of their Week 10 bye. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. ZACH ERTZ We finally have resolution on the Eagles’ intentions for Ertz. The team originally signed him to their practice squad after Dallas Goedert suffered […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Zach Ertz #86 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced seven transactions on Monday afternoon in the aftermath of their Week 10 bye. Here’s an overview: TE Zach Ertz and OT John Ojukwu were signed from the practice squad to the active roster. RB Will Shipley’s 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve was opened. RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci were signed to the practice squad. DB Shaun Wade was released from the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. ZACH ERTZ We finally have resolution on the Eagles’ intentions for Ertz. The team originally signed him to their practice squad after Dallas Goedert suffered an injury in Week 2. They then maxed out his three temporary elevations over the next three weeks. There was thought they’d sign the franchise legend to the roster after that … but they just … didn’t. And so Ertz remained on the practice squad as the Eagles lost games to the Carolina Panthers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders, and New York Giants. But now the 36-year-old (who celebrated his birthday on November 10) is eligible to suit up on game day again. How much will Ertz actually play? That much remains to be seen. Goedert is still here. Johnny Mundt’s playing time has been going down, as it should. Honestly, there’s really no reason for him to still be on the roster. There’s really no need to play Grant Calcaterra on offense, either. Meanwhile, the Eagles should be looking to find more snaps for Eli Stowers. The rookie tight end hasn’t done much to deserve them … but that much should be moot at this point in a lost season. If he’s going to struggle, so be it. It’s time to get him much-needed experience. The most interesting angle on Ertz playing for the Eagles at this point is his pursuit of the franchise’s all-time receptions record, currently held by Harold Carmichael. Ertz is eight catches away from taking over sole possession of first place in that category. With eight games left to play, it’s more than doable. I don’t know that force-feeding Ertz for the sake of breaking the record feels very fun. But it also wouldn’t have been fun to see him spending the rest of the year on the practice squad. Either let him play or cut him free. The Eagles chose the former. JOHN OJUKWU In case you missed it, the Eagles released Fred Johnson late last week. That move left them without a swing tackle on the roster. Promoting Ojukwu gives the Birds depth behind Jordan Mailata and rookie Markel Bell. I don’t know that Ojukwu, who turns 28 in January, offers much in terms of long-term upside. But he does bring some experience to the table with nine starts over 16 career games played. Not exactly surprising since Ojukwu has been with the Eagles longer but it is notable they went with him over former Giants first-round pick Evan Neal. WILL SHIPLEY The Eagles currently have one running back on their active roster: Saquon Barkley. And he’s been playing through multiple injuries. It looks like Shipley will be returning from IR to give the Eagles more depth behind Barkley. He missed time after suffering “ a partial tear of his plantar fascia .” The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday, November 21 to activate Shipley in time to play in Philly’s Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. It’s worth noting that the Eagles did NOT open Tank Bigsby’s practice window to return from IR. He’s on track to miss at least one more game, if not multiple. JAYDON BLUE Blue has bounced between the Eagles’ practice squad and roster this season. The team has been reluctant to play the former Dallas Cowboys draft pick on offense (save for garbage time). He’s really only around as a break glass in case of emergency option. Plus, maybe the Eagles think he has some long-term potential. CHANCE CAMPBELL The Eagles previously terminate Campbell’s contract with an injury settlement after he went on the practice squad injured list in October. Now he’s back in Philly to potentially provide linebacker depth and help on special teams if called upon. With Jihaad Campbell dealing with multiple injuries, the Eagles could look to use his two remaining temporary elevations for this season. HAYDEN RUCCI Rucci is a newcomer. The Lititz, Pennsylvania native played college football at Wisconsin before entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. He’s since spent time with the Miami Dolphins, Detroit Lions, San Francisco 49ers, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Los Angeles Chargers. With 144 offensive snaps and 104 special teams snaps played in 10 career games, Rucci has logged a single reception for seven yards. Rucci gives the Eagles another body at tight end for practice purposes. SHAUN WADE Wade, 28, had two different stints on the Eagles’ practice squad this season after previously spending time with the team in training camp. I know people probably don’t care much about who’s on the practice squad but I do think it makes sense to get younger there at this point in the season. As opposed to investing in more veteran players if the Eagles were actually good and competitive. The Eagles should be using their practice squad spots on younger guys with upside. So long (again), Shaun Wade.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: 10 Eagles things I think I think coming out of the bye week
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles didn’t lose this week — because they didn’t play. The bye week is normally a time for players to regroup and get healthy. There are a lot of players the Eagles could use back, but this is a team that’s 2-7 with their season a lost cause. They haven’t won a game […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles and Dom DiSandro look on prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles didn’t lose this week — because they didn’t play. The bye week is normally a time for players to regroup and get healthy. There are a lot of players the Eagles could use back, but this is a team that’s 2-7 with their season a lost cause. They haven’t won a game since September 20, a good two months once Philadelphia returns to action against the Pittsburgh Steelers on November 22. This was a good week to get away from the Eagles, but there are still eight more games to be played in his dismal season. A lot happened during the bye week, with the Eagles and around the NFL (there never seems to be a shortage of storylines in this league). As the Eagles bye week came and went, here were a few things I noticed watching the NFL this weekend — and other sports. 1. The NFC East isn’t good — again Every year this seems to be a thing, even when the Eagles have a Super Bowl contending team. Outside of 2022 and 2024, there isn’t much to brag about when it comes to watching the football teams play in the NFC East. The Washington Commanders win over the New York Giants on Thursday night was a rough watch, but playing on a short week didn’t help either of those teams either. I also wasn’t impressed with the Giants’ win over the Eagles in Week 9, wondering how New York was ahead of the Dallas Cowboys in the division. Then, the Cowboys gave up 584 yards and 9.4 yards per play to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. This comes a week after surviving against the Indianapolis Colts — who might be as bad as the Eagles. The NFC East has a combined record of 14-21-2 — a .405 win percentage. The four NFC East teams are 7-14 against opponents not in the division — a .333 win percentage. Who wins the NFC East is anyone’s guess (it won’t be the Eagles), but that division champion has the look of a one-and-done team in the playoffs. Dallas should be the best team in this division, but can’t get out of its own way. 2. The Sixers have taken over this city I spent the bye week going to see the Philadelphia Sixers on Sunday afternoon, and it’s incredible how the vibes changed with this team over the last five months. Even though the Sixers finally beat the Boston Celtics in the playoffs last year, that team wasn’t going to win the championship as they were constructed. Mike Gansey changed the direction of this franchise in a month, getting Jaylen Brown followed by LeBron James in the blockbuster moves of the offseason. Xfinity Mobile Arena was buzzing towards that team on Sunday, with every LeBron pass and brown shot. Not to mention Tyrese Maxey is one of the best scorers in the league and V.J. Edgecombe is a blossoming star. The building erupted when Maxey lobbed an alley-oop to James, and had me reminiscing of how much fun that 2000-2001 team was that won the Eastern Conference. The Sixers are everything the Eagles aren’t right now. They have a lot of stars that are performing at a high level and they’re fun to watch. They also win games, as their 11-3 record is second in the Eastern Conference, and their best start since 2000-2001. With the Eagles season a lost cause, the Flyers being the Flyers, and the Phillies getting older, the Sixers are the only hope in Philadelphia for a championship in the coming months. This city used to have that vibe for the Eagles… 3. Why I think Nick Sirianni won’t be back Watching a few NFL games this weekend (and keep in mind I covered the league for a decade), other teams just are more exciting to watch than the Eagles. The San Francisco 49ers have an aging roster of skill players and create explosive plays on the regular. The Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions are the same way, even though those teams have their flaws. The Los Angeles Rams don’t have Davonte Adams and Puka Nacua and the offense don’t seem to miss a beat. Why can’t the Eagles get anything going on offense? This lies deeper than the team being on the QB5 and WR3 and WR4 as the starters as recently as last game. This offense was a problem last year when the Eagles had their skill players healthy and had the most expensive offense in the NFL. The Eagles are only 20th in cash spending on offense (currently), but this unit is last in yards per game (260.4), yards per play (4.3), and 30th in offensive points per game (16.4). They lead the league in three-and-out percentage (42.9%) and are last in 20+ yard play percentage (3.5%). The Eagles are also 25th in explosive play rate (9.3%). Sirianni has an offensive background, yet the Eagles offense gets worse every year — no matter the play caller. On top of the seven-game losing streak and his inability to fix what’s broken, the NFL may have evolved past Sirianni. The Eagles may have to change things up to keep up with the current NFL. Other teams are playing offense at a way different level than the Eagles. 4. Eagles won the A.J. Brown trade Brown had degenerative knee issues during his time with the Eagles, and his production was slowly decreasing over the last few years in Philadelphia. brown’s best years were with the Eagles, but he still had some good years in him once he was traded to the New England Patriots right? The first year in New England has been a disaster — for Brown and the Patriots. Brown has 11 catches for 128 yards and 0 TD in four games, having three drops and battling numerous injuries to his ankle, knee, and hamstring. Brown is averaging career-lows in yards per catch (11.6), yards after catch per reception (3.4), receptions per route (10.6%), receptions per target (42.3%), yards per route run (1.23), yards per target (4.92), and drop rate (12.0%). The Patriots gave up a 2028 first-round pick for this. Give credit to Eagles general manager Howie Roseman. He had no other suitors for Brown and had to wait until the June 1-deadline to even deal Brown due to his contract and all the dead money tied into it. Roseman still got a first-round pick for Brown, not worrying about the year of the pick — but the value of it. Brown can still turn things around in 2027, but his best football was clearly with the Eagles. The Patriots paid for past production. 5. Speaking of the WR1 DeVonta Smith has been out since Week 6 with a hamstring injury. He’s only played in four games this season, totaling 26 catches for 310 yards and 2 TD, averaging a career-high 77.5 yards per game. The Eagles really haven’t gotten to see Smith perform as the WR1 since he’s been battling this hamstring injury all season, and Smith only caught passes from Jalen Hurts for three games. He only played one game with Tanner McKee before the injury cost him the last three games. Hopefully the hamstring injury is past Smith and he’s back following the bye. The same goes for Dontayvion Wicks and his injury, as the Eagles need both wide receivers to have a pulse on offense. The offense is hurting Smith’s production too. He’s averaging career-lows in yards per catch (11.9), yards after catch per reception (1.8), yards per target (7.56), explosive play rate per target (17.1%). The good news? Smith has a career-high in yards per route run (2.26). Hopefully Smith can made the most out of this year, or at least help out whoever plays quarterback. 6. No more Hollywood Brown or Fred Johnson The Eagles released Hollywood Brown and Fred Johnson during the bye week, cutting ties with a wide receiver who couldn’t see the field and a swing tackle who wasn’t playing over rookie Markel Bell. Philadelphia signed Brown to a $5 million deal, and he had five catches for 63 yards in four games — or $1 million per catch. Brown couldn’t get on the field over Makai Lemon (even when he was struggling) or Darius Cooper, so there was no need to keep him around on a 2-7 team.…
author: Jeff Kerr

title: Eagles vs. Steelers odds: Opening lines for Week 11 matchup
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles made history in a bad way in Week 9. They lost a home game to the New York Giants for the first time since 2013. An even longer streak in Philly’s favor might be coming to an end in Week 11. Returning from their Week 10 bye, the Eagles are 4.5-point home […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 15: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs the ball against Minkah Fitzpatrick #39 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on December 15, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles made history in a bad way in Week 9. They lost a home game to the New York Giants for the first time since 2013. An even longer streak in Philly’s favor might be coming to an end in Week 11. Returning from their Week 10 bye, the Eagles are 4.5-point home underdogs (per FanDuel ) to the Pittsburgh Steelers in a game where the start time was moved up to 1:00 PM Eastern . The last time the Steelers got a win in the City of Brotherly Love? You have to go all the way back to October 24, 1965. Maybe the Eagles can win this game. They have the rest advantage. They could be getting DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back. They could’ve made some much-needed tweaks during their week off. And it’s not like the Steelers are looking very threatening at the moment. They just got blown out by the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday night. Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 in less than a month, has an 82.9 passer rating over his last four starts. For context, Tanner McKee has a 76.6 passer rating this season. Go Birds! But I refuse to fall into the trap of being removed enough from the Eagles’ last loss to gloss over the same issues that continue to plague this team each and every week. They simply don’t deserve the benefit of the doubt at this point in time. The Eagles are 0-9 as home dogs in the Nick Sirianni era. However, I’ve seen a number of Eagles fans cite a stat from PFF that says that Lemon has a high “separation percentage.” If you’ve seen this stat and have been encouraged by it, I hate to yuck your yum but there may not be a more useless metric in the NFL statistical zeitgeist. Here were PFF’s “separation percentage” leaders in 2025. It’s a “who’s who” of low impact receivers. I mean, JAHAN DOTSON (!) was in the top 10, lol. […] Lemon is not Jalen Reagor. title: Steelers grades: Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy trying too hard to relive their glory years
summary: We’re going to do something a bit different this week. Usually, you’d see Joey and I going through individual performances or position groups and giving our thoughts. In Week 10, though, the Pittsburgh Steelers showed nothing but negatives, and we’d just be shouting into an echo chamber. So instead, we decided to just share our […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re going to do something a bit different this week. Usually, you’d see Joey and I going through individual performances or position groups and giving our thoughts. In Week 10, though, the Pittsburgh Steelers showed nothing but negatives, and we’d just be shouting into an echo chamber. So instead, we decided to just share our thoughts on the negative performance as a whole. Joey Bray: It would be hard to give any single position group or player better than a “C” grade for their performance last night. I have been trying to think of the worst Steelers loss I have ever witnessed, and this is certainly up there, if not at the top of the list. I would argue that this was even worse than the team’s most recent playoff loss to the Houston Texans last January. At least in that game, the team had a fighting chance going into the final quarter down one point. I think we learned what the Steelers really are last night. Pittsburgh was always bound to get off to a hot start this season due to the first half of their schedule being fairly easy. However, this is going to be a bumpy second half of the season. Sure, the team will probably pick up a few more wins against teams like the Eagles, Panthers, and Titans, but they have not proven they can beat any kind of quality opponent yet. They are a team that is fighting for a playoff spot, but still firmly below the class of the AFC. With an offense quarterbacked by a 42-year-old who is 28th in EPA/play, coupled with a lackluster and injured receiver room, there is only so far you can go. A quality team cannot have complete and total failures on offense at this point in the season, especially against divisional opponents. The Steelers pass rush could not get their hands on Joe Burrow last night, and he picked apart their secondary all night long. The Steelers have major holes on both sides of the ball that they will need to address in the offseason. For now, they are playing the patchwork game while trying to limp into the playoffs for another year with a team that has desperately needed a reset for a long time. Pittsburgh’s ceiling is the same as it has been for years now, good enough to make it to the postseason, but not good enough to hang with the teams that are serious about winning a Super Bowl. Jarrett Bailey: You can tell how a Steelers game will go from their first offensive drive. Look at what they did against the Saints. Jaylen Warren ran the ball down the field and they were in the red zone in four plays. They ran the ball for just under 200 yards and averaged just under five yards per carry, which is how they won the game. Against the Browns, they ran the ball four out of five plays on their second drive (after seemingly learning from their first series that went three-and-out) and scored a touchdown to go up 10-0. Despite being one of the best rushing teams in the NFL, the Steelers came out in empty on their first play against the Bengals. A bobbled snap and rushed throw led to an incompletion, followed by the shotgun pitch that never works and then another incompletion. Going empty right away just felt like the Steelers thinking they could beat the Bengals at their own game, which they absolutely cannot do. It’s easy to say in hindsight, sure, but look at what the Steelers’ receivers bring to the table in terms of separation. Per Next Gen Stats, 120 receivers ran a route and were targeted in Week 10. The Steelers’ ranking in average yards of separation when targeted are as follows: Germie Bernard: 116th Ben Skowronek: 115th DK Metcalf: 103rd Brandon Smith: 77th This isn’t an offense capable of being a spread system. There’s a stubbornness to the offense. Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers want to be the 2010 Packers. They don’t have the bandwidth to do so, and their pride and/or egos get in the way too often. And look, we all have that. I used to be a guy who got up at 7:00 AM after going to bed at 1:00 AM. That works when you’re 19, not so much almost a decade later. You have to adjust. And for Rodgers, he has to accept that he isn’t the star of the show anymore. He isn’t the main event wrestler that is going to be winning world titles – it’s okay to be Adam Copeland winning the TNT Championship and Tag Team Championships or John Cena getting a late-career run with the United States Championship. Rodgers has to be willing to allow that to happen, and at times it feels like he’s trying to relive the glory years. This isn’t all to bash on Rodgers because everyone loves to find excuses to do that. The Steelers have just proven to be a much better, and much more efficient offense, when they are a run-first team. It’s who they are when they are most effective, and they need to accept it rather than run from it. Steelers Nation, bring the party to the SB Nation app! title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The Steelers fell woefully flat in a battle for the AFC North lead on Sunday Night Football, losing to the Cincinnati Bengals 38-13 in primetime. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers aren’t there yet The 20-point margin of victory probably speaks for itself here, no? There were a […]
full_text: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers fell woefully flat in a battle for the AFC North lead on Sunday Night Football, losing to the Cincinnati Bengals 38-13 in primetime. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers aren’t there yet The 20-point margin of victory probably speaks for itself here, no? There were a solid five weeks of building hype for the Steelers, with a four-game winning streak and a Week 9 bye ahead of Sunday’s Bengals matchup. However, despite the Steelers’ last game being a dominant, 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns, I couldn’t shake the feeling that Pittsburgh wasn’t for real just yet. Frankly, we’ve seen enough good, not great Steelers seasons in recent years that the “Pittsburgh is a Super Bowl contender” narrative felt incredibly premature yet again, as predicted . While the Steelers haven’t been entirely unchallenged this season up to this point, the unavoidable truth was that the team hadn’t exactly faced a murderer’s row of quarterbacks outside of Joe Burrow in Week 3 (who saw success against the Pittsburgh secondary for 282 yards and three touchdowns) and Drake Maye in a down year for him and the Patriots in Week 2 (the Steelers still lost by 17). And facing a white-hot Bengals offense in Cincinnati Sunday night, the Steelers didn’t even look like they belonged in the same sport. It’s still a quarterback-driven league, and the Steelers’ effort on Sunday night showed what many have known all season: Pittsburgh doesn’t have what it takes yet to consistently compete with elite quarterbacks, and the team doesn’t have one itself. It’s worth clarifying that while a loss to the Bengals wasn’t exactly unsurprising, the way in which the Steelers lost was unbecoming of a professional football team. The internet is already exploding with takes along the lines of “I’ve been a Steelers fan since the Paleolithic Age and I’ve never seen the team lose like this” — I feel like I see that exact post every season — but they’re not entirely wrong. But as the Steelers veterans clarified postgame, these losses are par for the course in the NFL. Teams will move on and rebound — something the Steelers have done time after time. However, even if the Steelers had protected Aaron Rodgers for a tick longer on each play, won more in the pass rush, or cleaned up miscommunications in coverage, it was clear the team just doesn’t have the firepower to compete with a roster operating on the level Cincinnati was on Sunday. Pittsburgh beaten the Bengals earlier this season. But there’s a reason why coaches such as Mike McCarthy preach the differences of “November football.” The games are tougher. The stakes are higher. And the Steelers, once again, didn’t look like a team built for that stretch of the season. Despite two weeks to prepare for what was without a doubt the biggest game of their season so far, the Steelers couldn’t even manage to look competitive against the Bengals. Is it time to be worried about the Steelers? Not necessarily, unless you legitimately believed they were part of the AFC’s elite. But it was a brutal way to prove where Pittsburgh needs to grow before it can get back to contending status. To improve from the late Tomlin era, the Steelers need to win in the playoffs, and Sunday’s matchup was the closest thing to postseason football Pittsburgh has faced all year. 2. The defense failed on every level TL;DR: Joe Burrow had 302 passing yards and three touchdowns… in the first half. Not great! I don’t think any NFL defense matches up well with the Bengals, but for the Steelers, it’s an especially bad pairing. Pittsburgh relies on strong run defense and a chaotic pass rush that masks a vulnerable secondary. Cincinnati simply doesn’t need to run that much because of its overpowered passing game. And Burrow is ruthlessly efficient, even versus pressure — and it helps that he’s throwing to the best wide receiver duo in the league. It’s a perfect storm for the Steelers, and the results on Sunday showed that. Film review of even Pittsburgh’s big win over Cleveland in Week 8 revealed that the defense wasn’t as lockdown against the pass as the numbers might suggest, and the Bengals’ offense is tailor-made for exploiting any weaknesses in a secondary. The Steelers were beat through the air in every way imaginable on Sunday: over the top, missed tackles underneath, miscommunications, and simply losing matchups to better athletes. Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3 — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 Meanwhile, the Steelers couldn’t counter with their star-studded pass rush. Burrow was pressured the second-least of any quarterback in Week 10 (pending Monday Night Football) at just 17.4%, with right tackle Amarius Mims once again stonewalling T.J. Watt and the Bengals having an answer for every blitz thrown at them by Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. Trying to tackle Ja'Marr Chase is really tough 😅 PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JbQWYD0kNG — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 The coverage struggles were expected. But the Steelers’ pass rush is too highly-paid and celebrated to drop off like it did in such a big game, even against an offensive line as underrated as Cincinnati’s. 3. Pittsburgh’s offense has some fatal flaws The Steelers’ offense, like its defense, is still far from “bad” despite some games firmly in that territory. Over the course of the season, the Steelers’ rushing game has proven to be one of the better ones in the league, but Pittsburgh is still somewhat limited in the games where it can succeed. The patented “bully ball” approach really only works when you’re punching down — and in a negative game script against the Bengals, the Steelers looked like they were floundering. A standout play in that sense was a third-and-long fake screen that resulted in a deep incompletion to tight end Darnell Washington. For one, it wasn’t much of a surprise that the Bengals defense didn’t bite on the fake short pass in that scenario. And for another, the Steelers ran that exact play last week! Aaron Rodgers Tries To Go To Darnell Washington, But Overshoots Him. Jordan Battle Is Right There To Pick It Off. Rodgers Is Now 0 For 7 Today With An Interception. The Worst Start To A Game In His Career. Not The Night He Was Hoping For In Cincy. pic.twitter.com/eW3VmXIQ2M — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 16, 2026 Despite an extra week of preparation in a battle for the AFC North lead, the Steelers tried to run back the hits on offense instead of innovating. Honestly, I’d put the Bengals loss more on the Pittsburgh offense than the defense. The game was always going to be a high-scoring one, but by the time the Steelers gained their second first-down of the night, they were already down two scores with 3:28 remaining in the second quarter. Pittsburgh had just 8:19 of time of possession at the half. No wonder the defense looks exhausted and uninspired! One of the benefits of writing this column a bit later than usual is that there’s a bit more time to digest the game and see some tape breakdowns, which backed up the eye test from watching the game: The Steelers’ offensive struggles weren’t just the fault of scheme and play-calling, but also poor execution on just about everyone’s part. The offensive line struggled to move Dexter Lawrence in the run game and protect Rodgers from pressure. DK Metcalf, despite scoring the rare NFL “octopus” , had another game where he failed to make a contested catch and recorded a procedural penalty. And Rodgers, when he was kept clean, failed to capitalize on opportunities downfield. Remember Joe Burrow’s halftime numbers? Rodgers, on the other hand, was 4/12 for 25 yards at the break. Steelers passing game in a nut shell right here. -DK Metcalf getting completely erased off the map by press coverage -Brandon Smith, who (respectfully)…

title: The Steelers have reason to worry, but not to panic
summary: Yes, but also no. That is my final answer to a question we’ll get to in a bit. My fandom of the Pittsburgh Steelers can be traced back to 2004. I don’t know why I said “traced back” like an archeologist who is figuring out where a specific dinosaur bone came from, but that is […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yes, but also no. That is my final answer to a question we’ll get to in a bit. My fandom of the Pittsburgh Steelers can be traced back to 2004. I don’t know why I said “traced back” like an archeologist who is figuring out where a specific dinosaur bone came from, but that is the earliest memory I have of being a fan. In my now 22 years of watching football, Sunday night was pound-for-pound the worst performance I’ve ever seen out of a Steelers team. Where do you want to start with how outmatched the Steelers were? How about 484 yards to 222 in favor of the Bengals? Or Ja’Marr Chase having more receiving yards (231) than the Steelers did yards of offense. Quarterback wise, Joe Burrow had more passing yards in the first half than Aaron Rodgers has had in any game in his tenure as the Steelers’ quarterback. I could keep going – and I will. Rodgers’ 143 yards passing are the third-fewest he’s thrown in a full game as a Steeler. However, 118 of those came in the fourth quarter during garbage time. So if you took away those last two meaningless drives, Rodgers was 8-of-20 for 25 yards. The defense had by far its worse game of the season, as well, allowing Joe Burrow to put up the third-highest total EPA of any quarterback in any game this season, behind only to Drake Maye in Week 5 against the Las Vegas Raiders and Brock Purdy on Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys. That brings me back to the teased question, which is should the Steelers be panicked? After any game like that, yes there should be more concern than not. Constant defensive miscommunications, Asante Samuel’s inability to look like an NFL caliber player when lined up agains top tier receivers, blitzes being dissected like nothing, an inability to get any pressure on Burrow, and a passing game that is completely dead in the water – those are all massive, massive concerns. So if those are all real, major issues, what is the case for taking a deep breath and not proclaiming the season to be over? Well, the remaining schedule is much more favorable than we originally thought. Next week, they’ll play the Joe Milton-led Philadelphia Eagles, who haven’t scored more than 20 points just twice this season – that’s a game they should absolutely win. They then host the Broncos, whose defense is incredible, but offensively, they are brutal. Denver is 28th in offensive success rate and 25th in passing yards per game. At home, the Steelers can beat Bo Nix and make life hell for the Broncos’ less-than-stellar offense. They then face a Texans team that is currently 3-6 and allowed the Browns to come back from a 17-0 hole to win. On the road against the Jaguars will be tough, and I don’t expect them to beat the most complete team in the AFC. But then they have a home game against the Panthers – should be a win – followed by a road game against the Titans – should be a win. Those games are sandwiched between both tilts against the Ravens in Weeks 15 and 18, both of which are likely to not feature Lamar Jackson, especially if the Ravens are mathematically eliminated from playoff contention. Is this all to say the Steelers are Super Bowl contenders? No, and I’m not going to gaslight you by saying they are. And if in your eyes that means that everything else isn’t worth talking about, then I don’t know what you’re doing here, frankly. A team is never as great as their greatest highs or as bad as their lowest lows. The Steelers are still a 6-3 team with seven very winnable games remaining on their schedule, and a Jaguars game that I don’t expect them to win, but you never know what can happen any given week. 12 wins is still very much on the table, 11 even more so, and 10 at the absolute worst. I can already see some of you pounding at the keyboard. “THEY AREN’T WINNING ANOTHER GAME THIS SEASON.” Relax. The Steelers find themselves at a crossroads, not a dead end. Was it an awful performance? Absolutely. Is that the norm this team has put on display this season? Absolutely not. Hell, the 2020 Buccaneers were blown out 38-3 on Sunday Night Football and they won the Super Bowl. Performances like this happen to every good-great team each season to varying degrees. The Steelers are still going to be a playoff team. What happens after that, we can be angry about if and when it goes south when the time comes. For now, deep breaths. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Seahawks create open roster spot ahead of bye week
summary: The Seattle Seahawks enter the bye week on the outside looking in when it comes to midseason positioning for the postseason, however, following a pair of wins and with victories in three of the last four contests, the season is far from over. In particular, if the roster can have a little bit better luck […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks enter the bye week on the outside looking in when it comes to midseason positioning for the postseason, however, following a pair of wins and with victories in three of the last four contests, the season is far from over. In particular, if the roster can have a little bit better luck in the health department in the coming weeks compared to the past couple of months, Mike Macdonald and his squad have an opportunity to make some noise in the postseason. From Sam Darnold’s glute injury in the season opener, to the defensive front seven suffering several injuries, there has been no shortage of time missed by members of the roster this season. With injuries hitting the roster hard and needing depth on the defensive front ahead of the matchup against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9, the Seahawks promoted 2026 seventh round pick Deven Eastern to the active roster. Now, after a pair of games on the 53, the Seahawks have created an open roster spot by waiving Eastern. Today's @Seahawks roster move: https://t.co/YuBIGgo273 — Seahawks PR (@seahawksPR) November 16, 2026 Should Eastern clear waivers, he would seem a prime candidate to return to the practice squad, but perhaps the more interesting question is what Macdonald and John Schneider plan to do with the open roster spot as they head into the bye week.

full_text: The Seattle Seahawks entered Sunday’s game over the Las Vegas Raiders pretty banged up, and exited Las Vegas even more banged up after their 21-13 win. Their injury-filled afternoon started literally on the opening kickoff, when running back George Holani hurt his knee on Jadarian Price’s kick return. This is the play in which George Holani injured his left knee. Watch for No. 50 on the Raiders as he tries to tackle Jadarian Price. Keep in mind he tore his left MCL at Boise State back in 2020. pic.twitter.com/XM7A45jRWM — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 16, 2026 According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Holani suffered an MCL sprain. The injury doesn’t appear to be long-term, but we might know more before Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers. #Seahawks RB George Holani suffered an MCL sprain and is considered to be week-to-week, sources say. Seattle has a bye coming, so the hope is he’s not an IR candidate. But will evaluate it next week. pic.twitter.com/7bchySL4mw — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 16, 2026 Holani had injury issues at Boise State, including a torn left MCL. He was on practice squad IR for an ankle injury as a rookie in 2024, then injured reserve again for a hamstring injury in 2025. Seattle noticeably made Emanuel Wilson a healthy scratch against the Raiders, with Holani expected to be the third-string running back (potentially in two-minute drills, as we saw against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9) and a special teams contributor. Unfortunately, the Week 10 plan went up in flames quickly, leaving Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price as the only active backs on the roster. Seattle has Velus Jones Jr available on the practice squad in case the Seahawks need to elevate him to effectively assume Holani’s role.

title: Seahawks ‘really optimistic’ Sam Darnold will return and start vs. 49ers
summary: After missing their last two games, Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold appears to be on track to return to practice next week, according to head coach Mike Macdonald. The Seahawks starter has been out with quad and rib injuries he suffered against the Chicago Bears, his second injury stint of the 2026 season. Macdonald said […]
full_text: After missing their last two games, Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold appears to be on track to return to practice next week, according to head coach Mike Macdonald. The Seahawks starter has been out with quad and rib injuries he suffered against the Chicago Bears, his second injury stint of the 2026 season. Macdonald said on the Brock and Salk morning radio show that he’s “very optimistic” that Darnold could return to practice after the bye week and start for Seattle in their rematch against the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29. Mike Macdonald on @SeattleSports on if they think Darnold will be able to practice next week… "Yeah, I'd say we're really optimistic that he's going to be able to get a full week's worth of work and be able to play against San Fran." — Maura Dooley (@Maura_Dool) November 16, 2026 In his six full games, Darnold has thrown for 1,478 yards, 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions, while completing 60% of his passes. His completion percentage and success rate are his lowest since he was a starter for the Carolina Panthers back in 2021, leaving many with second thoughts about the quarterback that led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl last season. It hasn’t helped that backup quarterback Drew Lock has steadied the ship, going 3-0 in his starts and topping the NFL in passer rating, while playing against some of the league’s worst defenses. For what it’s worth, Macdonald has steered clear of any quarterback controversy and repeatedly stood by Darnold through a turnover-filled rollercoaster season. With the offense beginning to find rhythm in the run game and Jaxon Smith-Njigba putting up historic numbers, the situation Darnold returns to should be one better than when he left. The bye week should give the entire battered Seahawks time to heal, including tackle Charles Cross and guard Quenton Nelson, which would be massive for Darnold’s success down the stretch. For now, the Seahawks will play the waiting game as they take a week off and see if they’ll get their starter back for a pivotal divisional showdown after Thanksgiving.
