title: Washington Commanders free agency: Has Odafe Oweh been a bust?
summary: When Commanders general manager Adam Peters signed edge rusher Odafe Oweh to a four-year, $96 million deal in free agency this offseason, fans and analysts alike were excited about his potential in Washington’s new attacking defense. Although Oweh had only one season with double-digit sacks (10 in 2024) and went without a sack in the […]
full_text: When Commanders general manager Adam Peters signed edge rusher Odafe Oweh to a four-year, $96 million deal in free agency this offseason, fans and analysts alike were excited about his potential in Washington’s new attacking defense. Although Oweh had only one season with double-digit sacks (10 in 2024) and went without a sack in the first five games of 2025, a midseason trade to the Chargers saw him finish the last 12 games with 7.5 sacks, a pace that would have put Oweh on track for double digit sacks over a full 17 game schedule. Seemingly a strong fit for coordinator Daronte Jones’ defensive scheme, fans were excited about the prospect of high-level production from the EDGE position after the team suffered from a lack of talent at the position last season. Nine games into the season, the preseason optimism has cooled. According to Pro Football Reference , Odafe Oweh has five sacks, 13 pressures, six hurries, and 20 tackles. While the numbers are respectable — Oweh ranks 14th in total sacks — his impact hasn’t been exactly what fans had hoped for before the season began. In this article, we will look at Oweh’s impact so far, his free agent value and what to expect for the rest of the season. We start our evaluation with Odafe’s performance in the run game. Before the start of the season, there were conflicting reports regarding his performance in this aspect of the game, but so far he has lived up to his 2025 numbers and has set the edge well. Analytics site Pro Football Focus continues to give him a poor run defense grade (60.0), but Oweh has six tackles for a loss, and Next Gen Stats credits him with 15 run stops while he generally looking disciplined in contain. Hell of a play by Javon Kinlaw (#99) and Odafe Oweh (#98) creating a pileup on this counter call. Excluding all Hurts carries the Eagles only had a 38.9% rushing success rate, 27th in the NFL last week pic.twitter.com/ZXM6ncFRka — JP Acosta (@acosta32_jp) September 17, 2026 great play by Odafe Oweh (#98) to make a mess of the edge and get the stuff. also, Sonny Styles is really, really fast. pic.twitter.com/HRb52oIcWX — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 22, 2026 Oweh plays this about as good as an EDGE can pic.twitter.com/FlHkGQ413I — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 28, 2026 Odafe’s performance as a pass rusher has been more mixed. Highly athletic ( 9.92 RAS ), Oweh has demonstrated both power and speed rushing off the edge. His second sack of the season came against the Colts, when Odafe showed off his strength in London, driving the offensive tackle backwards into Daniel Jones, creating a fumble and recovering the ball for an early turnover while flashing his pure speed on a sack against the 49ers in Week 6. Odafe Oweh is a strong man pic.twitter.com/9fmY0jPYvG — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 4, 2026 Odafe Oweh stepping up to get the sack 💪 WASvsSF on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zVad5MpO89 — NFL (@NFL) October 20, 2026 Oweh also stays disciplined in his rushing attack which is a key in Jones’ scheme. He has also exhibited the ability to convert speed to power, as demonstrated during his fourth sack of the year in Week 7 versus the Philadelphia Eagles and former All-Pro left tackle Jordan Mailata. Odafe Oweh is up to 5 sacks on the season. This one was schemed up via the Nick Cross blitz. pic.twitter.com/GHcIU0b3l2 — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) November 13, 2026 Oweh absolutely DESTROYED Mailata for the sack!!! pic.twitter.com/ZkYTFdnpCd — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 The problem with Oweh’s play lies in his lack of consistency. Heady readers will have already noted that the edge defender’s sacks haven’t come on a consistent basis over the full course of the Commanders schedule. Oweh has disappeared from several games during the season. After a strong opener, Odafe went the next two games without a sack before bottoming out in Weeks 5 and Week 9, recording zero tackles, no sacks, with just 1 quarterback hit and 1 quarterback hurry, respectively. The issue is that Oweh has failed to take the next step in his development that many projected after the strong closing with the Chargers. While thought to have finally possessed the necessary pass-rush tools, Odafe has yet to demonstrate the ability to consistently win his one-on-ones on the outside even when the matchups have been favorable. Oweh gets a 1 on 1 with a TE and is easily handled pic.twitter.com/lIgEVYxJaX — RefTheDistrict (@RefTheDistrict) October 20, 2026 Although his total pressure rate is higher, per Next Gen Stats , headed into Week 8, when facing one or more blockers, Oweh had produced a 10.0% pressure rate, which was below the league average of 11.8% at the time. Oweh’s pass rush win rate of 8.6% through Week 9 ranks him 51st out of all qualifying edge rushers and, with Oweh’s $96 million contract value fresh in their minds, some fans have begun calling the free agent signing a bust, based upon the idea he was a reach that was overpaid in March. However, is that really the case? As usual with NFL contracts, the devil is in the details. Per Spotrac , Oweh’s average contract value ranks 17th out of all edge defenders in the league. This summer, Hogs Haven cap guru Bill Horgan compared the key metrics for several players with similar contract values, including former Washington EDGE Montez Sweat, to project a benchmark for Odafe’s production this season. By stepping out from the shadow of playing behind other veteran rushers, Oweh is expected to see his snap share rise from 575 snaps per year to 670+ defensive snaps in Washington’s scheme. If he can maintain his per-snap efficiency with the increased snap count, he could generate roughly 28 pressures and 10.5 sacks in 2026. If he plays closer to 800 snaps this season, then his production could align closely with that of Andrew Van Ginkel, who averaged 796 defensive snaps per season over the past two years. After nine games, Oweh is still playing in somewhat of a rotational role in the Commanders’ defense with 392 total defensive snaps (62%) heading into Week 10, which would give him 740 total defensive snaps for the season on an overall projection. Slightly past the halfway mark, PFF credits general manager Adam Peters’ marquee signing with 21 total pressures and five sacks, so while Odafe may be slightly behind in sacks, he is at or ahead of where he should be for expected pressures on the season. Furthermore, as BiB noted in his initial review of the signing , that, given the structure of Oweh’s contract which has a flat cap hit of $27.2m per year for the next 3 seasons and a minimal dead cap at the end of the deal, the signing will seem more affordable as the contract ages and the league salary cap increases annually. In conclusion, so far the signing of Odafe Oweh represents a solid addition at a position of need at, or slightly above, a fair market rate for edge defenders. The big commitment from a contract perspective was the associated $68 million guaranteed at signing and the length of the contract. But, if Oweh continues to play at his current level or above, he should continue to warrant his cap hit going forward. The issue for fans and the team is that the signing does not provide the Commanders’ defense a consistent pass-rushing threat who can win in one-on-one situations. Daronte Jones must continue to scheme opportunities for both Oweh and Chaisson in targeted situations instead of relying on them being able to generate pressure in a four-man rush. In the meantime, GM Adam Peters should continue to search for a true game-changing talent at the edge position via either another free agent addition or the NFL draft, which will likely cost more — in either cap space or draft capital — than the deal that Oweh signed this year. title: NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 11, plus non-QB MVPs
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 11? We made our 1-32 list and picked the non-quarterback MVPs for each roster.
full_text:
When the NFL Honors awards ceremony takes place the Thursday before  Super Bowl LXI , it's almost guaranteed that the player who accepts the MVP award will be a quarterback. Former Vikings running back Adrian Peterson is the only non-QB to be named MVP since 2010, and only three non-QBs have won in the 21st century.

 But what if quarterbacks were disqualified from winning the award? In addition to our weekly 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick the non-quarterback MVP for each team at midseason. Which defenders and skill players deserve love for what they've done this season?

 To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Patriots' trip to Munich could not have gone any worse, as they left Germany with a two-game losing streak and without quarterback Drake Maye ( ankle injury ). That caused them to fall the most out of any team in our Power Rankings compared to last week (three spots), and Maye could be out for the season if his ankle is fractured. New England is 1-3 in its past four games, with all of its losses coming to NFC North opponents. 
 The Browns are in the top 15 of our rankings for the first time this season after another comeback win -- this time against the Texans . Cleveland quarterback  Deshaun Watson  has conducted a winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime in all six of the Browns' wins. Watson joins the Cowboys' Troy Aikman (1990) and Lions' Matthew Stafford (2016) as the only QBs in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to achieve that feat, per ESPN Research. 
 The Commanders made the biggest climb of any team this week (three spots) after a Thursday night win over the Giants. Washington is 2-1 since its bye week, and it's still not out of the NFC East race yet, two games behind first-place New York while owning the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Giants. However, the Commanders have only one divisional game left to boost their playoff odds -- Week 18 versus the Cowboys . 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with a slight change at No. 1 from  last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

 While QB Brock Purdy is a top candidate for league MVP , Warner is making a strong case to be the first linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year since Luke Kuechly in 2013. Warner's 88 tackles rank sixth in the NFL. He's tied for first in forced fumbles (five) to go with a fumble recovery, 0.5 sacks and three pass breakups. He has done all that after returning from a broken and dislocated right ankle injury that cost him most of last season. For a defense on its fifth coordinator in five years, Warner is the constant and one of the primary reasons the Niners are 8-1. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 

 2. Buffalo Bills (8-1) 
 Week 10 result: Beat the Jets 31-12 
 Week 10 ranking: 1 

 Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge rusher  Greg Rousseau 

 

 The transition from 4-3 defensive end to 3-4 outside linebacker has worked wonders for Rousseau. He is in the midst of a career season, leading the NFL in quarterback pressures (41) and quarterback hits (27). He is also tied for fourth in sacks (eight). Just over halfway through the season, Rousseau has already matched or set career highs in just about every meaningful pass rushing or defending stat. -- Nick Suss

 Week 10 result: Beat the Titans 40-23 
 Week 10 ranking: 3

 Washington has been quarterback  Trevor Lawrence 's top target -- his 64 targets are 21 more than the next-closest player ( Jakobi Meyers ). Washington has 36 catches for 645 yards and six touchdowns, which puts him on pace to set career highs in catches and receiving yards. There's a good chance he surpasses his previous best yardage (847) before December. He also leads the NFL with a 17.9 yards-per-catch average. Sunday's game specifically showcased the trust Lawrence has in Washington's ability to win 50-50 balls. -- Michael DiRocco

 The Bears have maintained a top-five rushing offense (142 yards per game) despite a constant wave of injuries in the backfield. A big reason for that is the load Swift has carried in  Kyle Monangai 's five-game absence ( toe/thumb ). Swift has logged the third-most offensive snaps of any Bears skill player (63%), including 22 rushes against the Patriots and 27 at Seattle a week later . He ran in three second-half TDs against the Seahawks, has already reached a career-high of 10 TDs and is five away from setting the franchise's single-season record. Despite dealing with injuries of his own, Swift has not missed a game. -- Courtney Cronin 

 
 

 5. Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) 
 Week 10 result: Beat the Falcons 35-13 
 Week 10 ranking: 6 

 Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Kenneth Walker III 

 

 Walker has been a blessing for the Chiefs' offense, considering he has produced many of the team's explosive plays since  signing a three-year deal  this past offseason. He has already generated 1,044 all-purpose yards, and his 11 total touchdowns are already his career-high for a single season. By being a stabilizing presence, Walker has helped quarterback Patrick Mahomes find his groove following his return from the most significant injury of his career. Walker missed Week 10 because of a groin injury .  -- Nate Taylor

 Week 10 ranking: 7 

 Non-QB MVP at midseason: OT Amarius Mims 

 

 Not even pass block win rate, which is a great metric, does Mims full justice. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Mims is in one-on-one blocking situations at the second-highest rate in the league (87.6%). Yet he has the lowest pressure rate allowed among all offensive tackles (3.1%). Coach Zac Taylor gave Mims the highest praise Sunday by saying he wouldn't trade him for any other right tackle. Given Cincinnati's offensive success on a high dropback rate, it's hard to argue against Taylor's stance. -- Ben Baby

 The Broncos are the league's foremost escape artists -- six of their seven wins have come by one score -- so we're looking for an MVP from the defense that has closed out those contests. Linebacker  Alex Singleton leads the league in tackles per game (by more than a full tackle, no less) and run stop win rate (51%), but Allen's down-to-down relentlessness is the tone-setter for the group. He is second in the league in quarterback hits despite a double-team rate of 79.4% on his pass-rush snaps. Allen impacts most everything happening around him. -- Jeff Legwold

 There are multiple options to choose from on the Vikings' elite defense, and it's even reasonable to consider kicker Will Reichard . But Van Ginkel has been all over the field in coordinator Brian Flores' scheme. He leads the team in sacks (8.5) and pressure rate (15%) and is tied for the lead in forced fumbles (two). title: Kyle Hamilton rocks Christmas sweater ahead of 'MNF,' leads NFL Week 10 arrivals
summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
full_text:
Players across the NFL might want to look at the forecast before checking the mirror to finalize their Week 10 looks.

 

 Sunday's arrivals offer plenty of opportunities to layer up. Morning temperatures in the 30s in Green Bay and the 40s in Cleveland could make wool coats, chunky knits and beanies practical additions to the pregame rotation. The chill extends south, too: Atlanta and Nashville are forecast to start Sunday near freezing before warming into the 50s.

 Out West, sunglasses could be the accessory of choice. Mostly sunny skies and afternoon temperatures in the 70s in Glendale, Arizona, and upper 60s in Las Vegas favor lighter layers. Arlington, Texas, offers a different picture, with rain and temperatures hovering in the upper 40s -- another reason to give weather-ready outerwear a starring role.

 Here are the standout looks from Week 10.

 

 Monday night drip 

 It's never too early to get into the holiday spirit. Just look at Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton . He arrived for "Monday Night Football" in a Christmas sweater tied to Toyotathon that included reindeers flying with a car in front of them and the moon in the background.

 

 

 Sunday's best 
 
 Ja'Marr Chase fashionably mixed business with comfort ahead of a high-stakes night. The Bengals receiver paired a glossy beige jacket and matching snap-button pants with a white shirt and dark tie, carrying his cleats into Cincinnati's primetime showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers with the AFC North lead on the line. 
 Fernando Mendoza kept his first-start look simple. Ahead of his debut as the Las Vegas Raiders ' starting quarterback, he arrived in a navy bomber jacket with a dark shirt and pants, adding white sneakers and a smile to complete the look.

title: Cards rookie QB Beck struggles in debut, but keeps optimism
summary: Beck faced Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett in his first game, and it wasn't easy.
full_text:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck looked across the line of scrimmage in the first quarter Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams , saw Myles Garrett and  Aaron Donald  and smiled for a second.

 It was a moment that Beck dreamed of as he played football as a kid. And now it was his reality.

 But it was also, perhaps, the only reason for a smile from Arizona on Sunday.

 Beck's NFL debut ended with a 34-6 loss to the Rams in which he threw for 108 yards, two interceptions and no touchdowns. He also had a fumble and was sacked five times. Beck, who played every offensive snap, was the third player in the past 10 years with multiple interceptions and a fumble in his NFL debut, joining Bryce Young in 2023 and Spencer Rattler in 2024.

 "He did everything we asked him to do," coach Mike LaFleur said. "There was opportunities for us as an offense to make plays and help him."

 LaFleur added: "So, all in all, for the amount of plays and what we asked him to do, I was impressed."

 There were glimpses of why the Cardinals drafted Beck in the third round. He had two deep throws, one on each of his first two drives for 21 and 31 yards, respectively, that showcased Beck's talent.

 LaFleur described Beck's mentality as "awesome," despite the two picks, five sacks and a fumble that one of his teammates recovered.

 To Beck, that was all a by-product of him just playing football.

 

 "Everything that happens, it's all part of the game," Beck said. "It's the ebbs and flows of football. And I've been through it just about every situation, not at this level of course, but it's still the same game that we play. And I've been through the good, the bad, the ugly, the uglier. And again, it's just the ebbs and the flows and how are you able to respond when things go bad?

 "Obviously, we didn't respond well today and that starts with me obviously as a quarterback and being able to make a play or make a throw or make something happen for our team and our offense to have momentum and start to mount a comeback when things do go bad. But, just having the opportunity to play, I think that's what allows you to stay focused. Being out there is fun. Football's fun and obviously, again, the result that we got isn't what we wanted, but we have a lot to work on and improve on."

 LaFleur thought Beck threw intermediate passes "really well" and looked sturdy in the pocket. But Arizona's 34 offensive plays Sunday were the second fewest of the season across the league, and the Cardinals' fewest in a game in the last 25 seasons. They were also the fewest for a home team since 1999.

 Attacking the intermediate throws was part of the Cardinals' plan with Beck, and it helped get him in a rhythm.

 "He throws with rhythm, he throws with time, he knows how to layer balls," LaFleur said. "I know it sounds crazy, but if I'm just in the evaluation process of what he did, he did everything we asked him to do."

 Beck said he felt comfortable in his first start, something he attributes to his preparation. There were a few areas he felt he could improve in, namely converting on third down (0-for-6) and hitting deep shots (6.0 yards per attempt).

 

 After the game, Beck walked around the locker room and shook hands with his teammates. He let them know how much he appreciated all of them and their effort.

 It was Arizona's 22nd consecutive loss against a team that entered the game at .500 or better. The Cardinals' 123 yards and six first downs were both the fewest by any team this season.

 In his first NFL game, Beck had to navigate the emotional battle of fulfilling his lifelong dream and losing, especially the way it happened.

 When he looked at Garrett and Donald in the first quarter, his first thought was, "This is sick."

 And playing in his first game "was cool," but Beck wasn't satisfied with just playing.

 "Losing is awful, so I don't get that twisted," he said. "Losing is the worst thing ever. I mean, I hate losing."

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald ,  who unretired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape. We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 10 update 

 While Garrett didn't record a sack Sunday, Donald got his first sack of the season -- finishing with 1.5 to move ahead of Chandler Jones and Justin Houston for 31st at 112.5. 

 Hunter missed his first game of the season, and the rest of the list failed to record a sack -- with Mack and Campbell playing on "Monday Night Football."  

 Week 9 update 

 In his first game since Week 1, Garrett made his presence felt. He had three sacks to move ahead of Dwight Freeney, Derrick Thomas and Rickey Jackson for 18th on the list. He was the only one of the active leaders to record a sack this week. 

 Week 8 update 

 With two players on bye and Garrett out, only two of the five active players that played this week recorded sacks, but they were impactful. 

 Miller recorded his first sack as a Cowboy Sunday, moving him ahead of Terrell Suggs and into a tie with Jason Taylor for seventh.

 Watt added two sacks of his own, moving him ahead of Simeon Rice and Clyde Simmons for 23rd. He now has 7.5 sacks on the season. 

 

 Week 7 update 

 Hunter and Watt were the only ones to record sacks this week, with Hunter jumping back over Campbell in the rankings. 

 

 Week 6 update 

 With Garrett still out, it was another quiet week on the sack front. Of the active leaders, it was the oldest that recorded the lone sack of the week in Campbell. He moved back in front of Hunter. 

 

 Week 5 update 

 Hunter was the only player among the active leaders to record a sack this week, moving him ahead of Campbell to No. 26 all-time. Hunter now has three sacks through five games. 

 

 Week 4 update 

 Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR. 

 

 Week 3 update 

 There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

 

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

title: Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 11: Takes on four QBs, Lions, Rams, more
summary: Get ready for Week 11 with what makes Vikings-49ers must-watch football, Joe Burrow's MVP case and how Aidan Hutchinson's injury could impact the Lions.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 11 ? At first, it might look like a sleepy slate. Jaguars at Giants and Raiders at Broncos are two of our marquee games. But there's one contest that, to this enormous football nerd, is the game of the season.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll expand on why Joe Burrow looks like an MVP, tell you about another Rams personnel innovation, project eventual QB changes for two NFC South teams and wonder if Aidan Hutchinson is the final defensive injury the Lions can't overcome. But first, here's one matchup you won't want to miss.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Shanahan vs. Flores is matchup of the best   
 Why Burrow is the MVP 
 Rams should lean on their RBs 
 Hutchinson's injury wounds Lions bad   
 Do Falcons need a new 2027 QB? 
 Do Saints need a new 2027 QB? 
 Mendoza's debut is a scratch 
 Some extra inklings 

 
 

 

 I think ... Vikings-49ers is the coolest game of the season 
 The Vikings have had a fraught three weeks. Everyone was excited to see them face the Lions in Week 8 -- the best offense they'd faced in a while. Detroit stuck it to 'em with a sick schematic wrinkle for which the Vikings were not prepared -- multiple tight ends lined up in the backfield as quasi-fullbacks to pave open rushing lanes.

 

 Then the Vikings played the Bills in Week 9 -- Josh Allen and another grindy running game -- and the Packers in Week 10 with Jordan Love coming off a flamethrower performance against the Patriots. At various points over those three weeks, it has felt like the upcoming test for the Vikings has been the test for the Vikings. Will this be the offense to build a blueprint against Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unique defense? Or will Flores prove that his defense is insurmountable even by the league's top attacks?

 The NFL rarely exists in such absolutes. All of those particular matchups were exciting and educational in their own ways. But if there's one game I've been waiting for with bated breath in the seasonlong pursuit of an answer to the Flores defense, it's this one: Vikings against 49ers in Week 11.

 This is quite literally the best against the best. The 49ers lead the league in points per drive (3.0), success rate and EPA per play on offense. The Vikings lead the league in points per drive (1.24), success rate and EPA per play (if you eliminate the Bucs' rainstorm game against the Falcons, which is cheating, but I don't care) on defense. It does not get better for offensive football than what the 49ers are doing right now. It does not get better for defensive football than what the Vikings are doing right now. Snap the pool stick, toss it down at midfield and let's see who survives.

 Not only are these the most effective units on their respective sides of the ball, there's actually some structural similarity between the two. The Flores defense has been exhaustively covered this season, but if you've missed them to this point of the season: The Vikings are blitzing on 72.3% of opposing dropbacks through 10 weeks. I shouldn't need to tell you where that ranks among league defenses, but just in case: It's first.

 To blitz that much sounds deranged (and likely is), but Flores has greatly deepened the meaning of blitz packages in the modern NFL. He doesn't blitz to get the quarterback down, but blitzes to force the ball out fast to predictable hot reads. He blitzes to keep the back and tight end in protection and limit the pass-catching options the opponent can deploy. For many defensive coordinators, the blitz is an end to itself -- they want to get to third-and-long so they can blitz. For Flores, the blitz is a means to many different ends depending on the opponent and context.

 Let's consider the route distributions. Opposing offenses get all five routes into the concept 31.2% of the time against the Vikings, which is the lowest number in any season as far back as I have data (2017). The aggressive blitz fronts -- with five or six (or seven or eight) bodies on them -- keep backs and tight ends in the formation to protect, which makes the Vikings all the more dangerous when they drop bodies into coverage and only bring four on the rush. Against the Vikings' four-man rush, opposing quarterbacks are averaging an eternity to throw the ball (3.34 seconds, highest in the NFL Next Gen Stats database) and still suffer a 44% pressure rate, which leads the league.

 

 Flip the coin to the other side, and you'll discover that no offense gets five routes into the concept more often than the San Francisco 49ers . On 72.5% of Brock Purdy 's dropbacks this season, the 49ers have five eligible in the concept -- that's tied for the highest rate of any offense over the past two seasons with ... the 2025 49ers.

 Why so many players out in the concept? It is indicative of a change that's been underway in San Francisco's offense since the Christian McCaffrey trade in 2022.

 When you employ McCaffrey, you don't keep the back in to protect . Are you out of your mind? Have you seen this guy catch passes? The only season of the past five years in which the 49ers have been below 72.5% in five-out rate was 2024, when McCaffrey was hurt for much of the year. When the Cowboys called up a Cover 0 blitz in Week 10 in a got-to-have-it spot late against the 49ers, San Francisco had no issue getting McCaffrey into the route and quickly throwing him the ball against a defensive end ( Von Miller ) peeling off into coverage. A 74-yard touchdown later, the game was over.

 

 This peeling defensive end is a big part of how the Vikings like to deal with pass-catching backs, mind you. No edge rusher drops into coverage more often than Andrew Van Ginkel . But for as special of a Swiss Army knife as the Gink is ... do you like him dropping with McCaffrey in space?

 Much as Flores throws additional bodies at the offensive core to force players into protection, the 49ers throw as many eligible bodies as possible into the route to force defenders to win in coverage. Because the ball can go to George Kittle and McCaffrey at high volumes, it's hard to play man coverage against 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan -- your linebackers and safeties will be victimized -- so you have to drop into zone, which pulls players out of your blitz packages. Purdy has been blitzed on 29.1% of his dropbacks, 27th among 37 qualifying quarterbacks this season.

 When I say "five receivers in the route," you might instinctively think about spreading the defense out -- and you'd be right. But the 49ers, critically, do not play from spread formations. No offense has been more condensed in the entire Next Gen Stats era than the 2026 49ers, who have an average formational width of 18.9 yards -- a full yard tighter than second place (the 2025 49ers at 19.9 yards).

 This has been another big leap in the 49ers' offense since they acquired McCaffrey. From 2017 to 2021 -- B.C, or Before Christian -- the 49ers were in condensed sets on 42.3% of their offensive snaps. After the McCaffrey trade, that number leaps to 61.2% -- easily the highest among offenses.

 The condensed sets serve several purposes. They allow the 49ers to get extra blockers into the run concept more easily -- they wouldn't have nearly as complex of a running game otherwise. They allow pre-snap motions to hit faster across the formation, which strains how well a defense communicates -- linebackers have to see a lot more when all 11 players are in the offensive picture. title: Falcons WR Drake London cleared after being checked for concussion
summary: Falcons wide receiver Drake London has been cleared after being removed from Sunday's game against the Chiefs late with a possible concussion.
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London has been cleared after being removed from Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs late with a possible concussion, coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday.
London had six catches for 109 yards against the Chiefs in a 35-13 loss. He was removed in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a potential concussion and did not return in a game that was already essentially decided.
London has a team-high 801 receiving yards on 50 catches with one touchdown this season.
The Falcons have a bye this week before heading to face the Minnesota Vikings on the road on Thanksgiving weekend.
Stefanski also said that offensive coordinator Tommy Rees will remain the team's playcaller. Rees moved down to the sideline from the coaches' box for the first time Sunday, but the team's offense had similarly uneven results.
Stefanski said the coaching staff will take this bye week to self-scout on a deeper level and "with fresh eyes." He said the team has "to do better in multiple areas -- and then the first part of that is identifying those areas."
The Falcons have the sixth worst EPA per play on offense in the NFL (-0.16) and are 24th in points per game (20.1).
"I think we need to look at our process," Stefanski said. "A lot of this is we got to give the guys a plan that they can go execute, and we have to look at all the areas that we can do better there and then you have to execute said plan."

title: Fantasy buzz: Baltimore's Henry has confusing night, Chargers win first game
summary: Week 10 closes with Chargers winning their first game as Baltimore's offense adjusts to new QB.
full_text:
Derrick Henry had an interesting game on Monday night. I mean, it's hard to say he had a bad game when he scored 19 fantasy points. However, it was one of those games where you're happy with the result, but worried about what it means moving forward. Henry was quite inefficient as he turned his 15 touches into just 20 total yards. His 10 rushing yards are the second fewest he's had in any game with double-digit touches in his career. It was his also fifth consecutive game running for less than 60 yards.

 While Henry's struggles on the ground are worrisome, there's some good news. He was targeted much more frequently with Jacoby Brissett   under center for the  Baltimore Ravens .  His five catches tied for the second-highest total of his career. More targets could help make up for the lack of ground production. Henry has a potential rebound opportunity next week against the  Carolina Panthers  who rank top-two in both rushing touchdowns and fantasy PPG allowed to RBs.

 Other takeaways from Monday's game 

 
 The Ravens were not afraid to let Brissett air it out in his first start for the team. He threw 49 times, finishing with 340 passing yards and 11.8 fantasy points. Yes, the fact both Baltimore touchdowns came on the ground hurt his fantasy total, but the volume should not be ignored. With all the QB injuries, plus six teams taking their bye in Week 11, Brissett is in play as a streaming option against the Panthers. 
 Zay Flowers finished with six catches for 74 yards on seven targets. He has surpassed 11 fantasy points in every game -- except the two with QB  Joe Fagnano . That safe floor, paired with his upside, means he should be started every week. 
 Mark Andrews had his best game of the season, turning eight targets into eight catches for 82 yards. He finished with 16.2 fantasy points, all of which were season highs. I believe a resurgence has arrived for the star tight end, due to the team's QB change. Brissett has always targeted tight ends at a high rate. Fantasy managers in need of TE help should try to get Andrews on their roster this week -- whether it be adding off the waiver wire or trading for him. 
 Omarion Hampton had the best night for the no-longer winless  Los Angeles Chargers . He turned 22 carries into 105 yards and a touchdown. It was his second game of the season playing on over 60% of snaps and he reached 100 yards and scored a touchdown in both. Hopefully, the Chargers will continue to feature him. He has a favorable matchup coming up against the  New York Jets , who allow the second-most rushing yards before contact per carry. Consider him to be a low-end RB2 during the upcomng Bye-mageddon. 
 Justin Herbert had his best game of the season, scoring 16.26 fantasy points. He threw for only 129 yards with no touchdowns. However, the bulk of his fantasy points came via his legs, as he ran for 51 yards and a score. I'm reluctant to jump back on his bandwagon, though, due to the lack of passing results. 
 Tre' Harris finished with 86 receiving yards, which is even more impressive considering how few yards Herbert actually threw for in this one. Harris benefitted from  Ladd McConkey 's absence and is worth adding in deeper 12-team leagues. That said, I would be reluctant to trust any piece of this team's passing attack right now. 
 
 -- Michael F. Florio 

 
 Nov. 16: Who got the ball in Week 10? 
 

 The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out.

 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions 
 Rhamondre Stevenson  tried to play through his knee injury, but finished with just seven touches and 1.5 fantasy points. He narrowly outsnapped Corey Kiner , who had more rushing attempts (10-6) and ran more routes (14-12). Stevenson handled most of the backfield work early in the game but didn't play in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach. The upcoming bye week gives Stevenson more time to recover and, with TreVeyon Henderson on IR, he should remain the team's lead back. New England has upcoming favorable matchups against the Chargers and Bills, but much will depend on Drake Maye 's health .

 A.J. Brown returned from a two-game absence against the Lions, finishing with two receptions for 27 yards and 4.7 fantasy points before exiting with a hamstring injury. Brown was already seeing a reduced role following knee and ankle injuries, playing on only 65% of offensive snaps in the first half, down from 92% in Week 7. The bye week gives Brown additional time to recover. Mack Hollins led New England's receivers in routes run, targets (6) and receiving yards (48). He is worth keeping on watch lists in deeper leagues if Brown were to miss more time.

 Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons 
 Josh Downs caught four out of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut, finishing with a season-high 15.3 fantasy points after just three practices with Kansas City. Downs played on only 10 offensive snaps and ran eight routes, lining up exclusively in the slot. His presence also led to Rashee Rice lining up outside more frequently. Downs' playing time should increase as he becomes more familiar with the offense. He warrants flex consideration against the Cardinals in Week 11.

 Drake London led the Falcons in targets and ranked third in routes run against the Chiefs. He finished with six receptions for 109 yards and 16.9 fantasy points before leaving late in the fourth quarter due to a possible concussion. It was London's first 100-yard receiving game since Week 5, and Atlanta's bye week gives him time to recover.

 Kyle Pitts Sr . led the Falcons in routes, in part because Atlanta was playing from behind. Despite the additional playing time, Pitts has now seen just five targets in four consecutive games and hasn't scored double-digit fantasy points since Week 7 against the 49ers. He remains a TE2 moving forward.

 Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns 
 Nico Collins caught nine of a season-high 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown against the Browns, finishing with 24.4 fantasy points. Xavier Hutchinson ranked second on the team in routes run and targets (9), scoring a season-high 15.8 fantasy points. Despite Marvin Harrison Jr .'s absence, Tank Dell 's route participation remained the same for the second consecutive game. According to Mike Clay's strength of schedule matrix , the Texans have the 10th-easiest remaining schedule and sixth-easiest fantasy playoff schedule for wide receivers. Hutchinson is worth adding, though managers should monitor his health following a concussion evaluation. Dell remains a boom-or-bust flex option.

 

 Harold Fannin Jr . led the Browns in targets (9), receptions (7) and receiving yards (91) against the Texans. He's scored at least 12 fantasy points in each of his last four games, highlighted by a 23.4-point performance against the Steelers in Week 8.  KC Concepcion  led Cleveland's wide receivers with eight targets and remains a viable flex option. Denzel Boston led the team in routes despite a toe injury but has been held under 50 receiving yards in five of his last six games. As the team prepares for its bye, he becomes expendable in shallow leagues. Jerry Jeudy ran fewer routes than both rookies and gained 65 of his 74 receiving yards on one reception.

 Quinshon Judkins finished with 13 touches and 16.1 fantasy points against the Texans, finding the end zone despite a season-low 10 rushing attempts. Dylan Sampson outsnapped Judkins for the third consecutive game and again led the backfield in routes run. Game script has contributed to this trend, with Cleveland falling behind 17-0 on Sunday. Judkins is still the primary rushing option but has averaged just 3.4 yards per carry this season. According to Clay's strength of schedule matrix, Cleveland has the eighth-easiest remaining schedule for running backs. Judkins remains a low-end RB2, while Sampson is worth holding in deeper PPR leagues.

title: Kyle Hamilton says Ravens 'disgracing' standards after losing to 0-8 Chargers
summary: Pro Bowl safety Kyle Hamilton vented after the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the previously winless Chargers on Monday night, which was one of the most embarrassing defeats in team history.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- Pro Bowl safety Kyle Hamilton vented after the Baltimore Ravens ' 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night, which was one of the most embarrassing defeats in team history.
"Right now, we are disgracing those standards, as leaders, as players and as a team," Hamilton said. "Whatever flak we get is warranted."
Hamilton expressed more bitterness by adding, "All the talking that's been going on is all just talk. If you don't go out there and do what you're supposed to do, stop the run, nobody really cares, and stuff like this just stops mattering."
After losing their fifth straight game, the Ravens (4-6) watched their season bottom out and their reputation get tarnished by falling to the Chargers (1-8), who had been the NFL's last winless team.
Over the past 25 years, the Ravens had built a reputation as one of the league's most physical teams. On Monday night, Baltimore got pushed around by a team that hadn't won in 330 days.
Baltimore failed to establish the run on offense and couldn't stop the run on defense. When the Ravens had a chance to deliver a comeback victory late in the game, wide receiver Zay Flowers had the ball ripped from his grasp near midfield with two minutes remaining.
This marked the Ravens' second loss to a team 0-8 or worse in their 31-year existence. The other was an overtime loss to the 0-13 Dolphins 19 years ago, and that led to the firing of coach Brian Billick.
"At some point, you have to just decide about your manhood and what you want out of your job," Hamilton said. "This is our job. We can all get fired; that's the reality of it. If we don't do better, then we get fired."
The Ravens acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals 10 days ago, hoping to keep their season alive in case injured quarterback Lamar Jackson (right thumb surgery) could return late in the season. But those plans took a major hit with Monday's loss.
Baltimore fell two games back of the seventh and final playoff spot in the AFC. The Ravens' projected playoff chances dropped to 4%, according to ESPN Analytics.
"This week, we just have to have an outlook of, 'Look, it's do or die at this point," Hamilton said. "You show what you're made of, and we're going to rock with who we're going to rock with."
Unlike Hamilton, Flowers chose not to talk. He left the locker room as soon as reporters entered.
Flowers' four lost fumbles in the fourth quarter since 2023 are the most by a wide receiver during that span.
"You want the ball in his hands, but you also want to understand the situation [and] understand what they're going to be trying to do," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "[It's important to] know when the journey's over."
The Ravens' biggest struggle was running the ball, which has been a problem without Jackson. Running back Derrick Henry finished with 10 rushing yards because he was contacted at or behind the line of scrimmage on eight of his 10 carries.
Baltimore's 16 yards rushing were its third fewest in franchise history.
"Of course, Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it's a grown-man's league," Henry said. "We just haven't been doing our job good enough. It hasn't been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that."
The Ravens are in the midst of one of their most frustrating stretches ever. Baltimore entered Monday night having lost three consecutive games by 20 or more points for the first time in team history. Then, the Ravens lost to a winless team at home and on a national stage.
"You can hold people accountable; you can tell the truth," Minter said. "But in reality, you're playing on Monday night, and you have another game on Sunday, so it's going to be about getting up off the mat and coming back to work. And I think we have the guys to do that, but we have to do it. We keep talking about things, and [we need] more action."

title: Chargers relieved after beating Ravens for first win of season
summary: The Chargers beat the Ravens 23-30 on Monday night to earn their first win since Week 16 of last season, bringing a franchise-wide sigh of relief.
full_text:
It took 331 days, and probably far more bouts with indigestion, but the Los Angeles Chargers finally closed out a game with a win.
The Chargers' 23-20 victory over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night at M&T Bank Stadium was their first since Week 16 of the 2025 season (34-17 vs. the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 21) and brought a welcome, franchise-wide sigh of relief.
"Thrilled, let's do it every week,'' Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters after the game. "Good to see the smiles back on the faces.''
In a season in which so much has gone wrong for the Chargers -- from an injury-ravaged offensive line that featured three rookie starters Monday night, to quarterback Justin Herbert 's struggles in the league's lowest-scoring offense -- Monday's game was a most welcome experience all around.
The Chargers equaled their highest point total of the season, Herbert did not throw an interception for the first time this season and Los Angeles never trailed after scoring on its first possession of the game.
And even that touchdown, a 22-yard run by Herbert, came with a notable tag attached given it was Herbert's first touchdown run since Week 9 of 2025.
It was also the Chargers' (1-8) first game of the season without a turnover.
"It's been a tough year,'' Herbert said. "It hasn't gone our way this year and for those guys to continue to fight, not point fingers, and stick together -- they've earned it and I'm really happy for them.''
The team had been off to its worst start since opening the 2000 season 0-11 en route to a 1-15 finish.
But after a cross-country trip, the Chargers showed physicality on both sides of the ball from the start. Their defense forced three-and-outs on the Ravens' first three possessions, and the offense scored on two of its first three possessions.
Quarterback Jacoby Brissett , making his first start since being traded to the Ravens, threw for 340 yards, but Los Angeles held Baltimore to a season-low 16 yards rushing. Derrick Henry finished with only 10 yards on 10 carries.
"Heck of a run wall, [a] big emphasis on that,'' Harbaugh said. "Just trying not to let [Henry] get started ... guys just battled the whole night.''
The Chargers' offense also pounded out a season-best 160 rushing yards as running back Omarion Hampton finished with 105 yards on 22 carries for his first 100-yard game of the season. Herbert added 51 rushing yards even as he had a season-low 18 pass attempts.
"It was awesome,'' Herbert said. "It was so much up front, they work so hard ... and [Hampton] is about as talented as it gets, the way he runs.''
Not that there weren't some tense moments before the Chargers were able to close it out. The Ravens, down 23-20, had started to move the ball just before the two-minute warning when cornerback Tarheeb Still forced a fumble on Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers that Elijah Molden recovered at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:03 left to play.
Los Angeles then failed to get a first down that would have locked up the win, so Baltimore had one last gasp. But cornerback Cam Hart knocked down Brissett's last-ditch pass at the Chargers' 4-yard line to finish the game.
"You cherish them, let's do this every week,'' Harbaugh said. "Good to see the smiles back and that was something [safety] Derwin (James ) said, lot of fight in this team, and we all see it, glad it was rewarded.''

title: Justin Herbert, defense help lift Chargers past Ravens on MNF
summary: The Chargers' defense stifles Baltimore's running backs, and Justin Herbert steps up in Los Angeles' first win.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- The Los Angeles Chargers , who had opened the 2026 season at 0-8 and had not won a game since Week 16 of the 2025 campaign, finally breathed a sigh of relief after a 23-20 triumph  over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night.

 Not that they didn't have to slug it out to get there. The victory wasn't sealed until  Tarheeb Still forced a fumble from Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers that fellow cornerback  Elijah Molden recovered at the Chargers' 46-yard line with around two minutes left to play.

 Los Angeles had been off to its worst start since opening the 2000 season 0-11 on the way to a 1-15 finish, but the Chargers scored on their first possession of Monday's contest and never trailed the rest of the way.

 The Chargers were physical on both sides of the ball, as they limited Baltimore's run game to a season-low 16 yards while gaining 160 rushing yards of their own.

 And they did what they had only done one other time this season -- score the first time they had the ball -- to set the tone. Quarterback Justin Herbert , who had a season-low 18 pass attempts, finished off the six-play, 63-yard drive with a 22-yard rushing touchdown.

 Not only was it the first time since their Week 3 loss at the  Buffalo Bills  that the Chargers had scored on their opening drive, it was Herbert's first rushing touchdown since Week 9 last season. And as the evening unfolded, there were likely more smiles on the Bolts' sideline, including from coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert, than in the first eight games combined.

 

 

 Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) 

 Most surprising performance: An offense that has struggled to find impact on the perimeter, especially in wide receiver  Ladd McConkey 's absence (back), got a bump from  Tre' Harris . Harris, who had just six yards receiving on seven targets in last week's loss to the visiting  Houston Texans , posted 86 yards in Monday's first half alone. He registered five of the Chargers' six first-half receptions, and the 86 yards represented a career high before the second quarter was even over. (Harris didn't tally a catch in the second half.)

 Stat to know: The Ravens' 16 rushing yards were Baltimore's season low and a season low allowed by the Chargers' D. Los Angeles handled the line of scrimmage with such physicality that Baltimore's Derrick Henry finished with 10 yards rushing on 10 carries. Before Monday, the Chargers had held just one team under 100 yards rushing this season ( Las Vegas Raiders  with 57 in Week 2).

 What to make of the QB performance: Herbert entered the game second in the league with 11 interceptions ( Daniel Jones  has 12) and second in sacks (32), but he found some rhythm thanks to his mobility. His first completion -- a 22-yarder to Harris -- came on a roll to his right, and the signal-caller was a willing runner at critical moments. Herbert's 22-yard run to finish off the Chargers' first possession was his first rushing score since Week 9 in 2025. His 18 pass attempts were a season low, but the approach kept Herbert out of harm's way -- a week after he was sacked eight times by the Texans. -- Jeff Legwold 

 Next game: vs. New York Jets (4:05 p.m. ET Sunday)

 

 

 

 Baltimore Ravens (4-6) 

 The Ravens' season has officially bottomed out. The loss to the previously winless Chargers is one of the most embarrassing defeats in franchise history -- and it happened at home on the national stage.

 Wideout Zay Flowers' fumble with 2:01 remaining was costly for the Ravens, who lost to a team 0-8 or worse for just the second time in their 31-year existence. The other was an overtime setback to the 0-13  Miami Dolphins  19 years ago that led to the firing of coach Brian Billick.

 Holding onto the ball in critical situations has been a problem for Flowers, who has logged four lost fumbles in the fourth quarter (including playoffs) since 2023. That's the most by any wide receiver over that span, according to ESPN Research.

 The Ravens were hoping to keep their season alive in case injured quarterback Lamar Jackson (right thumb) could return. But Baltimore's playoff chances took a major hit in falling to the NFL's last winless team.

 Baltimore, which lost for the fifth straight time, has dropped two games back of the final playoff spot in the AFC with eight weeks remaining. The Ravens' projected playoff chances plummeted to 4%, according to ESPN Analytics.

 In his Ravens debut, quarterback Jacoby Brissett was inconsistent, but he didn't receive much help from a struggling running game and a lackluster offensive line. Brissett was sacked twice but hit nine times.

 The Ravens' home dominance has completely disappeared. Baltimore has lost seven of its past eight games at M&T Bank Stadium.

 Trend to watch: The Ravens continue to dig themselves into an early hole, allowing a touchdown on the opening drive for the third straight game. To make matters worse, Justin Herbert went untouched on that 22-yard scoring scramble, which is tied for the longest run by a quarterback against Baltimore this season. Baltimore has allowed 57 points in the first quarter; only three teams (Raiders, Falcons and Browns) have given up more. Coach Jesse Minter, who calls the defensive plays, hasn't had this unit ready at the outset of games.

 Stat to know: On a night when running back Derrick Henry did relatively nothing on the ground, he scored two touchdowns for his first multiple-score game in seven weeks. Henry recorded his ninth season with 10 or more rushing touchdowns, which ties LaDainian Tomlinson for the most in NFL history. Henry finished with 10 rushing yards, which were his fewest in three years. He was hit at the line or behind it on eight of his 10 carries.

 Most surprising performance: Tight end Mark Andrews made an immediate connection with Brissett, catching eight passes for 82 yards. That's the most receiving yards for Andrews in 24 games, dating back to September 2025. Andrews has been dealing with a broken hand since Week 3. -- Jamison Hensley 

 Next game: at Carolina Panthers (1 p.m. ET Sunday)

title: Bears RB Kyle Monangai says he's 'on track' to return Sunday against Saints
summary: Bears running back Kyle Monangai said Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints after sitting out five games because of a thumb injury and turf toe.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- The Chicago Bears backfield is nearing the return of Kyle Monangai .
Monangai said Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the New Orleans Saints after sitting out five games because of a thumb injury and turf toe. He has not played since he rushed for a career-high 30 carries for 146 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears' 23-12 victory over the New York Jets on Oct. 4.
The second-year running back practiced Monday as the Bears returned to Halas Hall for a 70-minute session after their bye week. It marked the second practice for Monangai in more than month after he logged limited participation on Nov. 5, two days before the Bears hosted the Buccaneers on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 9.
"The time off definitely helped, but I mean it's going to be there," Monangai said. "Offseason I'll heal it. That will be for then. It's something I can manage now. The time off was needed though for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago."
Monangai said his turf toe injury, which is in his right foot, is something he can "manage" for the rest of the season with the support of plates and orthotics inside of his cleats.
Before his five-game absence, Monangai logged 60 carries for 324 yards and three touchdowns. His 5.4 yards per rush ranks fourth among all players.
The Bears leaned on a combination of running backs Roschon Johnson and Salvon Ahmed to compliment lead rusher D'Andre Swift in Monangai's absence. Chicago has the fourth-best rushing offense (144 yards per game) but has struggled to convert in goal-to-go situations (27th), which prompted coach Ben Johnson to reevaluate the run game during the bye.
"I think over the course of nine games, there's only been three of those nine where we're averaging over four yards a carry," Johnson said last week. "Which, simply in our terms, it's just not good enough right now. And those guys know that, particularly as the weather continues to turn into Bear weather, we're going to need to lean on that run game more and it's going to need to come through for us. I got to look at, is it the fact that we're not getting as many explosives in the run game right now? Is that why the average is low? Or is it, we're just not moving the line of scrimmage? What are those factors? And so being able to have nine games of sample size at this point is going to be really good for us to look into."
Monangai was originally classified as week-to-week by Johnson, which is why the Bears did not put him on injured reserve as they expected him back within four games. The running back did not initially understand the severity of his turf toe injury, which he called "very painful."
"Originally, I thought it was my thumb I was dealing with," Monangai said. "I thought I'd be back very quickly. I didn't foresee this length of time being out."
Getting Monangai back after more than a month is the kind of boost the Bears believe can reignite their run game during a difficult stretch of second-half games that features four NFC North opponents along with two AFC division leaders ( Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills ).
