title: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 10: Playoff spin for Vikings, Pats, Browns, more
summary: Will Kirk Cousins be the difference in the NFC North? The Browns are going to the playoffs ... but not the Patriots? Patrick Mahomes for MVP and Kyle Shanahan for COY?
full_text:
We did not do post- trade deadline overreactions last week, preferring to see at least one weekend's worth of NFL games before rushing to judgment about the immediate impact of any of the completed deals.

 Now that we've seen the bulk of the Week 10 Sunday games, though? Well, as Dak Prescott would say if we hired him to introduce the weekly overreactions column: Here we gooooo ...

 Let's look at five potential takeaways from all the action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the end.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Cousins as the difference for the Vikings? 
 Mahomes to win MVP? 
 Browns going to the playoffs? 
 But Patriots missing the playoffs? 
 Shanahan to win COY? 
 Fantasy overreactions 

 
 

 

 The Kirk Cousins acquisition will win the NFC North for the Vikings 
 The biggest move at the deadline was Minnesota shipping a third-round pick to Las Vegas for Cousins, the former Vikings QB who was instantly installed as the starter to no one's surprise. Kyler Murray is still hurt (and wasn't playing well anyway), and Carson Wentz 's disastrous performance last Monday night was the main reason the Vikings decided they needed to make this deal. Fair to say the early returns are positive.

 Cousins was 21-for-31 for 207 yards, two touchdown passes and an interception in a 30-10 victory over the Packers on Sunday. Solid numbers, nothing eye-popping, but there is important context here about team confidence and vibes in general. This Vikings team looked energized by the return of Cousins, who ran the offense with a proficiency that has eluded all Vikings quarterbacks for the past two seasons. And he did it with just one week of practice.

 

 Minnesota scored the first 20 points of this game. The Vikings' all-world defense overwhelmed Packers quarterback Jordan Love , becoming the first NFL team in 11 years to record eight sacks and three takeaways in the first three quarters of a game. They finished with four takeaways for the game. On offense, star wideout Justin Jefferson set season highs in targets with 13 and catches with nine, finishing with 74 yards and the kind of smile he hasn't flashed since 2024.

 The Vikings completed the two-game season sweep of the division-rival Packers and moved into a three-way tie for first place in the historically awesome NFC North. Minnesota, Chicago and Detroit are all 7-2, and Green Bay is 6-4. The Vikings have a 3-1 record in division games, having beaten the Bears in Chicago and losing to the Lions in Detroit .

 Verdict: OVERREACTION 

 Yeah, you probably could have guessed where I was going with this answer just by reading the last two sentences of the last paragraph. There is no way to predict anything with confidence with four teams in one division playing this well. Sure, the Packers are 1-3 in division games and their offensive line is struggling, but they're also getting Micah Parsons back at some point. The Lions have won five in a row but might have lost star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a knee injury in Sunday's victory over the Patriots in Munich. The Bears are off this week, so there's not a ton new to say about them, but they've won four in a row and are obviously quite good.

 What we can say with confidence is that the acquisition of Cousins forces us to take the Vikings' chances very seriously, even in a division where everyone seems to be excellent. They just need a representative offense to pair with their elite defense, and Cousins right now appears to give them that.

 Will it last? No way to know. Cousins is 38 years old and certainly not all he used to be. But he's also clearly better than what the Vikings have been working with since they let Sam Darnold walk after the 2024 season. And the way they looked Sunday tells us his impact has already been felt beyond the white lines. It's a major move -- it's just way too soon to feel sure about anyone's chances to win this NFC North.

 

 
 

 Patrick Mahomes will win his third MVP award 
 Josh Downs  also had a fun debut after being  acquired by Kansas City , as the Chiefs cruised past the Falcons 35-13 . Running back Kenneth Walker III  has been the Chiefs' MVP so far this season, Kansas City's big free agent acquisition from the spring. But Walker missed this game because of a groin injury , which left the Chiefs to rely on rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who had 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, and of course Mahomes, who had a vintage game.

 The quarterback was 22-for-35 for 348 yards and five touchdown passes, including an 18-yarder to Downs that put the Chiefs up 14-3 just before halftime. Mahomes has 19 touchdown passes this season.

 

 Verdict: OVERREACTION 

 I think Mahomes is still the best player in the NFL, and he reminded us of that a bit Sunday. But he has also won this award twice. Based on how the voting tends to go, it will probably be harder for him to win again this year. Voters like to give it to someone new. (Before you ask: I am not an NFL MVP voter and never have been.)

 Mahomes has also taken a back seat on the hype train to Walker, and Mahomes's overall numbers, though very good, lag behind the performances of  Brock Purdy , Joe Burrow , Josh Allen , Trevor Lawrence , etc. Comeback Player of the Year might already be in the bag, and if he keeps throwing five touchdown passes every week, then yeah, MVP would be, too. But I think Mahomes and the Chiefs are very happy to build this season's offense around the running backs and focus on postseason success ahead of individual awards.

 

 
 

 The Patriots will miss the playoffs 
 Rough day in Munich for the Pats. Not only did they get smoked 35-10 by the Lions , but they lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury after the first series. Wide receiver A.J. Brown 's injury-plagued Patriots debut season continued, as he returned from his ankle injury but had to leave in the second half because of a hamstring injury. New England came into the game already banged up at running back and on the offensive line.

 Tommy DeVito relieved Maye and was ineffective, leading us to wonder if the offense can function if Maye has to miss much time -- especially if Brown also sits. New England is 5-5, 3½ games behind first-place Buffalo in the AFC East and a game behind Cleveland, which holds the final wild-card spot, in the AFC standings.

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 Twelve of the past 26 teams to lose the Super Bowl have missed the playoffs the following season, and the Patriots are in danger of making that 13 of 27. After making it through last season as one of the healthiest teams in the league, the Patriots are feeling the sting of regression in that area. They have a bye next week, so maybe that gives Maye and/or Brown enough time to get back in the lineup. (It does sound like Maye will be out an extended period of time .) But the problems range beyond that, including a defense that has given up 80 points during the past two weeks and has suddenly developed a disturbing propensity for allowing explosive plays.

 It's not over yet, don't get me wrong. I'm not locking the Browns into that No. 7 spot just yet, and the Raiders, Ravens and Texans -- all of whom are in similar spots in the standings -- have plenty of issues. But it's absolutely possible that the Patriots miss the postseason, and if Maye is out for a while, it might even be likely at this point.

 

 

 
 

 The Browns will make the playoffs 
 After falling behind the Texans 17-0 in the second quarter and still being behind 24-20 in the final minutes of the game, the Browns stormed back for an improbable 27-24 victory and improved to 6-4. After missing last week's game , Deshaun Watson had 312 passing yards and 50 rushing yards, leading a winning fourth-quarter drive for the sixth time this season. The blitzing Browns defense of first-year coordinator Mike Rutenberg made life tough for C.J. Stroud , and Cleveland wore…

title: No quick fix for Cowboys' defense, and 2027 looks bleak too
summary: Even setting aside the status of DC Christian Parker, Dallas is light on draft picks and has big contract decisions ahead.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Last week, San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak was asked about a Dallas Cowboys defense that was ranked near the bottom in most statistical categories.

 "We never look at a team's stats," Kubiak said. "We don't let that tell us anything. We watch the tape. ... The Dallas Cowboys are a very talented defense. They've got players on all three levels: defensive line, linebacker and in the back end."

 Perhaps it was just coach speak, especially considering that a few days later the 49ers hung 584 yards on Dallas -- the most allowed in a Cowboys home game.

 A day after the 46-40 loss to the 49ers, Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer did not put to bed the possibility of making a staff change with first-time coordinator Christian Parker or any of the assistants.

 "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today," he said.

 

 How did the Cowboys get here? The promising signs during training camp in Oxnard, California, and in joint practices against the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints have been replaced by the same story as last season and the season before that.

 Too many big plays allowed. Too many missed tackles. Too many communication breakdowns. Schottenheimer mentioned doing more drills in practice to lower the target when tackling. He also discussed simplifying things defensively.

 "That's definitely a potential solution that we're talking about," Schottenheimer said.

 In the past six weeks, the Cowboys traded for cornerback  Joey Porter Jr . to boost their coverage and added veteran coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant. Now, with seven games remaining, they are still looking for answers.

 Maybe the Cowboys weren't going to be a top-of-the-line defense, but should they be this bad?

 Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams is having one of his better seasons. Defensive tackle Kenny Clark might not be the Pro Bowler he was with the Green Bay Packers , but he is more than serviceable. Same with edge Rashan Gary . Von Miller is 37, but he had nine sacks last season for Washington. Linebacker  Donovan Ezeiruaku was viewed as a second-round steal when the Cowboys got him last year.

 There other questions at linebacker, but Shemar James might have some promise.

 

 At cornerback, when Porter has played since the trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers , he has performed ably. DaRon Bland owns an NFL record for interceptions returned for a touchdown in a season (five), but that seems eons ago with how he has played. Cobie Durant has forged a solid career.

 The Cowboys signed safety Jalen Thompson to a three-year, $33 million deal, but he has not played since Week 3 because of a serious hamstring injury. Rookie Caleb Downs was perceived to be the most NFL-ready defender in last spring's draft.

 And yet the Cowboys' defense is as bad as it was in 2025 -- and 2024.

 Blame can be placed on the players; on Parker and the staff; on Schottenheimer, who hired Parker; and on owner and general manager Jerry Jones, who has final authority on everything.

 Parker's inexperience has been seen in how the Cowboys defended the final play against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 3, playing man coverage instead of zone and giving up a long catch to set up the Ravens' winning field goal, and had Miller in coverage on running back  Christian McCaffrey on Sunday's 66-yard clinching touchdown.

 

 Miller, 37, took accountability for the coverage breakdown -- he jumped too far outside on McCaffrey, creating the passing lane -- but he defended Parker.

 "We've got great teachers on this team. I can appreciate great teaching and great coaches," Miller said. "I've been around a lot of great coaches. Christian Parker is a genius. He's a great coach. The schemes that he has for us, we're just not bringing it to life."

 Parker's immediate predecessors, the experienced Mike Zimmer and Matt Eberflus, had tons of experience but similar outcomes.

 Over the past two seasons, Jones has lamented all of the coordinator changes. Parker is their fourth in as many seasons. Does Jones want to have a fifth DC in as many seasons in 2027? Does he change out the entire coaching staff, Schottenheimer included?

 There has to be an honest assessment of the talent on hand. Too often the Cowboys have overvalued their own players and made mistakes.

 Perhaps Bland's drop in play is because of health -- two foot surgeries the past two years, and he now has a high ankle sprain -- or maybe his success was a product of a Micah Parsons ' led pass rush that forced quarterbacks to make quicker decisions.

 For the past two seasons after Parsons was traded to Green Bay, the Cowboys have gone with the premise that a group of pass rushers is better than a singular star. That has not worked. Of the Cowboys' five sacks of 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy  on Sunday, 4.5 came from defensive tackles. The Cowboys' group of pass rushers has combined for eight sacks in 10 games.

 

 Rebuilding the defense will be difficult.

 The Cowboys will have salary cap decisions to make on Gary, Bland and maybe Clark. They will have to determine whether they want to sign Porter long term or use the franchise tag on him in 2027, which would have a trickle-down effect on what might happen with wide receiver George Pickens .

 The Cowboys have 11 defensive contributors set to become free agents when the season ends. Beyond Porter and defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia , the Cowboys might not have another worth keeping.

 The Cowboys can't even get too excited about the draft. Because of last year's Williams trade, the best of the Cowboys' two first-round picks will go to the New York Jets . At the moment, that would be the No. 13 pick. The Cowboys own the Packers' first-round pick from the Parsons trade, which is currently No. 21.

 After that, the Cowboys have only three more selections in the 2027 draft. Beyond the first, they have picks in Rounds 2, 4 and 7. In 2028, without knowing potential compensatory picks, they have six picks: first, third, fourth, fifth and two sixth-rounders.

 Do they use all of those picks on defense, and will they make the right selections? In the past 10 years they have missed on early-round picks in DE  Taco Charlton (first, 2017), DT  Trysten Hill (second, 2019), CB  Kelvin Joseph (second, 2021) LB  Sam Williams (second, 2022) and DT  Mazi Smith (first, 2023).

 These are issues that need to be addressed whenever the season ends.

 "At some point something's got to give, and we're kind of trying to figure that out now," safety Malik Hooker said. "I mean, it's late in the season. We shouldn't be having those issues, but sometimes the journey takes longer than what you think it's going to take."

title: Sources: Cowboys RG Tyler Booker, CB DaRon Bland have high ankle sprains
summary: The Cowboys are looking at multiple week absences for right guard Tyler Booker and cornerback DaRon Bland because of high ankle sprains, sources told ESPN.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys are looking at multiple week absences for right guard Tyler Booker and cornerback DaRon Bland because of high ankle sprains suffered in Sunday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers , per sources.
Bland suffered the injury on San Francisco's first touchdown drive, attempting to tackle Deebo Samuel Sr . and did not return to the game. Booker was injured later in the first half and did not return to the game in the second half.
Both players were scheduled to get more testing done Monday that would better define the length of their absences.
If either player is placed on injured reserve, they would miss the next four games, which would put their earliest return coming Dec. 27 against the Jacksonville Jaguars with the Cowboys having their bye week Dec. 13.
With the bye week, the Cowboys could choose to keep both on the active roster.
Last year, Booker missed three games with a high ankle sprain. Bland has been bothered by foot injuries in the last two years and entered Sunday as a game-time decision because of an ankle sprain suffered in practice. The injury he suffered Sunday was to his other ankle.
Complicating matters for the Cowboys is whether to put either or both on injured reserve. The Cowboys have used most of their eight return designations this season. They could see the return of safety Jalen Thompson , who has not played since Week 3 because of a hamstring injury, this week.
The Cowboys have used the return designations on linebacker Marist Liufau , cornerback Devin Moore , left guard Tyler Smith , defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard and safety P.J. Locke .
In addition to Thompson, the Cowboys have linebacker Malachi Lawrence (ankle) and running back Tyler Goodson (knee) potentially coming off injured reserve. Tight end Jake Ferguson (knee) is expected to miss multiple weeks as well with a knee injury, but he remains on the active roster.

title: What Broncos are doing to try to make Bo Nix more consistent throughout games
summary: Nix has a knack for coming through big late in games, but the Broncos want him to play better earlier to lessen the fourth-quarter drama.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos would like Bo Nix to go from being a fourth-quarter quarterback to a four-quarter QB.

 This season, and for much of his three-year career, Nix and the team's offense have shown an innate, repeated ability to put it all together in the final quarter, regardless of whatever troubles they faced in the first three. Six of the Broncos' seven wins this season have been by one score. They've won 16 one-score regular-season games in a row, dating to 2025, and Nix has thrown five of his 11 touchdown passes this season in the final period.

 So as the 7-2 Broncos emerge from their bye week to host the 4-6 Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday ( 4:25 p.m. ET, Empower Field at Mile High, CBS ), everyone -- from coach Sean Payton to Nix on down -- would like to see the offense utilize its fourth-quarter success much earlier, so the Broncos don't have to perpetually live in a one-score world.

 "I don't have the answer," Payton said days before the Broncos beat the Panthers 26-21 in Week 9 after erasing another fourth-quarter deficit. "... I look at it internally myself like, 'Alright, let's get going.' [But] we want to start fast."

 

 The Broncos enter the post-bye portion of their schedule riding a five-game winning streak -- the third time in four seasons under Payton they've had a 5-0 stretch. And Nix had arguably his three most impactful outings of this season in the three games preceding the bye.

 The Broncos hope that recent uptick is a sign of things to come for the QB. Nix has thrown for at least 220 passing yards during each of the past three games (had done it only twice in Denver's first six contests). He has also completed 62% of his passes in three of the past four games after doing it only once in his first five. He has thrown five touchdown passes in the past three games, compared with six over the first six. And, yes, the Broncos have four one-score wins during the current win streak.

 All of this has occurred since Payton abruptly reassumed playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb after a 2-2 start. Five wins later, the Broncos are tied with the Kansas City Chiefs atop the AFC West and are in the mix to secure home-field advantage in the AFC playoffs for a second consecutive season. And the numbers say that Nix has found a little more in his game over the past month, potentially leading to more consistent, four-quarter performances from him and the offense.

 "Look, the guy we see every day is the same, ready, prepared, tough, never down, never looking to blame anybody, he shows up, works his ass off and we win," Broncos offensive tackle Mike McGlinchey said of Nix. "... I feel like that's been the same every week. I think maybe we've played a little better overall, all of us, and maybe people think they see a difference in him."

 Nix's play has been a hot-button topic this season, especially during the first month. When Payton took over playcalling, Denver was mired at, or near, the bottom of most major statistical categories, as was Nix.

 Some of the offense's struggles before the playcaller change have remained. The Broncos were 20th in passing yards before the change and are 25th now. They averaged 3.6 yards per carry before the change and 3.7 since. But they've scored more, going from 16.8 offensive points per game the first four weeks (tied for 28th) to 24.8 since Week 5 (11th). Their offensive EPA has also increased, going from minus-7.48 expected points added (21st) in the first four weeks to plus-14.49 since Week 5 (12th).

 

 A key to that increased effectiveness is adding more runs to the mix. Payton has used words such as "efficiency" and "balance" to describe his efforts to calm the waters for Nix.

 "When we improve the picture around him, it will improve what he can do," Payton said. "... It is truly all of us in there."

 The Broncos were 29th in rushing yards per game (81.3), 27th in attempts per game (22.5) and tied for last in the league in runs of 10 yards or more (four) in the first four games. Though the rushing yards (99.6, 25th) and runs of 10-plus yards (nine, 25th) have slightly increased, the number of carries (26.6, 10th) has seen a more dramatic leap.

 Defenses have also played Nix differently since Payton took over playcalling, most notably increasing the frequency of zone defense. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Nix has seen zone looks on a league-leading 74.8% of his dropbacks since Week 5, a drastic increase from 60.8% over the first four weeks (15th among NFL starting quarterbacks). Nix's touchdown-to-interception ratio has improved in concert, with him throwing six touchdown passes and one interception since Week 5 after tossing five touchdowns and three picks in the first four weeks.

 His completion percentage has moved from 60% in Weeks 1-4 to 61.3% over the past five games, and his completion percentage above expectation has moved from 27th (minus-5.3%) in the first four games to 23rd (minus-2.1%) in the past five, per Next Gen Stats.

 The improvements, though noteworthy, aren't significant enough for Payton and Nix to announce a cure. "We still have a lot of work to do ... a lot of things to fix," Payton said.

 But there has always been a feeling that if Nix's late-game calm and precision could be more uniform across four quarters, the Broncos will be closer to having the offense everyone in the organization wants. The schedule could help continue the process. Five of the Broncos' final eight games, including Sunday's matchup, are against teams currently ranked 20th or worst in scoring defense. Only one of the Broncos' final eight opponents -- the Pittsburgh Steelers -- has a scoring defense ranked in the top half of the NFL.

 

 Though Nix wants to spread his effective play throughout an entire game, he also hopes to keep the fourth-quarter edge that has defined his early career.

 "I've always felt like I've wanted to feel like a clutch player," Nix said. "It's an important quality as a player when everybody's looking at you and the pressure's on. I don't think you do it individually ... I just think we have a lot of guys with a clutch gene.

 "We have a lot of guys that when the game's on the line, will just find ways to go score ... I'd much rather be clutch than the other way around."

title: Packers' Matt LaFleur still plans on Micah Parsons to return on Thanksgiving Eve
summary: The Packers still hope Micah Parsons will be ready to make his return for the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Rams in Week 12.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Micah Parsons still has work to do to make his return from last year's knee injury in time for the Green Bay Packers ' next game, but the hope is that the All-Pro edge rusher will be ready for the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12.
"Well, that's my plan," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Monday. "I think my plan's been different than everyone else's this whole time. We'll see."
The Packers have been without Parsons since Week 15 of last year, when he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee. He took part in 11-on-11 drills in practice last week, although he missed one day due to an illness. The previous week he only participated in individual drills, when the Packers opened his 21-day practice window while he's still on the physically unable to perform list.
"Obviously, having been in practice and banking some reps, there's still a couple more hurdles for him to clear before we can definitely say that he's a go," LaFleur added. "But he's been showing progress and we'll see where he's at by the end of the week."
Packers tight end Tucker Kraft said last week that it was good just to get Parsons back into full team drills.
"It's been good out there pressing against Micah," Kraft said. "Took on a bull rush from him [in practice]. He's trying to back me into Jordan [Love's] lap. No comment [on who won the rep]. Maybe it was a stalemate. I'm going to say it's a stalemate. Yeah, he'll be making his return soon. He's looking great, but our defense is rolling, and we just hope that they can remain consistent."
The Packers (6-4) technically have their bye this week, but it's a shortened break because they play on the Wednesday of the following week. In fact, the Packers had to get approval from the league and the NFL Players Association to give their players the mandatory four days off during a bye week after the game against the Rams instead of during their Week 11 bye. LaFleur said the players will have off Tuesday to Thursday this week.
"We'll bring them back in on Friday, and then kind of gear up for the week because Saturday will be like a Wednesday in our world," LaFleur said.
Parsons' return won't solve the offensive line issues that led to their downfall in Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings , who sacked Jordan Love eight times. LaFleur said Monday after reviewing the film that the pass protection was as bad as it looked live.
"It was pretty bad, yeah," LaFleur said. "It wasn't good enough. Certainly some things schematically that we didn't do a good job with and then ultimately there was some execution things as well."
Still, LaFleur said he does not plan to make any staff changes, meaning offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich and offensive line coach Luke Butkus will remain on the job. The Packers had to make a late change to their offensive line after right guard Kevin Zeitler sustained a triceps injury in practice. LaFleur said Zeitler had been slated to make his first start of the season until his injury. LaFleur said Zeitler was pushing to play, but the Packers held him out.
As far as the injuries from Sunday's game, LaFleur said he does not have concerns about cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib) or receiver/kick returner Bo Melton (thigh) but will need more time to make a determination about receiver/kick returner Skyy Moore (ankle).

title: How an NFL referee crew worked two games in one day
summary: An inside look at the 14-hour day of four referees who worked an afternoon game in Indianapolis and the Sunday night game in Cincinnati.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- IT'S HARD  to tell when an NFL referee is actually in a hurry because they're always jogging from here to there.

 Jogging onto the field with a bag of footballs, jogging to take their position behind the quarterback, jogging over to the replay monitor to screen a review. But at 4:37 p.m. ET Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium, when referee Don Willard power-walks with his suitcase and bag through the concrete bowels of the stadium, led by a police officer and flanked by three other game officials and an NFL security staffer, it's clear that he is in a hurry.

 "Next stop: Beep! Beep!" umpire Terry Killens yells as the group walks out of the official's locker room in street clothes.

 Kickoff for their second NFL game of the day is less than four hours away, and Cincinnati is still two hours down the dark and construction-interrupted I-74. The crew has a police escort to the highway and then they'll be on their own. Willard, Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew hold their snack boxes in one hand and roll their small suitcases with the other. Willard totes a pink Pedialyte -- necessary for replenishing the 3 hours and 13 minutes of intense focus he had just put in during the Colts' 24-22 victory over the Dolphins. Larrew munches on a cookie while he walks and then accidentally drops it on the floor.

 

 Two stadium security workers wave goodbye and yell, "Drive safe!" But these four VIPs won't be driving themselves anywhere. A black sprinter van waits for the entourage, tucked just behind the Dolphins' team buses. Another stadium security worker escorts a CBS videographer into the area to capture their departure. He backpedals to get the perfect shot: four officials boarding a van that will take them from Indianapolis to Cincinnati for the Bengals' Sunday night game against the Steelers -- pulling double-duty to officiate two NFL games on the same day.

 The security worker tells another stadium worker, "Wow, this is really a big deal, huh?" He explains that the CBS camera he has shepherded into place is going to send its footage to NBC's "Sunday Night Football" broadcast (which will later highlight the feat).

 The NFL declined ESPN's request to speak to the four officials and Ramon George, the league's head of officiating training and development, who was responsible for sorting through the travel disaster created by the FAA's nationwide ground stop Friday.

 George worked through the night Friday to create new crews for each game based on geographic convenience so the game officials didn't need to use unreliable air travel. The result was flip-card changes for the game officials that were longer than the inactive players lists.

 Each of the four double-duty referees work on different crews. At the Sunday night game, the inactives sheet handed out to the media pregame featured an entirely different crew of the seven on-field officials than what had been previously slated, with the parenthetical "the instant replay official still is Chad Adams."

 The situation is likely unprecedented in NFL history because it's risky. The league intentionally arranges for officials to travel on the day before games (except in the case of international games, for which they travel further in advance), so they are settled and adjusted and can get good rest before they work.

 Former NFL vice president of officiating and current Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino told ESPN that when he was running the department, having a game official work two games on the same day "would be the last resort," which shows how extreme the circumstances were. Typically an emergency alternate scenario would impact one crew and two officials, not the entire 17-crew system.

 "I am sure they went through all the different iterations and exhausted every option," Blandino said.

 

 Blandino said officiating two games in one day is the last resort because "it would be like playing two football games back-to-back. There's the physical aspect of running and the mental exhaustion after a game because you are doing a pre-snap routine for every snap, and then the eight-second play, and then a post-snap routine.

 "The officials look like they are not exerting themselves the same way the players are, but they don't get breaks. They don't play one side of the ball. They are out there every snap and every kick. Then to say now I have to reset without any recovery time? That is a challenge."

 "It's exhausting because you're looking for something on every single play," said Russell Yurk, ESPN's rules analyst and former VP of replay for the league office. "You're analyzing every single play. You're watching your players. You're watching your keys, you're making judgment calls, and it doesn't really let up the entire game."

 

 1:03 p.m. 

 Kickoff in Indianapolis. Willard, normally a side judge, has never refereed a regular-season NFL game before, only preseason games and Big Ten conference matchups before he began working for the NFL in 2018. So when he first speaks into the microphone at Lucas Oil Stadium to announce the coin toss, it sounds weird, because his voice is totally unfamiliar.

 Following Willard's announcement of an illegal formation penalty that the Colts declined, CBS analyst Spero Dedes says, "I think we need to lower the volume on the officiating mic -- he is interfering with our call."

 Walker, the field judge, calls two Miami field goals wide left, and an extra point is no good.

 2:40 p.m. 

 Willard and Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley have a spirited conversation with a lot of hand gesturing on Miami's sideline before the second half kicks off.

 On the first play of the second half, Willard's instincts are tested. Colts cornerback Justin Walley hits Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord in the back of his throwing arm. McCord loses the ball with his arm drawn back, poised to throw. The Colts recover in the end zone for a touchdown. But is it a fumble or did he already start to move his arm forward? Willard throws his blue bean bag to mark the spot of the fumble and calls it a fumble recovery touchdown for Indianapolis.

 "This is a tough play, because Walley comes behind Kyle McCord and it's the defensive arm that really hits the ball and makes it go forward. As an official you think that ball is going forward because of the pass," said Gene Steratore, a retired official and CBS rules analyst. "But Don has fumble all the way, and it's a great job by him."

 Colts tight end Alec Ogletree gets to talking with Willard during a break. "Are you one of the ones going to Cincy after this?" he asks.

 Yep, that's us, Willard tells him.

 Ogletree knew there were going to be changes to the crew because on Friday, the Colts had gone over information about the officiating crew as a team, but it was all with an asterisk: it was only who they thought would be working the game.

 "But we didn't really know who was going to be out there till we got out here," Ogletree said.

 "I did ask [Willard], 'So how long you been the ref, like head ref?' He's like, 'First game.'" 

 3:07 p.m. 

 Miami cornerback Chris Johnson picks off Daniel Jones  and runs it it back 59 yards for a touchdown. Willard is standing at the Indianapolis 42, behind the quarterback as he throws, then runs that same distance back to the end zone to keep the play in front of him.

 4:16 p.m. 

 The first game ends after three hours and 13 minutes -- a long one because Miami kept it close. The double-duty refs shower and change into street clothes for their trip to Cincinnati. They've all packed a second uniform, this one for an outdoor game. It will be much colder at Paycor Stadium.

 

 6:37 p.m. 

 The weary travelers arrive at Paycor Stadium and bring their luggage straight into the security meeting at the 100-minute mark before game time. Willard carries a massage gun with him, hinting that his focus on the bus ride was as much about recovery as anything else.

 "They're going to be tired…

title: Jaguars outscoring opponents by 125 points through 10 weeks: Three reasons why
summary: Sunday's victory over the Titans was Jacksonville's fifth win by 17 or more points this season -- the most in the NFL.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are dominating teams and approaching a historic pace.

 Sunday's 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium was their fifth win by 17 or more points this season -- the most in the NFL (the Buffalo Bills are second with three) -- and one shy of the franchise record. They have the best point differential in the league through nine games (plus-125), too, which is the most through nine games since the Bills outscored teams by 145 points in 2021.

 In fact, it has been more than a month since the Jaguars have scored fewer than 30 points.

 Why have they been so dominant? Quarterback Trevor Lawrence is playing and operating head coach Liam Coen's offense at a high level, but the key to making the offense so effective is that it doesn't rely on one or two specific players (other than the QB, of course). The defense has been opportunistic and among the league's best at forcing turnovers, and there's more help on the way.

 There are other reasons, too -- kicker Cam Little has missed just two field goals and hit a 60-yard game winner in London, for example -- but those are the main reasons the Jaguars are 7-2, are in control of the AFC South and have the third-best odds to make and win the Super Bowl, per ESPN's FPI . Let's take a closer look.

 Trevor Lawrence is rolling 
 Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception against the Titans, which tied him with Blake Bortles for the most games with 300 yards and three or more passing touchdowns in franchise history with seven. He now has 21 touchdown passes this season and is on pace to throw for 40, which would break Bortles' single-season passing TD record (35).

 

 "[His performance on Sunday is] up there with one of the better [performances since] I've been with him," Coen said. "Can't say enough about how he's playing right now."

 It's a continuation of the way Lawrence played in the second half of last season. Since Week 11 of 2025, he has 40 touchdown passes, an NFL-best 45 total touchdowns and the third-best Total QBR (74.5). The Jaguars are an NFL-best 15-2 in that span, with both losses coming away from Jacksonville (in Denver and London).

 "I just have a lot of comfort in what we're doing, a lot of confidence I know what we're doing," Lawrence said. "I feel like, myself, and our whole offense, but myself and the staff, we're all on the same page. I know what we're trying to get done. It's not always perfect, but I think having that alignment has been great. We're on the same page and I think obviously the more you see things, the more you rep things, and the more comfortable you get.

 "I think you're seeing that come to life, not just for me, but our whole offense."

 Anyone, anytime 
 Receiver Parker Washington had a big day against the Titans, setting a career high with 152 yards (148 in the first half) and catching a touchdown. However, the Jaguars don't need that kind of performance every week for the pass offense to function at a high level.

 In fact, Washington had only three catches in the previous two games, and the Jaguars still scored 75 points combined in victories over Baltimore and Indianapolis. The pass offense isn't reliant on one pass catcher to have success. The more the merrier.

 "It is a fun group that each week you don't really know who's going to be the guy," Coen said. "And that's what's really fun about game-planning with this group and coming up with a plan throughout the course of the week, because on any given Sunday, any one of these guys can step up."

 

 In addition to Washington, receiver Josh Cameron and tight end Brenton Strange caught touchdown passes Sunday. Strange's TD catch was his second of the season, making him the sixth player with multiple touchdown catches. The only times the Jaguars had more players with multiple touchdown catches in a season in franchise history were in 2020 (seven) and last season, when a record eight players did it in Coen's first season.

 With eight games still remaining, it seems logical to expect Travis Hunter to end up on that list. (He has one TD catch.)

 "I feel like we've seen that time and time this whole year, just seeing other guys make plays," Washington said.

 Opportunistic defense 
 Hunter intercepted Titans quarterback Cam Ward in the first quarter Sunday, giving the defense at least one turnover in eight of nine games this season. Jacksonville leads the NFL in turnover margin (plus-9) and is second with 71 points off those turnovers. (Green Bay has 74.) The Jaguars also rank second in scoring defense (16 points per game allowed) and sixth in rushing defense (91 yards per game allowed).

 There's even more help on the way for the Jaguars with the acquisition of defensive tackles  Jordan Davis  and  Davon Godchaux  and safety  Jessie Bates III , all of whom were acquired via trade last Monday. Davis and Godchaux were added to help shore up a run defense that lost nose tackle DaVon Hamilton to a season-ending knee injury.

 Coen said he's also hoping Davis can help add some interior pass rush, which is something the defense has been missing. Bates, who is regarded as one of the best safeties in the NFL, was added to replace Eric Murray , who was lost for the rest of the season with an elbow injury. Bates has 28 career interceptions and has had at least one in every season of his nine-year career.

 

 Neither Davis nor Bates played Sunday because they had yet to have a bye week. The Jaguars were off in Week 7.

 "We feel confident every time we walk out on the grass on Sundays and hopefully those guys can only come and add to an already talented, tough team as we get down a stretch that we're trying to go on a run here, you know?" Coen said.

 A Super Bowl run, perhaps?

title: Emmett Johnson, Jaxon Smith-Njigba shine in big offensive week for Africa's NFL stars
summary: Week 10 in the 2026 NFL season was one of the most noteworthy in terms of standout performances from offensive players in the NFL with known African ties.
full_text:
Week 10 in the 2026 NFL season was one of the most noteworthy in terms of standout performances from offensive players in the NFL with known African ties.

 Last season's Offensive Player of the Year, Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who proudly represents Sierra Leone due to a connection to the country through his grandparents - is no stranger to prominence in our weekly recaps. However, the Seattle Seahawks wide receiver was not alone in delivering a huge performance over the past week.

 Emmett Johnson, who is of Liberian descent, had a memorable weekend for the Kansas City Chiefs, while Chuba Hubbard - who has Nigerian ties - was crucial in the Carolina Panthers' win over the New Orleans Saints.

 Africa Player of the Week: Emmett Johnson (Kansas City Chiefs) 
 

 Johnson - a running back who grew up in Minneapolis and was born to parents who moved from Liberia - made a mammoth contribution to the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons in his first NFL start.

 Johnson tallied a total of 171 yards - 101 yards across 22 carries and 70 more across six receptions - with two receiving touchdowns.

 The 23-year-old chipped at the Falcons defense bit by bit rather than looking to tear them apart all at once. His longest reception was for 34 yards, but he was ruthlessly efficient and scored touchdowns in both the first and last quarters.

 This was the third game in a row in which the former Nebraska running back scored at least one touchdown. Previously, he picked up a receiving touchdown in defeat to the Denver Broncos and a rushing touchdown in the 35-12 win over the New York Jets.

 

 With a 7-2 record, the Chiefs narrowly lead the AFC West and look set for a fight to the finish for that top spot against the Broncos.

 Africa Moment of the Week: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (Seattle Seahawks) 
 Smith-Njigba left plenty for the highlights reel with his eight catches totalling 171 yards in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, but nothing could top his third-quarter 71-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the corner.

 Largely due to Smith-Njigba's offensive contribution already up until that point, the reigning Super Bowl champions held a slender 14-10 lead when their star wide receiver caught a pass from Drew Lock, dodged a diving tackle attempt from Quay Walker, ran round the outside of Eric Stokes, and went all the way for the touchdown. From there, the Raiders had simply left themselves a mountain too high to climb.

 Honorable mentions 
 Chuba Hubbard - born in Canada but of Nigerian descent - starred with two rushing touchdowns and a total of 172 yards (92 rushing and 80 receiving) in the Carolina Panthers' 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints.

 Alvin Kamara - who has family ties to Liberia - scored two touchdowns for the Saints in defeat.

 Nigerian-American defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore was the unlikely scorer of a crucial touchdown in the Indianapolis Colts' 24-22 win over the Miami Dolphins.

 Defensively, Odafe Oweh - whose roots are in Nigeria - picked up his fifth sack of the season in the Washington Commanders' 24-21 win over the New York Giants.

 His compatriot, Foyesade Oluokun, made 10 tackles in the Jacksonville Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans.

 Elsewhere among representatives of the Nigerian diaspora, Boye Mafe made a sack in the Cincinnati Bengals' 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Malik Mustapha defended two passes and made one interception in the San Francisco 49ers' 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys, while Davison Igbinosun also defended two passes and made an interception in the Buffalo Bills' 31-12 win over the New York Jets.

 Africa-born Player Watch 
 On this front, Week 10 was relatively quiet. Guinea-born Liberian defensive end Kwity Paye picked up five tackles for the Raiders in their loss to the Seahawks, but it was overall not his best game. 

 Zimbabwe's Nate Landman played his part in the LA Rams' 34-6 win over the Arizona Cardinals, but elsewhere across the league, players born on the continent face a struggle for consistency in terms of minutes. 

 The Philadelphia Eagles - one franchise that has handed chances to African stars in abundance in recent years - had a bye, but will return to action on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

title: Rams center Coleman Shelton out 4-6 weeks with hamstring injury
summary: Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Cardinals.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams center Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring and is expected to sit out the next four to six weeks, a team spokesperson said Monday.
Shelton sustained the injury in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Arizona Cardinals . He had not missed an offensive snap this season for the Rams before his injury.
Shelton was replaced at center by Dylan McMahon , who played only nine offensive snaps before he injured his knee. The Rams said Monday that McMahon partially tore his patellar tendon and will be put on injured reserve.
Offensive lineman Beaux Limmer moved to center after McMahon's injury, and backup offensive lineman Bill Murray moved to left guard, playing 49 offensive snaps.
The injuries are just the latest for a Rams offense that is also currently without wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , tight end Terrance Ferguson , and guard Steve Avila .
The Rams, 6-4 after winning four games in a row, are on their bye this week. They host the Green Bay Packers in Week 12.

title: Behind Raiders fans' tribute to Fernando Mendoza's mother
summary: Tom Joanides' social media campaign became a meaningful tribute when Mendoza scored in his first NFL start.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders fan Tom Joanides, 46, had his first viral moment on social media for a good cause.

 He went on X asking Raiders fans, who were attending Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium, to stay seated after No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza scored his first touchdown.

 

 The idea was meant to honor Mendoza's mother, Elsa, who has been confined to a wheelchair due to her multiple sclerosis diagnosis.

 Watching the game at home with his family, Joanides saw thousands of Raiders fans remain in their seats while celebrating Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run in the first quarter of his first career start. Elsa and Mendoza's father, Fernando Mendoza Sr., were seated in a suite, cheering on their son. "The fan base has an understanding that these are people; I'm shocked and elated that it actually happened. I've never had anything go viral ever," Joanides told ESPN. "But I'm not surprised that Raider Nation has the heart that it does."

 Despite the Raiders losing to the Seahawks 21-13 , Mendoza was "super grateful" for the fans' gesture, and it meant a lot to his family.

 "On a dark day, that brings a smile to my face," Mendoza said postgame . 

 In July, Joanides, a Los Angeles native, went on X and wrote a post, asking fans to stay seated whenever Mendoza scored his first touchdown at home.

 However, his post didn't receive much traction .

 "I don't have a huge account or anything, so I was like yelling into the void," Joanides said.

 Five days before the Raiders' home matchup, Joanides went on X to reshare his message from the summer.

 This time, the fan base heard him. Joanides' post received more than 800,000 views and close to 400 reposts.

 

 Joanides, who began attending Raiders games with his dad when he was 3, said he would list "Raider Nation" as his ethnicity on government forms if he could.

 Joanides was inspired after watching a Front Office Sports interview , in which Mendoza said he donated $500,000 to the University of Miami Health System and the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine to help fight against multiple sclerosis.

 Mendoza's advocacy for the cause is inspired by Elsa, who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2008. His family launched the Mendoza Family Fund in April, which directly supports the National MS Society.

 Through their foundation, Mendoza's family has raised more than $1 million .

 "I just found it really touching," Joanides said. "This [was] an opportunity for this fan base to welcome [Mendoza] and his family in a very particular way and show what Raider Nation is all about."

title: Dolphins cut kicker Zane Gonzalez a day after costly misses in loss to Colts
summary: The Dolphins waived kicker Zane Gonzalez on Monday, a day after he missed two field goals and an extra point in a 24-22 loss to the Colts.
full_text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- The Dolphins waived kicker Zane Gonzalez , a day after a series of missed kicks hindered Miami in a 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts .
Gonzalez joined the Dolphins in Week 7 after the team released Riley Patterson but missed kicks in three consecutive games -- including two field goals and an extra point in Sunday's loss to Indianapolis. Speaking to reporters after the game, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was blunt in his assessment of how the missed kicks impacted the game's outcome.
"We got to make the extra point, and we got to make the field goals," Hafley said. "I'm not going to ever B.S. you. It's 24-22. A missed extra point forces us to go for two, and we missed two field goals. That's seven points. We have to make those."
Dolphins special teams coordinator Chris Tabor said last week that he still "had a lot of confidence" in Gonzalez, and suggested he was still acclimating after missing the first six weeks of the season.
He made two of three field goal attempts against the New England Patriots in Week 8, before hitting three of four attempts against the Detroit Lions last week.
Gonzalez made a 53-yard field goal Sunday, but missed from 47 yards and 51 yards, including a go-ahead kick early in the fourth quarter.
"You look at the misses, you look at why he missed and what he's done in the body of work and the time that we've had him and you give him a shot and that's what we did," Hafley said Monday. "And that was the decision that was made. And unfortunately, the results weren't very good this week, and now we're going to find another kicker."
Hafley said the Dolphins had a pair of available kickers in mind and would make a decision later this week. The team has tried out multiple kickers over the past several weeks, including former All-Pros Daniel Carlson and Justin Tucker .
Also, defensive tackle Zeek Biggers will have season-ending knee surgery to repair his lateral meniscus, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Monday night.

title: Vikings WR Jordan Addison needs thumb surgery, is candidate for IR
summary: Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison needs to undergo surgery on his thumb and is a candidate for injured reserve, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Vikings receiver Jordan Addison could be out for a month because of a thumb injury that will require surgery, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.
O'Connell termed it a "freak injury" that occurred while Addison was "catching passes on air" during practice last Friday, aggravating a minor injury Addison had dealt with since training camp. The Vikings listed him as questionable on their injury report and then made him inactive after a short warmup Sunday morning before their 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
O'Connell said Addison's projected return is "right around hopefully that short-term IR kind of window." Players who are placed on injured reserve must miss at least four games.
"I don't anticipate it being a long-term kind of thing," O'Connell said.
If Addison goes on injured reserve, the earliest he could return is for the Vikings' Week 15 game against the Detroit Lions at U.S. Bank Stadium, scheduled to be played on "Sunday Night Football."
Addison missed the Vikings' Week 5 game against the New Orleans Saints because of a hamstring injury. In seven starts this season, he has caught 18 passes for 277 yards and one touchdown.
With Addison sidelined against the Packers, and veteran Jauan Jennings already declared out because of a calf injury, second-year receiver Tai Felton got his third NFL start alongside Justin Jefferson . Felton caught three passes for 33 yards. Another second-year receiver, Myles Price , caught four passes for 49 yards, including a 38-yard touchdown.
The Vikings waived veteran Odell Beckham Jr . last week but he re-signed to their practice squad and would be available for Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City if needed.

title: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
summary: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.
full_text:
The outlook for the  New England Patriots ' 2026 season has been dramatically altered. After suffering an injury on the Patriots' first drive against the  Detroit Lions  on Sunday, quarterback Drake Maye did not fly back from Munich with the team out of caution, as the team is concerned he might have sustained a fractured ankle .

 The 5-5 Patriots haven't been among the AFC's elite in 2026, but were hoping to make a charge to the playoffs -- and Maye potentially finding his past runner-up MVP form was one of their silver linings.

 When Maye was taking care of the football and extending plays, the Patriots were explosive and flashed potential to hang with the best -- as a Week 4 win at the Buffalo Bills showed. But when Maye was not buttoned-up with his decision-making (he entered Sunday with 11 INTs) the Patriots struggled. When he was cleaner in that area, it was just enough to get by some of the league's lower-echelon teams, with close wins against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins , who have won a combined three games this season.

 Coach Mike Vrabel often says it's hard to win when a team's best players don't play well, and simply put, Maye is the team's best offensive player.

 Entering Week 10, he ranked top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3).

 Now potentially without Maye for weeks or even the season, the question is can the team make it back to the playoffs?

 ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss answers some of the top questions about the trickle-down effect of Maye's injury and analyst Matt Bowen answers a fantasy question on what to expect if you have Patriots players in your lineup.

 

 

 Is the Patriots' 2026 season over? 
 When Vrabel was hired as head coach in January 2025, he said the team's goals were to win the division, host home playoff games and compete for championships. Their odds of doing that without Maye are closer to zero, starting with the current standings -- they are 5-5 while the AFC East rival Bills are 8-1.

 

 Here is the rest of the Patriots' schedule: they are on the bye in Week 11 before a road trip to face the winless  Los Angeles Chargers , then two huge home games in a span of five days -- vs. the Bills (Dec. 6) and the  Minnesota Vikings  (Dec. 10). Then they're at the Kansas City Chiefs and the New York Jets before finishing the year with home games against the Denver Broncos and the  Miami Dolphins .

 They have played poorly the past two weeks in blowout losses to the Packers and Lions, ravaged by injuries across the roster, but Maye's presence -- even as he battled through inconsistent play with turnovers -- gave them a sliver of hope.

 Consider what happened Sunday: After New England's opening drive when Maye was injured on the final play, the Patriots totaled seven points and gained 82 yards over 10 drives, averaging 1.9 yards per play (not including kneel down). New England punted on eight of those drives, with seven three-and-outs.

 Maye has been the driving force behind the passing game. Entering Sunday, Patriots pass catchers recorded 38.1% of their yards after the catch, the third-lowest total in the NFL behind the Texans (37.1%) and Giants (36.8%), per ESPN Research.

 The defense has also mightily struggled as of late, giving the offense little room for error. Since Week 7, the Patriots are giving up the second-most yards per game (411.5), behind only the 1-8 Tennessee Titans .

 With some of the NFL's elite teams on the horizon, life without Maye could look bleak.

 

 What is Drake Maye's possible recovery timeline? 
 The recovery timeline for similar injuries have varied, depending on the severity.

 In January, Broncos QB Bo Nix suffered a broken ankle and underwent surgery two days later. The initial recovery timetable reported was 12 weeks . In April, he underwent a clean-up surgery to fix bone spurs. Nix, who had a history of ankle injuries, was ready for training camp in July.

 In September 2022, 49ers QB Trey Lance underwent surgery on his right ankle after suffering "a fibula fracture and ligament disruption" in a game. The injury ended his season and required a follow-up surgery in December of that year to remove hardware that was causing irritation. He was cleared to participate in OTAs the following April.

 In 2024, 49ers linebacker Fred Warner said he had been playing most of the season with a fractured bone in his ankle .

 As we learn more about the specific type of ankle injury Maye has, the timeline will become clearer.

 

 What can the offense get out of Tommy DeVito ? 
 Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has been through this before, most recently in 2016 when Tom Brady was serving a four-game NFL suspension and Jimmy Garoppolo and Jacoby Brissett stepped in to help the team to a 3-1 record. McDaniels' offense has flexibility to play to the specific strengths of the quarterback, with an obvious example coming with some designed runs for Brissett in 2016 that never would have been called with Brady.

 DeVito struggled Sunday when taking over for Maye, and Vrabel noted it was a tough position for him to be thrust into because backups don't receive many, if any, first-team repetitions during the week of practice.

 

 "There were some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp, and really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye," Vrabel said. "I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand, whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket, get us in the right play, get the ball out quicker or look at protections or rotation, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve."

 DeVito had success with the deep ball in the preseason, and made improvements processing information on defensive coverages, so some of the things he has going for him are similar to Maye. And, of course, DeVito briefly caught fire with the  New York Giants  when thrust into a similar situation.

 In eight career starts (all with the Giants), DeVito is 3-5 with a 26.4 QBR, 65.3% completion rate, 1,170 passing yards for seven touchdowns, one interception and 34 sacks. He isn't as mobile as Maye, with only 36 rushes for 198 yards during those starts.

 Vrabel reflected optimism in the backup QB they signed to a  two-year contract with a maximum value of $7.4 million in March. 

 "I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said Monday. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."

 

 Could the Patriots explore other options at quarterback?  
 That is a longer-shot scenario in terms of signing someone to be the starter, mainly due to the intricacies of the offense and the time crunch -- and also because there aren't many, if any, capable starters available. A more likely option initially is to utilize the 17-player practice squad to add a third layer of quarterback depth behind DeVito and rookie Behren Morton , the seventh-round pick from Texas Tech.

 Another avenue to explore would be other teams' practice squads to see if there is a worthy option to sign to the 53-man roster in a backup role. There are 15 quarterbacks on practice squads, a group including Will Levis (Jets), Nick Mullens (Jaguars), Kyle Trask (Cowboys) Hendon Hooker (Titans), Jake Browning (Chargers) and Luke Altmyer (Lions).

 "I don't see that being the case right now, but we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see," Vrabel said Monday about the possibility of adding a quarterback.

 

 How have injuries decimated the Patriots this season? 
 New England mostly had good fortune health-wise in its surprise run to the Super Bowl last year, and 2026 has been the other side of the coin. Vrabel noted in a Monday radio interview that it evens out over time.

 

 It began in the spring when tight end Julian Hill , who they signed…

title: Giants QB J.J. McCarthy's growth is showing in the numbers
summary: After only three starts and four games playing for New York, the quarterback's numbers are staggering.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Quarterback  J.J. McCarthy played "very well" in Thursday night's  24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders , according to coach John Harbaugh. He set a career high with 293 yards passing and had the New York Giants moving the ball the entire evening. 
 
 The night ended with McCarthy throwing his first interception since he entered the game in the fourth quarter last month against the New Orleans Saints . It still didn't come close to ruining the overall performance or change the impression that McCarthy has been impressive since becoming the team's starting quarterback. 
 
 It's not perfect, but it's promising. 
 
 "There were some plays made, he made some throws, scrambled. I thought J.J. played very well," Harbaugh said. 
 
 He later added that McCarthy "threw some dimes" and made some "great throws." McCarthy also seemed to be more comfortable in the pocket than last week against the Philadelphia Eagles , when he took five sacks, and did better getting through his progressions. In a lot of ways, he barely resembled the quarterback who struggled his first two seasons with the Minnesota Vikings , the first because of injury and then as he got acclimated to the NFL game. 
 
 
 
 McCarthy, the No. 10 pick for the Vikings in the 2024 NFL draft, was traded to the Giants  in late September for a fifth-round pick. He was pleased but not blown away with his performance Thursday night. 
 
 "There's things I could've done better," he said afterward. 
 
 That just goes to show how far McCarthy has come in such a short time. He was the third-stringer in Minnesota just six weeks ago. 
 
 It may be only three starts and four games playing for the Giants, but the numbers are staggering. They suggest a much different quarterback than the one who started 10 games for the Vikings last season.   
 
 McCarthy's QBR has skyrocketed from 36.1 to 56.3 this season. His completion percentage has gone from second to last among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts at 57.6% to 63.5% with the Giants. His completion percentage over expectation has risen from an awful minus-5.2 with Minnesota (second worst only to Chicago's Caleb Williams last year) to plus-5.0, which puts him fifth among all quarterbacks this season. 
 
 His off-target throw percentage has dropped from 19.3% to 13.5% and his yards per dropback has gone from a bad 5.71 to 8.04 with the Giants, which is fourth in the NFL. Even McCarthy's precision passing percentage has gone from 45.3% (dead last) to a more than respectable 53.5%. 
 
 The improvement in his accuracy has been among the most noticeable differences. It was on display against the Commanders. Perhaps McCarthy's best throw came when he was under pressure with a blitzer in his face early in the fourth quarter. He hit tight end Isaiah Likely in stride with a laser through a tight window over the middle for a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown. 
 
 "That's probably as good a play as you're going to see in the National Football League all season, honestly," Harbaugh said. 
 
 It has McCarthy and the Giants feeling confident about this season and his future. The 23-year-old quarterback has been a good fit with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy's scheme and in New York. 
 
 
 At least so far. 
 
 "I just feel really good in terms of my preparation going into every week. They are very detailed in terms of what they want from me, what the intent is every single play. There is no gray area going into each play and I just really appreciate the heck out of that," he said. "It is all about building, constantly growing, and that is what we are focused on. Being in the league for a little over two years now, seeing defenses that I have seen before and running concepts that I have run before, everything seems to be slowing down for me. 
 
 "Just being able to keep stacking and keep growing 1% every single day and I am just so blessed to be in this offense and so blessed to be a part of this organization." 
 
 The spike in numbers is not all apples to apples. McCarthy is a year older, with more experience and in a completely different situation. But there clearly has been progress, especially in understanding the professional game. It has been apparent when he faces zone defenses. 
 
 McCarthy is averaging 10.9 yards per attempt against zone defenses through four games as a Giants quarterback. That's second best of any quarterback behind only Houston's C.J. Stroud since McCarthy entered the lineup. He was at a paltry 6.8 yards per attempt against zone defenses last season, which ranked him near the bottom of the league. 
 
 In fact, McCarthy's expected points added against zone defense of 0.22 is tops among all quarterbacks this season. It seems to be a sign that his understanding of the game is improving under the guidance of Nagy and quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan and trending in the right direction with more playing time and experience. 
 
 "I think he's done a great job," Harbaugh said Friday.   
 
 It's still early, but maybe, just maybe, the Giants hit on something here.

title: Sources: Jets QB Geno Smith avoided major ankle injury, testing shows
summary: Imaging tests performed on Jets quarterback Geno Smith's injured left ankle did not reveal any major concerns, sources said Monday.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith , who underwent imaging tests Monday on his left ankle, avoided a major injury, sources told the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
Smith dealt with a variety of injuries during Sunday's game, but his ankle provided the biggest concern. He will continue to be evaluated throughout the week, but the hope is that he will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers .
"He's good," a source told ESPN. "He'll be fine."
Coach Aaron Glenn declined to comment on the injury earlier Monday but emphasized that Smith remains New York's starter and pushed back on the notion of playing rookie Cade Klubnik for evaluation purposes.
"Geno's our starter," Glenn said on a videoconference with reporters. "Come on now, let's not do that.
"I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter."
Smith exited twice in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills . He missed the first series of the third quarter due to a concussion evaluation, then returned for one series before hurting his ankle later in the quarter while falling backward on a knockdown by blitzing safety Cole Bishop .
The Jets (2-8), losers of five straight, face the Chargers (0-8) on Sunday at SoFi Stadium.
The 36-year-old Smith, whose contract expires at the end of the season, is having a solid year as the Jets' bridge quarterback. He's 19th in Total QBR (53.3), with 12 touchdown passes and three interceptions, but the Jets are only 26th in scoring (19.4 points per game).
Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson, made his NFL debut Sunday. He threw an interception and was sacked three times while completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.
The Jets' third quarterback is former Tennessee Titans second-round pick Will Levis , who is on the practice squad.

title: Aaron Glenn gives up defensive playcalling
summary: Rich Cimini breaks down the Jets' decision to switch up the playcalling.

title: Jets Aaron Glenn ceded defensive playcalling to DC Brian Duker on Sunday
summary: Amid a prolonged defensive slide, Aaron Glenn handed the playcalling duties Sunday to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, Glenn revealed Monday.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn, who famously declared last offseason that defensive playcalling is "my superpower," has pulled the plug on himself.
Amid a prolonged defensive slide, Glenn handed the playcalling duties Sunday to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, Glenn revealed Monday in a videoconference with reporters.
It's a surprising twist, considering Glenn's strident position in the offseason. At the time, he said it was important for him to assume the playcalling, adding that it was a mistake not to run the defense last season. He ceded that responsibility to defensive coordinator Steve Wilks, whom he fired late in the season.
Now, with his job security waning by the week, Glenn has changed direction again.
Explaining his decision, Glenn said he made Duker the "lead" playcaller, adding that he still had input into what he described as a collaborative process.
"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."
Glenn, whose record dropped to 5-22 with a 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills , was noncommittal on whether Duker will continue to call plays. Duker, 37, is a first-time coordinator who had no playcalling experience before Sunday.
The Jets (2-8), losers of five straight, face the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) on Sunday at SoFi Stadium. After a promising start, the Jets have allowed 31.6 points per game during the losing streak. On Sunday, they allowed three second-half touchdowns to the Bills.
"They have a very similar mindset in calling the defense," safety Dane Belton said of Glenn and Duker. "There wasn't much difference from my perspective."
Glenn recently acknowledged the difficulty in calling plays and managing the entire game. Early in the season, he made several questionable clock-management decisions, fueling the narrative that he was overmatched by having both jobs.
The backstory is that Glenn appeared to be on the verge of hiring veteran coach Wink Martindale as his defensive coordinator and playcaller after last season, but there was an eleventh-hour shift that raised eyebrows.
Glenn wound up hiring Duker, who wasn't among the initial group of candidates, and announcing he'd do the playcalling himself. Glenn refuted reports that owner Woody Johnson insisted on that arrangement.
On Monday, Glenn was asked about his relationship with Johnson, and he praised the owner for his patient and consistent approach. He said Johnson is "the first thing I think about after every game because he's been so good to this team."
Johnson has presided over 15 consecutive non-playoff seasons, including 10 straight losing years. He signed Glenn to a five-year contract for a reported $60 million, but the Jets are mired in one of the worst losing cycles in franchise history.
Johnson hasn't spoken publicly in 13 months.
Glenn said "the good thing about me and Woody's relationship is we don't flip-flop on each other. We don't change. We're always honest. When we do have conversations, he will give me the good and the bad, same way I would give him the good and the bad. Then we'll move on and we'll go to the next week.
"I think that's the promising thing about having a relationship with men of stature, is that he's not going to be one way one week and then turn to be another way the next week. I pride myself on being that, too. Just because we're in a losing phase, I'm not going to change who I am for the players."

title: Mike McCarthy on Steelers' blowout loss: 'Needs to stop there'
summary: After a deflating loss at Cincinnati, Pittsburgh faces a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- In the wake of a 20-point loss Sunday night, Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen was soft-spoken and introspective as he outlined two paths forward for his team.

 "I think, for the most part, all of us are looking at ourselves and just knowing where we could have been better, what we could have done just to stop the bleeding here and there," he said. "The other way you could look at it is [that] it goes downhill, and we can just keep going downhill the whole season."

 Monday afternoon, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy emphatically chose the former.

 "This needs to be one game, and it needs to stop there," McCarthy said. "... This is a part of the journey of the season, but it needs to be one game, and that'll be our approach as we prepare for Philadelphia."

 After a deflating 38-18 Week 10 loss , the Steelers face a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 

 But just because McCarthy needs the loss to be a one-game speed bump in the Steelers' season doesn't mean it will be -- especially facing a cross-state rival in a city where the Steelers haven't won a regular-season game since 1965.

 And though the Steelers had a history of resilience under former coach Mike Tomlin and posted a 12-2 record in games following a loss of 20 or more points, McCarthy's units haven't rebounded as successfully. McCarthy is 8-15 in games following a loss of at least 20 points, including a 2-8 record in Dallas. Even so, McCarthy dismissed the idea Sunday night that the loss could turn the tide of the season.

 "Oh, wow," he said, somewhat incredulous at the question. "It's one loss, and it will be dealt with as much. I'm more focused on the details of the fundamentals and the things we needed to do.

 "We're not going to drive down the drama road of those types of things. It's a waste of time. It's a waste of energy, and we're going to pour our energy into ourselves looking in the mirror and stay focused on the things that we can control."

 The Steelers did that after each of their previous losses and responded with wins, including a four-game streak after the Thursday night loss in Cleveland during Week 4.

 But Sunday night's loss at Cincinnati felt different. A win against one of the league's hottest teams could have legitimized Pittsburgh's 6-2 start to a national audience, solidified its standing as a serious postseason contender and validated a series of front office decisions, including bringing back quarterback Aaron Rodgers this offseason and also standing pat at this month's NFL trade deadline.

 Though they entered Cincinnati as underdogs, the Steelers had reason to believe they could prove the sportsbooks wrong. Teams coming off a bye were undefeated in games against opponents who played in an international game the previous week. McCarthy was 12-6 after bye weeks. And perhaps most crucially, the Steelers beat the Bengals 30-27 seven weeks earlier.

 

 Instead, the Steelers were thoroughly dismantled and outplayed by Cincinnati in every phase. They were outgained by 262 yards, their worst margin in nearly three decades. Rodgers opened the game with a career-worst eight incompletions before finally connecting with tight end Darnell Washington late in the second quarter. And the Steelers' formidable edge rushers didn't record a quarterback pressure or sack on a near-flawless Joe Burrow , while Rodgers was sacked three times and hit six times total.

 "The biggest thing this week was handling how to win and coming off a four-game win streak and then we had a bye," Steelers left tackle Troy Fautanu said. "We were fresh. There was no real excuse for us going out there and performing like this. We just got to get better."

 That starts with another week of introspection and self-improvement. After the Week 4 loss to the Browns, McCarthy's mandate to his players was to clean up their house. This week, the Steelers have to break out the brooms and dustpans again.

 "Our toughness didn't go away because we got beat last week," Pittsburgh defensive coordinator Patrick Graham said Monday. "Our resiliency didn't go away because we got beat yesterday. We lost the game. We didn't play the way we wanted to play. We didn't coach the way we wanted to coach, and they beat us.

 "... We're going to pull closer together and get the answers and go out there. And we got a great opportunity this week against Philadelphia, against a team that's fighting right now an in-state rivalry, and it's going to provide some spark there.

 "But we got plenty of motivation to get it right as opposed to going the other route."
